> जगत उत्पादको यो विश्वकर्मा नोऽस्माकमुत्पन्नानि धामानि देवानां तेजः
> स्थानानि वेद वेत्ति । किं बहुना । विश्वा विश्वानि भुवना भूतजातानि वेद वेत्ति ।
> यश्च देवानामग्निवाय्वादीनां नामधा नाम्नां धाता इंद्रादीन्निर्माय
> तेषामिंद्रादि नाम कृत्वा तत्रत्यदेवेषु स्थापयिता एक एव । तं देवमन्यान्यानि
> भुवना भूतजातानि प्रश्नं कः परमेश्वर इति पृच्छां यंति । प्राप्नुवंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk beginning यो नः पिता (*yo naḥ pitā*) is the yājyā verse for the purodāśa offering in the animal sacrifice mentioned before; the sūtra says: यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता या ते धामानि परमाणि यावमा (*yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā yā te dhāmāni paramāṇi yāvamā*) (Ā. 3-8). Viśvakarman is our father, that is, our protector; and not merely protector, but also begetter, our producer. Sāyaṇa anticipates the doubt "how is he our producer?" and answers it with a hesitant concession. He who is the ordainer is the producer of the whole world. He, Viśvakarman, knows the abodes of the gods that have been brought forth for us, that is, their places of radiance. What more need be said: he knows all beings, all that is born. He who is the name-giver of the gods, Agni, Vāyu and the others, that is, the one who sets down their names, having fashioned Indra and the rest and having given them the names Indra and so on, establishes them among the gods; he alone is one. To that god the other beings come with the question "Who is the supreme Lord?"; that is, they approach him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which god
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पिता (*pitā*)—who is the protector
- जनिता (*janitā*)—and the producer
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- विधाता (*vidhātā*)—is the maker of the whole world
- धामानि (*dhāmāni*)—all the places of radiance
- वेद (*veda*)—knows
- विश्वा भुवना (*viśvā bhuvanā*)—knows the whole world
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods Agni and the rest
- नामधाः (*nāmadhāḥ*)—is the one who assigns the names, that god
- एक एव (*eka eva*)—is without a second
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Viśvakarman
- अन्या भुवना (*anyā bhuvanā*)—the other beings
- प्रश्नं (*praśnaṃ*)—with the question to know the nature of the Lord
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god who is our protector and producer, who is the maker of the whole world, who knows all the places of radiance, who gives the names to the gods Agni and the rest, that god is without a second. All the other beings approach him with the question to know the nature of the Lord.

##### English translation
He who is our preserver, our parent, the creator (of all), who knows our abodes (and knows) all beings, who is the name-giver of the gods—he is one ; other beings come to him to inquire.

### Printed p. 274

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the sacrifice of the animal offering to Viśvakarman spoken of earlier, in the offering of the purodāśa, this Ṛk beginning योनः पिता (*yonaḥ pitā*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is made clear by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता या ते धामानि परमाणि यावमा (*yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā yā te dhāmāni paramāṇi yāvamā*) (Ā. 3-8).

असूर्ते सूर्ते रजसि निषत्ते ये भूतानि समकृण्वन्निमानि (*asūrte sūrte rajasi niṣatte ye bhūtāni samakṛṇvannimāni*)—here the commentator has explained the words असूर्ते (*asūrte*) and सूर्ते (*sūrte*) in one way and Yāska in another. According to the commentator's explanation: असूर्ते सरणवर्जिते सूर्ते सरणसहिते स्थावरजंगमात्मक रजसि लोके । (*asūrte saraṇavarjite sūrte saraṇasahite sthāvarajaṃgamātmaka rajasi loke |*). That is, in this world, which is made up of moving and unmoving things, both together: of living beings that have the nature of moving about, and of mountains and the like that do not move (that is, are motionless).

But Yāska says: असूर्ते सूर्ते । असुसमीरिताः सुसमीरिते वातसमीरिता माध्यमका देवगणास्ते रसेन पृथिवीं तर्पयंतो भूतानि च कुर्वंति त आयुजंतेत्यतिक्रांतं प्रतिवचनं ॥ ( (*asūrte sūrte | asusamīritāḥ susamīrite vātasamīritā mādhyamakā devagaṇāste rasena pṛthivīṃ tarpayaṃto bhūtāni ca kurvaṃti ta āyujaṃtetyatikrāṃtaṃ prativacanaṃ ‖ (*) (Ni. 6-15). The groups of gods of the middle region, impelled by the breath, the vital air, or impelled by the wind (the gods of the atmosphere, the Maruts and others), dwelling in the atmosphere that is stirred by the wind, wet the earth with moisture and gratify the beings upon it, that is, the living creatures. The seer addresses the sacrificers: "Worship those gods."

In the present reasoning there are two main points. First: (1) Viśvakarman, the cause of all origin and subsistence, the one without a second, alone is the maker of all the gods and the one who assigns their names; likewise he is the possessor of the different kinds of names. (2) Second: since he is distinct from the whole created world, his nature is beyond grasp. Because his nature surpasses even the knowledge of the gods, all ask in order to learn what his nature is, but there is none who has known him.

### Printed p. 275

The Lord named Viśvakarman is all-pervading; the sun, the moon and all the planets, and all the gods, are contained in him alone. All are subject to his rule.

तस्याच्च देवा बहुदा संप्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि । प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च ॥ (*tasyācca devā bahudā saṃprasūtāḥ sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi | prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaśca śraddhā satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiśca ‖*) (Mu. U. 2-1-7) **NOTE**

From this Supreme Person alone come the gods, the Sādhyas, men, animals, birds and the rest, austerity, faith, truth and chastity; all these have been produced. Moreover, in answer to the question what देवानां नामधा एक एव (*devānāṃ nāmadhā eka eva*) means, there is the following:

एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासने गार्गि सूर्याचंद्रमसौ विधृतौ तिष्ठत एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रकाशने गार्गि द्यावापृथिव्यौ विधृते तिष्ठत एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रकाशने गार्गि निमेषा मुहूर्ता अहोरात्राण्यर्धमासा मासा ऋतवः संवत्सरा इति विधृतास्तिष्ठंत्येतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासने गार्गि प्राज्योऽन्या नद्यः स्यंदंते श्वेतेभ्यः पर्वतेभ्यः प्रतीच्योन्या ॥ (*etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi sūryācaṃdramasau vidhṛtau tiṣṭhata etasya vā akṣarasya prakāśane gārgi dyāvāpṛthivyau vidhṛte tiṣṭhata etasya vā akṣarasya prakāśane gārgi nimeṣā muhūrtā ahorātrāṇyardhamāsā māsā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarā iti vidhṛtāstiṣṭhaṃtyetasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi prājyo 'nyā nadyaḥ syaṃdaṃte śvetebhyaḥ parvatebhyaḥ pratīcyonyā ‖*)

Subject to the command of this Lord (Viśvakarman), the imperishable, the one without a second, the sun and the moon have received their appointed designations and keep their steady movements. According to this command the heaven and the earth too stand firm in their own appointed places. By his rule alone all the divisions of time carry on their going and coming in due order. Therefore this Lord is the cause of all dealings between gods and men.

Moreover, since the whole luminous world is a part of the Lord, the names of all the gods, Indra and the rest, are only other names of his. According to each action, he is dealt with under the respective designations. The many epithets such as पिता (*pitā*), जनिता (*janitā*) and विधाता (*vidhātā*) declare his actions that benefit the world.

यादृगेव ददृशे तादृगुच्यते सं छायया दधिरे सिध्रयाप्सा । महीमस्मभ्यमुरुषामुरु ज्रयो बृहत्सु वीरमनपच्युतं सहः ॥ (*yādṛgeva dadṛśe tādṛgucyate saṃ chāyayā dadhire sidhrayāpsā | mahīmasmabhyamuruṣāmuru jrayo bṛhatsu vīramanapacyutaṃ sahaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-44-6)

The Lord is one, but he has the form of the universe. Whatever form he assumes, he is spoken of by the designation suited to it. Because of his power, the gods too, who are his other forms,

### Printed p. 276

provide the world with the wealth suited to their respective natures. But the individual gods are not independent. All follow his rule. His resolve is the root; the others are its followers. The epithets according to the respective actions are as follows:

यजुरित्येष हीदग्ं सर्वं युनक्ति समिति छंदोगा एतस्मिन् हीदग्ं सर्वं समानमुक्थमिति बृहच्छा एष हीदग्ं सर्वमुत्थापयति यूतुरिति यातुविद एतेन हीदग्ं सर्वं यतं विषमिति सर्पाः सर्प इति सर्पविद ऊर्गिति देवा रयिरिति मनुष्या मायेत्यसुराः स्वधेति पितरो देवजन इति देवजनविदो रूपमिति गंधर्वा गंध इत्यप्सरसस्तं यथायथोपासते तदेव भवति ॥ (*yajurityeṣa hīdagṃ sarvaṃ yunakti samiti chaṃdogā etasmin hīdagṃ sarvaṃ samānamukthamiti bṛhacchā eṣa hīdagṃ sarvamutthāpayati yūturiti yātuvida etena hīdagṃ sarvaṃ yataṃ viṣamiti sarpāḥ sarpa iti sarpavida ūrgiti devā rayiriti manuṣyā māyetyasurāḥ svadheti pitaro devajana iti devajanavido rūpamiti gaṃdharvā gaṃdha ityapsarasastaṃ yathāyathopāsate tadeva bhavati ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-5-2-20)

The Adhvaryus designate him as यजुः (*yajuḥ*). Because he joins the whole universe into one, he has this name. Because everything is contained in him and all things of the universe have an equal state, the Sāma-singers designate him as सामन् (*sāman*). Because he causes everything to come into being, the Bahvṛcas call him उक्त (*ukta*). Because he holds every single thing in this world in an ordered bond, the sorcerers (the knowers of sorcery) call him यातु (*yātu*). Among serpents he is renowned as poison, among the catchers of serpents as the serpent, among the company of the gods as ऊर्ज (*ūrja*), among men as wealth, among the Asuras as illusion, among the fathers as स्वधॆ (*svadhè*). The Gandharvas call him beautiful in form, and the Apsarases call him fragrance. Therefore he is designated in many ways, according to the kinds of forms and actions that exist and also according to the power of knowledge of the respective persons. This same universal form was described in the preceding Ṛk by the epithets विश्वकर्मा विमनाः आद्विहायाः परमोतसंदृक् (*viśvakarmā vimanāḥ ādvihāyāḥ paramotasaṃdṛk*) and so on.

Just as he assigned names to the gods Indra and the others, and to all the remaining beings, the Yakṣas, Gandharvas, men and the rest, in the same way the beings in turn, according to their station and according to their nature, have also assigned names to Viśvakarman, the Lord of all. Thus, whether individual names are given to Indra and the others fashioned by Viśvakarman, or whether gods, men and the rest, according to their power of knowledge, give different names to one and the same principle, this diversity is merely a matter of everyday usage and not truth. How? Thus:

यथा सोम्यकेन मृत्पिंडेन सर्वं मन्मयं विज्ञातं स्याद्वाचारंभणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्येव सत्यं ॥ (*yathā somyakena mṛtpiṃḍena sarvaṃ manmayaṃ vijñātaṃ syādvācāraṃbhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttiketyeva satyaṃ ‖*) (Bhā U. 6-1-4) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 277

O Śvetaketu, just as, though many kinds of vessels such as pots are made from one lump of clay, the dealings in pots and the like are only a matter of name, and the original cause, the clay, alone is true, and for the rest there is a truth of everyday usage; so too the persons of the world produced from the Lord have a truth of everyday usage through difference of name. The Lord alone, the original cause, is without a second, eternal, of the nature of truth. Many more examples of this can be given, thus:

यथा सोम्यकेन लोहमणिना सर्वं लोहमयं विज्ञातं स्याद्वाचारंभणं विकारो नामधेयं लोहमित्येव सत्यं ॥ (*yathā somyakena lohamaṇinā sarvaṃ lohamayaṃ vijñātaṃ syādvācāraṃbhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ lohamityeva satyaṃ ‖*) (Chā. U. 6-8-5)

O dear son, just as many kinds of ornaments may be made from one lump of gold, and though they appear different, the gold, which is the original form, alone is true; so all the gods and the rest produced from the Lord are different through the assigning of names. In reality the Lord alone is true. Thus it is explained. The idea contained in यो देवानां नामधा एक एव (*yo devānāṃ nāmadhā eka eva*) is described in the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad in this way.

एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतांतरात्मा । कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥ (*eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ sarvavyāpī sarvabhūtāṃtarātmā | karmādhyakṣaḥ sarvabhūtādhivāsaḥ sākṣī cetā kevalo nirguṇaśca ‖*) (Kveṃ. U. 6-11) **NOTE**

The Lord is one, but he is hidden in all beings. He pervades every region. He is the inner Self of all beings. He is the overseer of all actions. All beings dwell in him. He alone is the witness of all dealings. He alone is the sole one. He is free from the qualities sattva, rajas and tamas.

एको वशी निष्क्रियाणां बहुनामेकं बीजं बहुधा यः करोति । तमात्मस्थं येऽनुपश्यंति धीरास्तेषां सुखं शाश्वतं नेतरेषां ॥ (*eko vaśī niṣkriyāṇāṃ bahunāmekaṃ bījaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti | tamātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyaṃti dhīrāsteṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣāṃ ‖*) (Śve. U. 6-12) **NOTE**

He alone is the controller of all beings. He causes the one seed to be transformed into many forms. Eternal happiness comes to those great seers who realise directly this Supreme Self dwelling in their own self; not to others.

नित्यो नित्यानां चेतनश्चेतनानां एको बहूनां यो विदधाति कामान् । तत्कारणं सांख्ययोगाधिगम्यं ज्ञात्वा देवं मुच्यते सर्वपाशैः ॥ (*nityo nityānāṃ cetanaścetanānāṃ eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān | tatkāraṇaṃ sāṃkhyayogādhigamyaṃ jñātvā devaṃ mucyate sarvapāśaiḥ ‖*) (Śve. U. 6-13)

### Printed p. 278

This Lord, whose permanence is greater than that of eternal things, and whose intelligence is greater than that of all the intelligent, is the one master who fulfils the wishes of all. If he is known through discriminating experience and through disciplined meditation, all bonds are destroyed. In this manner and so on the Lord's oneness without a second is described. In the Śvetāśvatara the supreme person (Viśvakarman), who is described by the epithets यो नः पिता जनिता (*yo naḥ pitā janitā*) and so on, is described in this way.

स विश्वकृद्विश्वविदात्मयोनिर्ज्ञः कालकालो गुणी सर्वविद्यः । प्रधानक्षेत्रज्ञपतिर्गुणेशः संसारमोक्षस्थितिबंधहेतुः । (*sa viśvakṛdviśvavidātmayonirjñaḥ kālakālo guṇī sarvavidyaḥ | pradhānakṣetrajñapatirguṇeśaḥ saṃsāramokṣasthitibaṃdhahetuḥ |*) (Prai. U. 6-16) **NOTE**

This Supreme Self is the maker of all. He is the knower of all. He causes time (at the time of realisation) to perish. He is the master of all the scriptures and the mine of good qualities. He is the controller of Prakṛti and Puruṣa. He is the master of the three qualities (sattva, rajas and tamas). His resolves are the cause of release from saṃsāra and also of being bound again. The nature of such a Supreme Lord, without a second, is not easily understood. Therefore it is stated that तं संप्रश्नं भुवना यंति (*taṃ saṃpraśnaṃ bhuvanā yaṃti*), that is, all beings ask what his nature is. There is a story in the Kena Upaniṣad to show that even Agni and the other gods did not know exactly what his nature is. This has been stated earlier. Moreover, किं स्विदासीदधिष्ठानं (*kiṃ svidāsīdadhiṣṭhānaṃ*) and so on (10-8-12). Besides the gods, there are many occasions on which many seers also asked this question. For example:

भगवन्नेतस्मिन् पुरुषे कानि स्वपंति कान्यस्मिञ्जाग्रति कतर एष देवः स्वप्नान् पश्यति कस्यैतत्सुखं भवति कस्मिन्नु सर्वॆ संप्रतिष्ठिता भवंतीति ॥ (*bhagavannetasmin puruṣe kāni svapaṃti kānyasmiñjāgrati katara eṣa devaḥ svapnān paśyati kasyaitatsukhaṃ bhavati kasminnu sarvè saṃpratiṣṭhitā bhavaṃtīti ‖*) (Praśna. 4-1.)

O revered one, who sleep in this Person? Who inside him are awake? And who (the gods) is it that sees dreams? Whose is this happiness? In whom are all these established? When Gārgya, the grandson of Sūra, asked Pippalāda thus, Pippalāda addressed him lovingly as यथा गार्ग्य (*yathā gārgya*), "O Gārgya", and gave the answer suited to the occasion. Moreover, the occasion on which Gārgī, who wished to gain knowledge of Brahman, questioned Yājñavalkya shows the greatness of her question and of his answer. Those questions and answers are as follows:

अथ कैनं गार्गी वाचक्कवी पप्रट्ट (*atha kainaṃ gārgī vācakkavī papraṭṭa*)

Question: यदिदं सर्वमप्स्वेतं च प्रोतं च कस्मिन्नु खल्वाप ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*yadidaṃ sarvamapsvetaṃ ca protaṃ ca kasminnu khalvāpa otāśca protāśca*) that is, if everything is woven like warp and woof in the water, in what is the water woven?

### Printed p. 279

Answer: पायौ गार्गि (*pāyau gārgi*)—O Gārgī, in the wind.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु वायुरोतश्च प्रोतश्च (*kasminnu khalu vāyurotaśca protaśca*)—in what is the wind woven like warp and woof?

Answer: अंतरिक्षलोकेषु (*aṃtarikṣalokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the atmosphere.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु अंतरिक्षलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu aṃtarikṣalokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of the atmosphere contained (joined together)?

Answer: गंधर्वलोकेषु (*gaṃdharvalokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the Gandharvas.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु गंधर्वलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu gaṃdharvalokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of the Gandharvas joined together?

Answer: आदित्यलोकेषु (*ādityalokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the Ādityas.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खल्वादित्यलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalvādityalokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of the Ādityas joined together?

Answer: चंद्रलोकेषु (*caṃdralokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the moon.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु चंद्रलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu caṃdralokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of the moon joined together?

Answer: नक्षत्रलोकेषु (*nakṣatralokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the stars.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु नक्षत्रलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu nakṣatralokā otāśca protāśca*)—where are the worlds of the stars joined together?

Answer: देवलोकेषु (*devalokeṣu*)—in the worlds of the gods.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु देवलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu devalokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of the gods joined together?

Answer: इंद्रलोकेषु (*iṃdralokeṣu*)—in the worlds of Indra.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु इंद्रलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu iṃdralokā otāśca protāśca*)—where are the worlds of Indra joined together like warp and woof?

Answer: प्रजापतिलोकेषु (*prajāpatilokeṣu*)—in the worlds of Prajāpati. **NOTE**

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु प्रजापतिलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu prajāpatilokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of Prajāpati contained?

Answer: ब्रह्मलोकेषु (*brahmalokeṣu*)—in the worlds of Brahmā.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु ब्रह्मलोका ओताश्च प्रोताश्च (*kasminnu khalu brahmalokā otāśca protāśca*)—in what are the worlds of Brahmā joined together like warp and woof?

Answer: गार्गि मातिप्राक्षीः मा ते मूर्धा व्यपप्तदनतिप्रश्न्यां वै देवतामतिपृच्छसि (*gārgi mātiprākṣīḥ mā te mūrdhā vyapaptadanatipraśnyāṃ vai devatāmatipṛcchasi*) (Ba. U. 3-6) (Bṛ. U. 3-6) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 280

To the last question there is no solution. Even questions about Brahman have a limit. What can be known through mere discussion can be known by question and answer. But as for यतो वाचो निवर्तंते अप्राप्यमनसा सह (*yato vāco nivartaṃte aprāpyamanasā saha*), it cannot be determined by speech. The nature of this Self is not known by the mind either. It passes beyond the limits of both. It is to be known only through meditation. To show that it passes beyond the limits of question and answer, Yājñavalkya gives Gārgī this answer: "O Gārgī, enough of your question, stop. If you put a question beyond this, your head will split."

Just as there was this conversation in the form of question and answer between Gārgī and Yājñavalkya, so there is a similar conversation in the form of question and answer between Yājñavalkya and Śākalya. That too concerns the supreme Brahman. It concerns the directions pervaded by Viśvakarman and the deities of the directions.

Question: यदिदं कुरुपंचालानां ब्राह्मणानामत्यवादीः किं ब्रह्म विद्वान् (*yadidaṃ kurupaṃcālānāṃ brāhmaṇānāmatyavādīḥ kiṃ brahma vidvān*)—O Yājñavalkya, what is the nature of Brahman that you explained to the Kurupāñcālas?

Answer: दिशो वेद सदेवाः सप्रतिष्ठा (*diśo veda sadevāḥ sapratiṣṭhā*)—the directions with their gods, of firm standing.

Question: किं देवतोऽस्यां प्राच्यां दिश्यसि (*kiṃ devato 'syāṃ prācyāṃ diśyasi*)—what is the deity of the eastern direction?

Answer: स आदित्यः (*sa ādityaḥ*)—he is Āditya.

Question: कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः (*kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is Āditya established?

Answer: चक्षुसि (*cakṣusi*)—in the eyes.

Question: कस्मिन्नु चक्षुः प्रतिष्ठितं (*kasminnu cakṣuḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ*)—in what is the eye established?

Answer: रूपेषु (*rūpeṣu*)—(in forms). चक्षुषा हि रूपाणि पश्यति (*cakṣuṣā hi rūpāṇi paśyati*)—it is with the eyes that we see forms.

Question: कस्मिन्नु रूपाणि प्रतिष्ठितानि (*kasminnu rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitāni*)—in what are forms established?

Answer: हृदय इति होवाच हृदयेन हि रूपाणि जानाति (*hṛdaya iti hovāca hṛdayena hi rūpāṇi jānāti*)—since forms are known by the heart alone, they are established in the heart. (Bṛ. A. 2.9-19-20) **NOTE**

Question: किं देवतोऽस्यां दक्षिणायां दिश्यसि (*kiṃ devato 'syāṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśyasi*)—what is the deity of the southern direction?

Answer: यमदेवत इति (*yamadevata iti*)—it is the deity named Yama.

### Printed p. 281

Question: स यमः कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः (*sa yamaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is that Yama established?

Answer: यज्ञे (*yajñe*)—in the sacrifice.

Question: कस्मिन्नु यज्ञः प्रतिष्ठितः (*kasminnu yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is the sacrifice established?

Answer: दक्षणायां (*dakṣaṇāyāṃ*)—in the sacrificial fee.

Question: कस्मिन्नु दक्षिणा प्रतिष्ठिता (*kasminnu dakṣiṇā pratiṣṭhitā*)—in what is the sacrificial fee established?

Answer: श्रद्धायां (*śraddhāyāṃ*)—in faith.

Question: कस्मिन्नु श्रद्धा प्रतिष्ठिता (*kasminnu śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā*)—in what is faith established?

Answer: हृदये हृदयेन हि श्रद्धां जानाति (*hṛdaye hṛdayena hi śraddhāṃ jānāti*)—since faith is known by the heart alone, it is established in the heart.

Question: किं देवतोऽस्यां प्रतीच्यां दिश्यसि (*kiṃ devato 'syāṃ pratīcyāṃ diśyasi*)—what is the deity of the western direction?

Answer: वरुणदेवत इति (*varuṇadevata iti*)—the deity of the western direction is Varuṇa.

Question: स वरुणः कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः (*sa varuṇaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is Varuṇa established?

Answer: अप्पु (*appu*)—in the waters.

Question: कस्मिन्नापः प्रतिष्ठितासः (*kasminnāpaḥ pratiṣṭhitāsaḥ*)—what is the standing of the waters?

Answer: रेतसि (*retasi*)—in seed.

Question: किं देवतोऽस्यामुदीच्यां दिश्यसीति (*kiṃ devato 'syāmudīcyāṃ diśyasīti*)—what is the deity of the northern direction?

Answer: सोमदेवत इति (*somadevata iti*)—the deity Soma.

Question: स सोमः कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः (*sa somaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—what is the place of Soma's establishment?

Answer: दीक्षायां (*dīkṣāyāṃ*)—in the consecration.

Question: कस्मिन्नु दीक्षा प्रतिष्ठिता (*kasminnu dīkṣā pratiṣṭhitā*)—in what is the consecration established?

Answer: in truth.

Question: कस्मिन्नु खलु सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितं (*kasminnu khalu satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ*)—in what is truth established?

Answer: हृदये (*hṛdaye*)—in the heart.

हृदयेन हि सत्यं जानाति हृदये ह्येव सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितं । (*hṛdayena hi satyaṃ jānāti hṛdaye hyeva satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ |*) Only the heart can know truth. Therefore truth is established in the heart. **NOTE**

Question: किं देवतोऽस्यां ध्रुवायां दिश्यसि (*kiṃ devato 'syāṃ dhruvāyāṃ diśyasi*)—what is the deity of the fixed direction?

Answer: अग्नि देवतॆ इति (*agni devatè iti*)—Agni is the deity of this direction.

### Printed p. 282

Question: सोऽग्निः कस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः (*so 'gniḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is Agni established?

Answer: वाचि (*vāci*)—in speech.

Question: कस्मिन्नु वाक्प्रतिष्ठिता (*kasminnu vākpratiṣṭhitā*)—in what is speech established?

Answer: हृदये (*hṛdaye*)—in the heart.

Question: कस्मिन्नु त्वं चात्मा च प्रतिष्ठिता (*kasminnu tvaṃ cātmā ca pratiṣṭhitā*)—in what are you, that is, your body and your self, both established?

Answer: पाणे (*pāṇe*)—in breath.

Question: कस्मिन्नु प्राणः प्रतिष्ठितः (*kasminnu prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ*)—in what is breath established?

Answer: अपान इति (*apāna iti*)—in the downward breath.

Question: कस्मिन्वपानः (*kasminvapānaḥ*)—in what is the downward breath?

Answer: व्याने (*vyāne*)—in the diffused breath.

Question: कस्मिन्नु व्यानः (*kasminnu vyānaḥ*)—in what is the diffused breath?

Answer: उदाने (*udāne*)—in the upward breath.

Question: कस्मिन्नुदानः (*kasminnudānaḥ*)—in what is the upward breath?

Answer: समाने (*samāne*)—in the equalising breath.

Then is this the Self? It is not. This is not the Self.

स एष नेति नेत्यात्मागृह्यो न हि गृह्यते आशीर्यो न हि शीरतेऽसंगो न हि सज्यतेऽसितो न व्यथते न रिष्यति । (*sa eṣa neti netyātmāgṛhyo na hi gṛhyate āśīryo na hi śīrate 'saṃgo na hi sajyate 'sito na vyathate na riṣyati |*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9)

This Self is none of these. It is beyond the range of the senses. It is not an object of direct perception. It is without destruction. It is without attachment. It is free from attachment to objects. It is free from bonds and in the state of release. For it there is no sorrow at all. If it is not known, the head falls off: thus is the supreme Self, beyond the range of the senses, extolled.

नायमात्मा प्रवचनेन लभ्यो न मेधया न बहुना श्रुतेन । यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यस्तस्येष आत्मा विवृणुते तनूग्स्वां ॥ (*nāyamātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena | yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyastasyeṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūgsvāṃ ‖*) (Kaṭha. 1-2-23) **NOTE**

The matter stated in the present mantra, तं संप्रश्नं भुवना यांत्यन्या । (*taṃ saṃpraśnaṃ bhuvanā yāṃtyanyā |*), has been illustrated above with some examples. It is clear from the examples above that although many kinds of questions are asked, a precise answer to them is not possible. Therefore—

### Printed p. 283

This Self is not known by teachings, by the power of intellect, or by hearing its description. It is known only by those who seek this Self with meditation. To him it shows its own form: thus the futility of questions and the like has been declared.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त आय॑जंत॒ द्रवि॑णं॒ सम॑स्मा॒ ऋष॑यः॒ पूर्वे॑ जरि॒तारो॒  ॒
> न भूना ।  
> अ॒सूर्ते॒ सूर्ते॒ रज॑सि निष॒त्ते ये भू॒तानि॑ स॒मकृ॑ण्वन्नि॒मानि॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । आ । आयजंत । द्रविणं । सं । अस्मै । ऋषयः । पूर्वे । जरितारः । न । भूना ।  
> असूर्ते । सूर्ते । रजसि । निसत्ते । ये । भूतानि । संअकृण्वन् । इमानि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते पूर्व ऋषयोऽस्मै विश्वकर्मणे द्रविणं चरुपुरोडाशादिलक्षणं धनं
> सं सम्यगायजंत । सर्वतो यजंते । जरितारो न भूना स्तोतारो यथा
> भूम्ना महता स्तोत्रेण यजंति तद्वत् । ये महर्षयोऽस्मूर्ते सरणवर्जिते
> सूर्ते सरणसहिते स्थावरजंगमात्मके रजसि लोके निषत्ते निषण्णे निश्चलमवस्थित
> इमानि भूतानि भुवनानि । प्राणिन इत्यर्थः । समकृण्वन् सम्यग्धनादिनापूजयन् ।
> अथवायमर्थः । ये स्थावरजंगमात्मके जगति वर्तमानानेतान्नाणिनस्तेजसा
> समकृण्वन् ते पूर्व ऋषयो द्रष्टारो रश्मयोऽस्मा आदित्यात्मकाय विश्वकर्मणे
> द्रविणं तेज आयजंत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those ancient seers worshipped Viśvakarman with wealth, that is, with riches such as the cooked offering and the sacrificial cake (चरुपुरोडाशादिलक्षणं (*carupuroḍāśādilakṣaṇaṃ*)), on all sides and completely; they worship as praisers worship with great praise (भूम्ना महता स्तोत्रेण (*bhūmnā mahatā stotreṇa*)). Those great seers who, in the world that is without motion and with motion, of the nature of the unmoving and the moving, seated and settled motionless, honoured these beings, that is, living creatures, completely with wealth and the like, they are the ancient seers who made the offering. Or else the meaning is this: those who with brilliance perfected these living creatures existing in the world of the unmoving and the moving, those ancient seers, the seers (the rays), offered brilliance (द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*) is तेज (*teja*)) to him, Viśvakarman, who is of the nature of the sun.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये (*ye*)—which great seers
- असूर्ते (*asūrte*)—in what is without consciousness
- सूर्ते (*sūrte*)—and what is endowed with consciousness
- रजसि (*rajasi*)—in the world
- निषत्ते (*niṣatte*)—existing
- इमानि भूतानि (*imāni bhūtāni*)—all these beings
- समकृण्वन् (*samakṛṇvan*)—refined
- ते (*te*)—such
- पूर्वे ऋषयः (*pūrve ṛṣayaḥ*)—ancient seers
- भूना (*bhūnā*)—with abundant praise
- जरितारो न (*jaritāro na*)—as praisers worship
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—with reference to Viśvakarman
- द्रविणं (*draviṇaṃ*)—with the cooked offering, the sacrificial cake and the like
- समयजंत (*samayajaṃta*)—worship everywhere

### Printed p. 284

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The ancient seers who refined all the beings existing in the world that is without consciousness and endowed with consciousness worship Viśvakarman everywhere with the cooked offering, the sacrificial cake and the like, as praisers worship with abundant praise.

##### English translation
Those ancient Rishis who adorned with light these beings in the animate and inanimate world, offer to him wealth (of sacrifice) as praisers with abundant (laudation).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the purport of the 2nd Ṛk above in this same sūkta, it was stated how the seers, who are of the form of senses, served Prajāpati, who is of the form of breath, and how, as the fruit of that service, they themselves attained and attain satisfaction; and it was said that its explanation would be given in the special topics of this Ṛk. The manner in which the seers, who are of the form of senses, perform sacrifice, the satisfaction obtained from it, its nature and so on, are explained in the Chāndogya and other Upaniṣads.

One meaning is that when the seers performed service in the form of sacrifice, Prajāpati, who is of the form of Viśvakarman, became satisfied. Or else the other meaning is that by the service of the senses designated seers, the Self, who is of the form of breath, is satisfied. How the satisfaction that is the fruit of sacrifice arises, and how complete satisfaction comes to the Self, who is of the form of breath and pervades the whole world, is stated in the Chāndogya in this way.

In the present Ṛk the word द्रविण (*draviṇa*) has been explained as the sacrificial cake of the cooked offering and the like.

तद्यद्भक्तं प्रथममागच्छेत्तद्धोमियं स यां प्रथमामाहुतिं जुहुयाप्राणाय स्वाहेति प्राणस्तृप्यति । (*tadyadbhaktaṃ prathamamāgacchettaddhomiyaṃ sa yāṃ prathamāmāhutiṃ juhuyāprāṇāya svāheti prāṇastṛpyati |*) (Chā. U. 5-19-1)

The food-oblation in the form of the cooked offering, the sacrificial cake and the like, which the present Ṛk calls द्रविण (*draviṇa*), is the very oblation that is offered first, and it is to be offered to breath. Then breath is satisfied. Breath here does not mean the satisfaction of one individual breath only. It means satisfaction for breath and for the other things of the universe connected with breath. How is that? Thus:

प्राणे तृप्यति चक्षुस्तृप्यति चक्षुषि तृप्यत्यादित्यस्तृप्यत्यादित्ये तृप्यति दौस्तुप्यति दिवि तृप्यंत्यां यत्किंच दौश्चादित्यश्चाधितिष्ठतस्ततृप्यति तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिरन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥ (*prāṇe tṛpyati cakṣustṛpyati cakṣuṣi tṛpyatyādityastṛpyatyāditye tṛpyati daustupyati divi tṛpyaṃtyāṃ yatkiṃca dauścādityaścādhitiṣṭhatastatṛpyati tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhirannādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ‖*) (Bhā. U. 5-19-2) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 285

If breath is satisfied, the eye is satisfied. As the result of the eye's satisfaction, Āditya is satisfied. Because Āditya is satisfied, the world of heaven is gratified. Then all the things that stand in the support of the world of heaven and in the support of Āditya attain contentment. Together with these, the Self, who is of the form of breath, also gains increase along with offspring, cattle and wealth, and further gains excellent knowledge.

अथ यां द्वितीयां जुहुयात्तां जुहुयाद्वानाय स्वाहेति व्यानस्त्रृप्यति । व्याने तृप्यति शोत्रं तृप्यति शोत्रे तृप्यति चंद्रमास्तृप्यति चंद्रमसि तृप्यति दिशस्त्रप्यंति दिक्षु तृप्यंतीषु यत्किंच दिशश्च चंद्रमाश्चाधितिष्ठंति तत्तृप्यति तस्यानुतृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिरन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति । (*atha yāṃ dvitīyāṃ juhuyāttāṃ juhuyādvānāya svāheti vyānastrṛpyati | vyāne tṛpyati śotraṃ tṛpyati śotre tṛpyati caṃdramāstṛpyati caṃdramasi tṛpyati diśastrapyaṃti dikṣu tṛpyaṃtīṣu yatkiṃca diśaśca caṃdramāścādhitiṣṭhaṃti tattṛpyati tasyānutṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhirannādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti |*) (Cha. U. 5-21) **NOTE**

The second oblation is to be offered to the diffused breath. Because there is a close connection between the diffused breath and the organ of hearing, the organ of hearing is satisfied. As the result of that, the moon is satisfied. Because the moon is delighted, all the directions are gratified. As the result of the satisfaction of the directions, all things that rest on the moon and on the directions attain satisfaction. As the result of that, the Self who makes the oblation gains increase of wealth such as cattle and sons, and the gain of excellent knowledge.

अथ यां तृतीयां जुहुयात्तां जुहुयादपानाय स्वाहेत्यपानस्तृप्यति । आपाने तृप्यति वाक् तृप्यति वाचि त्यप्यंतामग्निस्तृप्यत्यग्नौ तृप्यति पृथिवी तृप्यति पृथिव्यां तृप्यंतां यत्किंच पृथिवी चाग्निश्चाधितिष्ठतस्तत्तृप्यति तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिरन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥ (*atha yāṃ tṛtīyāṃ juhuyāttāṃ juhuyādapānāya svāhetyapānastṛpyati | āpāne tṛpyati vāk tṛpyati vāci tyapyaṃtāmagnistṛpyatyagnau tṛpyati pṛthivī tṛpyati pṛthivyāṃ tṛpyaṃtāṃ yatkiṃca pṛthivī cāgniścādhitiṣṭhatastattṛpyati tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhirannādyena tejasā brahmavarcaseneti ‖*) (Chā. U. 5-2-) **NOTE**

The third oblation is to be offered to the downward breath. By it the downward breath is satisfied. Because the downward breath is satisfied, contentment comes to speech. As the result of the satisfaction of speech, satisfaction comes to Agni. Then satisfaction comes to the earth. As the result of that, the Self who makes the oblation gains increase of wealth in the form of cattle and sons, and increase of excellent knowledge.

अथ यां चतुर्थी जुहुयात्तां जुहुयात्समानाय स्वाहेति समानस्यप्यति । समाने तृप्यति मनसि तृप्यति पर्जन्यस्यप्यति पर्जन्ये तृप्यति विद्युत्तृप्यति विद्युति तृप्यंत्यां यत्किंच विद्युच्च पर्जन्यश्चाधितिष्ठतस्तत्तृप्यति तस्यानु तृप्तिं तृप्यति प्रजया पशुभिरन्नाद्येन तेजना ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति ॥ (*atha yāṃ caturthī juhuyāttāṃ juhuyātsamānāya svāheti samānasyapyati | samāne tṛpyati manasi tṛpyati parjanyasyapyati parjanye tṛpyati vidyuttṛpyati vidyuti tṛpyaṃtyāṃ yatkiṃca vidyucca parjanyaścādhitiṣṭhatastattṛpyati tasyānu tṛptiṃ tṛpyati prajayā paśubhirannādyena tejanā brahmavarcaseneti ‖*) (Bhā. U. 5-21)

### Printed p. 286

The fourth oblation is to be offered to the equalising breath. By it satisfaction comes to the equalising breath. From the satisfaction of the equalising breath comes satisfaction of the mind. From the satisfaction of the mind comes satisfaction of Parjanya. From the satisfaction of Parjanya comes contentment of lightning. As the result of this satisfaction, all things that rest on Parjanya and lightning are contented. As the result of this, the Self who makes this oblation gains wealth such as cattle and sons, and excellent knowledge.

अथ यां पंचमीं जुहुयात्तां जुहुयादुदानाय स्वाहेत्युदानस्तृप्यति । उदाने तृप्यति त्वक् तृप्यति त्वचि तृप्यंत्यां वायुस्तृपति वायौ तृप्यत्याकाशस्त्रृप्यति आकाशे तृप्यति यत्किंच वायुश्चाकाशश्चाधितिष्ठतस्ततृपति प्रजया पशुभिरन्नाद्येन तेजसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन ॥ (*atha yāṃ paṃcamīṃ juhuyāttāṃ juhuyādudānāya svāhetyudānastṛpyati | udāne tṛpyati tvak tṛpyati tvaci tṛpyaṃtyāṃ vāyustṛpati vāyau tṛpyatyākāśastrṛpyati ākāśe tṛpyati yatkiṃca vāyuścākāśaścādhitiṣṭhatastatṛpati prajayā paśubhirannādyena tejasā brahmavarcasena ‖*) (Bhā. U. 5-23)

The fifth oblation is to be offered to the upward breath. By it the upward breath is satisfied. From the satisfaction of the upward breath comes the full satisfaction of the skin (the organ of the skin). From the satisfaction of the skin comes contentment of the wind. From that comes satisfaction of space. As the result of this, all things that rest on the wind and on space are satisfied. As the result of that, the Self who made this oblation gains wealth such as cattle and sons, brilliance and the radiance of Brahman. In this way the order of the offering of oblations stated in the present Ṛk, and the order of satisfaction stated earlier in the second Ṛk of this same sūkta, have been explained.

Two kinds of meaning have been given for the phrase असूर्ते सूर्ते रजसि (*asūrte sūrte rajasi*). The word सूर्त (*sūrta*) means that which has the nature of motion. The world that is of the nature of motion, that is, of the nature of the moving, and the world that is without motion, of the nature of the unmoving, are indicated by the words सूर्त (*sūrta*) and असूर्त (*asūrta*). One meaning is that the seers, knowing all the worlds, unmoving and moving, to be the abode of Viśvakarman, directly beheld Viśvakarman's pervasiveness everywhere and worshipped him.

Second, the worship of Āditya by the rays that are of the form of seers. The word seer means the rays of the sun that have supersensuous power of knowledge. These rays offer worship to Viśvakarman, who is of the form of Āditya. How? The purport is that first the rays spreading out from Āditya pervade all the worlds, unmoving and moving, with their brilliance. Afterwards they again draw the essences of those same worlds and offer worship to Āditya with that substance of the form of essence.

Thus there is one action, that of first spreading out, pervading all the worlds and diffusing brilliance. How is that? Thus:

### Printed p. 287

आसावादित्यो देवमधु तस्य द्यौरेव तिरश्चीनवंशोऽंतरिक्षमपूपो मरीचयः पुत्राः । तस्य ये प्रांचो रश्मयस्ता एवास्य प्राज्यो मधु. नाड्यः । ऋच एव मधुकृत ऋग्वेद एव पुष्पं ता अमृता आपस्तावा एता ऋचः ।.........तद्व्यक्षरत्तदादित्यमभितोऽश्रयत्तद्वा एतद्यदेतदादित्यस्य रोहितं रूपं ॥ (*āsāvādityo devamadhu tasya dyaureva tiraścīnavaṃśo 'ṃtarikṣamapūpo marīcayaḥ putrāḥ | tasya ye prāṃco raśmayastā evāsya prājyo madhu. nāḍyaḥ | ṛca eva madhukṛta ṛgveda eva puṣpaṃ tā amṛtā āpastāvā etā ṛcaḥ |.........tadvyakṣarattadādityamabhito 'śrayattadvā etadyadetadādityasya rohitaṃ rūpaṃ ‖*) (Cha. 30. 3-1) **NOTE**

Āditya, who contains all the gods, is the god-honey. If it is asked what the tree of this honey is, it is the world of heaven. The atmosphere is the nest. The rays are the sons. The rays that spread toward the eastern direction are the honey-channels of the eastern direction. The Ṛks are the bees. The Ṛgveda is the flower. The oblations offered in the sacrifice, of the form of ghee and milk, are the drops of nectar. After the Ṛk-mantras have ripened, fame, brilliance, sense-power, virility, strength and essence arise from sacrificial and other rites; then all the essences of the form of fruit spread out facing Āditya and join him again. These are the causes of the attractive form of the red disc of Āditya. (Here both the visible Āditya and the invisible, indirect Āditya who is of the form of Viśvakarman are included.) **NOTE**

अथ येऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मयस्ता एवास्य दक्षिणा मधुनाड्यः । यजूग् षेव मधुकृतः .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... तद्वक्षरत्तदादित्यमभितोश्रयत्तदा, एतद्यदेतदादित्यस्य शुक्लं रूपं । (*atha ye 'sya dakṣiṇā raśmayastā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyaḥ | yajūg ṣeva madhukṛtaḥ .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... tadvakṣarattadādityamabhitośrayattadā, etadyadetadādityasya śuklaṃ rūpaṃ |*) (Chā. U. 3-2)

The rays of Āditya that spread toward the southern direction are the honey-channels of the south. The Yajus-mantras are the bees. The Yajurveda is the flower. The ghee and milk of the sacrificial oblations are the drops of nectar. From this, essences and the like arise, spread out again facing Āditya and join Āditya himself. These supply Āditya with his white form.

अथ येऽस्य प्रत्यंचो रश्मयः ..... .... .... सामान्येव मधुकृतः .... एतदादित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपं । (*atha ye 'sya pratyaṃco raśmayaḥ ..... .... .... sāmānyeva madhukṛtaḥ .... etadādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpaṃ |*) (Chā. U. 3.3)

The rays that spread westward are the honey-channels of the west. The bees in the form of Sāmans create, in the flower in the form of the Sāmaveda, the drops of nectar in the form of oblations, and join Āditya. These procure the dark form of Āditya. (Bhā. U. 3-4)

अथ येऽस्योदंचो रश्मयः । .... ...... अथर्वांगिरस एव मधुकृत इतिहासपुराणं पुष्पं .... ....एतदादित्यस्य परं कृष्णं रूपं ॥ (*atha ye 'syodaṃco raśmayaḥ | .... ...... atharvāṃgirasa eva madhukṛta itihāsapurāṇaṃ puṣpaṃ .... ....etadādityasya paraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rūpaṃ ‖*) (Chā. U. 3-4)

### Printed p. 288

The rays that spread toward the northern direction are the honey-channels of the north. The bee in the form of the Atharvans creates, from the flower in the form of the Itihāsa and Purāṇa, the drop of nectar of the form of essence and the like, and joins Āditya. These procure the deep dark form of Āditya.

ते वा एते रसानां रसा वेदा हि रसास्तेषामेते रसास्तानि वा एतान्यमृतानाममृतानि वेदा ह्यमृतास्तेषामेतान्य मृतानि । (*te vā ete rasānāṃ rasā vedā hi rasāsteṣāmete rasāstāni vā etānyamṛtānāmamṛtāni vedā hyamṛtāsteṣāmetānya mṛtāni |*) (Bhā. U. 3-5)

The rays of Āditya that spread to all directions and all worlds are the cause of all colours and are the essences of all essences. The essences of the essences are the essence of the excellent things existing in all the worlds, namely the Veda. After they have undergone transformation into the form of sacrifice, the colours of the sun that arise as the result of its essence are the essence of sacrifices and the like. The multi-coloured brilliance of Āditya, kindled by the nectar-natured Vedas and the like, is the nectar even of all nectar.

Having thus described the fruit of the spreading of the rays, the text then explains in this manner that all kinds of gods are contained within Viśvakarman, who is of the form of Āditya.

यद्यत्प्रथमममृतं तद्वसव उपजीवंत्यग्निना मुखेन वै देवा अश्नंति न पिबंति एतदेवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यंति । अथ यद्वितीयममृतं तद्रुद्रा उपजीवंति । अथ यत्तृतीयममृतं तदादित्या उपजीवंति । अथ यच्चतुर्थममृतं तन्मरुत उपजीवंति । अथ यत्पंचमममृतं तत्साध्या उपजीवंति ॥ (*yadyatprathamamamṛtaṃ tadvasava upajīvaṃtyagninā mukhena vai devā aśnaṃti na pibaṃti etadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyaṃti | atha yadvitīyamamṛtaṃ tadrudrā upajīvaṃti | atha yattṛtīyamamṛtaṃ tadādityā upajīvaṃti | atha yaccaturthamamṛtaṃ tanmaruta upajīvaṃti | atha yatpaṃcamamamṛtaṃ tatsādhyā upajīvaṃti ‖*) (Chā. U. 3.6-10)

In the essence-natured forms of Āditya, which are of the form of nectar and of five kinds, the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Maruts and the Sādhyas dwell. They too enter the colours beginning with the red. One who knows the essences of these nectars obtains a place among the Vasus, Rudras and the rest. Āditya also is established, moving in the worlds of these Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas and beholding the greatness of their self-rule. That this Āditya is of one hundred and one kinds, that is, is none other than the supreme Brahman, was explained earlier on page 366 of the twelfth part.

In the present Ṛk too there is praise of this same Viśvakarman, who is of the form of Āditya.

### Printed p. 289

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प॒रो दि॒वा प॒र ए॒ना पृ॑थि॒व्या प॒रो दे॒वेभि॒रसु॑रै॒र्यदस्ति॑ ।  
> कं स्वि॒दर्भं॑ प्रथ॒मं द॑ध्र॒ आपो॒ यत्र॑ दे॒वाः स॒मप॑श्यंत॒  ॑
> विश्वे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परः । दिवा । परः । एना । पृथिव्या । परः । देवेभिः । असुरैः । यत् । अस्ति ।  
> कं । स्वित् । गर्भं । प्रथमं । दध्रे । अपः । यत्र । देवाः । संऽपश्यंत । विश्वे ॥५॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदीश्वरतत्त्वं दिवा परो द्युलोकादपि परस्ताद्वर्तमानं तथैनास्याः
> पृथिव्याः परः परस्ताद्वर्तमानं तथा देवेभिर्देवैः परस्ताद्वर्तमानमसुरैः
> परस्ताद्वर्तमानं च यदस्ति तद्गुहायामवस्थितं कं स्विदर्भं गर्भवत्सर्वस्य
> ग्राहकं तत्त्वमापः प्रथमं दध्रे ॥ धृतवत्यः । यत्र यस्मिन्गर्भे देवा
> इंद्रादयो विश्वे सर्वॆऽपि समपश्यंत संगताः परस्परं पश्यंति ! एवं जानन्नेव
> कश्चित्तत्त्ववित्पश्नं करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The divine principle that exists beyond heaven, beyond the sky, likewise beyond this earth, beyond the gods and beyond the Asuras, whatever it is, abides in the cave. What is this embryo-like principle, which grasps everything as an embryo does, which the waters first held? In which embryo all the gods, Indra and the others, saw one another, that is, being assembled they look at one another. Knowing it thus, some knower of the principle puts the question.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवा परः (*divā paraḥ*)—beyond the world of heaven
- एना पृथिव्याः परः (*enā pṛthivyāḥ paraḥ*)—beyond this earth
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—beyond the gods
- असुरैः (*asuraiḥ*)—beyond the Asuras
- यत्गर्भं अस्ति (*yatgarbhaṃ asti*)—which secret principle exists
- यत् (*yat*)—which
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—before everything
- दध्रे (*dadhre*)—held
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which embryonic principle
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods, Indra and the rest
- समपश्यंत (*samapaśyaṃta*)—attained sight of one another (that secret principle)
- कं स्वित् (*kaṃ svit*)—what is it? what is its nature?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

What is that secret principle in the form of an embryo, which is beyond the world of heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods, beyond the Asuras, which the waters first of all held, and in which all the gods, Indra and the rest, attained sight of one another? What is its nature?

### Printed p. 290

##### English translation
What was that embryo which was beyond the heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods, beyond the Asuras, which the waters first retained, in which all the gods contemplated each other ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This Ṛk describes the endless form and power of Viśvakarman, who is the embryo of the whole world. Three points are stated in it. First: (1) The Lord, who is of the form of Viśvakarman, has a nature that surpasses heaven, earth and the rest. (2) Second, since he is the embryo of the whole world, everything is contained in him. Therefore all the gods are contained in him alone. (3) Third, the waters first held him, who is the embryo of the world. These points explain the nature of the Lord.

The Lord is the smallest (the subtlest) and also the greatest. How? Thus:

एष म आत्मांतर्हृदयेऽणीयान् प्रीहेर्वा यवाद्वा सर्षपाद्वा श्यामाकाद्दा श्यामाकतंडुलाद्वा । एष म आत्मा अंतर्हृदये ज्यायान्पृथिव्या ज्यायानंतरिक्षाज्जायान् दिवो ज्यायानेभ्यो लोकेभ्यः ॥ (*eṣa ma ātmāṃtarhṛdaye 'ṇīyān prīhervā yavādvā sarṣapādvā śyāmākāddā śyāmākataṃḍulādvā | eṣa ma ātmā aṃtarhṛdaye jyāyānpṛthivyā jyāyānaṃtarikṣājjāyān divo jyāyānebhyo lokebhyaḥ ‖*) (Chā. U. 3-14-3)

This Self is contained within the heart. He is smaller than a grain of rice. He is subtler than a grain of barley. He is subtler than a mustard seed, or smaller than the kernel of a millet grain. In the same way this same Lord, who pervades the universe, is greater than the earth, surpasses the atmosphere, and is spread out beyond the world of heaven; it is described that he is greater than all the moving and unmoving worlds.

Moreover, all the above points are explained in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad in this way.

यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत । गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठंतं यो भूतेभिव्यपश्यत ॥ (*yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātamadbhyaḥ pūrvamajāyata | guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ yo bhūtebhivyapaśyata ‖*) (Kaṭha. 2-1-6) **NOTE**

This is the Self who was first born from austerity, first born from the water, who dwells in the most hidden region, and who looks out through all beings. This same Self is also of the form of Aditi. How? Thus:

### Printed p. 291

या प्राणेन संभवत्यदितिर्देवतामयी । गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठंतीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत ॥ (*yā prāṇena saṃbhavatyaditirdevatāmayī | guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhaṃtīṃ yā bhūtebhirvyajāyata ‖*) (Kaṭha. 2-1-7)

Aditi, who is the self of all the gods, who has arisen together with breath, who is established in the secret region of the heart, who has come into being together with all beings, is this Self.

अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ॥ (*araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ | dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ ‖*) (Kaṭha. 2-1.-8)

Agni, the all-knowing, who is hidden in the two fire-sticks like the child placed in the womb of pregnant women, being worshipped by the whole world, is of the form of this Self. In this Self all the gods are contained. The matter stated in the present Ṛk as देवाः समपश्यंत विश्वे (*devāḥ samapaśyaṃta viśve*) is stated in the Kaṭha in this manner.

यतश्चोदेति सूरोस्तं यत्र च गच्छति । तं देवाः सर्वेर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन ॥ (*yataścodeti sūrostaṃ yatra ca gacchati | taṃ devāḥ sarverpitāstadu nātyeti kaścana ‖*) (Kaṭha. 2-1-9)

In the universal Self, from the great principle from which the sun rises and in which it sets, all the gods are established. Beyond this universal Self neither gods nor men, none whatever, can go. This is the greatness of this Supreme Self. Explaining this same matter in the Ṛk-saṃhitā also:

आदितिद्र्यारदितिशंतरिक्षमदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः । विश्वे देवा अदितिः पंचजना आदितिर्जातमदितिर्जनित्वं ॥ (*āditidryāraditiśaṃtarikṣamaditirmātā sa pitā sa putraḥ | viśve devā aditiḥ paṃcajanā āditirjātamaditirjanitvaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-10)

Aditi, of undivided nature, is the producer of the whole universe. She is the mother of the world and the father of the world, everything. She is every created thing. She is the root of creation. She is the five peoples beginning with the gods. All the gods are contained in her. She is the shining heaven. She is the atmosphere. She is the whole universe. She is the controller of the universe: thus it is stated. Aditi means the endless. She is the principle that pervades the whole universe and also surpasses the universe. All the gods are each a limb of this body of the form of the universe.

अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चंद्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च देवाः । वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभृतांतरात्मा ॥ (*agnirmūrdhā cakṣuṣī caṃdrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāgvivṛtāśca devāḥ | vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvamasya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhṛtāṃtarātmā ‖*) (Kara. 2-1-10) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 292

Fire is the head of this universal Self. The sun and the moon are his eyes. The quarters are his ears. His speech is the Vedas. The wind is his breath. The whole world is his heart. From his feet this earth, which spreads out, has come into being. He is also the inner Self of all beings. Thus the description of the endlessness of this Self is given in the special topics of the Puruṣa-sūkta.

This verse also states that water is the first supporting abode of this embryo of the universe. In many places water is called Brahman, and the two are declared to be identical. As the world is pervaded by Brahman, so it is pervaded by water. How? Thus—

आप एनेमा मूर्ता येयं पृथिवी यदंतरिक्षं यद्भौरत्यर्वता यद्देवमनुष्या यत्पशवश्च वयांसि च तृणवनस्पतयः श्वापदान्याकीटपतंगपिपीलिकमाप एनेमा मूर्ता अप उपास्वेति ॥ (*āpa enemā mūrtā yeyaṃ pṛthivī yadaṃtarikṣaṃ yadbhauratyarvatā yaddevamanuṣyā yatpaśavaśca vayāṃsi ca tṛṇavanaspatayaḥ śvāpadānyākīṭapataṃgapipīlikamāpa enemā mūrtā apa upāsveti ‖*) (Chā. U. 7-10-1)

Water that pervades the universe takes on all the embodied forms of the universe: the earth, the atmosphere, the heavenly world, the mountains, the gods, men, cattle, birds, grass, trees, beasts of prey, worms, insects, ants. All things, from those of great extent down to those of the smallest size, are only transformations of water. Water itself has taken all these forms. Therefore meditate on water.

योऽपो ब्रह्मत्युपास्त आप्नोति सर्वकामांस्कृप्ति मान्भवति । (*yo 'po brahmatyupāsta āpnoti sarvakāmāṃskṛpti mānbhavati |*) (Chā. U. 7-10-2)

Those who meditate upon this water as Brahman, with contemplation, obtain all desired ends and attain contentment. The order in which the whole world arose from this water, and its details, is stated in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka as follows.

आप एवेदमग्र आसुस्ता अपः सत्यमसृजंत सत्यं ब्रह्म ब्रह्म प्रजापतिं प्रजापतिर्देवांस्ते देवाः सत्यमेवोपासते तदेतत्क्षरं सत्यं ॥ (*āpa evedamagra āsustā apaḥ satyamasṛjaṃta satyaṃ brahma brahma prajāpatiṃ prajāpatirdevāṃste devāḥ satyamevopāsate tadetatkṣaraṃ satyaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 5-5-1)

Before the creation of the world, water alone pervaded everywhere at first. From the water, truth appeared. From truth came Brahmā, from Brahmā Prajāpati, and from Prajāpati all the gods. The gods worship this truth alone. This truth, which has the three syllables स, ति, यं (*sa, ti, yaṃ*), is the universal Self. How these three syllables reflect the universe will be told later. The purport is that water is also the support of truth, which is the support of the world.

### Printed p. 293

अप एवैनदभ्यवहरामापो वा अस्य सर्वस्य प्रतिष्ठा तद्यत्रास्य सर्वस्य प्रतिष्ठा तदेनप्रतिष्ठाप्य यदत्राग्नेयं तदद्भोऽधि जनयिष्याम ॥ (*apa evainadabhyavaharāmāpo vā asya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadyatrāsya sarvasya pratiṣṭhā tadenapratiṣṭhāpya yadatrāgneyaṃ tadadbho 'dhi janayiṣyāma ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 6-8-2-2)

Water is the root and the support of the whole universe. By placing this ash in it, the true form of fire is, as it were, established in water.

तद्यत्तत्सत्यं । आप एव तदापो हि वै सत्यं तस्माद्येनापो यंति तत्सत्यस्य रूपमित्याहुरप एव तस्य सर्वसाग्रमकुर्वंस्तस्माद्यदैवापो यन्त्यथेदग्ं सर्वं जायते यदिदं किंच ॥ (*tadyattatsatyaṃ | āpa eva tadāpo hi vai satyaṃ tasmādyenāpo yaṃti tatsatyasya rūpamityāhurapa eva tasya sarvasāgramakurvaṃstasmādyadaivāpo yantyathedagṃ sarvaṃ jāyate yadidaṃ kiṃca ‖*) (Śa. Cā. 7-4-1.-6) **NOTE**

What was said above in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, that water, the chief cause of the whole world, is of the nature of all truth, is here explained still more fully. The meaning is that wherever water flows, there flow also a part and a form of truth. Before the creation of the world there was water. From it creation spread, and as its result all things came into being. How was that? What was the order? How did it hold the embryo of the form of Viśvakarman? What is meant by saying that all the gods are contained here? The explanation is as follows—

आपो ह वा इदमग्रे सलिलमेवास । ता अकामयंत कथं नु प्रजायेमहीति ता आश्राम्यंस्तास्तपोऽतप्यंत तासु तपस्तप्यमानासु हिरण्मयमांडग्ं संबभूवाजातो ह तर्हि संवत्सर आस तदिदग्ं हिरण्मयमांडं यावत्संवत्सरस्य वेला तावत्पर्यप्लवत । (*āpo ha vā idamagre salilamevāsa | tā akāmayaṃta kathaṃ nu prajāyemahīti tā āśrāmyaṃstāstapo 'tapyaṃta tāsu tapastapyamānāsu hiraṇmayamāṃḍagṃ saṃbabhūvājāto ha tarhi saṃvatsara āsa tadidagṃ hiraṇmayamāṃḍaṃ yāvatsaṃvatsarasya velā tāvatparyaplavata |*) (Pa. Prā. 11-1-6-1) **NOTE**

Before creation there was nothing else but water. Then those waters, desiring their own increase, thought: "How may we multiply and grow?" They exerted themselves and practised austerity. As the fruit of that austerity a golden egg came into being. At that time the division of time called the year did not exist. This golden egg floated on the water for the length of a year.

ततः संवत्सरे पुरुषस्समभवत् । स प्रजापतिस्तस्मादु संवत्सर एव स्त्री वा गौर्वा वडबा वा विज्ञायते संवत्सरे हि प्रजापतिरजायत स इदग्ं हिरण्यमांडं व्यरुजन्नाह तर्हि काचन प्रतिष्ठास तदेनमिदमेव हिरण्मयमांडं यावत्संपत्सरस्य वेलासीत्तावद्भिभ्रत्पर्यप्लवत । (*tataḥ saṃvatsare puruṣassamabhavat | sa prajāpatistasmādu saṃvatsara eva strī vā gaurvā vaḍabā vā vijñāyate saṃvatsare hi prajāpatirajāyata sa idagṃ hiraṇyamāṃḍaṃ vyarujannāha tarhi kācana pratiṣṭhāsa tadenamidameva hiraṇmayamāṃḍaṃ yāvatsaṃpatsarasya velāsīttāvadbhibhratparyaplavata |*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-62) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 294

After a year the Puruṣa, in the form of Prajāpati, came into being. [By this rule, woman, cow and mare also bring forth after the span of a year.] Prajāpati, who arose after the year, split this golden egg. As there was then no support, whether in the form of earth or in any other form, this golden egg itself carried Prajāpati for the length of a year.

चतुरक्षरः संवत्सरश्चतुरक्षरः प्रजापतिस्तेनो हैवास्येष प्रतिमा ॥ (*caturakṣaraḥ saṃvatsaraścaturakṣaraḥ prajāpatisteno haivāsyeṣa pratimā ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-6-13)

Prajāpati and the year are each of four syllables. Therefore the year is like an image of Prajāpati. Moreover—

ता वा एताः । प्रजापतेरधिदेवता असृज्यंताग्निरिंद्रः सोमः परमेष्ठी प्राजापत्यः ॥ ताः सहस्रायुषो जज्जिरे ॥ (*tā vā etāḥ | prajāpateradhidevatā asṛjyaṃtāgniriṃdraḥ somaḥ parameṣṭhī prājāpatyaḥ ‖ tāḥ sahasrāyuṣo jajjire ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-1-6-14)

Indra, Agni, Soma and Parameṣṭhin Prājāpatya, these four deities, arose from Prajāpati and reflect the four syllables of the name Prajāpati; so it is explained. Moreover, the explanation of the passage यत्र देवाः समगच्छंत विश्वे (*yatra devāḥ samagacchaṃta viśve*) is given in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka as follows. (All the gods are united in Brahman and have become of the form of Brahman.)

अथ हैनं विदग्धः शाकल्यः पप्रच्छ कति देवा याज्ञवल्कॆति स हैतयेव निविदा प्रतिपेदे यावंतो वैश्वदेवस्य निविद्युच्यंते त्रयश्च त्रि च शता श्रयश्च श्री च सहस्रेत्योमिति होवाच॥ कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆति त्रयस्त्रिंशदित्योमिति होवाच कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆति षडित्योमिति होवाच कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆति त्रय इत्योमिति होवाच कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆति द्वावित्योमिति होवाच कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆत्यर्थमित्यों इति होवाच कत्येव देवा याज्ञवल्कॆत्येक इत्योमिति होवाच कतमे ते त्रयश्च त्रि च शता त्रयश्च त्रि च सहस्रेति ॥ (*atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha kati devā yājñavalkèti sa haitayeva nividā pratipede yāvaṃto vaiśvadevasya nividyucyaṃte trayaśca tri ca śatā śrayaśca śrī ca sahasretyomiti hovāca‖ katyeva devā yājñavalkèti trayastriṃśadityomiti hovāca katyeva devā yājñavalkèti ṣaḍityomiti hovāca katyeva devā yājñavalkèti traya ityomiti hovāca katyeva devā yājñavalkèti dvāvityomiti hovāca katyeva devā yājñavalkètyarthamityoṃ iti hovāca katyeva devā yājñavalkètyeka ityomiti hovāca katame te trayaśca tri ca śatā trayaśca tri ca sahasreti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-1)

Vidagdha Śākalya questions Yājñavalkya: "O Yājñavalkya, how many are the gods?" The answer: "As many as are stated in the Nivid-mantras recited to the Viśvedevas, that is, three hundred and three, and three thousand and three."

"That is so. How many are the gods?" he keeps asking. In answer Yājñavalkya shows the number step by step in this manner.

### Printed p. 295

To the second question he answered that the number is thirty-three, to the third, six, the fourth time, three, to the fifth question, two, then one and a half, and at last just one.

Then Śākalya asks: "You said three hundred and three and three thousand and three; who and who are they?" As an answer to that:

स होवाच महिमान एवैषामेते त्रयस्त्रिंशत्त्वेव देवा इति कतमे ते त्रयस्त्रिंशदित्यष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्यास्त एकत्रिंशदिंद्रश्चैव प्रजापतिश्च त्रयस्त्रिंशाविति ॥ (*sa hovāca mahimāna evaiṣāmete trayastriṃśattveva devā iti katame te trayastriṃśadityaṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāsta ekatriṃśadiṃdraścaiva prajāpatiśca trayastriṃśāviti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-2)

When Yājñavalkya said that all those three hundred and three and three thousand and three are only special glories of the thirty-three chief gods, Śākalya asked: "Who are those thirty-three gods?" Then Yājñavalkya said: "The eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras and the twelve Ādityas make thirty-one. With Indra and Prajāpati they make thirty-three."

कतमे ते वसव इत्यग्निश्च पृथिवी च वायुश्चांतरिक्षं चादित्यश्च द्यौश्च चंद्रमाश्च नक्षत्राणि चैते वसव एतेषु हीदं सर्वं हितमिति तस्माद्वसव इति (*katame te vasava ityagniśca pṛthivī ca vāyuścāṃtarikṣaṃ cādityaśca dyauśca caṃdramāśca nakṣatrāṇi caite vasava eteṣu hīdaṃ sarvaṃ hitamiti tasmādvasava iti*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-3)

Who are the Vasus? Fire, earth, wind, atmosphere, the sun, the heavenly world, the moon and the stars: these are the Vasus. Because all beings are placed in these to dwell, all these are called Vasus.

कतमे रुद्रा इति दशेमे पुरुषे प्राणा आत्मैकादशस्ते यदाऽस्माच्छरीरान्मर्त्याद्तुत्क्रामन्यथ रोदयंति तद्यद्रोदयंति तस्माद्रुद्रा इति ॥ (*katame rudrā iti daśeme puruṣe prāṇā ātmaikādaśaste yadā 'smāccharīrānmartyādtutkrāmanyatha rodayaṃti tadyadrodayaṃti tasmādrudrā iti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-4)

Who are the Rudras? The ten vital breaths in a man together with the mind (the Self) make the eleven Rudras. When they leave the body they make (the relatives) weep. Therefore they bear the name Rudra.

कतम आदित्या इति द्वादश वै मासाः सुवत्सरस्यैत आदित्या एते हीदं सर्वमाददाना यंति ते यदिदं सर्वमावदाना यंति तस्मादादित्या इति ॥ (*katama ādityā iti dvādaśa vai māsāḥ suvatsarasyaita ādityā ete hīdaṃ sarvamādadānā yaṃti te yadidaṃ sarvamāvadānā yaṃti tasmādādityā iti ‖*) (3-9-25) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 296

Who are the Ādityas? The twelve months of the year are known as the twelve Ādityas. Because they move along taking everything into themselves, they bear the name Āditya, he said.

कतम इंद्रः कतमः प्रजापतिरिति स्तनयित्नुरेवेंद्रो यज्ञः प्रजापतिरिति कतमः स्तनयित्नुरित्यशनिरिति कतमो यज्ञ इति पशव इति ॥ (*katama iṃdraḥ katamaḥ prajāpatiriti stanayitnureveṃdro yajñaḥ prajāpatiriti katamaḥ stanayitnurityaśaniriti katamo yajña iti paśava iti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-6)

Who is Indra? Who is Prajāpati? The thundering cloud is Indra. The sacrifice is Prajāpati. What is the thundering of the cloud? The thunderbolt. What is the sacrifice? The cattle.

कतमे षडित्यग्निश्च पृथिवी च वायुश्चांतरिक्षं चादित्यश्च द्यौश्चैते षडेते हीदं सर्वं षडिति ॥ (*katame ṣaḍityagniśca pṛthivī ca vāyuścāṃtarikṣaṃ cādityaśca dyauścaite ṣaḍete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ ṣaḍiti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-7)

Whom does the number six indicate? Fire, earth, wind, atmosphere, the sun and the heavenly world: these are the six.

कतमे ते त्रयो देवा इतीम एव त्रयो लोका विषु हीमे सर्वे देवा इति कतमौ तौ द्वा देवावित्यन्नं चैव प्राणश्चेति कतमोऽध्यर्ध इति योऽयं पवत इति ॥ (*katame te trayo devā itīma eva trayo lokā viṣu hīme sarve devā iti katamau tau dvā devāvityannaṃ caiva prāṇaśceti katamo 'dhyardha iti yo 'yaṃ pavata iti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3.9-8)

Who are the three gods? The three worlds, in which all the gods dwell, are the three gods. Who are the two? Food and breath. Who is the one and a half? The wind that blows here.

तदाहुर्यदयमेक इवैव पवतेऽथ कथमध्यर्ध इति यस्मिन्निदं सर्वमध्याध्नोत्तेनाध्यर्ध इति कतम एको देव इति प्राण इति सब्रह्म सदित्याचक्षते॥ (*tadāhuryadayameka ivaiva pavate 'tha kathamadhyardha iti yasminnidaṃ sarvamadhyādhnottenādhyardha iti katama eko deva iti prāṇa iti sabrahma sadityācakṣate‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-9-9)

The wind that blows here is the one god indicated by a single number. Because everything grew while it blew, the number one and a half came to designate it. Who is the god indicated by the number one? Breath. That is Brahman, that is of the nature of truth. Thus, because all the gods are contained in Brahman, it is declared that all are gathered together in Brahman, who is of the form of Viśvakarman.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमिद्दर्भं॑ प्रथ॒मं द॑ध्र॒ आपो॒ यत्र॑ दे॒वाः स॒मग॑च्छंत॒ विश्वे॑ ।  
> अ॒जस्य॒ नाभा॒वध्येक॒मर्पि॑तं॒ यस्मि॒न्विश्वा॑नि॒ भुव॑नानि त॒स्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तं । इत् । गर्भं । प्रथमं । दध्रे । अपः । यत्र । देवाः । सं अगच्छंत । विश्वे ।  
> अजस्य । नाभौ । अधि । एकं । अर्पितं । यस्मिन् । विश्वानि । भुवनानि । तस्थुः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया पूर्वमंत्रोक्तस्य प्रश्नस्कोत्तरमभिधीयते । तमित्तमेव विश्वकर्माणं गर्भं गर्भस्थानीयं प्रथममितरसृष्टेः पूर्वमापो दध्रे । दृतवत्यः ।
> यत्र गर्भे विश्वे सर्वे देवा इंद्रादयः समगच्छंत संगता भवंति । तस्याजस्य
> नाभावधि नाभौ ! अधीति सप्तम्यर्थानुवादी । एकमर्पितमित्यंडाभिप्रायेणोक्तं ।
> अंडं हि प्राक्सर्गानाभिस्थाने तिष्ठति । यस्मिन्नंडे विश्वानि भुवनानि सर्वाणि
> भूतजातानि तस्तुः तिष्ठंति । अथवाजस्य जन्मरहितस्य ब्रह्मणः स्वसृष्टे जले शयानस्य
> नाभौ सर्वजगद्बंधक उदक एकं ब्रह्मांडमर्पितं स्थापितं । शिष्टं समानं ।
> अफास्मिन्नर्थे स्मृतिः । अप एव ससर्जाद् तासु वीर्यमवाकरत् । तदंडमभवद्धैमं सूर्यकोटसमप्रभमिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this verse the answer to the question stated in the preceding mantra is given. Those very waters first, before the creation of anything else, held that Viśvakarman as the embryo, the womb-like form; दध्रे (*dadhre*) means they held. यत्र (*yatra*), in which embryo, all the gods, Indra and the rest, came together. अधि (*adhi*) in नाभावधि (*nābhāvadhi*) merely repeats the sense of the locative: on the navel of that Unborn. The words "one is placed" are said with the egg in view, for before creation the egg stands in the place of the navel. In that egg all beings stand. Or else: in the navel of the Unborn, that is, of Brahman free from birth, who lies in the water created by himself, in the water that binds the whole world, one Brahma-egg is placed, established. The rest is the same. On this meaning there is a smṛti: अप एव ससर्जाद् तासु वीर्यमवाकरत् । तदंडमभवद्धैमं सूर्यकोटसमप्रभमिति ॥ (*apa eva sasarjād tāsu vīryamavākarat | tadaṃḍamabhavaddhaimaṃ sūryakoṭasamaprabhamiti ‖*) **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which womb
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- समगच्छंत (*samagacchaṃta*)—have gathered together
- तमित् (*tamit*)—such
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—the womb, of the form of Viśvakarman
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—before creation
- दध्रे (*dadhre*)—held
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which golden egg
- विश्वानि भुवनानि (*viśvāni bhuvanāni*)—all beings
- तस्थुः (*tasthuḥ*)—are established, such
- एकं (*ekaṃ*)—this unique Brahma-egg
- अजस्य नाभौ (*ajasya nābhau*)—in the navel of the unborn primal principle
- अर्पितं (*arpitaṃ*)—is placed (is established)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The waters, before creation, held that womb of the form of Viśvakarman, in which all the gods have gathered together. In this golden egg, in which all beings

### Printed p. 298

are established, in that unique Brahma-egg, is established in the navel of the unborn primal principle. (Or: this unique Brahma-egg is established in the water that binds the whole world.)

##### English translation
The waters verily first retained the embryo in which all the god, were aggregated, single, deposited on the navel of the unborn (creator), in which all beings abode. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Here is explained further what was stated in the preceding verse: that Hiraṇyagarbha, who contained the Brahma-egg within himself, was established in the water that existed before creation. The words अजस्य नाभौ (*ajasya nābhau*) here express the main purport.

The word aja means "that which is free from birth". The word bhuvana designates all the beings that have come into existence. The meaning is that all beings created by this Supreme Brahman are contained in the navel of this unborn Hiraṇyagarbha. Before creation they are contained in the unborn Hiraṇyagarbha in a subtle state, and after creation in a gross form. This is a description of Hiraṇyagarbha, who has contained the Brahma-egg in the water that binds the whole world. The only question that arises concerns what this Aja is. Is Hiraṇyagarbha a Person, or is it a description of the nature of the primal principle? The questions and answers on this point are as follows.

किं कारणं ब्रह्म? कुतः स्म जाता जीवाम केन, क्व च संप्रतिष्ठाः । अधिष्ठिताः केन सुखेतरेषु वर्तामहे ब्रह्मविदो व्यवस्थां ॥ (*kiṃ kāraṇaṃ brahma? kutaḥ sma jātā jīvāma kena, kva ca saṃpratiṣṭhāḥ | adhiṣṭhitāḥ kena sukhetareṣu vartāmahe brahmavido vyavasthāṃ ‖*) (Śve. U. 1.1) **NOTE**

What is the root cause of the world? Is it Brahman? Or what is that which is called Brahman? What is its nature? From where is our origin? What is the support of our existence? From where do our joys and sorrows arise? The answer to these questions is as follows.

कालः स्वभावो नियतिर्यदृच्छा भूतानि योनिः पुरुष इति चिंत्या ॥ (*kālaḥ svabhāvo niyatiryadṛcchā bhūtāni yoniḥ puruṣa iti ciṃtyā ‖*) (Śve. U. 8-2) **NOTE**

This great principle, the root of the world and unborn (aja), is called by some time, by some destiny, by some nature, and likewise by still other names, by different philosophers. But,

### Printed p. 299

स्वभावमेके कवयो वदंति कालं तथान्ये परिमुह्यमानाः । देवस्यैष महिमा तु लोके येनेदं भ्राम्यते ब्रह्मचक्रं ॥ (*svabhāvameke kavayo vadaṃti kālaṃ tathānye parimuhyamānāḥ | devasyaiṣa mahimā tu loke yenedaṃ bhrāmyate brahmacakraṃ ‖*) (Prai. U. 6-1) **NOTE**

Some seers call this great principle nature, and likewise by many other names. Even so, its true nature is not fully described. The Lord who has established the whole world by his power, has taken it within his own navel, and is the master of all the dealings of the universe, must be a conscious person. By whatever name any philosopher calls this primal principle, it is compared to the chariot wheel; no other fitting comparison can be given. Whether it is called Self, Brahman or destiny, the relation of this principle, which is of the nature of consciousness, to the world of action must be likened to the relation of the chariot wheel to its spokes. The details of this simile of the wheel were explained fully earlier, when the nature of the wheel of the sun was described. Still, because the word nābhi (navel) is used here, the same simile is set out briefly.

स ना अयमात्मा सर्वेषां भूतानामधिपतिः सर्वेषां भूतानां राजा तद्यथा रथनाभौ च रथनेमौ चाराः सर्वे समर्पिता एवमेवास्मिन्नात्मनि सर्वाणि भूतानि सर्वे देवाः सर्वे लोकाः सर्वे प्राणाः सर्व एवात्मनः समर्पिताः ॥ (*sa nā ayamātmā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmadhipatiḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā tadyathā rathanābhau ca rathanemau cārāḥ sarve samarpitā evamevāsminnātmani sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarve devāḥ sarve lokāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarva evātmanaḥ samarpitāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 2.5-15)

This Self is the lord of all beings. As the spokes are all contained in the nave and the rim of the chariot wheel, and have fixed positions, so all beings are contained in this Self and are subject to the rule of this Self. All beings, all gods, all worlds, all breaths, everything is dedicated to the rule of this Self and depends on it. Thus the likeness between the Self of the world and the chariot wheel is stated. Likewise in the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad and in the Praśna Upaniṣad:

आरा इव रथनाभौ संहता यत्र नाड्यः स एषोऽंतश्चरते बहुधा जायमानः ॥ (*ārā iva rathanābhau saṃhatā yatra nāḍyaḥ sa eṣo 'ṃtaścarate bahudhā jāyamānaḥ ‖*) (Mu. 2-2 6) **NOTE**

आरा इव रथनाभौ प्राणे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं । ऋचो यजूग्ंषि सामानि यज्ञः क्षत्रं ब्रह्म च ॥ (*ārā iva rathanābhau prāṇe sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ | ṛco yajūgṃṣi sāmāni yajñaḥ kṣatraṃ brahma ca ‖*) (Praśn. 2-6) **NOTE**

आरा इव रथनाभौ कला यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठिताः । तं वेद्यं पुरुषं वेद यथा मा वो मृत्युः परिव्यथा इति ॥ (*ārā iva rathanābhau kalā yasmin pratiṣṭhitāḥ | taṃ vedyaṃ puruṣaṃ veda yathā mā vo mṛtyuḥ parivyathā iti ‖*) (Praśn. 6-6)

### Printed p. 300

In these and similar passages the relation of the primal Person to all the principles of the world is likened to this. These details have been given before (Part 12).

Thus all the worlds are contained in the egg, which is of the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, and this egg, which includes them all, floats supported by the water. The purport of this description is that the Lord pervades the universe and also transcends the universe. **NOTE** Only when the beings of the world have become one with him do they have no individual form. Only in the time of the world's dealings do they have an individual form. Before creation they forget that individual form, all are contained in the navel of the Lord, and all take on the form of the Lord. This is described in the Chāndogya Upaniṣad as follows.

इमाः सोम्य नद्यः पुरस्तात्पाच्यः स्यंदंते पश्चात् प्रतीच्यः ताः समुद्रात् समुद्रमेवापियंति स समुद्र एव भवति ता यथा तत्र न विदुरियमहमस्मीयमहमस्मीति ॥ (*imāḥ somya nadyaḥ purastātpācyaḥ syaṃdaṃte paścāt pratīcyaḥ tāḥ samudrāt samudramevāpiyaṃti sa samudra eva bhavati tā yathā tatra na viduriyamahamasmīyamahamasmīti ‖*) (Bhā. U. 6-10-1) **NOTE**

O dear son, as the rivers of the eastern quarter flow facing east and those of the western quarter flow facing west, they set out from the sea and again join the sea. Only in the middle period do they have their individual form. Neither before this nor after it do they have an individual form. All are one in the form of the sea. There is no separate designation such as "This is I; this is my name".

एवमेव खलु स्कोम्येमाः सर्वाः द्रजाः सत आगम्य न विदुः सत आगच्छामह इति त इह व्याघ्रो ना सिंहो ना वृको ना वराहो ना कीडो ना पतंगो ना दंशो ना मशको ना यद्यद्भवंति तदा भवंति ॥ (*evameva khalu skomyemāḥ sarvāḥ drajāḥ sata āgamya na viduḥ sata āgacchāmaha iti ta iha vyāghro nā siṃho nā vṛko nā varāho nā kīḍo nā pataṃgo nā daṃśo nā maśako nā yadyadbhavaṃti tadā bhavaṃti ‖*) (Bhā. U. 6-10-2)

In the same way, all the beings of this world arise from one primal principle and have their individual forms, but they do not know that their source is one and that one consciousness pervades them all. In the world they may have the form of a tiger, or of a lion, wolf, bear, worm, gnat, insect or mosquito, and in many other forms, yet in the end they become one in that primal principle from which they arose. In this and similar ways the relation of the unborn Lord to all beings contained in the Supreme Self, who is of the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, is stated. The same matter is explained in the present verse.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O men, you do not know that Viśvakarman who generated these beings. If it were said, "I am Devadatta, I am Yajñadatta; we know ourselves as Viśvakarman," that would be false, for the soul known through the notion "I" is not the true nature of Viśvakarman, the supreme Lord. Rather, other than you, the souls known through the notion "I", there is बभूव (*babhūva*), that is, there exists, the principle of the Lord, to be known through the whole of the Vedānta. If it is asked why we do not know that principle, though it is like the soul, listen. You are covered by नीहारेण (*nīhāreṇa*), by ignorance like mist; therefore you do not know. As mist is not wholly non-existent, since it veils the sight, and not wholly existent, since, unlike wood or stone, it is not fit to be perceived, so ignorance is not wholly non-existent, since it veils the principle of the Lord, nor wholly existent, since it is removed by mere right knowledge. By such ignorance all souls are covered. They are covered not only so, but also by जल्पा (*jalpā*), by false prattle such as "I am a god, I am a man". Further, the असुतृपः (*asutṛpaḥ*) are those who by whatever means feed their breaths (asu), that is, belly-fillers, who have not reflected on the principle of the Supreme Lord. Not satisfied with the enjoyment of this world only, they move about in the various sacrifices reciting the uktha and prauga hymns, the niṣkevalya and so on; that is, they live on the earth. Being intent only on enjoyment in this world and the other, you live, therefore you do not know the god Viśvakarman. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Viśvakarman
- इमा (*imā*)—these beings
- जजान (*jajāna*)—produced
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Viśvakarman
- न विदाथ (*na vidātha*)—you cannot know
- युष्माकं (*yuṣmākaṃ*)—than the endless souls who possess individuality
- अंतरं (*aṃtaraṃ*)—different
- अन्यत् (*anyat*)—the supreme principle

### Printed p. 302

- बभूव (*babhūva*)—exists (without this knowledge of the supreme principle)
- नीहारेण (*nīhāreṇa*)—by ignorance like a lump of mist
- प्रावृताः (*prāvṛtāḥ*)—those who are covered
- जल्पा (*jalpā*)—those who are engaged proudly in worldly dealings
- असुतृपः (*asutṛpaḥ*)—those who hold mere enjoyment as the chief thing
- उक्तशासः (*uktaśāsaḥ*)—the ignorant, attached to enjoyment, who keep reciting the śastra and other mantras that are chief in rites done for desires
- चरंति (*caraṃti*)—are in the majority

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

You cannot know that Viśvakarman who produced these beings. There is a supreme principle different from the endless souls who possess individuality. Without knowledge of this supreme principle, those who are covered by ignorance like a lump of mist, who are engaged proudly in worldly dealings, who hold mere enjoyment as the chief thing, who keep reciting the śastra and other mantras that are chief in rites done for desires, the ignorant attached to enjoyment, are in the majority.

##### English translation
You know not him who has generated these (beings); (his life) is another, different from yours; wrapped in fog, and foolish speech (do they) wander (who are) gluttonous and engaged in devotion.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

All beings arise from the Lord, who is of the form of Viśvakarman. But no creature that has arisen from him is able to know his greatness. There are two reasons for this. First—

(1) The Lord is beyond the universe. He is not the kind of being that can be grasped by the senses and other instruments. Even great seers, rich in austerity, can realize only one part or another of the Lord; the realization of the whole Lord does not come to them. Second—

(2) All created beings, without the knowledge that their origin is from the Lord, are filled with mere selfishness and egoism and with craving for enjoyment, and become full of ignorance, so they have no fitness for the realization of the Lord. These two matters are stated in this verse.

(1) The Lord, the cause of the whole world, is of the nature of the thread: he makes a connection with the whole universe and establishes unity in variety. He is the inner controller of all. He knows everything. Though he pervades all things, no one knows his greatness. How? Thus—

यः पृथिव्यां तिष्ठन् पृथिव्या अंतरो यं पृथिविः न वेद यस्य पृथिवी शरीरं यः पृथिवीमंतरो यमयत्येष त आत्मा अंतर्याम्यमृतः ॥ (*yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā aṃtaro yaṃ pṛthiviḥ na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīmaṃtaro yamayatyeṣa ta ātmā aṃtaryāmyamṛtaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-7-3)

The Sūtrātman who is established in the earth, whose body is the earth, whose nature the earth cannot know, is within the earth and governs all the dealings of the earth. He is the eternal Lord.
