This Sūtrātman is the indweller in water. Water is his body. But water does not know his greatness. He is the controller of water.

He is the indweller in fire. Fire is his body. But fire cannot know his greatness. He is the controller of fire.

This same Lord is within the atmosphere. The atmosphere is his body, but the atmosphere cannot know his greatness. He is the controller of the atmosphere.

This Sūtrātman is within the wind. The wind is his body. But the wind cannot know his greatness. He is the controller of the movement of the wind. This Supreme Self is within the heavenly world. The heavenly world is his body. But the heavenly world cannot know his greatness.

### Printed p. 304

Likewise, in the sun, the moon, the stars, space and all the quarters, in each of them this Sūtrātman is pervading. All of them are bodies for him. Even so, none of them is able to know the greatness of this Supreme Self. He is hidden also in darkness. To darkness too he is beyond perception. The most excessive radiance cannot know his form. He alone is the controller of the sun and all the other planets and of all the quarters.

All beings are his body; he is the controller of all beings. But no creature is able to know his greatness. In all the organs of the body, breath, speech, eye, ear, mind, understanding, skin, this Sūtrātman is the inner controller. No organ can know him.

एष त आत्मांतर्याम्यमृतोऽदृष्टो द्रष्टा अश्रुतः श्रोतामशो मंताविज्ञातो विज्ञाता नान्योऽतोऽस्ति द्रष्टा नान्योऽतोऽस्ति श्रोता नान्योऽतोऽस्ति मंता नान्योऽतोऽस्ति विज्ञाता एष त आत्मांतर्यामृमृतोऽतोऽस्यदार्तं ततो होद्दालक आरुणिरुपरराम ॥ (*eṣa ta ātmāṃtaryāmyamṛto 'dṛṣṭo draṣṭā aśrutaḥ śrotāmaśo maṃtāvijñāto vijñātā nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā nānyo 'to 'sti śrotā nānyo 'to 'sti maṃtā nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā eṣa ta ātmāṃtaryāmṛmṛto 'to 'syadārtaṃ tato hoddālaka āruṇirupararāma ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 3-7-23)

No one sees this Sūtrātman, the inner controller of all; he is the one who sees everything. No one hears his divine song, but he is the one who can hear everything. No one knows him; he alone knows everything. As soon as Yājñavalkya taught that this Supreme Self is all-pervading, immortal and the inner mover of the universe, Uddālaka Āruṇi became calm. Because he is beyond perception, he is described in the Upaniṣads as follows.

अशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपमव्ययं तथारसं नित्यमगंधवच्च यत् । अनाद्यनंतं महतः परं ध्रुवं निजाय्य तन्नृत्युमुखात्पमुच्यते ॥ (*aśabdamasparśamarūpamavyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityamagaṃdhavacca yat | anādyanaṃtaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nijāyya tannṛtyumukhātpamucyate ‖*) (Kaṭha 1-3-15)

This Supreme Self is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, without smell, beginningless and endless, steadfast. To know such a supreme principle, very hard discipline is needed. Even so, complete realization is not obtained. Therefore this Self is described in the form of negation.

अस्य श्रीर्भवति य एवं वेदाथात आदेशो नेति नेति न ह्येतस्मादिति नेत्यन्यत्परमस्तथ नामधेयं सत्यस्य सत्य इति ............ ॥ (*asya śrīrbhavati ya evaṃ vedāthāta ādeśo neti neti na hyetasmāditi netyanyatparamastatha nāmadheyaṃ satyasya satya iti ............ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 2-3-6)

### Printed p. 305

This Supreme Self, who is beyond the body, cannot be described as "thus". One has to describe his nature only by negative statements, taking all the things of the universe and saying: this is not that Supreme Self, nor is that. Therefore the nature of that Sūtrātman is described by the Śruti sentence नेति नेति (*neti neti*). Those who try to know his form come to enter only darkness. How?

अंधं तमः प्रविशंति ये अविद्यामुपासते । ततो भूय इव ते तनो य उ विद्यायाग्ं रताः ॥ (*aṃdhaṃ tamaḥ praviśaṃti ye avidyāmupāsate | tato bhūya iva te tano ya u vidyāyāgṃ ratāḥ ‖*) (Īśa 9)

Those who, without complete means to know the nature of the Lord, worship him only with blind faith sit in darkness; but even the wise who strive with the means of knowing his nature, being unable to know his endless greatness, enter a still greater darkness. How? In the effort to know the endless qualities of the Lord, if one learns one new point, still greater problems arise from it. (Avidyā also means karma; the purport is those who, devoid of knowledge, are intent on ritual alone.)

(2) Secondly, it is not only that the Lord is beyond perception. Another reason is that all beings, covered by ignorance, have no fitness to realize the Lord. An excellent illustration of this is given in the present verse: covered by ignorance like mist, they have only the conceit that they themselves are all-knowing. In the same way the nature of the ignorant is described in the Bhagavad-gītā as follows.

धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथादर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्पेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतं ॥ (*dhūmenāvriyate vahniryathādarśo malena ca | yatholpenāvṛto garbhastathā tenedamāvṛtaṃ ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 3-38) **NOTE**

As fire is covered by smoke, as the mirror is covered by dirt, as the embryo is covered by the membrane, so the radiance of the Self is covered by the enemy in the form of desire.

आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा । कामरूपेण कौंतेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च ॥ (*āvṛtaṃ jñānametena jñānino nityavairiṇā | kāmarūpeṇa kauṃteya duṣpūreṇānalena ca ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 3-39)

This desire is, for the pure Self, an eternal enemy. Like a fire that knows no satisfaction, the longing of desire tries to burn the Self. Therefore knowledge is covered by this impurity. The ignorant, covered by this desire, boast that their own path is the best path. How?

### Printed p. 306

अविद्यायामंतरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पंडितं मन्यमानाः । जंघन्यमानाः परियंति मूढा अंधेनैव नीयमाना यथांधाः ॥ (*avidyāyāmaṃtare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṃḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ | jaṃghanyamānāḥ pariyaṃti mūḍhā aṃdhenaiva nīyamānā yathāṃdhāḥ ‖*) (Muṇḍaka 1-2-8)

Though sunk in the darkness of ignorance, the unwise, thinking themselves to be the knowers, become sharers of many kinds of afflictions. As it is when blind men become guides to other blind men, so these also, in their conceit and egoism, give instruction to others and push them too into the pit of ignorance.

अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यंति बालाः । यत् कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयंति रागात् तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्चवंते ॥ (*avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ kṛtārthā ityabhimanyaṃti bālāḥ | yat karmiṇo na pravedayaṃti rāgāt tenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāścavaṃte ‖*) (Muṇḍaka 1-2-9)

Because they lack mature knowledge, these are ignorant. Even so, from their petty, polished and impure delusion they hold the false pride that they themselves have accomplished their purpose. Great attachment in ritual is itself of the form of desire. From it arises room for many kinds of self-conceit. That does not become the path to liberation. It gives no room for the realization of the Lord. Such desire-afflicted ones, after their intoxication has abated, fall as a result into the nether world. **NOTE**

न सांपरायः प्रतिभाति बालं प्रमाद्यंतं वित्तमोमोहेन मूढं । अयं लोको नास्ति पर इति मानी पुनः पुनर्वशमापद्यते मे ॥ (*na sāṃparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyaṃtaṃ vittamomohena mūḍhaṃ | ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punarvaśamāpadyate me ‖*) (Kaṭha 1-2-6)

That which is beyond his senses is not known to this ignorant man. He is intoxicated by his earthly wealth. Believing that only this world is true and eternal and that there is nothing else besides it, the unwise man, thus filled with ignorance, undergoes the sorrow of worldly existence again and again. Therefore there is no room for him to obtain the realization of the Lord. In this and similar ways the nature of a man whose mind is covered with impurity is described.

It is also explained in this verse that such a man is endowed with many faults, beginning with false pride. The purport is that knowledge of the Lord is not easy. The purport is also that to be devoted to ritual alone causes a deficiency in the gain of knowledge. This purport is made clear by the words असुतृपः, उक्तशासः चरंति (*asutṛpaḥ, uktaśāsaḥ caraṃti*). The purport is that ritual is only a means of enjoyment and does not become a means of knowledge. How?

### Printed p. 307

यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदंत्य विपश्चितः । वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः ॥ (*yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadaṃtya vipaścitaḥ | vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 2-42)

Ritual consists of resolves made for desired ends. In this resolve mere enjoyment is the aim. The śastra mantras, the praüga, niṣkevalya and the rest, are only means to this enjoyment. Those who, deluded by these sentences that promise fruit, say that there is no other kind of good apart from this are the unlearned. Their nature is as follows.

कामात्मानः स्वर्गपराः जन्मकर्मफलप्रदां । क्रियाविरेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति ॥ (*kāmātmānaḥ svargaparāḥ janmakarmaphalapradāṃ | kriyāvireṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 2-43)

These devotees of the Veda's word, who seek only the enjoyment of heaven, have minds set only on desired ends. Captivated by enjoyment, they have their minds fixed on it alone. But they do not know that the enjoyment of heaven, the fruit of sacrifice, is not eternal. They have no awareness that after the time of enjoyment is over they will again fall into birth, death and the rest.

भोग्यश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसां । व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते ॥ (*bhogyaśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasāṃ | vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 2-44)

For this intellect is of the nature of resolve. Because they are engaged only in outward dealings of this kind, the calculation of enjoyment-oriented multiplication and of what is to be done and not done, they cannot become established in samādhi, that is, they cannot attain concentration and become steady in mind. **NOTE**  Sāyaṇa, in explaining the present verse, has stated just this: उदरंभराः । न तु पारमेश्वरं तत्त्वं विचारितवंतः (*udaraṃbharāḥ | na tu pārameśvaraṃ tattvaṃ vicāritavaṃtaḥ*), belly-fillers, subject only to enjoyment, fools who do not know how to reflect on the principle of the Lord. This view is also given in the Upaniṣads in this way. For example—

इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयंते प्रमूढाः । नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशंति ॥ (*iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ nānyacchreyo vedayaṃte pramūḍhāḥ | nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte 'nubhūtvemaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśaṃti ‖*) (Muṇḍaka 1-2-10)

These selfish ones, who hold to desired ends and are devoted to enjoyment, believe that the rites such as iṣṭāpūrta are the highest and that nothing else is conducive to good. These fools, having enjoyed the heavenly enjoyment that is the fruit of their rites and having exhausted that rite, then return again to this world and become sharers of sorrow. The purport is that sorrow is not avoided by people who, without acquiring knowledge of the supreme principle, are sunk in ritual alone. The same view is stressed over and over in many places.

### Printed p. 308

तैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयंते । ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेंद्रलोकमश्नंति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ॥ (*taividyā māṃ somapāḥ pūtapāpā yajñairiṣṭvā svargatiṃ prārthayaṃte | te puṇyamāsādya sureṃdralokamaśnaṃti divyāndivi devabhogān ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 9-20)

The Soma-drinkers, the Soma-sacrificers, and those who perform the rites enjoined by the three Vedas, Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, worship me with sacrifice and desire the attainment of heaven. They go to the most meritorious world of the lord of the gods and there enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods.

ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशंति । एवं त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना गतागतं कामकामा लभंते ॥ (*te taṃ bhuktvā svargalokaṃ viśālaṃ kṣīṇe puṇye martyalokaṃ viśaṃti | evaṃ trayīdharmamanuprapannā gatāgataṃ kāmakāmā labhaṃte ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 9-21)

Having obtained that vast enjoyment of heaven, when their merit is exhausted they are born again and come to the world of mortals. Thus, as long as they only perform sacrifices and the like and wish for objects of desire, they have no knowledge of the Lord. अतः विश्वकर्माणं देवं न जानंति (*ataḥ viśvakarmāṇaṃ devaṃ na jānaṃti*). Sāyaṇa has explained that the purport of this verse is that knowledge of the supreme principle, of the form of Viśvakarman, is not possible for them. The purport is that knowledge is greater than ritual.

In the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā the 81st and 82nd hymns of the tenth maṇḍala are famed as the Viśvakarman hymns. We have written here these same hymns, with small differences, as they are recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda. Although here and there in these mantras some words and the order of the mantras differ, there is no great difference in the explanation of the meaning, and so only the mantras as they stand in the Saṃhitā are quoted. As the explanation of the meaning is the same as we have given so far, there is no need to explain it again.

य इमा विश्वा भुवनानि जुह्वदृषिर्होता निषसादा पिता नः । स आषिसा द्रविणमिच्छमानः परमच्छदो वर आ विवेश ॥ १ ॥ (*ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni juhvadṛṣirhotā niṣasādā pitā naḥ | sa āṣisā draviṇamicchamānaḥ paramacchado vara ā viveśa ‖ 1 ‖*)
विश्वकर्मा मनसा यद्विहाया धाता विधाता परमोत संदृक् । तेषामिष्टानि समिषा मदंति यत्र सप्तर्षीन् पर एकमाहुः ॥ २ ॥ (*viśvakarmā manasā yadvihāyā dhātā vidhātā paramota saṃdṛk | teṣāmiṣṭāni samiṣā madaṃti yatra saptarṣīn para ekamāhuḥ ‖ 2 ‖*)
यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता यो नः सतो अभ्यासज्जजान । यो देवानां नामधा एक एव तग्ं संप्रश्नं भुवना यंत्यन्या ॥ ३ ॥ (*yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā yo naḥ sato abhyāsajjajāna | yo devānāṃ nāmadhā eka eva tagṃ saṃpraśnaṃ bhuvanā yaṃtyanyā ‖ 3 ‖*)
त आ यजंत द्रविणग्ं समस्मा ऋषयः पूर्णे जरितारो न भूना । असूर्ता सूर्ता रजसो विमाने ये भूतानि समकृण्वन्निमानि ॥ ४ ॥ (*ta ā yajaṃta draviṇagṃ samasmā ṛṣayaḥ pūrṇe jaritāro na bhūnā | asūrtā sūrtā rajaso vimāne ye bhūtāni samakṛṇvannimāni ‖ 4 ‖*)
न तं विदाथ य इदं जजानान्यद्युष्माकमंतरं भवाति । नीहारेण प्रावृता जल्पा चासुतृप उक्तशासश्चरंति ॥ ५ ॥ (*na taṃ vidātha ya idaṃ jajānānyadyuṣmākamaṃtaraṃ bhavāti | nīhāreṇa prāvṛtā jalpā cāsutṛpa uktaśāsaścaraṃti ‖ 5 ‖*)

### Printed p. 309

परो दिवा पर एना पृथिव्या परो देवेभिरसुरैर्गुहा यत् । कग्स्विद्धर्भं प्रथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाः समगच्छंत विश्वे ॥ ६ ॥ (*paro divā para enā pṛthivyā paro devebhirasurairguhā yat | kagsviddharbhaṃ prathamaṃ dadhra āpo yatra devāḥ samagacchaṃta viśve ‖ 6 ‖*)
तमिद्दर्भं प्रथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाः समगच्छंत विश्वे । अजस्य नाभावध्येकमर्पितं यस्मिन्निदं विश्वं भुवनमधि श्रितं ॥ ७ ॥ (*tamiddarbhaṃ prathamaṃ dadhra āpo yatra devāḥ samagacchaṃta viśve | ajasya nābhāvadhyekamarpitaṃ yasminnidaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanamadhi śritaṃ ‖ 7 ‖*)
विश्वकर्मा ह्यजनिष्ट देव आदिद्दंधर्वो अभवद्वितीयः । तृतीयः पिता जनितौषधीनामपां गर्भं व्यदभात्पुरुत्ता ॥ ८ ॥ (*viśvakarmā hyajaniṣṭa deva ādiddaṃdharvo abhavadvitīyaḥ | tṛtīyaḥ pitā janitauṣadhīnāmapāṃ garbhaṃ vyadabhātpuruttā ‖ 8 ‖*)
चक्षुषः पिता मनसा हि धीरो धृतमेने अजनन्नन्नमाने । यदेदंता अददृग्ंहंत पूर्व आदिद्दावापृथिवी अप्रथेतां ॥ ९ ॥ (*cakṣuṣaḥ pitā manasā hi dhīro dhṛtamene ajanannannamāne | yadedaṃtā adadṛgṃhaṃta pūrva ādiddāvāpṛthivī aprathetāṃ ‖ 9 ‖*)
विश्वतश्चक्षुरुत विश्वतोमुखो विश्वतोहस्त उत विश्वतस्सात् । सं बाहुभ्यां नमति संपतत्र्याद्यावापृथिवी जनयन्देव एकः ॥ १० ॥ (*viśvataścakṣuruta viśvatomukho viśvatohasta uta viśvatassāt | saṃ bāhubhyāṃ namati saṃpatatryādyāvāpṛthivī janayandeva ekaḥ ‖ 10 ‖*)
किग्स् स्विदासीदधिष्ठानमारंभणं कतमत्सित् किमासीत् । यदी भूमिं जनयन्विश्वकर्मा विद्यामौर्णोन्महिना विश्वचक्षाः ॥ ११ ॥ (*kigs svidāsīdadhiṣṭhānamāraṃbhaṇaṃ katamatsit kimāsīt | yadī bhūmiṃ janayanviśvakarmā vidyāmaurṇonmahinā viśvacakṣāḥ ‖ 11 ‖*)
किग्स् स्विदनं क उ स वृक्ष आसीद्यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्पचक्षुः । मनीषिणो मनसा पृच्छतेदु तद्यदधृतिष्ठद्भवनानि धारयन् ॥ १२ ॥ (*kigs svidanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsīdyato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣpacakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchatedu tadyadadhṛtiṣṭhadbhavanāni dhārayan ‖ 12 ‖*)
या ते धामानि परमाणि यावमा या मध्यमा विश्वकर्मन्नुतेमा । शिक्षा सखिभ्यो हविषि स्वधावः स्वयं यजस्व तनुवं जुषाणः ॥ १३ ॥ (*yā te dhāmāni paramāṇi yāvamā yā madhyamā viśvakarmannutemā | śikṣā sakhibhyo haviṣi svadhāvaḥ svayaṃ yajasva tanuvaṃ juṣāṇaḥ ‖ 13 ‖*)
वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतये मनोयुजं वाजे अद्या हुवेम । स नो नेदिष्टाहवनानि जोषते विश्वशंभूरवसे साधुकर्मा ॥ १४ ॥ (*vācaspatiṃ viśvakarmāṇamūtaye manoyujaṃ vāje adyā huvema | sa no nediṣṭāhavanāni joṣate viśvaśaṃbhūravase sādhukarmā ‖ 14 ‖*)
विश्वकर्मन् हविषा वावृधानः स्वयं यजस्व तनुवं जुषाणः । मुह्यं त्वन्ये अभितः सपत्ना इहास्माकं मघवा सूरिरस्तु ॥ १५ ॥ (*viśvakarman haviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṃ yajasva tanuvaṃ juṣāṇaḥ | muhyaṃ tvanye abhitaḥ sapatnā ihāsmākaṃ maghavā sūrirastu ‖ 15 ‖*)
विश्वकर्मन् हविषा वर्धनेन त्रातारमिंद्रमकृणोरवध्यं । तस्मै विशः समनमंत पूर्विरयमुग्रोविहव्यो यथासत् ॥ १६ ॥ (*viśvakarman haviṣā vardhanena trātāramiṃdramakṛṇoravadhyaṃ | tasmai viśaḥ samanamaṃta pūrvirayamugrovihavyo yathāsat ‖ 16 ‖*)
समुद्राय वयुनाय सिंधूनां पतये नमः । नदीनाग्ं सर्वासां पित्रे जुहुता विश्वकर्मणे विश्वाहामर्त्यग्ं हविः ॥ (*samudrāya vayunāya siṃdhūnāṃ pataye namaḥ | nadīnāgṃ sarvāsāṃ pitre juhutā viśvakarmaṇe viśvāhāmartyagṃ haviḥ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-6-2, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) **NOTE**

The two Viśvakarman hymns in the Ṛgveda have 14 Ṛks in all. But here there are 17 mantras. That is, three mantras are added here beyond what is in the Ṛgveda: the 8th mantra, beginning विश्वकर्मा ह्यजनिष्टदेवः (*viśvakarmā hyajaniṣṭadevaḥ*), the 16th mantra, beginning विश्वकर्मन् हविषावर्धनेन (*viśvakarman haviṣāvardhanena*), and the 17th mantra, beginning समुद्राय वयुनाय (*samudrāya vayunāya*).

### Printed p. 310

## Sūkta 83 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Introduction**

The deity of this sūkta and of the next is Manyu, that is, the god who presides over anger. There are some instances in which the seers took certain feelings that arise in the mind to be deities and praised them. Manyu (anger, wrath) is one of these. In the same way Śraddhā, dāna (giving), tapas (meditation), Medhā, Prajñā, Kāma, Satya, Dama, Śama, Dharma, Yajña, the mind, the year or time, peace and bliss, and so on, have been regarded as deities of feeling. In the present sūkta and in the next, the deity presiding over anger, named Manyu, is praised. In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad of the Yajurveda there is also an anuvāka addressed to this deity:

मन्युरकार्षिन्नमो नमः । मन्युरकार्षिन्मन्मन्युः करोति नाहं करोमि मन्युः कर्ता नाहं कर्ता मन्युः कारयिता नाहं कारयिता एष ते मन्यो मन्यवे स्वाहा ॥ (*manyurakārṣinnamo namaḥ | manyurakārṣinmanmanyuḥ karoti nāhaṃ karomi manyuḥ kartā nāhaṃ kartā manyuḥ kārayitā nāhaṃ kārayitā eṣa te manyo manyave svāhā ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-6) **NOTE**

"O Manyu, god who presides over anger, here is homage to you. In this world you alone do all deeds; I do not do them. Whatever work is to be done, you alone are its doer and its impeller, not I. To you, so greatly glorious, I offer this oblation." This is the chief meaning of this mantra.

We give some examples of mantras concerning the other deities of feeling, Śraddhā and the rest. Concerning the deity Śraddhā, in the Ṛgveda:

श्रद्धयाग्निः समिध्यते श्रद्धया हूयते हविः । श्रद्धां भगस्य मूर्धनि वचसा वेदयामसि ॥ (*śraddhayāgniḥ samidhyate śraddhayā hūyate haviḥ | śraddhāṃ bhagasya mūrdhani vacasā vedayāmasi ‖*)

प्रियं श्रद्धे ददतः प्रियं श्रद्धे दिदासतः । प्रियं भोजेषु यज्जस्विदं म उदितं कृधि ॥ (*priyaṃ śraddhe dadataḥ priyaṃ śraddhe didāsataḥ | priyaṃ bhojeṣu yajjasvidaṃ ma uditaṃ kṛdhi ‖*)

यथा देवा असुरेषु श्रद्धामुग्रेषु चक्रिरे । एवं भोजेषु यज्वस्वस्माकमुदितं कृधि ॥ (*yathā devā asureṣu śraddhāmugreṣu cakrire | evaṃ bhojeṣu yajvasvasmākamuditaṃ kṛdhi ‖*)

श्रद्धां देवा यजमाना वायुगोपा उपासते । श्रद्धां हृदय्यं याकूत्या श्रद्धया विंदते वसु ॥ (*śraddhāṃ devā yajamānā vāyugopā upāsate | śraddhāṃ hṛdayyaṃ yākūtyā śraddhayā viṃdate vasu ‖*)

श्रद्धां प्रातर्हवामहे श्रद्धां मध्यंदिनं परि । श्रद्धां सूर्यस्य निम्रुचि श्रद्धे श्रद्धापयेह नः ॥ (*śraddhāṃ prātarhavāmahe śraddhāṃ madhyaṃdinaṃ pari | śraddhāṃ sūryasya nimruci śraddhe śraddhāpayeha naḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-151-1 to 5) **GLOSS**

श्रद्धायां प्राणे निविष्टोऽमृतं जुहोमि । ................................................अमृतापिधानमसि ॥ (*śraddhāyāṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi | ................................................amṛtāpidhānamasi ‖*) (Tri. U. 4-69) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

श्रद्धायां प्राणे निविश्यामृतग्ं हुतं........... । समानमन्येनाप्यायस्व........................ ॥ (*śraddhāyāṃ prāṇe niviśyāmṛtagṃ hutaṃ........... | samānamanyenāpyāyasva........................ ‖*) (Trai. U. 4-70) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

In mantras such as these there is praise of the deity Śraddhā. Concerning Kāma (desire):

कामोऽकार्षिन्नमो नमः । कामोऽकार्षित्कामः करोति नाहं करोमि कामः कर्ता नाहं कर्ता कामः कारयिता नाहं कारयिता एष ते काम कामाय स्वाहा ॥ (*kāmo 'kārṣinnamo namaḥ | kāmo 'kārṣitkāmaḥ karoti nāhaṃ karomi kāmaḥ kartā nāhaṃ kartā kāmaḥ kārayitā nāhaṃ kārayitā eṣa te kāma kāmāya svāhā ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-61.) **GLOSS**

क इदं कस्मा अदात् । कामः कामाय । कामो दाता । कामः प्रतिग्रहीता । कामग्० समुद्रमाविश । कामेन त्वा प्रतिगृह्णामि । कामैतत्ते । एषा ते काम दक्षिणा । उत्तानस्त्वांगीरसः प्रतिगृह्णातु ॥ (*ka idaṃ kasmā adāt | kāmaḥ kāmāya | kāmo dātā | kāmaḥ pratigrahītā | kāmag0 samudramāviśa | kāmena tvā pratigṛhṇāmi | kāmaitatte | eṣā te kāma dakṣiṇā | uttānastvāṃgīrasaḥ pratigṛhṇātu ‖*) (Tai. U. 3-10-1, 2) **GLOSS**

Medhā:

मेधा देवी जुषमाणान आगाद्विश्वाची भद्रा सुमनस्यमाना । त्वया जुष्टानुदमानादुरुक्तान्नृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥ (*medhā devī juṣamāṇāna āgādviśvācī bhadrā sumanasyamānā | tvayā juṣṭānudamānāduruktānnṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*)

त्वया जुष्टऋषिर्भवति देवि त्वया ब्रह्मागतश्रीरुत त्वया । त्वया जष्टश्चित्रं विंदते वसु सानो जुषस्व द्रविणो न मेधे ॥ (*tvayā juṣṭaṛṣirbhavati devi tvayā brahmāgataśrīruta tvayā | tvayā jaṣṭaścitraṃ viṃdate vasu sāno juṣasva draviṇo na medhe ‖*) (Tai. U. 4.41-1, 2) **GLOSS**

मेधां म इंद्रो ददातु मेधां देवी सरस्वती । मेधां मे अश्विनावुभावाधत्तां पुष्करस्रजा । अप्सरासु च या मेधा गंधर्वेषु च यन्मनः । दैवीं मेधा सरस्वती सा मां मेधा सुरभिर्जुषताग् स्वाहा ॥ (*medhāṃ ma iṃdro dadātu medhāṃ devī sarasvatī | medhāṃ me aśvināvubhāvādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajā | apsarāsu ca yā medhā gaṃdharveṣu ca yanmanaḥ | daivīṃ medhā sarasvatī sā māṃ medhā surabhirjuṣatāg svāhā ‖*) (Trai. U. 4-42-1, 2) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 312

आमां मेधा सुरभिर्विश्वरूपा हिरण्यवर्णा जगती जगम्या । ऊर्जस्वती पयसा पिन्वमाना सामां मेधा सुप्रतीका जुषंतां ॥ (*āmāṃ medhā surabhirviśvarūpā hiraṇyavarṇā jagatī jagamyā | ūrjasvatī payasā pinvamānā sāmāṃ medhā supratīkā juṣaṃtāṃ ‖*) (Śrī. U. 4-43-1) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मय्यग्निस्तेजो दधातु मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मयींद्र इंद्रियं दधातु मयि मेधां मयि प्रजां मयि सूर्यो भ्राजो दधातु ॥ (*mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayyagnistejo dadhātu mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayīṃdra iṃdriyaṃ dadhātu mayi medhāṃ mayi prajāṃ mayi sūryo bhrājo dadhātu ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-44-1) **GLOSS**

Vāc (speech):

बृहस्पते प्रथमं वाचो अग्रं यश्चरत नामधेयं दधानाः । यदेषां श्रेष्ठं यदरिप्रमासीत्रेणा तदेषां निहितं गुहाविः ॥ (*bṛhaspate prathamaṃ vāco agraṃ yaścarata nāmadheyaṃ dadhānāḥ | yadeṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ yadaripramāsītreṇā tadeṣāṃ nihitaṃ guhāviḥ ‖*) **NOTE**

सक्तुमिव तितउना पुनंतो यत्र धीरा मनसा वाचमुक्रत । अत्रा सखायः सख्यानि जानते भद्रेषां लक्ष्मीर्निहिताधि वाचि ॥ (*saktumiva titaunā punaṃto yatra dhīrā manasā vācamukrata | atrā sakhāyaḥ sakhyāni jānate bhadreṣāṃ lakṣmīrnihitādhi vāci ‖*)

यज्ञेन वाचः पदवीयमायन्ता मन्वविंदन्नृषिषु प्रविष्टां । तामा भृत्या व्यदधुः पुरुत्रा तां सप्त रेभा अभि सं नवंते ॥ (*yajñena vācaḥ padavīyamāyantā manvaviṃdannṛṣiṣu praviṣṭāṃ | tāmā bhṛtyā vyadadhuḥ purutrā tāṃ sapta rebhā abhi saṃ navaṃte ‖*)

उत त्वः पश्यन्न ददर्श वाचमुत त्वः शृण्वन्न शृणोत्येनां । उतो त्वस्यॆ तन्नं १ वि सस्रे जायेव पत्य उशती सुवासाः ॥ (*uta tvaḥ paśyanna dadarśa vācamuta tvaḥ śṛṇvanna śṛṇotyenāṃ | uto tvasyè tannaṃ 1 vi sasre jāyeva patya uśatī suvāsāḥ ‖*)

उत त्वं सख्यॆ स्थितपीतमाहर्नैनं हिन्वंतपि वाजिनेषु । आधेन्वा चरति माययैष वाचं शुश्रुवा अफलामपुष्पां ॥ (*uta tvaṃ sakhyè sthitapītamāharnainaṃ hinvaṃtapi vājineṣu | ādhenvā carati māyayaiṣa vācaṃ śuśruvā aphalāmapuṣpāṃ ‖*)

यस्तित्याज सचिविदं सखायं न तस्य वाच्यपि भागो अस्ति । यदीं शृणोत्यलकं शृणोति नहि प्रवेद सुकृतस्य पंथां ॥ (*yastityāja sacividaṃ sakhāyaṃ na tasya vācyapi bhāgo asti | yadīṃ śṛṇotyalakaṃ śṛṇoti nahi praveda sukṛtasya paṃthāṃ ‖*)

अक्षण्यंतः कर्णवंतः सखायो मनोजवेष्टसमा बभूवुः । आदघ्नूस उपकक्षास उ त्वे प्रदा इव स्नात्वा उ त्वे ददृश्रे ॥ (*akṣaṇyaṃtaḥ karṇavaṃtaḥ sakhāyo manojaveṣṭasamā babhūvuḥ | ādaghnūsa upakakṣāsa u tve pradā iva snātvā u tve dadṛśre ‖*)

हृदा तप्पेषु मनसो जवेषु यद्ब्राह्मणाः संयजंते सखायः । अत्राह त्वं वि जहुर्वेद्याभिरोहब्रह्माणो वि चरंत्यु त्वे ॥ (*hṛdā tappeṣu manaso javeṣu yadbrāhmaṇāḥ saṃyajaṃte sakhāyaḥ | atrāha tvaṃ vi jahurvedyābhirohabrahmāṇo vi caraṃtyu tve ‖*)

इमे ये नार्वाङ्ग परश्चरंति न ब्राह्मणासो न सुतेकरासः । त एते वाचमभिपद्य पापया सिरीस्तंत्रं तन्वते अप्रजज्ञयः ॥ (*ime ye nārvāṅga paraścaraṃti na brāhmaṇāso na sutekarāsaḥ | ta ete vācamabhipadya pāpayā sirīstaṃtraṃ tanvate aprajajñayaḥ ‖*)

सर्वॆ नंदंति यशसागतेन सभासाहेन सख्या सखायः । किल्पिषस्पृत्पितुषणिर्हैषामरं हितो भवति वाजिनाय ॥ (*sarvè naṃdaṃti yaśasāgatena sabhāsāhena sakhyā sakhāyaḥ | kilpiṣaspṛtpituṣaṇirhaiṣāmaraṃ hito bhavati vājināya ‖*)

### Printed p. 313

ऋचां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान्गायत्रं त्वो गायति शक्वरीषु । ब्रह्मा त्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिवीत उ त्वः ॥ (*ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣvāngāyatraṃ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu | brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vi mivīta u tvaḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-71-1 to 11) **GLOSS**

Satya (truth):

सत्येन वायुरावाति सत्येनादित्यो रोचते दिवि सत्यं वाचः प्रतिष्ठा सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्मात्सत्यं परमं वदंति ॥ (*satyena vāyurāvāti satyenādityo rocate divi satyaṃ vācaḥ pratiṣṭhā satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmātsatyaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-79) **GLOSS**

Tapas (austerity):

तपसा देवा देवतामग्र आयन्तपसर्षयः सुवरन्वविंदन्तपसा सपत्नान्प्रणुदामारातीस्तपसि सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्मात्तपः परमं वदंति ॥ (*tapasā devā devatāmagra āyantapasarṣayaḥ suvaranvaviṃdantapasā sapatnānpraṇudāmārātīstapasi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmāttapaḥ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-79) **GLOSS**

Dama (self-control):

दमेन दान्ताः किल्पिषमवधून्वंति दमेन ब्रह्मचारिणः सुवरगच्छन्मो भूतानां दुराधर्षं दमे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माद्दमः परमं वदंति ॥ (*damena dāntāḥ kilpiṣamavadhūnvaṃti damena brahmacāriṇaḥ suvaragacchanmo bhūtānāṃ durādharṣaṃ dame sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmāddamaḥ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 40-9) **GLOSS** **NOTE**

Śama (tranquillity):

शमेन शांताः शिवमाचरंति शमेन नाकं मुनयोऽन्वविंदञ्छमो भूतानां दुरादर्शञ्छमे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माच्छमः परमं वदंति ॥ (*śamena śāṃtāḥ śivamācaraṃti śamena nākaṃ munayo 'nvaviṃdañchamo bhūtānāṃ durādarśañchame sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmācchamaḥ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 4 79) **GLOSS**

Dāna (giving):

दानं यज्ञानां वरूथं दक्षिणा लोके दातारग्ं सर्वभूतानुपजीवंति दानेनारातीरपानुदंत दानेन द्विषंतो मित्रा भवंति दाने सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माद्दानं परमं वदंति ॥ (*dānaṃ yajñānāṃ varūthaṃ dakṣiṇā loke dātāragṃ sarvabhūtānupajīvaṃti dānenārātīrapānudaṃta dānena dviṣaṃto mitrā bhavaṃti dāne sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmāddānaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Trai. 4 79) **GLOSS** **NOTE**

Dharma:

धर्मो विश्वस्य जगतः प्रतिष्ठा लोके धर्मिष्ठं प्रजा उपसर्पंति धर्मेण पापमपनुदति धर्मे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माद्धर्मं परमं वदंति ॥ (*dharmo viśvasya jagataḥ pratiṣṭhā loke dharmiṣṭhaṃ prajā upasarpaṃti dharmeṇa pāpamapanudati dharme sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmāddharmaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-79) **GLOSS**

Yajña (sacrifice):

यज्ञ इति यज्ञेन हि देवा दिवं गता यज्ञेनासुरानपानुदंत यज्ञेन द्विषंतो मित्रा भवंति यज्ञे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्माद्यज्ञं परमं वदंति॥ (*yajña iti yajñena hi devā divaṃ gatā yajñenāsurānapānudaṃta yajñena dviṣaṃto mitrā bhavaṃti yajñe sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmādyajñaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti‖*) (Tai. U. 4-79) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 314

The mind:

मानसं वै प्राजापत्यं पवित्रं मानसेन मनसा साधु पश्यति मनसा ऋषयः प्रजा असजृंत मानसे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्मान्मानसं परमं वदंति ॥ (*mānasaṃ vai prājāpatyaṃ pavitraṃ mānasena manasā sādhu paśyati manasā ṛṣayaḥ prajā asajṛṃta mānase sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmānmānasaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Trai. U. 4-79) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

The year or time:

स्वयंभुप्रजापतिः संवत्सर इति संवत्सरोऽसावादित्यो य एष आदित्ये पुरुषः स परमेष्ठी ब्रह्मात्मा ॥ (*svayaṃbhuprajāpatiḥ saṃvatsara iti saṃvatsaro 'sāvādityo ya eṣa āditye puruṣaḥ sa parameṣṭhī brahmātmā ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-79) **GLOSS**

Dakṣiṇā (sacrificial fee):

दक्षिणाश्वं दक्षिणा गां ददाति दक्षिणा चंद्रमुत यद्धिरण्यं । दक्षिणान्नं वनुते यो न आत्मा दक्षिणां वर्म कृणुते विजानन् ॥ (*dakṣiṇāśvaṃ dakṣiṇā gāṃ dadāti dakṣiṇā caṃdramuta yaddhiraṇyaṃ | dakṣiṇānnaṃ vanute yo na ātmā dakṣiṇāṃ varma kṛṇute vijānan ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-107-7) **GLOSS**

Ānanda (bliss):

आनंदो ब्रह्मेति व्यजानात् । आनंदाद्द्येव खल्विमानि भूतानि जायंते । आनंदेन जातानि जीवंति । आनंदं प्रयंत्यभिसंविशंति ॥ (*ānaṃdo brahmeti vyajānāt | ānaṃdāddyeva khalvimāni bhūtāni jāyaṃte | ānaṃdena jātāni jīvaṃti | ānaṃdaṃ prayaṃtyabhisaṃviśaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 3-6) **GLOSS**

Śānti (peace):

पृथिवी शांता साग्निना शांता सा मे शांता शुचग्ं शमयतु । अंतरिक्षग्ं शांतं तद्वायुना शांतं तन्ने शांतग्ं शुचग्ं शमयतु । द्यौः शांता सादित्येन शांता सा मे शांता शुचग्ं शमयतु । पृथिवी शांतिरंत. रिक्षग्ं शांतिर्दौः शांतिर्दिशः शांतिरनांतरदिशा: शांतिरग्निः शांतिर्वायुः शांतिरादित्यः शांतिश्चंद्रमाः शांतिर्नक्षत्राणि शांतिरापः शांतिरोषधयः शांतिर्वनस्पतयः शांतिर्गौः शांतिरजा शांतिरश्वः शांतिःपुरुषः शांतिर्ब्रह्म शांतिर्भ्राह्मणः शांतिः शांतिरेव शांतिः शांतिर्मे अस्तु शांतिः । तया. हगं शांत्या सर्वशांत्या मह्यं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे च शांतिं करोमि शांतिर्मे अस्तु शांतिः ॥ (*pṛthivī śāṃtā sāgninā śāṃtā sā me śāṃtā śucagṃ śamayatu | aṃtarikṣagṃ śāṃtaṃ tadvāyunā śāṃtaṃ tanne śāṃtagṃ śucagṃ śamayatu | dyauḥ śāṃtā sādityena śāṃtā sā me śāṃtā śucagṃ śamayatu | pṛthivī śāṃtiraṃta. rikṣagṃ śāṃtirdauḥ śāṃtirdiśaḥ śāṃtiranāṃtaradiśā: śāṃtiragniḥ śāṃtirvāyuḥ śāṃtirādityaḥ śāṃtiścaṃdramāḥ śāṃtirnakṣatrāṇi śāṃtirāpaḥ śāṃtiroṣadhayaḥ śāṃtirvanaspatayaḥ śāṃtirgauḥ śāṃtirajā śāṃtiraśvaḥ śāṃtiḥpuruṣaḥ śāṃtirbrahma śāṃtirbhrāhmaṇaḥ śāṃtiḥ śāṃtireva śāṃtiḥ śāṃtirme astu śāṃtiḥ | tayā. hagaṃ śāṃtyā sarvaśāṃtyā mahyaṃ dvipade catuṣpade ca śāṃtiṃ karomi śāṃtirme astu śāṃtiḥ ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 4-42) **GLOSS**

Many more such examples can be given.

It is necessary to say here a few things about the deity Manyu, the deity of the present sūktas. Manyu means anger, wrath. What great importance has this anger? The answer is that many works can be done through anger. A work that a man in his ordinary state cannot do, a man possessed by anger will do.

### Printed p. 315

Anger produces in a man a kind of zeal and strength. But it is rare for anger to help in a good work. Its strength and power are used chiefly in doing evil, that is, in striking, killing, tormenting and the like. Then why should it be regarded as a deity and honoured? What use is it? The answer is that in any work in which anger helps, its help is indispensable. Since strength and power are needed in war and the like, and when enemies are being slain, anger has to be honoured in a special way on those occasions. Therefore the slaying of enemies and war are set out at length in both these sūktas, and through them the praise of the deity Manyu is made especially great.

In general, when war is made, it is unlikely that the soldiers on the two sides have seen one another before. They are not acquainted with one another. That being so, apart from the order of the commander of the army there is no reasonable cause for killing one another; that is, there is no personal hatred between them. Without hatred there is no chance of anger arising. Without anger the destruction of enemies does not take place. Therefore it is the custom among those eager for battle to work themselves into anger. They taunt one another, abuse one another, boast of themselves, raise questions of right and wrong, and put forward reasons such as "what we do is right, what the opponent does is wrong," and so make anger rise in their own minds. Even among forest peoples, when war has to be made, they perform a kind of dance (War-dance) and bring their anger to a high pitch.

Concerning the application (viniyoga) and the fruit-statement (phalaśruti) of these two sūktas addressed to the deity Manyu, the work called Ṛgvidhāna, ascribed to Śaunaka, says as follows:

यस्ते मन्यो इति सदा सपत्नष्टे त्वमे जपेत् । धृतेनाभिहुतं चाभ्यां धारयेदायसं मणिं ॥ (*yaste manyo iti sadā sapatnaṣṭe tvame japet | dhṛtenābhihutaṃ cābhyāṃ dhārayedāyasaṃ maṇiṃ ‖*) **NOTE**

बुहुयादायसं शंकुमाध्यामेव चतुर्दशीं । खादिरे सुसमिद्धेग्नौ सपत्नान् प्रतिबाधते ॥ (*buhuyādāyasaṃ śaṃkumādhyāmeva caturdaśīṃ | khādire susamiddhegnau sapatnān pratibādhate ‖*) **NOTE**

The man who wishes to conquer his enemies should always recite these two sūktas, beginning yaste manyo and tvayā manyo. Reciting each mantra of these sūktas, he should offer an iron bead in the fire together with a stream of ghee, and afterwards wear it on his body. And in a well-kindled consecrated fire, if he offers khadira sticks and iron nails

### Printed p. 316

(or arrow-heads) while reciting the fourteen mantras of these sūktas, that man becomes certainly able to harm his enemies.

यथा हि परमं ब्रह्म गुह्यं पावनमद्भुतं । तथा संवननं हृद्यं नह्यस्माद्विद्यते परं ॥ (*yathā hi paramaṃ brahma guhyaṃ pāvanamadbhutaṃ | tathā saṃvananaṃ hṛdyaṃ nahyasmādvidyate paraṃ ‖*)

Just as the knowledge of Brahman, most holy, wonderful and secret, is supreme, so there is no other knowledge, delightful to the mind, for the slaying of enemies.

उपोष्य द्वादशाहानि जपन्नेतमृषिं सदा ! तन्मनाः प्रयतः स स्यात् त्रिरहोऽभ्युपयादपः ॥ (*upoṣya dvādaśāhāni japannetamṛṣiṃ sadā ! tanmanāḥ prayataḥ sa syāt triraho 'bhyupayādapaḥ ‖*)

अंते तु द्वादशाहस्य शुचौ देशे समाहितः । पुंसः प्रतिकृतिं कुर्याद्भूमौ पांसुमयीं तथा ॥ (*aṃte tu dvādaśāhasya śucau deśe samāhitaḥ | puṃsaḥ pratikṛtiṃ kuryādbhūmau pāṃsumayīṃ tathā ‖*)

तस्या हृदयदेशं तु समाक्रम्य जपेदृषिं । अमोघं कर्म जानीयादहोरात्रे गते सति ॥ (*tasyā hṛdayadeśaṃ tu samākramya japedṛṣiṃ | amoghaṃ karma jānīyādahorātre gate sati ‖*)

The man who desires victory over an enemy should fast for twelve days and recite the mantras of these sūktas, pure and with his mind in it. For three days he should consecrate water with the mantras. At the end of the twelfth day, sitting in a clean place, he should make a doll of clay in the likeness of his enemy, or spread a thin layer of dust on the ground and draw on it the likeness (picture) of the enemy. Then, placing his hand on the heart of that doll or picture, he should recite the mantras until a day and a night have passed.

त्रैहेण धनिनं वैश्यं चतूरात्रेण क्षत्रियं । राजानं पंचरात्रेण षड्रात्रेण द्विजोत्तमं ॥ (*traiheṇa dhaninaṃ vaiśyaṃ catūrātreṇa kṣatriyaṃ | rājānaṃ paṃcarātreṇa ṣaḍrātreṇa dvijottamaṃ ‖*)

तपस्विनं सप्तरात्राज्जयोद्भुंजीत चैव तं । अपि वोपोषितः स्नातो जपेदेतत्सदा स्थितः ॥ (*tapasvinaṃ saptarātrājjayodbhuṃjīta caiva taṃ | api vopoṣitaḥ snāto japedetatsadā sthitaḥ ‖*)

By reciting in this way for three days one can conquer a very wealthy Vaiśya. If he recites for four nights, a Kṣatriya; if for five nights, a king; if for six nights, an excellent Brāhmaṇa; if for seven nights, even an ascetic can be conquered. Afterwards, whether having eaten, or fasting and having bathed, he should continue to recite this mantra always.

### Printed p. 317

य इच्छेदात्मनः कर्तुं हीनां तु परिवर्जयेत् । सहस्रसंपातहुतं बिल्वानां चूर्णमावपेत् ॥ ८६ ॥ (*ya icchedātmanaḥ kartuṃ hīnāṃ tu parivarjayet | sahasrasaṃpātahutaṃ bilvānāṃ cūrṇamāvapet ‖ 86 ‖*)

उदपाने वशं नेतुं तं जनं क्षिप्रमानयेत् । (*udapāne vaśaṃ netuṃ taṃ janaṃ kṣipramānayet |*)

One who wishes others to come under his control should bring a thousand bilva leaves, grind them to powder, mix it in water, consecrate that water with the mantra and give it to them to drink; then those people become subject to him.

मातर्यात्मनि पुत्रेषु पितृभ्रातृसुहृत्सु च ॥ ८७ ॥ (*mātaryātmani putreṣu pitṛbhrātṛsuhṛtsu ca ‖ 87 ‖*)

हृद्यमेतत्पयुंजीत शिरसा भारयेद्गुडं । सुमित्रं तु परिष्वज्य मूर्धन्याघ्राय चात्मजं ॥ ८८ ॥ (*hṛdyametatpayuṃjīta śirasā bhārayedguḍaṃ | sumitraṃ tu pariṣvajya mūrdhanyāghrāya cātmajaṃ ‖ 88 ‖*)

If one desires peace and happiness for his own people, he should act as follows. In respect of his mother, himself, his sons, his father, his brothers and his friends, he should consecrate jaggery and place it on the head; he should embrace a friend; he should smell the head of a son.

असंसिद्धे संवनने पांसुप्रतिकृतिं पथि ॥ ८९ ॥ प्रज्वाल्य जुहुयादग्निं धृतेन ब्राह्मणो यदि । पत्नियस्य तु तैलेन सार्षपेण विशामपि ॥ ९८ ॥ (*asaṃsiddhe saṃvanane pāṃsupratikṛtiṃ pathi ‖ 89 ‖ prajvālya juhuyādagniṃ dhṛtena brāhmaṇo yadi | patniyasya tu tailena sārṣapeṇa viśāmapi ‖ 98 ‖*) **NOTE**

आयसीं वै प्रतिकृतिमग्निमध्ये निधापयेत् । तां च प्रज्वलितां मत्वा जुहुयात्तन्मनाः शुचिः ॥ ९१ ॥ (*āyasīṃ vai pratikṛtimagnimadhye nidhāpayet | tāṃ ca prajvalitāṃ matvā juhuyāttanmanāḥ śuciḥ ‖ 91 ‖*)

उग्रेण मनसा हन्यात्कुद्धश्च जुहुयाद्भृतं । यथा यथा प्रज्वलिते हूयते जातवेदसि ॥ ९२ ॥ (*ugreṇa manasā hanyātkuddhaśca juhuyādbhṛtaṃ | yathā yathā prajvalite hūyate jātavedasi ‖ 92 ‖*)

दीप्ता प्रतिकृतिर्विप्रस्तथा स्वं वशमेष्यति । (*dīptā pratikṛtirviprastathā svaṃ vaśameṣyati |*)

If the work is not accomplished, he should draw a picture of the enemy on the dust of a road, then establish a fire, and in the blazing fire a Brāhmaṇa should offer oblations with ghee, a Kṣatriya with oil, and a Vaiśya with sarpasa **NOTE**. Then he should make a figure of iron and place it in the middle of the fire. When it has become well heated and glows, he should become pure, fix his mind on the slaying of the enemy, and with an angry mind offer ghee. As the figure heats and shines, he should offer more and more ghee into the fire. If he does so, the enemy will come under his control. Since in what follows too only rites of this kind of sorcery are stated, and an explanation of their meaning is not necessary, only the original verses are given.

### Printed p. 318

शृशानदग्ध पांसूनां कुर्याद्वेदिं विलक्षणां (*śṛśānadagdha pāṃsūnāṃ kuryādvediṃ vilakṣaṇāṃ*) (93) **GLOSS**

वैभीतकेध्मे ज्वलिते लोहप्रतिकृतिं न्यसेत् । (*vaibhītakedhme jvalite lohapratikṛtiṃ nyaset |*) अर्धरात्रे स्थिते तैलं सार्षपं लवणान्वितं (*ardharātre sthite tailaṃ sārṣapaṃ lavaṇānvitaṃ*) (94) **GLOSS**

तत्र शरमयं कुर्यात्पस्तरं प्रतिलोमतः । (*tatra śaramayaṃ kuryātpastaraṃ pratilomataḥ |*) त्रिषु शंकुषु चासीनो जुहुयादुग्रदर्शनः (*triṣu śaṃkuṣu cāsīno juhuyādugradarśanaḥ*) (95) **GLOSS**

मुक्तकेशो वधं प्रेप्पुरचिरेण प्रसादयेत् । (*muktakeśo vadhaṃ preppuracireṇa prasādayet |*) अथवाभिचरेदेवं जुहुयादात्मशोणितं (*athavābhicaredevaṃ juhuyādātmaśoṇitaṃ*) (96) **GLOSS**

वशं नयति राजानं क्षिप्रं जनपदं पुरं । (*vaśaṃ nayati rājānaṃ kṣipraṃ janapadaṃ puraṃ |*) पुष्टिकर्मापि कर्तव्यं हृद्येनोक्तं यतात्मना (*puṣṭikarmāpi kartavyaṃ hṛdyenoktaṃ yatātmanā*) (97) **GLOSS**

अनागसि न कुर्वित ब्राह्मणो वधसंयुतं । (*anāgasi na kurvita brāhmaṇo vadhasaṃyutaṃ |*) सरूपवत्सायाश्च गोः पयसा साधयेच्चरुं (*sarūpavatsāyāśca goḥ payasā sādhayeccaruṃ*) (98) **GLOSS**

सहस्रसंपातहुतं पाययेद्वत्समग्रजं । (*sahasrasaṃpātahutaṃ pāyayedvatsamagrajaṃ |*) सहस्रानुचरो वत्सः स स्याद्रोगैर्विवर्जितः (*sahasrānucaro vatsaḥ sa syādrogairvivarjitaḥ*) (99) **GLOSS**

गाश्चैव पाययेत्ताश्च भवंति व्याधिवर्जिताः । (*gāścaiva pāyayettāśca bhavaṃti vyādhivarjitāḥ |*) पुत्रांश्च प्राशयेन्नित्यं प्रियानन्यांत्व सज्जनान् (*putrāṃśca prāśayennityaṃ priyānanyāṃtva sajjanān*) (100) **GLOSS**

निरामयाश्च स्निग्दाश्च भवंति निगतज्वराः । (*nirāmayāśca snigdāśca bhavaṃti nigatajvarāḥ |*) स्त्रीयं जेदभिमन्येत तस्माः संवननं महत् (*strīyaṃ jedabhimanyeta tasmāḥ saṃvananaṃ mahat*) (101) **GLOSS**

व्रीहीणां नखभिन्नानां तंडुलान् सूक्ष्मचूर्णितान् । (*vrīhīṇāṃ nakhabhinnānāṃ taṃḍulān sūkṣmacūrṇitān |*) सहस्रसंपातहुतान् स्वेदयेत्कुशलोग्निना (*sahasrasaṃpātahutān svedayetkuśalogninā*) (102) **GLOSS**

तेन प्रतिकृतिं कुर्यात्तां ध्यात्वा मनसा स्त्रियं । (*tena pratikṛtiṃ kuryāttāṃ dhyātvā manasā striyaṃ |*) अक्तां सर्पपतैलेन जुहुयादंगशश्च तां (*aktāṃ sarpapatailena juhuyādaṃgaśaśca tāṃ*) (103) **GLOSS**

पादौ प्रथमतश्चिंद्यात् फडित्यग्नौ निधापयेत् । (*pādau prathamataściṃdyāt phaḍityagnau nidhāpayet |*) अथ जंघे जानुनी च ऊरू बाहू ततः शिरः (*atha jaṃghe jānunī ca ūrū bāhū tataḥ śiraḥ*) (104) **GLOSS**

च्छित्वा हृदयदेशं तु हृदये स्वे निवेशयेत् । (*cchitvā hṛdayadeśaṃ tu hṛdaye sve niveśayet |*) जपन्निममृषिं विप्रः स्त्री वशं साधिगच्छति (*japannimamṛṣiṃ vipraḥ strī vaśaṃ sādhigacchati*) (105) **GLOSS**

नैतत्परिगृहीतासु न साद्धीषु कथंचन । (*naitatparigṛhītāsu na sāddhīṣu kathaṃcana |*) न धर्मव्रतशीलासु कुर्वित द्विजसत्तमः (*na dharmavrataśīlāsu kurvita dvijasattamaḥ*) (106) **GLOSS**

कामं परिगृहीतासु हीनवर्णासु यश्चरेत् । (*kāmaṃ parigṛhītāsu hīnavarṇāsu yaścaret |*) पतिमस्का गुणीकुर्यात्तूर्वं पश्चात्तु तां स्त्रियं (*patimaskā guṇīkuryāttūrvaṃ paścāttu tāṃ striyaṃ*) (107) **GLOSS**

भुक्ता वा पायसं सद्यश्वर्दयित्वा निधापयेत् । (*bhuktā vā pāyasaṃ sadyaśvardayitvā nidhāpayet |*) तच्चूर्णं कृष्णजायाय्कॆ देयं संवननं स्मृतं (*taccūrṇaṃ kṛṣṇajāyāykè deyaṃ saṃvananaṃ smṛtaṃ*) (108) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 319

महावृक्षफलान्येवमयुग्मान्यभिमंत्रयेत् (*mahāvṛkṣaphalānyevamayugmānyabhimaṃtrayet*) तेषां युग्मानि भुंजीत स्वयमर्धानि शेषयेत् (*teṣāṃ yugmāni bhuṃjīta svayamardhāni śeṣayet*) (189) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

तानि दद्याद्यमिच्छेत्तु वशीकर्तुं जपन्नृषिं । (*tāni dadyādyamicchettu vaśīkartuṃ japannṛṣiṃ |*) सुहृद्भूत्वा सुहृदस्य देयं संवननं स्मृतं (*suhṛdbhūtvā suhṛdasya deyaṃ saṃvananaṃ smṛtaṃ*) (110) **GLOSS**

एकैकमभिरूपं तु हृद्यसूक्ताद्यतः पुनः । (*ekaikamabhirūpaṃ tu hṛdyasūktādyataḥ punaḥ |*) कर्माणि त्वभिरूपाणि कुर्याद्यस्तु यथेच्छति (*karmāṇi tvabhirūpāṇi kuryādyastu yathecchati*) (111) **GLOSS**

पराकदासस्य विधिं हृद्येनोक्तं विदुर्बुधाः । (*parākadāsasya vidhiṃ hṛdyenoktaṃ vidurbudhāḥ |*) स्त्रीणां संवननं चैतत्पुंसामपि विधीयते (*strīṇāṃ saṃvananaṃ caitatpuṃsāmapi vidhīyate*) (112) **GLOSS**

द्वेष्यं तु ज्ञातिनामेव जयश्चैव सदा युधि । (*dveṣyaṃ tu jñātināmeva jayaścaiva sadā yudhi |*) खादिरं कारयेच्छंकुं हृदि तं संनिवेशयेत् (*khādiraṃ kārayecchaṃkuṃ hṛdi taṃ saṃniveśayet*) (113) **GLOSS**

कृत्वा प्रतिकृतिं पूर्वं पांसुभिर्वाथवा तुष्टैः । (*kṛtvā pratikṛtiṃ pūrvaṃ pāṃsubhirvāthavā tuṣṭaiḥ |*) इषुमष्यनुमंत्रैव संग्रामं संप्रकल्पयेत् (*iṣumaṣyanumaṃtraiva saṃgrāmaṃ saṃprakalpayet*) (114) **GLOSS**

रिपुघ्नमेतज्ञानीयात्पयुक्तमपराजितं (*ripughnametajñānīyātpayuktamaparājitaṃ*) पराकदासद्वेष्यार्थं हृद्यं संवननं स्मृतं (*parākadāsadveṣyārthaṃ hṛdyaṃ saṃvananaṃ smṛtaṃ*) (115) **GLOSS**

(Ṛgvidhāna. Adhyāya 3. Ślo. 78-115)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यस्ते मन्यो इति सप्तर्चं पंचदशं सूक्तं । मन्युर्नाम तपसः पुत्र
> ऋषिः । आद्या जगती शिष्टा स्त्रिष्टुभः । इदमुत्तरं च मन्युदैवतं। तथा चानुक्रांतं।
> यस्ते मन्यो मन्युस्तापसो मान्यवं तु जगत्यादीति ॥ अजिरनाम्नभिचारसाधने
> यज्ञ एतत्तूक्तं निविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । त्वया मन्यो यस्ते मन्यो । आ. ९-७ ।
> इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यस्ते मन्यो (*yaste manyo*) has seven Ṛks and is the fifteenth sūkta. Its seer is Manyu, the son of Tapas. The first Ṛk is in Jagatī and the rest in Triṣṭubh. This sūkta and the one after it have Manyu as deity. The Anukramaṇī says: यस्ते मन्यो मन्युस्तापसो मान्यवं तु जगत्यादीति ॥ (*yaste manyo manyustāpaso mānyavaṃ tu jagatyādīti ‖*). In the sacrifice called Ajira, which is a means of sorcery, this sūkta is to be used as the nivid-dhāna sūkta; this is laid down by the sūtra त्वया मन्यो यस्ते मन्यो (*tvayā manyo yaste manyo*) (Ā. 9-7).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning यस्ते मन्यो (*yaste manyo*) is the fifteenth sūkta in the sixth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Manyu, the son of the seer named Tapa. Manyu is the deity of this sūkta and of the next one. The first Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Jagatī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: यस्ते मन्यो मन्युस्तापसो मान्यवं तु जगत्यादि (*yaste manyo manyustāpaso mānyavaṃ tu jagatyādi*). By the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra त्वया मन्यो यस्ते मन्यो (*tvayā manyo yaste manyo*) (Ā. 9.7) it is laid down that in the sacrifice called Ajira, a means of sorcery, this sūkta is to be recited as the nivid-dhāna sūkta.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मन्यो क्रोधाभिमानिन्नेव । मन्युर्मन्यतेर्दिप्तिकर्मणः क्रोधकर्म
> णो वधकर्मणो वेति निरुक्तं । १०-२९ । यो यजमानस्ते तुभ्यमविधत् परिचरति
> हे वज्र वज्रवत्सारभूत सायक सायकवच्छत्रूणां हिंसक स मनुष्यः सहो बलं
> वाह्यमोजः शारीरं बलं चानुषगनुषक्तं पुष्यति त्वदनुग्रहात्संग्रामे । यस्मा
> देवं तस्माद्वयं दासमुपक्षयकर्तारमार्यमस्मत्तोऽधिकं चोभयविधं शत्रुं
> साह्याम । अभिभवेम । केन साधनेनेति तमच्यते । त्वया युजा त्वया सहायेन।
> सहायो विशेष्यते । सहस्कृतेन बलोत्पादितेन सहसा सहमानेन परान् सह्वता
> बलवता । ईदृशेन त्वया सहायेनेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, presiding spirit of anger. The Nirukta says that manyu is from the root meaning to blaze, or that it is an act of anger or of killing (Ni. 10-29). The sacrificer who serves you, O thunderbolt (that is, as solid as a thunderbolt), O arrow (that is, destroyer of enemies like an arrow), that man nourishes continuously his strength (external might) and his ojas (bodily strength) in battle through your favour. Therefore we would overcome the दासं (*dāsaṃ*), one who causes ruin, and the आर्यं (*āryaṃ*), one superior to us, the enemy of both kinds. By what means: by you as ally, strengthened by might, overpowering others, mighty. Such is the meaning: with you as helper.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This garment causes burning. It is astringent in nature. It is like old Soma called Ṛjīṣa. It is like poison. It is not fit to be used. Only the Brāhmaṇa who knows the nature of the goddess Sūryā becomes fit to obtain this garment of the bride.

##### English translation
This (garment) is inflaming , it is pungent; it is like stale Soma ; it is like poison ; it is not fit to eat ; the Brahman, who knows Surya, verily desires the bridal (garment).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अशसनं तूषाधानं । तच्चान्यवर्णं भवति । विशसनं शिरसि निधीयमानं ।
> तादृशं दशांते निधीयमानमधिविकर्तनं यत्रिधा वासो विकृंतंति । तान्याशसनादीनि वासांस्यवस्थितानि सूर्याया रूपाणि भवंति । तानि पश्य । एवंभूतान्याशसनादीनि पुरा सूर्यास्वशरीरे स्थितान्यमंगलानि वासांसि विधत्ते ! तानि रूपाणि

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The अशसनं (*aśasanaṃ*) is the placing of तूषाधानं (*tūṣādhānaṃ*) **NOTE**, and it is of another colour. The विशसनं (*viśasanaṃ*) is what is placed on the head. The अधिविकर्तनं (*adhivikartanaṃ*) is what is placed at the hem, the cloth that they cut in three. Those garments, तान्याशसनादीनि (*tānyāśasanādīni*), are the forms of Sūryā; look at them. Garments of this kind, inauspicious, which formerly stood on Sūryā's own body, he ordains. The ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*) who knows Sūryā, that is, a Brāhmaṇa alone, removes from that garment.

> दासं आर्यं—ई शब्दगळिगॆ भाष्यकाररु दासं उपक्षपयितारं । आर्यं अस्मत्तोऽधिकं चोभयविधं शत्रुं ॥ हिंसकनाद शत्रु मत्तु नमगिंतलू बलशालियाद शत्रु
> ऎंब ऎरडु विध शत्रुगळु ऎंदु अर्थविवरणॆमाडिद्दारॆ. आदरॆ दासं ऎंब शब्दक्कॆ अनार्य,
> ई देशद पूर्वनिवासियाद कप्पुजन ऎंदू आर्यं ऎंदरॆ चातुर्वण्यगळिगॆ सेरिद आर्यजनांग
> दवनु ऎंदू अर्थमाडबहुदु. ई ऎरडु विध जनरल्लि नमगॆ शत्रुभावदिंदिरुववनन्नु
> ऎंदभिप्रायवु.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The commentators explain the words दासं आर्यं (*dāsaṃ āryaṃ*) as दासं उपक्षपयितारं । आर्यं अस्मत्तोऽधिकं चोभयविधं शत्रुं ॥ (*dāsaṃ upakṣapayitāraṃ | āryaṃ asmatto 'dhikaṃ cobhayavidhaṃ śatruṃ ‖*): the one who causes ruin, and the one who is superior to us, enemies of two kinds, that is, the destroying enemy and the enemy stronger than we. But the word dāsa can be understood as the non-Aryan, the dark people who were the earlier inhabitants of this country, and ārya as one of the Aryan people belonging to the four varṇas. The meaning is that among these two kinds of people the one who is hostile to us is meant.

> मन्युरेव होता होमनिष्पादकोऽग्निः । तथा मन्युर्वरुणोऽपि जातवेदा

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Manyu is Indra; Manyu alone is god; everything has become Manyu. Manyu alone is the होता (*hotā*), Agni who accomplishes the oblation. Likewise Manyu is Varuṇa, and जातवेदा (*jātavedā*) is Varuṇa, born of wisdom, since Manyu exists in all brilliant ones. The human subjects, the offspring of Manu, praise Manyu alone as god. O Manyu, you who are equal in affection with Tapas, so named **NOTE**, protect us.

- आस (*āsa*)—has become
- मन्युः (*manyuḥ*)—Manyu
- होता (*hotā*)—Agni, accomplisher of the oblation

- मानुषीः विशः (*mānuṣīḥ viśaḥ*)—those who are subjects belonging to the company of men

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Manyu is Indra, Manyu is the lord, Manyu is Agni who accomplishes the oblation, and Varuṇa of born wisdom. Those who are subjects belonging to the company of men praise Manyu alone. O Manyu-deva, united with Tapa our father, protect us.

##### English translation
Manyu is Indra; Manyu verily was a god; Manyu is the sacrificing priest (Agni), the omniscient Varuna; the people who are of human descent, praise Manyu; protect us, Manyu, well pleased along with Tapas.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, when the deity Manyu is praised, this god Manyu is praised with the names of other deities: Indra, Deva, Hotā, Varuṇa and so on. That is, to show that all the great qualities found in the other deities are in this god Manyu, he is addressed by the names of various deities. Everyone knows that in worldly usage, too, when a man of excellent qualities is praised, words such as "you are Indra, Candra, Devendra" are used. In the same way the seer here should be understood to have praised the god Manyu. Earlier the seer Gṛtsamada also said:

त्वमग्न इंद्रो वृषभः सतामसि त्वं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः । त्वं ब्रह्मा रयिविद्ब्रह्मणस्पते त्वं विधर्तः सचसे पुरंध्या ॥ (*tvamagna iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāmasi tvaṃ viṣṇururugāyo namasyaḥ | tvaṃ brahmā rayividbrahmaṇaspate tvaṃ vidhartaḥ sacase puraṃdhyā ‖*)

ा ॥ त्वमग्ने राजा वरुणो धृतव्रतस्त्वं मित्रो भवसि दस्म ईड्यः । त्वमर्यमा सत्पतिर्यस्य संभुजं त्वमंशो विदथे देव भाजय (*ā ‖ tvamagne rājā varuṇo dhṛtavratastvaṃ mitro bhavasi dasma īḍyaḥ | tvamaryamā satpatiryasya saṃbhujaṃ tvamaṃśo vidathe deva bhājaya*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-3, 4)

In Ṛks such as these, when praising Agni, the seer addresses and praises Agni with the names of various deities: Agni himself is Indra, he is the best among the good, he is Viṣṇu, he is Brahmā, he is Bṛhaspati, he is the creator, he is Varuṇa, he is Mitra, he is Aryaman, and so on. Such praises are many in the Ṛgveda.

> हे मन्यो त्वमभीहि । अभिगच्छास्मद्यज्ञं । कीदृशस्त्वं । तवसो बलवतोऽपि
> तवीयानत्यंतं बलवान् । स त्वं तपसास्मत्पित्रा युजा सहायेन शत्रुन्वि जहि ।
> किंचामित्रहामित्राणां हंता । अमित्रोऽस्निग्धः । तथा वृत्रहावरकाणां शत्रुणां
> हंता तथा दस्युहा च । दस्युरुपक्षयकारी शत्रुः । तादृश मन्युदेव त्वं विश्वा
> सर्वाणि वसूनि धनानि नोऽस्मभ्यमा भर । आहर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, come to our sacrifice. What kind are you? Mightier even than the mighty. As such, with Tapas, our father, as ally, strike down the enemies. Moreover, be the slayer of foes; अमित्र (*amitra*) means one who is unfriendly. Likewise be the slayer of Vṛtra-like, obstructing enemies, and the slayer of the dasyu; the dasyu is an enemy who causes ruin. O Manyu-deva, such as you are, bring to us all riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मन्यो (*manyo*)—O Manyu-deva
- अभीहि (*abhīhi*)—come graciously to us
- तवसः (*tavasaḥ*)—than the powerful
- तवीयान् (*tavīyān*)—you who have greater power
- तपसा युजा (*tapasā yujā*)—united with Tapa, our father
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—the enemies
- वि जहि (*vi jahi*)—defeat and destroy
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—and the all-pervading destroyer of enemies
- अमित्रहा (*amitrahā*)—the destroyer of the treacherous
- दस्युहा (*dasyuhā*)—and the destroyer of the destroying enemy
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, come graciously to us. You who have greater power than the powerful, united with Tapa our father, defeat and destroy the enemies. You who are the all-pervading destroyer of enemies and the destroyer of the destroying enemy, bring to us all riches.

##### English translation
Come to us Manyu, who are the strongest of the strong; withas Tap

### Printed p. 325

as your ally overthrow our enemies; do you who are the slayer of enemies, the slayer of adversaries, the slayer of foes, bring to us all riches.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒श्वच॑र्षणिः॒ सहु॑रिः॒ सहा॑वान॒स्मास्वोजः॒ पृत॑नासु धेहि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वचर्षणिः । सहुरिः । सहावान् । अस्मासु । ओजः । पृतनासु । धेहि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मन्यो त्वमभिभूत्योजाः परेषामभिभावुकबलः स्वयंभूः स्वयमेवोत्पन्नो भामः क्रुद्धोऽभिमातिषाहः । अभितो हिंसंतीत्यभिमातयः शत्रवः ।
> तेषामभिभविता विश्वचर्षणिः सर्वेषां द्रष्टा सहुरिः सहनशीलः सहावान् सहनवान्
> ईदृशस्त्वमस्मासु हृतनासु संग्रामेष्टोजो बलं धेहि । देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, you are one whose strength overcomes others (अभिभूत्योजाः (*abhibhūtyojāḥ*)), self-born, that is, arisen of yourself, wrathful, and the overcomer of foes. Those who attack from all sides are the enemies; you overcome them. You are the beholder of all, enduring, and possessed of endurance. Being such, grant strength to us in battles.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्वयंभूः (*svayaṃbhūḥ*)—self-arisen
- भामः (*bhāmaḥ*)—of the nature of wrath
- अभिमातिषाहः (*abhimātiṣāhaḥ*)—the destroyer of enemies

- सहुगिः (*sahugiḥ*)—the enduring
- सहावान् (*sahāvān*)—who are able to overcome enemies

- अस्मासु हृतनासु (*asmāsu hṛtanāsu*)—in our battles
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, you who are the destroyer of enemies, self-arisen, of the nature of wrath, the beholder of all, and enduring, produce strength for us in battles.

> भागरहितः सन् । त्वां यज्ञेऽयाजकः सन्नित्यर्थः । त्वदनुकूलरहितोऽहमप
> परेतोऽस्मि । युद्धे शत्रुभिरभिभूतः सन्नूरं गतोऽस्मि । तं तादृशं भागरहितं

> शरीरभूतस्त्वं बलडेयाय बलदानाय मेहि । मां । प्राप्नुहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu of excellent knowledge, by your great rite I am without a share, that is, I was not a sacrificer to you in the sacrifice, and being without your favour I have gone away; defeated by enemies in battle I have gone far. To you, thus shareless, I, without rite, have given anger; that is, I have made you angry. Or else: I myself have angered one who was my helper. Now you, who are as my own body, approach me, in order to give me strength.

- तं त्वा (*taṃ tvā*)—you, the worshipful
- अक्रतुः (*akratuḥ*)—being without rite

- जिहीळ (*jihīḷa*)—have made you angry
- स्वा तनूः (*svā tanūḥ*)—you who are of the form of my body
- बलदेयाय (*baladeyāya*)—to give me strength
- मा (*mā*)—to me
- एहि (*ehi*)—come graciously

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva of excellent knowledge, because I took no share in your rite I have been defeated by enemies. O Manyu-deva, I, being without rite, have made you, the worshipful, angry. You who are of the form of my body, come graciously to me, to give me strength.

## Sūkta 84 (Maṇḍala 10)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्वया मन्यो इति सप्तर्चं षोडशं सूक्तं । आदितस्त्रिस्रस्तिष्टुभस्ततश्चतस्रो
> जगत्यः । पूर्ववदृषिदेवते । तथा चानुक्रांतं । त्वया मन्यो चतुर्जगत्यंतमिति ॥
> अजिरनाम्मेकाह इदं सूक्तं मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रे निविद्धानं । सूत्रं पूर्वसूक्त
> एवोदाहृतं ॥ विनुत्त्यभिभूतिषु वज्रेष्टेकाहेष्टेते सूक्ते मरुत्वतीयनिष्केवल्ययोः शस्यॆ । सूत्रितं च । विनुत्त्यभिभूत्योरिषुवज्रयोश्च मन्युसूक्ते ।
> आ. ९-८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning त्वया मन्यो (*tvayā manyo*) has seven Ṛks and is the sixteenth sūkta. Of its Ṛks the first three are in Triṣṭubh and the next four in Jagatī. The seer and deity are as before. So it is recorded in the Anukramaṇī: चतुर्जगत्यंतमिति (*caturjagatyaṃtamiti*). In the one-day rite called Ajira this sūkta is the nivid-dhāna in the Marutvatīya śastra. The Sūtra has been quoted already under the previous sūkta. In the one-day rites Vinutti, Abhibhūti, Iṣu and Vajra these two sūktas are recited in the Marutvatīya and Niṣkevalya śastras. It is stated in the Sūtra: विनुत्त्यभिभूत्योरिषुवज्रयोश्च मन्युसूक्ते (*vinuttyabhibhūtyoriṣuvajrayośca manyusūkte*) (Ā. 9-8).

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning त्वया मन्यो (*tvayā manyo*) is the sixteenth sūkta in the sixth Anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. As in the previous sūkta, the seer and deities of this sūkta are the same. The first three Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Triṣṭup metre; the next four Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said त्वया मन्यो चतुर्जगंत्यंतं (*tvayā manyo caturjagaṃtyaṃtaṃ*). In the one-day rite named Ajira this sūkta is to be recited as the nivid-dhāna sūkta among the mantras of the Marutvatīya śastra, as is indicated in the

### Printed p. 330

passage of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, which has been quoted earlier. In the one-day rites Vinutti, Abhibhūti and Vajra, these two sūktas that have Manyu as deity are to be recited, as is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, विनुत्यभिभूत्योरिषु वज्रयोश्च मन्युसूक्ते (*vinutyabhibhūtyoriṣu vajrayośca manyusūkte*) (Ā. 9-8).

Sūkta 84. Maṇḍala 10, Anuvāka 6, Sūkta 84. Aṣṭaka 8, Adhyāya 3, Varga 19. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Ṛṣi: Manyustāpasaḥ. Devatā: Manyu. Chandas: 1-3 Triṣṭup; 4-7 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वया॑ मन्यो स॒रथ॑मारु॒जंतो॒ हर्ष॑माणासो धृषि॒ता  ॑
> मरुत्वः ।  
> ति॒ग्मेष॑व॒ आयु॑धा सं॒शिशा॑ना अ॒भि प्र यं॑तु॒ नरो॑ अ॒ग्निरू॑पाः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वया । मन्यो इति । सरथं । अरुजंतः । हर्षमाणासः । धृषिताः । मरुत्वः ।  
> तिग्मइषवः । आयुधा । संशिशानाः । अभि । प्र । यंतु । नरः । अग्निरूपाः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मन्यो हे मरुत्वः त्वया सरथं समानमेकमेव रथमारुह्यति शेषः ।
> आरुजंतो गच्छंतो हर्षमाणासो हृष्टा धृषिता धृष्टास्तिगेषवस्तीक्ष्णबाणा
> आयुधायुधानि संशिशानाः सम्यग्निश्यंतो नरो युद्धस्य नेतार इंद्रादयो
> देवास्त्रदनुचरा वाग्निरूपा अग्निवत्तीक्ष्णदाहादिकर्माणः यद्वा संनद्धाः
> कवचिनोऽभि प्र यंतु युद्धे सहायार्थं । अत्र त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुह्य
> रुजंत इत्यादि निरुक्तमनुसंधेयं । १०-३० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, O lord of the Maruts, going together with you in one and the same chariot (having mounted it is to be supplied), rejoicing, bold, with sharp arrows, whetting their weapons well, may the leaders of the battle, Indra and the other gods, your followers, fire-like, that is, doing fiery acts of burning and the like, or else armoured, advance to our side in battle for help. Here the Nirukta beginning त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुह्य रुजंत इत्यादि (*tvayā manyo sarathamāruhya rujaṃta ityādi*) is to be consulted (10-30).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुत्वः (*marutvaḥ*)—you who are accompanied by the Maruts
- मन्यो (*manyo*)—O Manyu-deva
- त्वया (*tvayā*)—with you
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—mounting the same chariot
- आरुजंतः (*ārujaṃtaḥ*)—those who go
- हर्षमाणासः (*harṣamāṇāsaḥ*)—the joyful
- धृषिताः (*dhṛṣitāḥ*)—the powerful
- तिग्मेषवः (*tigmeṣavaḥ*)—those who have sharp arrows
- आयुधा (*āyudhā*)—weapons
- संशिशानाः (*saṃśiśānāḥ*)—those who whet
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the gods, leaders in the work of battle
- अग्निरूपाः (*agnirūpāḥ*)—wearing the form of Agni
- अभि प्र यंतु (*abhi pra yaṃtu*)—may they come facing us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, accompanied by the Maruts, may the gods who mount the same chariot with you and go, joyful, powerful, with sharp arrows, whetting their weapons, leaders in the work of battle, wearing the form of Agni, come facing us.

##### English translation
May the leaders (of rites) wearing the form of Agni, (ascending) the same car with you, Manyu, who are accompanied by the Maruts, proceed to combat, advancing. exulting, indignant, armed with sharp arrows, whetting their weapons.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk Yāska has stated the Nirukta:

त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुह्य रुजंको हर्षमाणासोऽधृषिता मरुत्वस्तिग्मेषव आयुधानि संशिश्यमाना अभिप्रयंतु नरो अग्निरूपा अग्निकर्माणः सन्नद्धाः कवचिन इति वा ॥ (*tvayā manyo sarathamāruhya rujaṃko harṣamāṇāso 'dhṛṣitā marutvastigmeṣava āyudhāni saṃśiśyamānā abhiprayaṃtu naro agnirūpā agnikarmāṇaḥ sannaddhāḥ kavacina iti vā ‖*) (Ni. 10-30)

O Manyu-deva, may our warriors, seated with you in one chariot, rejoicing, and gone forth for battle, unvanquished by their opponents, thrilled, whetting their arrows and weapons, engaged like Agni in burning or destroying, and wearing armours for battle, set out toward the battlefield: this is the main purport of the Nirukta.

> बलं कुर्वनृधः शत्रुन्वि नुदस्व । घातयेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, blazing like Agni, overcome the enemies. O enduring one, be our general, invoked by us in battle. Further, having slain the enemies, apportion to us the wealth that belongs to the enemy. And, producing strength in us, drive the foes away, that is, have them slain.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहुरे (*sahure*)—you who overcome enemies
- मन्यो (*manyo*)—O Manyu-deva
- अग्निरिव (*agniriva*)—like Agni
- त्वषितः (*tvaṣitaḥ*)—radiant
- सहस्व (*sahasva*)—confront and overcome the enemies
- सेनानीः (*senānīḥ*)—like a commander of the army
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- हूतः (*hūtaḥ*)—as soon as you are called
- विधि (*vidhi*)—come graciously
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—the enemies
- हत्वाय (*hatvāya*)—having destroyed
- वेदः (*vedaḥ*)—their wealth
- वि भजस्व (*vi bhajasva*)—distribute to us
- ओजः (*ojaḥ*)—strength
- मिमानः (*mimānaḥ*)—producing in us
- मृधः (*mṛdhaḥ*)—the enemies
- वि नुदस्व (*vi nudasva*)—drive away and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, destroyer of enemies, radiant like Agni, confront the enemies and overcome them. As soon as you are called, come to us like a commander of the army. Destroy the enemies and distribute their wealth to us. Producing strength in us, drive them away and destroy them.

##### English translation
Manyu, blazing like Agni, overthrow (our foes), come as our general, enduring (Manyu) when invoked (by us) in battle; having slain the

### Printed p. 333

enemies divide (among us) the treasure; granting (us) strength, scatter (our) foes.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the sentence in this Ṛk अग्नि रिव मन्यो त्वषितः सहस्व (*agni riva manyo tvaṣitaḥ sahasva*) Yāska has stated the explanation:

अग्नि रिव मन्यो त्वषितः सहस्व ऎंब वाक्यक्कॆ यास्करु निर्वचनवन्नु हेळिद्दारॆ— अग्निरिव मन्यो त्वषितः सहस्व इति तथाग्निर्मान्यवे मंत्रे । त्वषितो ज्वलितः । त्वषिरित्यप्यस्य दीप्तिनाम भवति ॥ (*agni riva manyo tvaṣitaḥ sahasva èṃba vākyakkè yāskaru nirvacanavannu heḷiddārè— agniriva manyo tvaṣitaḥ sahasva iti tathāgnirmānyave maṃtre | tvaṣito jvalitaḥ | tvaṣirityapyasya dīptināma bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 1-17)

Here त्वषितः (*tvaṣitaḥ*) means shining. The word त्वषि (*tvaṣi*) means lustre, brilliance.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, overcome our assailant, the enemy who attacks. Harming, crushing, and destroying utterly, so that he may not live again, advance against the enemies. Your fierce, uplifted strength, who obstructs? It is not possible that anyone should. O you who are born alone and without helper, being self-controlled, you bring the enemy under your control.

- रुजन् (*rujan*)—paining
- मृणन् (*mṛṇan*)—harming

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, overcome our hostile enemies. Harming and destroying them, confront them. Who can withstand your terrible strength? O Manyu, born unique, as lord you bring everyone under your control.

##### English translation
Overthrow, Manyu, our assailant ; advance against our foes, wounding, killing, annihilating them ; (who) can resist your fierce might ? O you who are without companion, subjecting them you lead them subject.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Manyu, like Indra the maker of victory, and of unblamed speech; Yāska says that अनवब्रवोऽनवक्षिप्तवचन इति यास्कः (*anavabravo 'navakṣiptavacana iti yāskaḥ*) (Ni. 6-29). Being such, be our supreme protector, our guardian, here in this sacrifice. O enduring one, patient toward enemies, we utter your dear name, that is, we praise you; the praise from which you grow strong, that source which stirs up strength, we know.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मन्यो (*manyo*)—O Manyu-deva
- इंद्रइव (*iṃdraiva*)—like Indra

- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—to us
- आधिपाः (*ādhipāḥ*)—as complete protector
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- सहुरे (*sahure*)—O Manyu, destroyer of enemies
- ते (*te*)—praising you
- प्रियं नाम (*priyaṃ nāma*)—a beneficial hymn
- गृणीमसि (*gṛṇīmasi*)—we recite
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—by which praise
- आबभूथ (*ābabhūtha*)—you attain strength
- तं उत्सं (*taṃ utsaṃ*)—that stimulating praise
- विद्म (*vidma*)—we have known

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu-deva, victorious like Indra and free of blame, be our complete protector in this sacrifice. O Manyu, destroyer of enemies, praising you we recite a beneficial hymn. That same stimulating praise by which you attain strength, we have known.

##### English translation
Manyu, the giver of victory like Indra, irreproachable, be our protector at this (sacrifice); enduring one, we sing to you acceptable praise; we know this to be the source whence you have become (mighty)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अनवब्रवः (*anavabravaḥ*)—अनिंदितवचनः (*aniṃditavacanaḥ*), one whose speech is faultless. For this word Yāska has stated the explanation:

अनवब्रवोऽनवक्षिप्तवचनः । विजेषकृदिंद्र इवानवब्रवः इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*anavabravo 'navakṣiptavacanaḥ | vijeṣakṛdiṃdra ivānavabravaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-29)

अनवब्रवः (*anavabravaḥ*) means one in whose speech there are no faults. The meaning is one who speaks excellent, faultless, unblamable or courteous words. Since the speech of Indra is faultless in that manner, the seer has given the example of Indra here, to show that the speech of the deity Manyu is also of that kind.

> आभू॑त्या सह॒जा व॑ज्र सायक॒ सहो॑ बिर्भ्यभिभूत॒ उत्त॑रं ।  
> क्रत्वा॑ नो मन्यो स॒ह मे॒द्ये॑धि महाध॒नस्य॑ पुरुहूत  ॒॑

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्र वज्रवत्सारभूत हे सायक शत्रूणामंतकराभिभूते शत्रूणामभिभावुक मन्यो आभूत्या । आभूतिरभिभवः । तेन सहजाः सहैवोत्पन्नस्त्वमुत्तरमुत्कृष्टतरं सहो बलं बिभर्षि । धारयसि । हे मन्यो क्रत्वा कर्मणा सह
> नोऽस्माकं मेद्येधि । स्निग्धो भव । कुत्रॆति तदुच्यते । महाधनस्य । संग्रामनामैतत् । संग्रामस्य संसृजि सर्गे । हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूतेति मन्युसंबोधनं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O you who are the essence like the thunderbolt, O you who are the destroyer of enemies, O overcomer of enemies, Manyu: ābhūti is overcoming; born together with it, you bear superior, more excellent strength. O Manyu, by your deed be gracious to us. Where? In the mahādhana, which is a name for battle, in the clash of battle. O you who are invoked by many: this is an address to Manyu.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्र (*vajra*)—you who are hard like the thunderbolt
- सायक (*sāyaka*)—you who are destructive like an arrow
- अभिभूते (*abhibhūte*)—and destroyer of enemies, O Manyu
- आभूत्या (*ābhūtyā*)—together with the overcoming of enemies
- सहजाः (*sahajāḥ*)—you who are born together
- उत्तरं (*uttaraṃ*)—excellent

- भिभर्षि (*bhibharṣi*)—you bear
- महाधनस्य (*mahādhanasya*)—battle
- संस्कृजि (*saṃskṛji*)—when it has come
- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—you who are called many times
- मन्यो (*manyo*)—O Manyu-deva
- क्रत्वा सह (*kratvā saha*)—who are with the work of battle
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- मेध्येधि (*medhyedhi*)—be affectionate

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Manyu, hard like the thunderbolt, destructive like an arrow, destroyer of enemies, you who are born together with the overcoming of enemies bear excellent strength. O Manyu-deva, who are called many times when battle has come, be affectionate to us who are engaged in the work of battle.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Wealth that is undivided, of both kinds, and well brought together, let Varuṇa and Manyu give to us. The enemies hostile to us, bearing fear in their hearts, defeated, let them go away and disappear.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—Varuṇa
- मन्युः (*manyuḥ*)—and Manyu

- उभयं (*ubhayaṃ*)—and of two kinds
- धनं (*dhanaṃ*)—wealth
- समाकृतं (*samākṛtaṃ*)—so as to become our own
- दत्तां (*dattāṃ*)—let them give
- हृदयेषु (*hṛdayeṣu*)—in the hearts

- वधानाः (*vadhānāḥ*)—having
- शत्रपं (*śatrapaṃ*)—our enemies

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Varuṇa and Manyu provide to us wealth that is undivided and of two kinds, so that it becomes our own. May our enemies, who bear fear in their hearts, be defeated by us and meet destruction at our hands.
