## Sūkta 85 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Introduction**

In the first five Ṛks of this sūkta the subject of the deity Soma, and in Ṛks 6-16 the subject of the marriage of the goddess Sūryā, are stated. The goddess Sūryā herself is the seer of this sūkta. At the beginning of the sūkta Sūryā, having praised her husband Soma, then praises the matter of her own marriage. Therefore in this context it is necessary to examine closely the matter of the deity Soma and the matter of the marriage of the goddess Sūryā. The matter of the deity Soma we shall discuss in the Special Topics of the first Ṛk of this sūkta. Now only the matter of Sūryā's marriage is set out.

In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa it is thus:

प्रजापतिः सोमग्ं राजानमसृजत । तं त्रयो वेदा अन्वसृज्यंत । तान् हस्तेऽकुरुत । अथ ह सीता सावित्रि । सोमग्ं राजानं चकमे । श्रद्धामु स चकमे । सा ह पितरं प्रजापतिमुपससार । तग्ं होवाच । नमस्ते अस्तु भगवः । उपत्वाऽयानि । प्र त्वा पद्ये । सोमं वै राजानं कामये । श्रद्धामु स कामयत इति । (*prajāpatiḥ somagṃ rājānamasṛjata | taṃ trayo vedā anvasṛjyaṃta | tān haste 'kuruta | atha ha sītā sāvitri | somagṃ rājānaṃ cakame | śraddhāmu sa cakame | sā ha pitaraṃ prajāpatimupasasāra | tagṃ hovāca | namaste astu bhagavaḥ | upatvā 'yāni | pra tvā padye | somaṃ vai rājānaṃ kāmaye | śraddhāmu sa kāmayata iti |*) तस्या उ हस्तागरमलंकारं कल्पयित्वा! दशहोतारं पुरस्ताद्व्याख्याय। चतुर् होतारं दक्षिणतः। पंचहोतारं पश्चात् । षड्भोतारमुत्तरतः । सप्तहोतारमुपरिष्टात् । संभारैश्च पत्निभिश्चमुखेऽलंकृत्य। आस्त्यार्थं वप्राज ! ताग्ं होदीक्ष्योवाच । भोगं तु म आचक्ष्व । एतन्म आचक्ष्व । यत्ते पाणाविति । तस्याउहत्रीन् वेदान् प्रददौ ॥ (*tasyā u hastāgaramalaṃkāraṃ kalpayitvā! daśahotāraṃ purastādvyākhyāya| catur hotāraṃ dakṣiṇataḥ| paṃcahotāraṃ paścāt | ṣaḍbhotāramuttarataḥ | saptahotāramupariṣṭāt | saṃbhāraiśca patnibhiścamukhe 'laṃkṛtya| āstyārthaṃ vaprāja ! tāgṃ hodīkṣyovāca | bhogaṃ tu ma ācakṣva | etanma ācakṣva | yatte pāṇāviti | tasyāuhatrīn vedān pradadau ‖*) (Tai. Brā. 2-3-10-1, 2. 3)

In former times Prajāpati created the god Soma. Then the creation of the three Vedas, called Ṛg, Yajus and Sāman, also took place. He held them in his hand, and a daughter of the god Savitṛ

### Printed p. 340

Sāvitrī (the goddess Sūryā) saw it. Then desire of love for the god Soma arose in her. But that god Soma had his mind on the goddess Śraddhā. He did not agree to marry the goddess Sūryā. Then the goddess Sūryā went to Prajāpati, the father of Soma, and prayed: "O lord, here I bow to you. I have come to you for a purpose. You must favour me by granting the boon I ask." Then, when Prajāpati said, "What do you want?", Sūryā said: "O revered one, I am infatuated with the god Soma. I wish to marry him alone. But that Soma, without love for me, is attached to the goddess Śraddhā." Hearing this, Prajāpati thought in his mind and said to Sūryā: "Good. If you are to appear attractive to the eye of the god Soma, adorn your body well with ornaments and the like; then Soma will like you and marry you." Having said so, he adorned her with garments, ornaments and the like of many kinds, led her a little way, and left her near King Soma. Then Sūryā asked Prajāpati: "So that I may enjoy pleasures and the like with my husband, give me as a gift what you have in your hand." Prajāpati agreed, "So be it", and gave her the three Vedas that he had in his hand: this history is stated. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa this matter is described somewhat differently.

Skandasvāmin has commented अत्र प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राजे (*atra prajāpatirvai somāya rāje*) (Ai. Brā. 4-7-1) इत्याद्यैकरेयब्राह्मणाधीतमिहाप्याकृष्टव्यं (*ityādyaikareyabrāhmaṇādhītamihāpyākṛṣṭavyaṃ*): that is, the passage of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa that tells the history that Prajāpati gave his daughter to King Soma is to be explained here. And he has given all of it by way of example:

प्रजापतिः सवितुः दुहितरं सूर्यां सोमाय राजे प्रायच्छत् । ये त्वन्ये देवाः तां वरयितुमागच्छन् । तेभ्यो विवाहादनंतरमृक्सहस्रमददात् । यदेतदाश्विनं नाम तस्मिन् देवा विवादमकुर्वन् । ममेदमस्तु ममेदमस्त्विति । तेऽब्रुवन् । आजिं धावाम । यो नो जेष्यति तस्येदं भविष्यतीति । तेऽग्निर्गृहपतेरुपर्यादित्यं काष्ठां कृत्वाभिधावन् । काष्ठा आज्यंत उच्चते अश्वतरीरथेनाग्निराजिमधावत् । गोभिररुणैरुषाः । हरिरथेनेंद्रः । गर्दभरथेनाश्विन् । तत्राश्विनावजयताम् । (*prajāpatiḥ savituḥ duhitaraṃ sūryāṃ somāya rāje prāyacchat | ye tvanye devāḥ tāṃ varayitumāgacchan | tebhyo vivāhādanaṃtaramṛksahasramadadāt | yadetadāśvinaṃ nāma tasmin devā vivādamakurvan | mamedamastu mamedamastviti | te 'bruvan | ājiṃ dhāvāma | yo no jeṣyati tasyedaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | te 'gnirgṛhapateruparyādityaṃ kāṣṭhāṃ kṛtvābhidhāvan | kāṣṭhā ājyaṃta uccate aśvatarīrathenāgnirājimadhāvat | gobhiraruṇairuṣāḥ | hariratheneṃdraḥ | gardabharathenāśvin | tatrāśvināvajayatām |*)

Brahmā gave the daughter of the god Savitṛ, named Sūryā, in marriage to King Soma. Then the other gods came to choose her. After the marriage he gave them a thousand Ṛks. These Ṛks are well known by the name Āśvina Ṛks. The gods who had come there disputed about these Ṛks, each saying that he wanted them. Afterwards

### Printed p. 341

they decided among themselves that these Ṛks should go to the one who won the contest, the battle. Then they fixed that the end of the contest should be going from above Agni the householder's fire up to Āditya, and set out to run. Then Agni came to the contest with a chariot yoked with mules. Uṣas came to the contest with a chariot yoked with red cows. Indra came with a chariot yoked with horses named Hari. The Aśvins came to the contest with a chariot yoked with asses. In the contest that took place the Aśvins won. A thousand Ṛks were obtained by them. Hence these Ṛks are famed as Āśvina. Thus the history is explained.

Sāyaṇa has told the story of this context thus:

सविता सूरो दुहितरं सूर्य्याख्यां प्रदातुमनाः देवानाहूय सामर्थ्यसमीक्षणाय आजिं परिकल्प्य य इमं जेष्यति स एतां कन्यकामृक्सहस्रक्लप्तं स्तोत्रं च लभते इत्यकल्पयत् । तमग्निः प्रथममजयत् । तमन्वश्विनावपि जित्वा अग्निं प्रधृष्ट्य ऋक्सहस्रं कन्यकां च चालभेतां । तत इंद्र उषाश्चालभेतां । तौ च तैरग्न्यादिभिः प्रार्थितौ स्वशस्त्रस्य कंचित्कंचिद्भागं तेभ्यः परिकल्प्य सूर्यः स्वरथे आधारयतां इति ॥ (*savitā sūro duhitaraṃ sūryyākhyāṃ pradātumanāḥ devānāhūya sāmarthyasamīkṣaṇāya ājiṃ parikalpya ya imaṃ jeṣyati sa etāṃ kanyakāmṛksahasraklaptaṃ stotraṃ ca labhate ityakalpayat | tamagniḥ prathamamajayat | tamanvaśvināvapi jitvā agniṃ pradhṛṣṭya ṛksahasraṃ kanyakāṃ ca cālabhetāṃ | tata iṃdra uṣāścālabhetāṃ | tau ca tairagnyādibhiḥ prārthitau svaśastrasya kaṃcitkaṃcidbhāgaṃ tebhyaḥ parikalpya sūryaḥ svarathe ādhārayatāṃ iti ‖*)

Savitṛ, wishing to give his daughter named Sūryā in marriage, called the gods and, to test their ability, arranged a contest. He announced that to the one who won it he would hand over his daughter and a śastra measuring a thousand Ṛks. When Agni won, the Aśvins opposed him and took both for themselves. Afterwards, when Indra and Uṣas also won the contest, the two, begged by them and by Agni, assigned to them also a small share in their śastra and seated Sūryā in their chariot: this story he has told. This same matter he has told in the fourteenth part, in Ṛk 1-184-1, while telling the importance of the Āśvina śastra, quoting the words of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa प्रजापतिर्वै सोमाय राजे (*prajāpatirvai somāya rāje*) (Ai. 4.7), and the story described there. In the Ṛksaṃhitā the sūkta describing Sūryā's marriage is separate (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85). Before knowing that description, it is highly necessary to know how the form of the divine maiden or goddess named Sūryā is described in various places. The form of Sūryā is told in the Bṛhaddevatā thus:

तस्य मुख्यतमौ देवावश्विन् सूर्यमाश्रित् । वृषाकपायी सूर्योषाः सूर्यस्यॆव तु पत्नयः ॥ अमुतोऽर्वाज् निवर्तंते प्रतिलोमास्तदाश्रयाः । (*tasya mukhyatamau devāvaśvin sūryamāśrit | vṛṣākapāyī sūryoṣāḥ sūryasyèva tu patnayaḥ ‖ amuto 'rvāj nivartaṃte pratilomāstadāśrayāḥ |*)

### Printed p. 342

पुरोदयात्तामुषसं सूर्यां मध्यंदिने स्थिते ॥ वृषाकपायीं सूर्यस्य तामेवाहुस्तु निम्रुचि । तस्याश्रये सरण्यूश्च भगः पूषा वृषाकपिः ॥ (*purodayāttāmuṣasaṃ sūryāṃ madhyaṃdine sthite ‖ vṛṣākapāyīṃ sūryasya tāmevāhustu nimruci | tasyāśraye saraṇyūśca bhagaḥ pūṣā vṛṣākapiḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. Hade. 2-8 to 10) **NOTE**

The two Aśvin deities are deities connected with the sun. Vṛṣākapāyā, Sūryā and Uṣas, these three are the wives of the sun. Those of the atmospheric world, having obtained connection with the sun, turn back toward this world. One and the same goddess, in three forms, is named Uṣas before sunrise, Sūryā at midday, and Vṛṣākapāyā at sunset. Having said so, he describes again, when telling the matter of the Sūryā-sūkta, in this manner:

सावित्रि चैव सूर्या च सैव पत्नि विवस्वतः । स्तुता वृषाकपायीति उषा इति च योच्यते । उषा एषा त्रिधात्मानं विभज्य प्रैति गोपतिं ॥ उषाः पुरोदयादूत्वा सूर्या मध्यंदिने स्थिते । भूत्वा वृषाकपायी च दिनांतेष्टवगच्छति ॥ (*sāvitri caiva sūryā ca saiva patni vivasvataḥ | stutā vṛṣākapāyīti uṣā iti ca yocyate | uṣā eṣā tridhātmānaṃ vibhajya praiti gopatiṃ ‖ uṣāḥ purodayādūtvā sūryā madhyaṃdine sthite | bhūtvā vṛṣākapāyī ca dināṃteṣṭavagacchati ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-119 to 121)

Sāvitrī and Sūryā, these two are both wives of Vivasvān. This same Sūryā is also called Vṛṣākapāyī and Uṣas: having restated what was said before, he describes the matter of the marriage of this Sūryā and praises the distinctiveness of the Sūryā-sūkta. Thus, when there is a description of the maiden named Sūryā, it is necessary to know what her relation is to the sun and what is the meaning of her having chosen the Aśvins. In the Ṛks of the Sūryā-sūkta cited below, Sūryā's joining the Aśvins for marriage is described.

यदश्विना पृच्छमानावयातं त्रिचक्रेण वहतुं सूर्यायाः । विश्वे देवा अनु तद्वामजानन् पुत्रः पितराववृणीत पूषा ॥ (*yadaśvinā pṛcchamānāvayātaṃ tricakreṇa vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ | viśve devā anu tadvāmajānan putraḥ pitarāvavṛṇīta pūṣā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85.14)

In this Ṛk: "O Aśvins, when you came in your three-wheeled chariot to take the hand of Sūryā, all the gods also approved your marriage, and your son Pūṣan chose you as father." In it the very words वहतुं सूर्यायाः (*vahatuṃ sūryāyāḥ*) that are used in the present Ṛk are used. Besides this,

### Printed p. 343

स्तोमा आसन्प्रतिधयः कुरीरं छंद ओपशः । सूराया अश्विना वराग्निरासीत्पुरोगवः ॥ (*stomā āsanpratidhayaḥ kurīraṃ chaṃda opaśaḥ | sūrāyā aśvinā varāgnirāsītpurogavaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.85-8) **GLOSS**

यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप । क्वैकं चक्रं नामासीत्कृदेष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ॥ (*yadayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryāmupa | kvaikaṃ cakraṃ nāmāsītkṛdeṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85.15) **GLOSS**

In these Ṛks also there is a description. Besides this,

अधि श्रिये दुहिता सूर्यस्य रथं तस्थौ पुरुभुजा शतोतिं । प्र मायाभिर्मायिना भूतमत्र नरा नृतू जनिमन्यज्जियानां ॥ (*adhi śriye duhitā sūryasya rathaṃ tasthau purubhujā śatotiṃ | pra māyābhirmāyinā bhūtamatra narā nṛtū janimanyajjiyānāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-63-5) **GLOSS**

ओ त्यमह्व आ रथमद्या दंसिष्ठ मूतये । यमश्विना सुहवा रुद्रवर्तनी आ सूर्यायै तस्थथुः ॥ (*o tyamahva ā rathamadyā daṃsiṣṭha mūtaye | yamaśvinā suhavā rudravartanī ā sūryāyai tasthathuḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-22-1) **GLOSS**

को मृळाति कतम आगमिष्ठो देवानामु कतमः शंभविष्यः । रथं कमाहुर्द्रवदश्वमाशुं यं सूर्यस्य दुहितावृणीत ॥ (*ko mṛḷāti katama āgamiṣṭho devānāmu katamaḥ śaṃbhaviṣyaḥ | rathaṃ kamāhurdravadaśvamāśuṃ yaṃ sūryasya duhitāvṛṇīta ‖*) (Mi. Saṃ, 4-43-2) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

In all such contexts it is well known that Sūryā chose the Aśvins in a svayaṃvara. In the Ṛk 6-53-5 cited above, it is said that the Aśvins, seated in their three-wheeled chariot, won the victory in the contest that had been arranged for the gods. **NOTE**

But in the Ṛk 10-85-15, cited above from the sūkta's mantras, it is described that when they set out to approach Sūryā, one of their chariot wheels became invisible. Explaining what this means, the English scholar Maryla Falk has stated her opinion in this manner.

The substance of this opinion is as follows. **NOTE**

यो वां परिज्मा सुवृदश्विना रथो दोषामुषासो हव्यो हविष्मता । शश्वत्तमासस्तमु वामिदं वयं पितुर्न नाम सुहवं हवामहे ॥ (*yo vāṃ parijmā suvṛdaśvinā ratho doṣāmuṣāso havyo haviṣmatā | śaśvattamāsastamu vāmidaṃ vayaṃ piturna nāma suhavaṃ havāmahe ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-29-1) **GLOSS**

In Ṛks such as this it is stated that the Aśvins are invoked at the time of dawn and also at the time of evening twilight. Not only that,

### Printed p. 344

उता यातं संगवे प्रातरहो मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य । दिवा नक्तमवसा शंतमेन नेदानीं पीतिरश्पिना ततान (*utā yātaṃ saṃgave prātaraho madhyaṃdina uditā sūryasya | divā naktamavasā śaṃtamena nedānīṃ pītiraśpinā tatāna*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5.76-3) **GLOSS**

By such mantras they are invited to the midday libation also. In this way, the authors of the Nirukta have made clear that the real nature of the Aśvins, who hold a prominent place in all three libations, cannot be stated precisely, and that each person gives a different opinion. (Ni. 12-1)

And,

नाना जातावरेपसा समस्मे बंधुमेयथुः (*nānā jātāvarepasā samasme baṃdhumeyathuḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-73-4) **GLOSS**

In such places their separate birth and growth are shown by नाना जात्! पृथगेव समृद्धौ (*nānā jāt! pṛthageva samṛddhau*). In some places it is also stated that the two names Nāsatya and Dasra are separate individual forms of the pair of Aśvins (Journal of Oriental Research, Madras Vol XV). It is understood that they are deities that shine in the morning and in the evening. Therefore the twilight-red colour of their chariot and of their chariot wheel is described in हिरण्ययाः वां पवयः (*hiraṇyayāḥ vāṃ pavayaḥ*) (1-180-1) and similar passages. The Aśvins, of such a nature,

युवोः श्रियं परियोषावृणीत सूरो दुहिता परितक्क्यायां । यद्देवयंतमवथः शचीभिः परि फ्रंसमोमाना वां वयो गात् ॥ (*yuvoḥ śriyaṃ pariyoṣāvṛṇīta sūro duhitā paritakkyāyāṃ | yaddevayaṃtamavathaḥ śacībhiḥ pari phraṃsamomānā vāṃ vayo gāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-69-4) **GLOSS**

are praised thus in this verse: "O Aśvins, Sūrya's daughter, ever devoted to the service of your beauty, joins you at the time of the libation and pervades you." Besides this description, in some places it is also stated that this same daughter of Sūrya overtakes the Aśvins and joins them when they are in the middle of the sun's path in the atmosphere. At such times,

ईर्मान्यद्वपुषे वपुश्चक्रं रथस्य येमधुः । पर्यन्या नाहुषा युगा मह्ना रजांसि दीयथः ॥ (*īrmānyadvapuṣe vapuścakraṃ rathasya yemadhuḥ | paryanyā nāhuṣā yugā mahnā rajāṃsi dīyathaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5.73-3) **GLOSS**

by such mantras the third wheel of the Aśvins' chariot and its radiance are described. That Sūryā joins the Aśvins who have such a chariot wheel is praised in

आ यद्वां सूर‍्या रथं तिष्ठद्रघुष्यदं सदा (*ā yadvāṃ sūryā rathaṃ tiṣṭhadraghuṣyadaṃ sadā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-73-5) **GLOSS**

and similar places. And in this same mantra, that as soon as Sūryā mounted the chariot of the Aśvins their chariot was filled with the golden rays of the sun is praised by the sentence

### Printed p. 345

परि वामरुषा वयो फृणावरंत आतपः (*pari vāmaruṣā vayo phṛṇāvaraṃta ātapaḥ*) **GLOSS**

That is, the meaning is that Sūryā's radiance made their chariot wheel disappear.

Some of the opinions of the scholar Maryla Falk cited above are critical and are explanations in accordance with tradition. But some other explanations in that article are merely imaginary. How they are opposed to tradition will be explained in detail later, when the Sūryā-sūkta is expounded. In the present context, one should note one or two points of apparent contradiction, visible to a superficial view, in the matter of Sūryā's marriage; after that, one has to consider who the remaining deities are who are described as identified with Sūryā and what their nature is. And what kind of harmony there is in these contradictions visible to a superficial view will be explained later.

अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते । उताश्विनावभरदत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥ (*apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate | utāśvināvabharadattadāsīdajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.17-2)

In this Ṛk there is the description that the gods gave Saraṇyū to Vivasvān in marriage, and that she, in the form of a mare, bore the Aśvins. That is, it is understood from this that the Aśvins are the sons of Vivasvān. But from the statement of the Bṛhaddevatā cited above,

सावित्रि चैव सूर्या च सैवपत्नी विशेषतः (*sāvitri caiva sūryā ca saivapatnī viśeṣataḥ*) (Bṛ. De- 7-119) **GLOSS**

it is understood that Sūryā is the wife of Vivasvān. What is the meaning of the Aśvins having chosen her? In the same way,

सोमो वधूयुरभवदश्विनास्तामुभा वरा । सूर्यां यत्पत्ये शंसंतीं मनसा सविताददात् ॥ (*somo vadhūyurabhavadaśvināstāmubhā varā | sūryāṃ yatpatye śaṃsaṃtīṃ manasā savitādadāt ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-9)

here it is said that Savitṛ gave his daughter Sūryā in marriage to Soma; that the Aśvins were then merely onlookers; and that after the marriage Sūryā went to the house of her husband Soma and joined him. How the meaning is to be stated here and so on will be explained in detail in the exposition of the Sūryā-sūkta, and harmony will be shown for these contradictions.

In the Ṛk-saṃhitā, in the description of Sūryā and her marriage set forth in the Sūryā-sūkta, a profound

### Printed p. 346

spiritual principle lies hidden. Some mantras of the Sūryā-sūkta convey this point. The principle described in the Upaniṣadic statements is conveyed by these mantras. For example—

मनो अस्या अन आसीद्भौरासीदुत च्छदिः । शुक्रावनड्वाहावास्तां यदयात्सूर्या गृहं ॥ ऋक्सामाभ्यामभिहितौ गानौ ते सामनावितः । श्रोत्रं ते चक्रे आस्तां दिवि पंथाश्चराचरः ॥ (*mano asyā ana āsīdbhaurāsīduta cchadiḥ | śukrāvanaḍvāhāvāstāṃ yadayātsūryā gṛhaṃ ‖ ṛksāmābhyāmabhihitau gānau te sāmanāvitaḥ | śrotraṃ te cakre āstāṃ divi paṃthāścarācaraḥ ‖*) (Pu. Saṃ, 10.85.10,11) **NOTE** **GLOSS**

In Ṛks such as these there is not merely a description of Sūryā's purely material body; there is a description that gives the meaning that Sūryā is a power that reflects the principle of the universe. According to this description, the mind is her chariot; the atmosphere is the covering above; the two luminous orbs shining in the atmosphere are her draught animals. Those draught animals, yoked by the Ṛk and by the Sāman, carried Sūryā. Those chariot wheels are her ears. The path on which she travelled was in the atmosphere. It is said that when the Aśvins came to choose Sūryā, adorned with such wedding accessories, all the gods approved.

Further, from some other descriptions it is understood that Sūryā is stated to be identical with Vāk, the word-Brahman in essence. Explaining this very point in the Bṛhaddevatā,

यदा तु वाग्भवत्येषा सूर्यामुं लोकमाश्रिता । तथा सूक्तमुषा भूत्वा सूर्या च भजतेऽखिलं ॥ (*yadā tu vāgbhavatyeṣā sūryāmuṃ lokamāśritā | tathā sūktamuṣā bhūtvā sūryā ca bhajate 'khilaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-79) **GLOSS**

सूर्यामेव सतीमेतां गौरीं वाचं सरस्वतीं पश्यामो वैश्वदेवेषु निपातेनैव केवलाः ॥ (*sūryāmeva satīmetāṃ gaurīṃ vācaṃ sarasvatīṃ paśyāmo vaiśvadeveṣu nipātenaiva kevalāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De- 2-80) **GLOSS**

by these verses it is described that Vāk, which is of the nature of the word-Brahman, abides in the atmosphere in the form of Sūryā. This very one is Sūryā, this very one is the goddess Uṣas, Gaurī and Sarasvatī. The greatness of this Vāk has been explained in detail earlier, in the Special Topics of the Ṛk 1-164-41. Because identity with Vāk has been stated in this way, the conjugal relation between Sūryā and the Gandharvas also becomes intelligible. How Sūryā came to be obtained by the Gandharva who had received Soma is described in the last Ṛks of the Sūryā-sūkta in this manner.

### Printed p. 347

तुभ्यमग्रे परवहन्सूर्यां वहतुना सह । पुनः पतिभ्यो जायां दा अग्ने प्रजया सह ॥ पुनः पत्निमग्निरदादायुषा सह वर्चसा । दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जिवाति शरदः शतं ॥ सोमः प्रथमो विविदे गंधर्वो विविद उत्तरः । तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ॥ सोमोऽददद्दंधर्वाय गंधर्वोऽदददग्नये । रयिं च पुत्रांश्चादाग्निर्मह्यमथो इमां ॥ (*tubhyamagre paravahansūryāṃ vahatunā saha | punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agne prajayā saha ‖ punaḥ patnimagniradādāyuṣā saha varcasā | dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjivāti śaradaḥ śataṃ ‖ somaḥ prathamo vivide gaṃdharvo vivida uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo agniṣṭe patisturīyaste manuṣyajāḥ ‖ somo 'dadaddaṃdharvāya gaṃdharvo 'dadadagnaye | rayiṃ ca putrāṃścādāgnirmahyamatho imāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85.38 to 41)

In these Ṛks it is stated that Sūryā was first given to Agni, and afterwards passed from Agni to Soma, from Soma to the Gandharva, and from the Gandharva again to Agni. The relation between this Gandharva and Soma is stated elsewhere. The story of Soma having handed over the goddess of speech to the Gandharva is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in this manner.

सोमो वै राजा गंधर्वेष्वासीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति सा वागब्रवीत् स्त्रीकामा वै गंधर्वा मयैव स्त्रिया भूतया पणध्वमिति नेति देवा अब्रुवन्कथं वयं त्वदृते स्यामेति साब्रवीत्क्रीणीतैव यर्हि वाव वो मयार्थो भविता तर्ह्येव वोऽहं पुनरागंतास्मीति तथेति तया महानग्न्याभूतया सोमुं राजानमक्रीणन् ॥ (*somo vai rājā gaṃdharveṣvāsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti sā vāgabravīt strīkāmā vai gaṃdharvā mayaiva striyā bhūtayā paṇadhvamiti neti devā abruvankathaṃ vayaṃ tvadṛte syāmeti sābravītkrīṇītaiva yarhi vāva vo mayārtho bhavitā tarhyeva vo 'haṃ punarāgaṃtāsmīti tatheti tayā mahānagnyābhūtayā somuṃ rājānamakrīṇan ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2)

King Soma was among the Gandharvas. The gods and the seers were also thinking how they might obtain him. Then the goddess of speech, knowing the Gandharvas' infatuation with women, said that she would become a beautiful woman and that, by offering her to the Gandharvas, Soma could be obtained. Then the gods did not wish to remain without her. Then, when she gave the assurance that she would rejoin them whenever she was desired again, they changed her into a naked woman, handed her over to the Gandharvas, and obtained Soma. Such is the story. What is this world of the Gandharvas? What is the meaning of Sūryā, in the form of Vāk, having joined this world? This also is explained in the sūkta 10-85. The scholar Eggeling has stated this relation of Sūryā and the Gandharvas in this manner—

The Rigvedic Gandharva was primarily wedded to the hypercosmic Sūryā—original immortal abode of Soma—and the wedding of king Soma

### Printed p. 348

who was derived from the Gandharva to Sūryā—in other words, the return of the moon to the hypercosmic sphere of the nocturnal Sun—is the happy ending of the Gandharva's drama so tragically started. Soma's dying is not a death, for he is actually re-born through his union with Sūryā.

In this manner the relation of Sūryā has been stated: as wife of Soma, as wife of the Gandharva, and, as explained above, at times as wife of Sūrya. It is said that the Aśvins themselves are the sun and the moon. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-184-3, by सूर‍्यां वहतुं (*sūryāṃ vahatuṃ*) the matter of the Aśvins seating Sūryā in their three-wheeled chariot is stated.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्तमेऽनुवाके षट् सूक्तानि । तत्र सत्येनेति सप्तचत्वारिंशदृचं प्रथमं
> सूक्तं सवितृसुतायाः सूर्याया आर्षं । नवोनव इति तिस्रोऽनृक्षरा इति द्वे
> गृभ्नामीति द्वे यदश्विना पृच्छमानावित्येषा पूषा त्वेतो नयत्तित्येकाघोरचक्षुरिति चैवमेता दशर्चस्त्रिष्टुभः । तृष्टमेतदित्येषोरोबृहत्यष्टकद्वादशद्वृष्टकवती।
> पूर्वापरं चरत इह प्रियं प्रजया नः प्रजां जनयत्वित्येतास्ति सो जगत्यः ।
> शिष्टास्त्रयस्त्रिंशदनुष्टुभः । आदितः पंचानामृचां सोमो देवता । तत एकादशभिः सूर्या स्वविवाहं स्तुतवती । अतस्तत्र योऽर्थः प्रतिपाद्यते स एव देवतात्वेन
> विज्ञेयः। या तेनोच्यते सा देवतीति न्यायात् । सप्तदश्या देवा देवता। अप्पादश्याः सोमार्कौ । एकोनविंशाश्चंद्रमाः । सुकिंशुकमित्याद्या नवर्चो विवाहमंत्रा आशिषः प्रतिपादकाः । अतस्तत्र तत्र प्रतिपाद्योऽर्थो देवता । परा देह्यश्रीरा तनूरिति द्वे वध्वा विवाहकाले परिहितस्य वाससः संस्पर्शनिंदयित्र्यौ । ये
> वध्वश्चंद्रमिति दंपत्योः क्षयरोगस्य नाशिनी । अतस्तद्देवताका । परिशिष्टानां
> षोडशानां सूर्या देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सत्येन सप्तचत्वारिंशत् सर्वमनुक्रांतं ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the seventh anuvāka there are six sūktas. Of these, the first, सत्येनेति (*satyeneti*), of forty-seven Ṛks, is the seer-hymn of Sūryā, the daughter of Savitṛ. Of its Ṛks, three beginning नवोनव (*navonava*), two beginning अनृक्षरा (*anṛkṣarā*), two beginning गृभ्नामीति (*gṛbhnāmīti*), one यदश्विना (*yadaśvinā*), one पूषा (*pūṣā*) and one more, ten in all, are Triṣṭubh. One Ṛk is Urobṛhatī, with eight, twelve, eight and eight syllables. Three Ṛks, whose openings he gives, are Jagatī, and the remaining thirty-three are Anuṣṭubh. For the first five Ṛks Soma is the deity. In the next eleven Sūryā praises her own marriage; by the principle that the deity is that very subject which is set forth in the Ṛk, the subject set forth there is the deity. The seventeenth has the gods as deity, the eighteenth Soma and Arka, the nineteenth the moon. The nine Ṛks beginning सुकिंशुकमित्याद्या (*sukiṃśukamityādyā*) are marriage mantras that convey blessings, so the matter set forth in each place is the deity. Two Ṛks censure the touching of the garment worn by the bride at the time of marriage. One Ṛk, beginning with ये (*ye*), destroys consumption in the couple, so that is its deity. For the remaining sixteen Ṛks Sūryā is the deity. So the Anukramaṇī also records: forty-seven Ṛks from सत्येन (*satyena*) onwards, everything recorded. The ritual use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika. **NOTE**

The Anuvāda: In the seventh anuvāka of the tenth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā there are six sūktas. Among them, सत्येनोत्तभिता भूमिः (*satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ*) is the first sūkta; it has forty-seven Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the woman named Sūryā, the daughter of Savitṛ. Among the Ṛks of this sūkta, the three Ṛks beginning नवोनवः (*navonavaḥ*) (19-21), the two Ṛks beginning अनृक्षरा (*anṛkṣarā*) (23-24), the two Ṛks beginning गृभ्णामि ते (*gṛbhṇāmi te*) (36-37), the one Ṛk यदश्विना (*yadaśvinā*) (14), the one Ṛk पूषा त्वेतो नयतु (*pūṣā tveto nayatu*) (26), and the one Ṛk आघोर चक्षुः (*āghora cakṣuḥ*) (44), ten Ṛks in all, are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the Ṛk तृष्णमे (*tṛṣṇame*)

### Printed p. 349

तत् (*tat*) (34) is of the metre called Urobṛhatī. In this metre there are four pādas: the first pāda has eight syllables, the second twelve syllables, and the third and fourth eight syllables each. The three Ṛks पूर्वापरं चरतः (*pūrvāparaṃ carataḥ*) (18), इह प्रियं प्रजया (*iha priyaṃ prajayā*) (27) and आ नः प्रजां जनयतु (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu*) (43) are in the Jagatī metre; the remaining thirty-three Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In this sūkta, Soma is the deity of the first five Ṛks. In the following 11 Ṛks (6-16), Sūryā has included the matter of her own marriage. By the rule that the subject expounded in the Ṛks is the deity of those Ṛks, the mention of Sūryā's marriage is the deity of those 11 Ṛks; for the seventeenth Ṛk the gods are the deity; for the eighteenth Ṛk Soma and Arka are the deity; for the nineteenth Ṛk the moon is the deity. Since in the nine Ṛks beginning सुकिंशुकं (*sukiṃśukaṃ*) (20-28) the blessings used in marriage mantras are stated, the blessings themselves are the deity of these Ṛks. Since in the two Ṛks परा देहि (*parā dehi*) and अश्रीरा तनूः (*aśrīrā tanūḥ*) (29-30) the censure of touching the bride's garment at the time of marriage is stated, that same is the deity of these Ṛks. Since in the Ṛk ये वध्वश्चंद्रं (*ye vadhvaścaṃdraṃ*) (31) the destruction of consumption in the couple is stated, that same is the deity of that Ṛk. For the remaining sixteen Ṛks (32-47) the goddess Sūryā herself is the deity. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated: सत्येन (*satyena*) forty-seven. The ritual use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒त्येनोत्त॑भिता॒ भूमिः॒ सूर्ये॒णोत्त॑भिता॒ द्यौः ।  
> ऋ॒तेना॑दि॒त्यास्ति॑ष्ठंति दि॒वि सोमो॒ अधि॑ श्रि॒त ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 350

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सत्येन । उत्तभिता । भूमिः । सूर्येण । उत्तभिता । द्यौः ।  
> ऋतेन । आदित्याः । तिष्ठंति । दिवि । सोमः । अधि । श्रितः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्येन ब्रह्मणानंतात्मना । ब्रह्मा खलु देवानां मध्यॆ सत्यभूतः । तेनाधः
> स्थितेन भूमिरुत्तभिता । उपरि स्तंभिता । यथाधो न पतेत्तथा कृता । यद्वा ।
> सत्येनानृतप्रतियोगिना धर्मेण भूमिरुत्तभितोद्धृता फलिता भवतीत्यर्थः । असति
> सत्ये भूम्यां सस्यादयो न फलंति । तथा सूर्येण देवेन द्यौरुत्तभिता ।
> सूर्यो हि द्युस्थानत्वाद्दिवं दधार । ऋतेन यज्ञेनादित्या अदितेः पुत्रा देवास्तिष्ठंति । यज्ञेन यजमानदत्तेन खल्वाहुत्या देवा उपजीवंति । दिवि द्युलोके
> सोमो देवानामाप्यायनकारी वल्लिरूपो देवतारूपश्चाधि श्रितः । अधितिष्ठति ।
> इति स्वपतिं सोमं सूर्या स्तोति॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By सत्येन (*satyena*) is meant Brahman, whose self is infinite; among the gods Brahman is the truly real one. Standing below, by him the earth is upheld above: it is so made that it does not fall downward. Or else, by truth, the opposite of untruth, that is, by dharma, the earth is upheld and made fruitful; when there is no truth, crops and the like do not bear fruit on the earth. Likewise by the god Sūrya heaven is upheld, for Sūrya, standing in the region of heaven, supports heaven. By ऋतेन (*ṛtena*), that is by sacrifice, the Ādityas, the gods who are sons of Aditi, subsist: the gods live on the oblation that the sacrificer gives in the sacrifice. In heaven, in the world of heaven, Soma, who nourishes the gods and is both of the form of a creeper and of the form of a deity, is established. Thus Sūryā praises Soma, her husband.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- भूमिः (*bhūmiḥ*)—the earth
- सत्येन (*satyena*)—by truth, which is of the form of Brahman
- उत्तभिता (*uttabhitā*)—has been lifted up and held
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the world of heaven
- सूर्यण (*sūryaṇa*)—by the sun
- उत्तभिता (*uttabhitā*)—is held
- आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*)—the gods, the sons of Aditi
- ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)—depending on the sacrifice
- तिष्ठंति (*tiṣṭhaṃti*)—subsist
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- अधिश्रितः (*adhiśritaḥ*)—has obtained a support

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The earth is lifted up and held by truth, which is of the form of Brahman. The world of heaven is held by the sun. The gods, the sons of Aditi, subsist depending on the sacrifice. In the world of heaven Soma has obtained a support.

##### English translation
Earth is upheld by truth ; heaven is upheld by the sun ; the Adityas are supportcd by sacrifice, Soma is supreme in heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सत्येन भूमिः उत्तभिता (*satyena bhūmiḥ uttabhitā*)—सत्येन ब्रह्मणानंतात्मना । ब्रह्मा खलु देवानां मध्यॆ सत्यभूतः ॥ तेनाधः स्थितेन भूमिः उपरि स्तंभिता । यथाधो न पतेत्तथा (*satyena brahmaṇānaṃtātmanā | brahmā khalu devānāṃ madhyè satyabhūtaḥ ‖ tenādhaḥ sthitena bhūmiḥ upari staṃbhitā | yathādho na patettathā*)

### Printed p. 351

कृता (*kṛtā*). Here the commentator has explained the word सत्य (*satya*) as Brahman. For among the gods it is Brahman who is truly real. His world is called Satyaloka. The earth, which was below, was lifted upward by such a Brahman, who is of infinite self and truly real, and was made to stand so that it does not shake and is firm. Or else another meaning can be given to this sentence. If the word सत्य (*satya*) is explained as dharma—सत्येन अनृतप्रतियोगिना धर्मेण भूमिरुद्धता फलिता भवतीत्यर्थः । असति सत्ये भूम्यां सस्यादयो न फलंति । (*satyena anṛtapratiyoginā dharmeṇa bhūmiruddhatā phalitā bhavatītyarthaḥ | asati satye bhūmyāṃ sasyādayo na phalaṃti |*). That is, this earth stands by truth or by dharma: all the dealings that go on upon the earth go on only in dependence on dharma. If there were no truth or dharma, crops and the like would not grow on the earth. Therefore everything rests on dharma alone. This matter is also supported by this statement of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad—

सत्येन वायुरावाति सत्येनादित्यो रोचते दिवि सत्यं वाचः प्रतिष्ठा सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितं तस्मात्सत्यं परमं वदंति ॥ (*satyena vāyurāvāti satyenādityo rocate divi satyaṃ vācaḥ pratiṣṭhā satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmātsatyaṃ paramaṃ vadaṃti ‖*) (Tai. U. 4-80) **GLOSS**

सूर्येण द्यौः उत्तभिता (*sūryeṇa dyauḥ uttabhitā*)—सूर्यो हि द्युस्थानत्वाद्दिवं दाधार (*sūryo hi dyusthānatvāddivaṃ dādhāra*). Because the sun shines in heaven (in the atmosphere), the idea is that he supports and nourishes heaven and the atmosphere by his greatness.

ऋतेनादित्यास्तिष्ठंति (*ṛtenādityāstiṣṭhaṃti*)—अदितेः पुत्रा देवा यज्ञेन तिष्ठंति । यज्ञे यजमानदत्तेन खल्वाहुत्या देवा उपजीवंति । (*aditeḥ putrā devā yajñena tiṣṭhaṃti | yajñe yajamānadattena khalvāhutyā devā upajīvaṃti |*). Here the word आदित्या (*ādityā*) is explained as अदितिपुत्राः इंद्रादयो देवाः (*aditiputrāḥ iṃdrādayo devāḥ*), the gods beginning with Indra, the sons of the goddess Aditi. It is said that the gods in heaven live by the oblations that human sacrificers on earth offer in sacrifice, addressed to the gods. The god Agni carries the oblations offered into the fire, addressed to the gods, to the gods in heaven. It is through Agni alone that the gods receive the oblations. For that very reason it is the custom to call the gods अग्निजिह्वा (*agnijihvā*).

दिवि सोमो अधि श्रितः (*divi somo adhi śritaḥ*)—दिवि (*divi*) means that Soma is established in the world of heaven. Although the Soma used in sacrifices and the like grows on the earth and on the mountains, it is well known from śruti statements such as तृतीयस्कामितो दिवि सोम आसीत् (*tṛtīyaskāmito divi soma āsīt*) (Tai. Brā. 3-2-1-1) that formerly it was in heaven itself, and that Gāyatrī, flying off in the form of a hawk, brought it to the earth. We have explained this matter in detail in the earlier parts. With regard to Soma it can be conceived in two ways, as a creeper and as a presiding deity. We have said that earlier. Yāska has given the explanation of the word सोम (*soma*) in this manner—

### Printed p. 352

ओषधिस्सोमः सुनोतेर्यदेनमभिषुण्वंति (*oṣadhissomaḥ sunoteryadenamabhiṣuṇvaṃti*)—a herb that is well known by the name Soma; this—

आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सना अयुतं च साकं । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥ (*ādāya śyeno abharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ sanā ayutaṃ ca sākaṃ | atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-7)

he has explained the greatness of Soma by saying that the Gāyatrī metre, taking the form of a hawk, brought it from heaven to the earth, and that, in the contexts in which Indra drinks this Soma, sacrificers, having performed sacrifices with a thousand pressings, gave a sacrificial fee numbering ten thousand. And: बहुलमस्य नैघंटुकं वृत्तं आश्चर्यमिव प्राधान्येन (*bahulamasya naighaṃṭukaṃ vṛttaṃ āścaryamiva prādhānyena*)—the praise of this Soma too indicates its importance, and it is wonderful. This has been recited in the ninth maṇḍala. And the greatness of this Soma is stated in the form of praise in this Ṛk—

स्वादिष्टया मदिष्टया पवस्व सोम धारया । इंद्राय पातने सुतः । (*svādiṣṭayā madiṣṭayā pavasva soma dhārayā | iṃdrāya pātane sutaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-1-1) **GLOSS**

सोमं मन्यते पपिवान् यत्संपिषंत्योषधिं । सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुर्न तस्याश्नाति कश्चन ॥ (*somaṃ manyate papivān yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyoṣadhiṃ | somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo vidurna tasyāśnāti kaścana ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-3)

The word सोम (*soma*) is understood to mean the moon. In this Ṛk both the Soma creeper and the moon are praised. But the superiority of this Soma over the well-known moon has been described by Yāska in this manner.

सोमं मन्यते पपिवान् यत्संपिषंत्योषधिमिति वृथासुतमसोममाह सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुरिति न तस्याश्नाति कश्चनायज्वेत्यधियज्ञं । अथाधिदैवतं सोमं मन्यते पपिवान् यत्संपिषंत्योषधिमिति यजुस्सुतमसोममाह सोमं यं ब्रह्माणो विदुश्चंद्रमसं न तस्याश्नाति कश्चनादेव इति । (*somaṃ manyate papivān yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyoṣadhimiti vṛthāsutamasomamāha somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo viduriti na tasyāśnāti kaścanāyajvetyadhiyajñaṃ | athādhidaivataṃ somaṃ manyate papivān yatsaṃpiṣaṃtyoṣadhimiti yajussutamasomamāha somaṃ yaṃ brahmāṇo viduścaṃdramasaṃ na tasyāśnāti kaścanādeva iti |*) (Ni. 11-4)

Although those who make rasāyanas and the like bring Soma, press out the juice and drink it, they do not become renowned in the sacrifice as Soma-drinkers; therefore, because Soma is used as a part of the sacrifice, it is praised as producing the renown of being a Soma-drinker, in the prescribed manner, only for sacrificers. In the adhidaivata view also, (in explaining the word सोम (*soma*) as the moon)

### Printed p. 353

the Soma that is a part of the sacrifice is denoted by the word सोम (*soma*). By the śruti statement “सोमो नूनमेष यद्देवानामन्नं (*somo nūnameṣa yaddevānāmannaṃ*)”, although the moon is denoted by the word सोम (*soma*), he is food only for the gods. Therefore, although by the mantra सोमं मन्यते (*somaṃ manyate*) two kinds of meaning, adhiyajña and adhidaiva, are given for the word सोम (*soma*), the ritualists have assigned the principal place in the sacrifice to the Soma that is of the form of a herb.

यत्त्वा देव प्रपिबंति तत आ प्यायसे पुनः । वायुस्सोमस्य रक्षिता समानां मास आकृतिः ॥ (*yattvā deva prapibaṃti tata ā pyāyase punaḥ | vāyussomasya rakṣitā samānāṃ māsa ākṛtiḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-5)

यत्वा देव प्रपिबंति तत आप्यायसे पुनरिति नाराशंसानभिप्रेत्य पूर्वपक्षापरपक्षाविति वा वायुसोमस्य रक्षिता वायुमस्य रक्षितारमाह साहचर्यात् रसहरणाद्वा! समानां संवत्सराणां मास आकृतिः सोमो रूपविशेषैरोषधिश्चंद्रमा ना । (*yatvā deva prapibaṃti tata āpyāyase punariti nārāśaṃsānabhipretya pūrvapakṣāparapakṣāviti vā vāyusomasya rakṣitā vāyumasya rakṣitāramāha sāhacaryāt rasaharaṇādvā! samānāṃ saṃvatsarāṇāṃ māsa ākṛtiḥ somo rūpaviśeṣairoṣadhiścaṃdramā nā |*) **NOTE**

In the sense relating to the sacrifice (adhiyajña), Soma is drunk in the three libations by the officiating priests beginning with the sacrificer; by this, this Soma becomes the one who nourishes. Although Vāyu sucks the juice of the herbs, he does not suck the Soma juice, and so he is its protector. The rasāyana-makers who know Āyurveda say that this Soma undergoes increase of its leaves in accordance with the tithis of the bright fortnight of each month, and decrease of its leaves (apacita) in accordance with the tithis of the dark fortnight. In the adhidaivata view, the moon, who is denoted by the word सोम (*soma*), nourishes the gods by his phases in accordance with the respective tithis. The gods also drink the phases of the moon. The moon undergoes increase and decrease in the respective fortnights through his phases. Thus, in both ways, adhiyajña and adhidaivata, the similarity of the moon (his equal state) to the Soma creeper has been stated, identity with Soma has been established, and the Soma creeper has been praised as abundant and a great flood.

Now one has to examine what Soma is. Soma is a particular kind of creeper. This Soma creeper is not now found anywhere in the country of India. It grows especially on plains, on river banks and on hills. The higher it grows, the more juice it gives. It grows even at a height of about 7000 feet. Therefore there are descriptions in many places in the Ṛgveda of Soma being brought from the mountains (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-6 ; 3-48-2 ; 5-43-4 etc.). The mountain called Maujavata is famous for the Soma creeper. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10 34-1; Nā. Saṃ. 3-61-1 ; Ni. 9-8 etc.) **NOTE** It is said here and there in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-29, 8-64-11, 9-65-22 etc.) that the Soma creeper is found on the shores of the lake called Śaryaṇāvat.

### Printed p. 354

And it is said that Soma is found also in the place called Arjīka (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-29, 8-64-11 etc.), in the country called Pastā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-65-3), in the place where the five peoples, the Pañcajanas, live (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9.65-23, 9-92-3 etc.), and in the regions around the river called Suṣomā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8.7-29, 8-64-11 etc.). Of the last, Suṣomā means su + soma = a place where good Soma is obtained; so this region may have received the name Suṣoma. Therefore it is understood that in the time of the Ṛgveda the Soma creeper grew abundantly on the plains and river banks of what is now the Punjab. Because the creeper that grows on the plains did not yield as much juice as the creeper that grows on the hills, they used to soak the creeper of the plains thoroughly in water and use it. (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-63-4, 9-74-9 etc.).

The stem of this creeper grows to a height of about 4 feet. Its stem is round and soft, of a reddish colour mixed with white, and about the thickness of a finger. The leaves are very few, white and small. Generally the leaves fall off. At the tip of the plant there is a cluster (like that of millet) with a few seeds. Its juice is whitish mixed with green. Though slightly sweet in taste, it turns sour if kept for a few days. When it grows near a big tree, it spreads and grows around the tree like a creeper. There are joints here and there. It can be broken easily.

Here we shall briefly describe the procedure to be followed when preparing the Soma juice—

The Soma creeper that grew on river banks and on the mountains was brought with great effort, or bought from those who brought it, and used in sacrifices. Even now the rite called सोमविक्रयण (*somavikrayaṇa*) is performed in sacrifices. After the Soma creeper has been brought, it is crushed with stones (ग्राव (*grāva*), अद्रि (*adri*)), pressed, strained through cloth, mixed as the occasion requires with curds, milk and flour, offered to the gods, and then drunk by the sacrificer and the priests. This preparation of the Soma juice takes place on the principal days of a sacrifice in the morning, at midday and in the evening. It is called अभिषवण (*abhiṣavaṇa*) or सवन (*savana*) (pressing out the juice). The pressing done in the evening is called the third pressing.

The Soma creeper (the vines) is brown, ruddy (dull red), or of a red colour mixed with yellow. Because it has been said that the creeper that has grown very high on the mountains is excellent and that more juice can be extracted from it, they used to bring the Soma creeper from the mountains themselves wherever possible. Among such mountains the mountain called Mūjavata was famous. **NOTE** The tip of this Soma creeper

### Printed p. 355

is called by the name अंग (*aṃga*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168.3 ; 3.48.2 ; etc.), the tip with shoots is called वक्षणा (*vakṣaṇā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-1-17) and वाण (*vāṇa*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4.28-9 ; 9.50-1), the Soma juice is called अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-28-7 ; 3-48-1 ; 4.16-1), and the stalk (vine) of the Soma creeper is called पर्वन् (*parvan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-9-1). **NOTE**

**The method of preparing the Soma juice**

They remove the leaves from the Soma creeper or vine, put it in a mortar and crush it with a stone. If the creeper is not fresh, they soak it in water for a day or two, and when it has become soft they extract the juice. The mortar in which the Soma creeper is crushed is called उलूखल (*ulūkhala*). It is generally made of stone; it is also sometimes made of wood. The stone that is put into the mortar and pounded from above has the names ग्रावा (*grāvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-83-6 ; 1-135-7) and अद्रि (*adri*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-130-2 ; 1-135-5 ; 1-137-1). It may be supposed that the उलूखल (*ulūkhala*) was a stone with only a slight hollow in the middle, like the mortar we use now. This mortar called उलूखल (*ulūkhala*) was used for pounding grain with a pestle (मुसल (*musala*)).

The method of crushing the Soma creeper and preparing the Soma juice is nowhere described in detail in the Ṛgveda. The method can be inferred from some sentences stated here and there. The stones that crush the Soma creepers have the names ग्राव (*grāva*) and अद्रि (*adri*). In some contexts wooden boards, well known by the name अधिषवण फलक (*adhiṣavaṇa phalaka*), are also used. If the creeper is fresh, the juice comes out in plenty. If not, that is, if some days have passed since it was cut and brought, they soak it in water and afterwards place it on a skin. Then they crush it with stones and extract the juice. Because the juice extracted in this way has bits of the creeper's bark, fragments and the like mixed in it, they strain that juice either through the gaps between the fingers of the hands, or through a strainer or cloth called पवित्र (*pavitra*), or through sheep's wool. The juice strained in this way is clear, without impurities. It has the names शुक्र (*śukra*) and शुचि (*śuci*). In appearance this juice is dull red or of a red colour mixed with yellow. It is the custom to offer to Indra and to Vāyu pure Soma juice, that is, juice not mixed with आशिर (*āśira*) substances. For the other gods they sometimes use it mixed with milk, curds and grain flour. The Soma juice mixed with these has respectively the names गवाशिर (*gavāśira*), दध्याशिर (*dadhyāśira*) and यवाशिर (*yavāśira*).
