> यात् । अश्विना । पृच्छमानौ । आयातं । त्रिचक्रेण। वहतुं । सूर्यायाः ।  
> विश्वे । देवाः । अनु । तत् । वां । अजानन् । पुत्रः । पितरा । अवृणीत । पूषा ॥१४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनाश्विन् यद्यदा पृच्छमानौ सवितारं प्रष्टुमयातं अगच्छतं। केन
> साधनेनायातं तदुच्यते । त्रिचक्रेण चक्रत्रययुक्तेन रथेन । किं पृच्छमानौ ।
> सूर्याया वहतुं । विवाहमित्यर्थः । तत्तदानीं नां युवां सवितारं प्रति
> गच्छंतौ विश्वे सर्वे देवा अन्वजानन् । अनुज्ञातवंतः । तथा पितरौ पुत्रोऽश्विनोः
> पुत्रः पूषावृणीत । वृतवान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, when you went to ask Savitṛ, by what means did you go? That is stated: with a three-wheeled chariot, that is, a chariot having three wheels. What were you going to ask? Sūryā's vahatu, which means the marriage. Then, as you two went to Savitṛ, all the gods gave their assent **NOTE**. And Pūṣan, the Aśvins' son, chose them as parents.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvin deities
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सूर्यायाः (*sūryāyāḥ*)—Sūryā's
- वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)—the question of the marriage
- पृच्छमानौ (*pṛcchamānau*)—for the sake of asking
- त्रिचक्रेण (*tricakreṇa*)—with three wheels

### Printed p. 388

in a chariot that has them.

- अयातं (*ayātaṃ*)—you went
- तत् (*tat*)—then
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your wish
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the deities
- अन्वजानन् (*anvajānan*)—approved
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—your son
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- पितरौ (*pitarau*)—as parents
- अवृणीत (*avṛṇīta*)—chose you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, when you went in the chariot with three wheels to ask for the marriage of Sūryā, then all the deities approved your wish. Your son, the god Pūṣan, chose you as his parents.

##### English translation
W e n, Aswins, you came in your three-wheeled car soliciting the marriage of Surya, then all the gods assented, and Pushan (your) son chose (you as) his parents.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk also there is a description of the chariot of the Aśvin deities. The import of epithets such as त्रिचक्रः (*tricakraḥ*), त्रिवंधुरः (*trivaṃdhuraḥ*) and मनसः जवीयन् (*manasaḥ javīyan*) has been explained earlier. Here it must be examined in what way the epithets त्रिचक्रः (*tricakraḥ*) and त्रिवंधुरः (*trivaṃdhuraḥ*) show the all-pervading nature of the Aśvin deities. Just as the pervasiveness of Viṣṇu is known from sentences such as त्रिषु विक्रमणेषु (*triṣu vikramaṇeṣu*), and the all-pervading nature of Agni from sentences such as त्रीणि जाना परिभूषंति (*trīṇi jānā paribhūṣaṃti*), so the nature of the Aśvin deities is known from epithets such as त्रिचक्रः (*tricakraḥ*). It is noteworthy that the descriptions of Agni, Viṣṇu, Savitṛ and the Aśvin deities all set out one and the same principle, and in all contexts set out a feature common to all these deities. The English scholar Hopkins, explaining this point, has stated as follows:

A comparison with the abodes of other Vedic Deities who are said to traverse the whole Universe like Vishnu conforms the same view. One of these deities is सवितृ (*savitṛ*). The second deity that traverses or measures the Universc is अग्नि (*agni*). He has three stations. His light is spoken of as three-fold. Although these three stations do not seem to be always conceived alike, yet, one of them at any rate can be clearly identified with the third step of Vishnu. Agni sometimes represents the Sun in the Rig-Veda and Vishnu is also the same
### Printed p. 389

Sun under a different name and the third or the hidden abode of Agni can therefore, be easily recognised as identical in character. The third Deity that traverses the Universe is the Aswins to whom the epithet परिज्मन् (*parijman*) is applied several times in the Rig-Veda. The Aswins are said to have three stations and their chariot which is to go over both the worlds alike has three wheels one of which is represented as deposited in a cave or a secret place like the third step of Vishnu which is beyond the ken of mortals. This coincidence between the third stations of three different world traversing Gods cannot be treated as accidental. (J. A. O. S. Vol. 15. p. CXLIX to CL.)

Two points are clearly understood from the above sentences. First: 1. The three worlds, the earth, the heaven and the atmosphere, are the abodes of Agni, Viṣṇu and the Aśvin deities. Second: 2. All these three deities have three steps, and the third step of every one of these deities spans a world that lies beyond the reach of man. Both these points are noteworthy. If only some of the sentences that describe the first point are examined:

प्र तद्विष्णुः स्तवते वीर्येण मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्टाः । यस्कोरुषु त्रिषु विक्रमणेष्वधिक्षियंति भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ (*pra tadviṣṇuḥ stavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭāḥ | yaskoruṣu triṣu vikramaṇeṣvadhikṣiyaṃti bhuvanāni viśvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-2)

यस्य त्री पूर्णा मधुना पदान्मक्षीयमाणा स्वधया मदंति । य उ त्रिधातु पृथिवीमुत द्यामेको दाधार भुवनानि विश्वा ॥ (*yasya trī pūrṇā madhunā padānmakṣīyamāṇā svadhayā madaṃti | ya u tridhātu pṛthivīmuta dyāmeko dādhāra bhuvanāni viśvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-4)

श्रीणि जाना परि भूषंत्यस्य समुद्र एकं दिव्येकमप्पु । पूर्वामनु प्र दिशं पार्थिवानामृतून्प्रशासद्वि दधावनुष्टु ॥ (*śrīṇi jānā pari bhūṣaṃtyasya samudra ekaṃ divyekamappu | pūrvāmanu pra diśaṃ pārthivānāmṛtūnpraśāsadvi dadhāvanuṣṭu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.95.3)

अग्निस्त्रीणि त्रिधातून्या क्षेति विदथा कविः । स त्रेरेकादशा इह यक्षच्च पिप्रयच्चि नो विप्रो दूतः परिष्कृते नभंतामन्यके समे ॥ (*agnistrīṇi tridhātūnyā kṣeti vidathā kaviḥ | sa trerekādaśā iha yakṣacca piprayacci no vipro dūtaḥ pariṣkṛte nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8 39-9)

### Printed p. 390

श्रीणि पदान्यश्विनोराविः सांति गुहा परः । (*śrīṇi padānyaśvinorāviḥ sāṃti guhā paraḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8 la-23) **NOTE**

कवी ऋतस्य पत्मभिरर्वाग्जीवेभ्यस्परि ॥ (*kavī ṛtasya patmabhirarvāgjīvebhyaspari ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8 8-23)

Of these Ṛks, the first two describe the pervasiveness of Viṣṇu. Accordingly, in the casts of Viṣṇu's steps, which are exceedingly wide and three in number, all created beings abide and stand. The three step-casts of Viṣṇu, filled with sweet nectar and imperishable, delight the people who depend on them with the gift of pure food. And the same Viṣṇu is described, in the account of the pervasiveness of his three steps, as holding up all the fourteen worlds, the seven below and the seven above, as though joined with the three elements, earth, water and fire. In the third and fourth Ṛks the nature of Agni is stated. Agni has three birthplaces: one in the sea in the form of the submarine fire, one in the heaven in the form of the Sun, and one in the atmosphere in the form of lightning; and it is described that this same Agni has overspread the three elements, that is, that Agni pervades the three worlds. In the same way, in the fifth Ṛk there is a description of the three steps of the Aśvin deities, and, just as the abodes of Viṣṇu and Agni are described,

इदं हि वां प्रदिवि स्थानमोक इमे गृहा अश्विनेदं दुरोणं । आ नो दिवो बृहतः वर्वतादाद्भ्यो यातमिषमूर्जं वहंता ॥ (*idaṃ hi vāṃ pradivi sthānamoka ime gṛhā aśvinedaṃ duroṇaṃ | ā no divo bṛhataḥ varvatādādbhyo yātamiṣamūrjaṃ vahaṃtā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-76-4)

here too the three worlds, the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven, are described as abodes of the Aśvin deities as well. One more point must also be noticed in these descriptions. In the Ṛk 1-154-4 that describes the steps of Viṣṇu, in the Ṛk 8-39.9 that describes the pervasiveness of Agni, and in the present Ṛk (1-183-1) that describes the passage of the chariot of the Aśvin deities, the word त्रिधातु (*tridhātu*) is a word that indicates the common nature of these three deities. Secondly, the description that the third step (or station) of all of them lies in a secret place beyond reach shows the common nature that belongs to all.

विष्णुरित्था परममस्य विद्वाञ्चातो बृहन्नभि पाति तृतीयं । आसा यदस्य पयो अक्रत स्वं सचेतसो आभ्यर्चंत्यत्र ॥ (*viṣṇuritthā paramamasya vidvāñcāto bṛhannabhi pāti tṛtīyaṃ | āsā yadasya payo akrata svaṃ sacetaso ābhyarcaṃtyatra ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-1-3)

क इमं वो निण्यमा चिकेश वत्सो मात्वर्जनयत स्वधाभिः । (*ka imaṃ vo niṇyamā cikeśa vatso mātvarjanayata svadhābhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-4)

### Printed p. 391

द्वे इदस्य क्रमणे स्वर्दृशोऽभिख्याय मर्त्यो भुरण्यति । तृतीयमस्य नकिरा दधर्षति वयश्चन पतयंतः पतत्रिणः ॥ (*dve idasya kramaṇe svardṛśo 'bhikhyāya martyo bhuraṇyati | tṛtīyamasya nakirā dadharṣati vayaścana patayaṃtaḥ patatriṇaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-155-5)

In these Ṛks and others it is stated that the third station of Agni and the encompassing by the third step of Viṣṇu cannot be known by any man. As it is said, "Man knows, by praising them, only the earth and the atmosphere, the two worlds on which Viṣṇu, who gazes at the heaven, sets his two steps. No man can ever know the world on which this Viṣṇu sets his third step," so also the motion of the three-wheeled chariot of the Aśvin deities, and its movement beyond reach, are stated.

यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप । कैकं चक्रं वामासीत्त्व देष्ट्राय तस्थथुः ॥ द्वे ते चक्रे सूर्ये ब्रह्माण ऋतथा विदुः । अथैकं चक्रं यद्दुहा तदद्धातय इद्दिदुः ॥ (*yadayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryāmupa | kaikaṃ cakraṃ vāmāsīttva deṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ‖ dve te cakre sūrye brahmāṇa ṛtathā viduḥ | athaikaṃ cakraṃ yadduhā tadaddhātaya iddiduḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-85, 16) **NOTE**

Here it is described that of the three wheels of the chariot of the Aśvin deities one is visible to no one and is known only to the seers who have the power of vision. In this way, in the description of their extraordinary nature, a common character of the three deities is shown in two main points. It has been stated all along before that the three deities are also of the nature of the Āditya, the Sun. In the epithets त्रिचक्रः (*tricakraḥ*), त्रिबर्हिः (*tribarhiḥ*), त्रिषधस्थः (*triṣadhasthaḥ*), त्रिवंधुरः (*trivaṃdhuraḥ*), त्रिविक्रमः (*trivikramaḥ*) and so on, a symbolic meaning is indicated. The same matter is stated in the present Ṛk too. And since, as said above, their all-pervading nature is conveyed by the word त्रिचक्र (*tricakra*), the meaning of the word त्रिचक्र (*tricakra*) is to be understood.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदया॑शं शुभस्पती वरे॒यं सू॒र्यमुप॑ ।  
> क्वैकं॑ च॒क्रं ना॑मासी॒त्त्व॑ दे॒ष्टाय॑ तस्थथुः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । अयातं । शुभः । पती इति । वरेऽयं । सूर्यां । उप ।  
> क्व । एकं । चक्रं । नां । आसीत् । क्व । देष्ट्राय । तस्थथुः ॥ १५ ॥

### Printed p. 392

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शुभस्पती उदकस्य स्वामिनौ यद्यावयातं अगच्छतं । कं प्रति । वरेयं
> वरणीयायाः सूर्यायाः संबंधिनं वरैर्या९चितव्यं वा । सवितारमित्यर्थः ।
> किमर्थ० । सूर्यामुप गंतुं । वां भवतोः संप्रति दृश्यमानविदमेकं चक्रं
> क्वासीत्पुरा । क्व वां युवां देष्ट्राय दानाय प्रवृत्तौ तस्थथुरित्यश्विन् नोर्निवासं
> पृच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śubhaspatī, lords of water, when you went, to whom did you go? To the one to be chosen, that is, to the one who is the relative of Sūryā, the desirable bride, and who is to be approached by suitors with requests: that is, to Savitṛ. For what purpose? To go to Sūryā. Where was this one wheel of yours, which is seen now, formerly? And where did you two stand, engaged in giving, that is, in the gift? Thus the Aśvins' abode is asked.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुभस्पती (*śubhaspatī*)—O Aśvin deities, protectors of water
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सूर्यां उप (*sūryāṃ upa*)—to obtain Sūryā
- वरेयं (*vareyaṃ*)—to Savitṛ, who gives her away
- आयातं (*āyātaṃ*)—you went, then
- वां (*vāṃ*)—of your chariot
- एकं चक्रं (*ekaṃ cakraṃ*)—the one wheel that is seen now
- क्व आसीत् (*kva āsīt*)—where was it
- देष्ट्राय (*deṣṭrāya*)—you who were engaged in giving
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- तस्थथु (*tasthathu*)—were you standing

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, protectors of water, when you went to Savitṛ, who gives away Sūryā, to obtain her, where was the wheel of your chariot that is now seen? Where were you standing, engaged in giving?

##### English translation
When, lords of water, you came to the giver-away (to get) Surya, where was the one wheel of your car, where did you stand to make the gift ?

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्वे ते॑ च॒क्रे सू॑र्ये ब्र॒ह्माण॑ ऋतु॒था वि॑दुः ।  
> अथैकं॑ च॒क्रं यद्गुहा॒ तद॑द्धा॒तय॒ इद्दि॑दुः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अथ । एकं । चक्रं । यत् । गुहा । तत् । अद्धातयः । इत् । विदुः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथ स्वयमेव स्मात्मानं प्रति सूर्या वदति । हे सूर्ये ते तव द्वे चक्रे
> प्रज्ञाते पुरा दृष्टे द्वे एव चंद्रसूर्यात्मके ऋतुधर्तुषु विनिर्दिष्टे चक्रे
> ब्रह्माणो ब्राह्मणा विदुः । अथैकं चक्रं तृतीयं संवत्सरात्मकं गुहा गुहायां
> निहितं यदस्ति तदद्धातय इत् । एतन्मेधाविनामसु पठितं । मेधाविन एव विदुः ।
> ज्ञानंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Sūryā herself speaks, addressing herself **NOTE**. O Sūryā, your two wheels, known and seen before, being only two, of the nature of the moon and the sun, specified with regard to the seasons, the Brāhmaṇas know. Then the one wheel, the third, of the nature of the year, which lies hidden in a cave: that wheel only the अद्धातयः (*addhātayaḥ*) know. This word is read among the names of the wise; only the wise know it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूर्ये (*sūrye*)—O goddess Sūryā
- ते (*te*)—of your chariot
- द्वे चक्रे (*dve cakre*)—the two wheels
- ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*)—in the respective specified seasons
- ब्रह्माणः (*brahmāṇaḥ*)—the knowers of the mantras
- विदुः (*viduḥ*)—have known
- अथ (*atha*)—and moreover
- यत् एकं चक्रं (*yat ekaṃ cakraṃ*)—the one wheel which
- गुहा (*guhā*)—is secret
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- अद्धातय इत् (*addhātaya it*)—only the wise
- विदुः (*viduḥ*)—know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sūryā, the knowers of the mantras have known the two wheels of your chariot in the respective specified seasons. And the nature of your one wheel, which lies hidden in secret, only the wise know.

##### English translation
Surya, the Brahmans know your two chariot wheels in their season ; the single wheel that is concealed, the sages know it also.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यायै सूर्यस्य पत्नै देवेभ्योऽग्न्यादिभ्यो मित्राय वरुणाय
> च ये च भूतस्य भूशजातस्य प्रचेतसः सुमतयोऽभिमतप्रदा भवंति तेभ्यः
> सर्वेभ्य इदं नमो नमस्कारमकरं । करोमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

To Sūryā, the wife of Sūrya; to the gods, Agni and the others; to Mitra and to Varuṇa; and to all those who are प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*) towards created beings, that is, well-disposed, granters of what is desired: to all of these I offer this homage, that is, I make it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूराय्यै (*sūrāyyai*)—to the wife of Sūrya
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the deities
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—to Mitra
- वरुणाय (*varuṇāya*)—to Varuṇa
- च (*ca*)—and
- ये (*ye*)—those deities who
- भूतस्य (*bhūtasya*)—among all created beings
- प्रचेतसः (*pracetasaḥ*)—are possessed of an excellent mind of favour
- तेभ्यः (*tebhyaḥ*)—to all of them
- इदं नमः (*idaṃ namaḥ*)—this homage
- अकरं (*akaraṃ*)—I offer

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I offer this homage to the goddess Sūryā, to Mitra, Varuṇa and the other deities, and to the other deities who have a mind of favour towards the beings of the world.

##### English translation
I offer this adarotation to Surya, to the gods, to Mitra and Varuna, (and to all those) who are considerate to created beings. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒र्वा॒प॒रं च॑रतो मा॒यय्यै॒त् शिशू॒ क्रीळं॑तौ॒ परि॑ यातो  ॒
> अध्वरं ।  
> विश्वा॑न्य॒न्नो भुव॑नाभि॒चष्ट॑ ऋ॒तूर॒न्नो वि॒दध॑ज्जायते॒ पुनः॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पूर्वऽअपरं । चरतः । मायया । एतौ । शिशू इति । क्रीळंतौ । परि । यातः ।  
> अध्वरं ।  
> विश्वानि । अन्यः । भुवना । अभिचष्टे । ऋतून् । अन्यः । विदधत् । जायते ।  
> पुनरिति ॥ १८ ॥

### Printed p. 395

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कश्चित्तूर्वं गच्छति सूर्यः । अन्यस्तमनुचरति चंद्रमाः । एवं पूर्वापरं
> पूर्वापर्येण मायया स्वप्रज्ञानेनैतावादित्यचंद्रौ चरतः । गच्छतो दिवि ।
> तौ शिशू : शिशुवद्भ्रमणाज्जायमानत्वाद्वा शिशू इत्युच्येते । शिशू संतौ क्रीळंतावंतरिक्षे विहरंतावध्वरु परि यातः । यज्ञं प्रति गच्छतः । तयोरन्य आदित्यो
> विश्वानि भुवनान्यभिचष्टे । अभिपश्यति । ऋतून्वसंतादीनन्यश्चंद्रमा विदधत्कुर्वन्मासानर्धमासांश्च कुर्वन्नर्जायते । यद्युभयोरपि पुनर्जातिरस्ति तथापि
> सूर्यस्य सर्वदा प्रवृद्धेरुदयो नाभिप्रेतः । चंद्रस्य तु ह्रासवृद्धिसद्भावात्पुनः
> पुनर्जायत इत्युक्तियुक्ता । चंद्रमा वै जायते पुनः । तै. ब्रा. ३-९.५-४ ।
> इत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

One goes first, the Sun, and another follows him, the Moon. Thus, in the order of before and after, these two, the Sun and the Moon, move through the sky by māyā, that is, by their own knowledge. They are called children (शिशू (*śiśū*)) either because they move about like children or because they are born again and again. Being children, sporting and wandering in the atmosphere, they go round towards the sacrifice. Of the two, one, the Sun, looks over all the worlds. The other, the Moon, makes the seasons beginning with spring, and also the months and the half-months, and is born. Although both have rebirth, a rising of the Sun by constant growth is not what is meant; but for the Moon, because there is waning and waxing, "born again and again" is fitting. For there is the Vedic text "The moon is born again" (Tai. Brā. 3-9.5-4), and so on. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शिशू (*śiśū*)—who are infants
- एतौ (*etau*)—these Sun and Moon
- पूर्वापर (*pūrvāpara*)—in turn (one after the other)
- मायया (*māyayā*)—endowed with their extraordinary knowledge
- चरतः (*carataḥ*)—move about
- क्रीळंतौ (*krīḷaṃtau*)—roaming in the atmosphere
- अध्वरं परि (*adhvaraṃ pari*)—towards the sacrifice
- यातः (*yātaḥ*)—come
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—one of the two, the Āditya (Sun)
- विश्वानि भुवना (*viśvāni bhuvanā*)—all the worlds
- अभिचष्टे (*abhicaṣṭe*)—looks at
- अन्यः (*anyaḥ*)—the other, the Moon
- ऋतून् (*ṛtūn*)—the seasons beginning with spring
- विदधत् (*vidadhat*)—regulating
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- जायते (*jāyate*)—is born

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These infant Sun and Moon, endowed with their extraordinary knowledge, move about in turn. Roaming in the atmosphere, they come towards the sacrifice. Of them, the Āditya, one of the two, looks at all the worlds. The other, the Moon, regulating the seasons beginning with spring, is born again and again.

##### English translation
These two (the sun and moon) wandering in thought one after the other, youthful, sportive, approach the sacrifice; one (of them) looks over all worlds, the other regulating the seasons is born repeatedly.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नवो॑नवो भवति॒ जाय॑मा॒नोऽह्नां॑ के॒तुरु॒षसा॑मे॒त्यग्रं॑ ।

### Printed p. 396

> भागं देवेभ्यो वि दधात्यायन्प्र चंद्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नवः नवः । भवति । जायमानः । अह्नां । केतुः । उषसां । एति । अग्रं ।  
> भागं । देवेभ्यः । वि । दधाति । आयन् । प्र । चंद्रमाः । तिरते । दीर्घं । आयुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अतिमूर्तिनाम्न्येकाहे शुक्लपक्षे चांद्रमसीष्टिः । तत्र नवोनव इत्येषा
> याज्या । सूत्रितं च । नवोनवो भवति जायमानस्तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतः । आ. ९-८ ॥ इति॥
> अयं चंद्रमा जायमानः प्रतिदिनं जायमान एकैककलाधिक्येनोत्पद्यमानः सन्नवोनवो भवति । प्रतिदिनं नूतन एव भवति । एतत्पूर्वपक्षाद्यभिप्रायं ।
> तथाह्नां दिवसानां केतुः प्रज्ञापकः प्रतिपदादीनां तिथीनां चंद्रकलाह्रासवृद्धधीनत्वात् । तादृशश्चंद्रमा उषसां प्रभातीनामग्रमेति । एतत्कृष्ण पक्षांताभिप्रायं । केचनैतं पादमादित्यदैवत्यमाहुः । तन्निन्पक्षेह्नां केतुत्वमुषसामग्रगतिश्च प्रसिद्धे । देवेभ्यो भागं हविर्भागं वि दधाति । करोति । उभयपक्षांते ।
> किं कुर्वन् । आयन् प्रतिदिनं ह्रासवृद्ध्या पक्षांतमभिगच्छन् । एतदर्धमासाभिप्रायं । चंद्रमा उक्तलक्षणो देवो दीर्घमायुस्तिरते । वर्धयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the one-day rite called Atimūrti, in the bright fortnight, there is the Cāndramasī offering; in it this verse, नवोनव (*navonava*), is the yājyā. And it is stated in the sūtra: नवोनवो भवति जायमानस्तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतः (*navonavo bhavati jāyamānastaraṇirviśvadarśataḥ*) (Ā. 9-8). This moon, being born, that is, rising day by day with the addition of one digit each, becomes ever new, new every day; this is meant for the bright fortnight and the rest. Likewise he is the banner of the days, their indicator, since the tithis beginning with pratipad depend on the waning and waxing of the moon's digits. Such a moon goes at the head of the dawns; this is meant for the end of the dark fortnight. Some say that this pāda is addressed to the Āditya: on that view it is well known that, in the fortnight, the sun is the banner of the days and goes at the head of the dawns. He apportions the share, the share of the oblation, to the gods, at the end of both fortnights. Doing what? Coming, going towards the end of the fortnight each day by waning and waxing: this is meant for the half-month. The moon, the god so characterised, prolongs a long life, that is, makes it grow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चंद्रमाः (*caṃdramāḥ*)—the moon
- जायमानः (*jāyamānaḥ*)—being born every day
- नवो नवो भवति (*navo navo bhavati*)—appears ever new
- अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*)—of the days beginning with the first day of the fortnight
- केतुः (*ketuḥ*)—the moon, the indicator
- उषसां अग्रं (*uṣasāṃ agraṃ*)—in front of the dawns
- एति (*eti*)—goes
- आयन् (*āyan*)—appearing in his own course
- देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the deities
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—the share of the sacrifice
- वि दधाति (*vi dadhāti*)—assigns
- दीर्घं आयुः (*dīrghaṃ āyuḥ*)—a long life
- तिरते (*tirate*)—makes grow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The moon, being born every day, appears new every day. The moon, the indicator of the days beginning with the first day of the fortnight, goes in front of the dawns. Appearing in his daily course, he assigns the share of the sacrifice to the deities. He makes a long life grow.

### Printed p. 397

##### English translation
New every day (the moon) is born ; the manifester of days he goes in front of the Dawns! he distributes their portion to the gods as he goes ; the moon protracts a long existence.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The one-day offering called Atimūrti, when it is performed in the bright fortnight, is named the Cāndramasī offering. That in that offering the Ṛk नवोनवः (*navonavaḥ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, नवोनवो भवति जायमानस्तरणिर्विश्वदर्शतः (*navonavo bhavati jāyamānastaraṇirviśvadarśataḥ*) (Ā. 9-8). Yāska has given the Nirukta for this Ṛk:

नवोनवो भवति जायमान इति पूर्वपक्षादिमभिप्रेत्य । अह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रं इत्यपरपक्षांतमभिप्रेत्य । आदित्यदैवतो द्वितीयः पाद इत्येके । भागं देवेभ्यो विदधात्यायन् इत्यर्धमासेज्यामभिप्रेत्य । प्रवर्धयते चंद्रमा दीर्घमायुः ॥ (*navonavo bhavati jāyamāna iti pūrvapakṣādimabhipretya | ahnāṃ keturuṣasāmetyagraṃ ityaparapakṣāṃtamabhipretya | ādityadaivato dvitīyaḥ pāda ityeke | bhāgaṃ devebhyo vidadhātyāyan ityardhamāsejyāmabhipretya | pravardhayate caṃdramā dīrghamāyuḥ ‖*) (Ni. 11-6)

In a month there are two fortnights, the earlier (waxing) and the later (waning). In each fortnight there are fifteen days. When the moon rises in the days of the earlier fortnight, he rises increased from day to day; that is, the form of the second day is a little larger than the form in which he rose on the first day. In the same way, increasing a little each day, on the fifteenth day, that is, the day of the full moon, he rises as the full moon. The moon who thus rises every day of the earlier fortnight in a different (slightly larger) form is described in this Ṛk by नवो नवो भवति जायमानः (*navo navo bhavati jāyamānaḥ*): he is born every day in a new form. This sentence indicates the course of the moon in the earlier fortnight. Next, the sentence अह्नां केतुरुषसामेत्यग्रं (*ahnāṃ keturuṣasāmetyagraṃ*) indicates the course of the moon in the later fortnight. In the later fortnight the moon's course is contrary to the course in the earlier fortnight: in the later fortnight the form of the moon grows smaller from day to day, and on the last day of the fortnight, the new moon, the moon is not seen at all and stays set. Besides, in the later fortnight the moon does not rise every day in the evening; he rises later each day by two ghaṭikās, rises after sunrise and sets. For this reason it is said here अह्नां केतुरुषसामेतृग्रं (*ahnāṃ keturuṣasāmetṛgraṃ*): after the time of dawn he is seen in the day like a banner. That is, after sunrise

### Printed p. 398

the moon too, though visible, does not shine. Some are of the opinion that this second pāda indicates the Āditya; for at the time of dawn the sun appears first as the banner of the day (at its beginning); that is, the meaning is that the sun rises after the time of dawn as the banner of the day.

Next, for the third pāda, the sentence भागं देवेभ्यो विदधात्यायन् (*bhāgaṃ devebhyo vidadhātyāyan*): the moon distributes to the deities the portions of oblation due to each of them. That is, the moon is the cause of the divisions of time, the earlier and the later fortnight, in every month. In connection with these two fortnights people perform at the end of the fortnight the Darśa (new moon) and Paurṇamāsa offerings. In those offerings the sacrificers offer oblations and the like to the deities. Therefore, as the maker of the divisions of time, and as the moon is the cause of supplying oblations to the deities when the offerings are performed at those times, it is explained here that भागं देवेभ्यो विदधाति (*bhāgaṃ devebhyo vidadhāti*), he distributes the shares of oblation to the deities.

Next, in the fourth pāda, the sentence प्र चंद्रमास्तिरते दीर्घमायुः (*pra caṃdramāstirate dīrghamāyuḥ*), the wish is stated that the moon, possessed of the qualities mentioned above, may give long life also to the sacrificers who perform the sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒किं॒शु॒कं श॑ल्म॒लिं वि॒श्वरू॑पं॒ हिर॑ण्यवर्णं सु॒वृतं॑ सुच॒क्रं ।

> सुकिंशुकं । शल्मलिं । विश्वरूपं । हिरण्यवर्णं । सुवृतं । सुचक्रं ।  
> आ । रोह । सूर्ये । अमृतस्य । लोकं । स्कोनं । पत्ये । वहतुं । कृणुष्ट ॥२०॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुकिंशुकं शोभनकिंशुकवृक्षनिर्मितं तथा शल्मलिं शल्मलिवृक्षनिर्मितं
> विश्वरूपं नानारूपं हिरण्यवर्णं हितरमणीयवर्णं हिरण्यालंकारयुक्तं वा
> सुवृतं सुष्णुवर्तनं सुचक्रं शोभनचक्रोपेतं रथं हे सूर्य आ रोह ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sūryā, ascend the chariot that is made of the excellent kiṃśuka tree and made of the śalmali tree, of many forms, of beautiful colour or provided with golden ornaments, well-turning, and furnished with good wheels.

### Printed p. 399

> अमृतस्य लोकं स्थानं स्कोनं सुखकरं पत्ये सोमाय वहतुं वहसमात्मनः
> प्रापणं कृणुष्ट । कुरुष्ट । अत्र निरुक्तं । १२-८ । द्रष्टव्यं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Make the place of the immortal, a comfortable and happy one; for your husband Soma make the vahatu, that is, the means of conveying yourself to him. He says "make" in the sense of "do". On this the Nirukta (12-8) is to be seen.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरै (*sūrai*)—O goddess Sūryā
- सुकिंशुकं (*sukiṃśukaṃ*)—made of the excellent kiṃśuka tree
- शल्मलिं (*śalmaliṃ*)—made of the śalmali tree
- विश्वरूपं (*viśvarūpaṃ*)—having many forms
- हिरण्यवर्णं (*hiraṇyavarṇaṃ*)—having ornaments of gold
- सुवृतं (*suvṛtaṃ*)—having an excellent covering
- सुचक्रं (*sucakraṃ*)—having excellent wheels
- आ रोह (*ā roha*)—the chariot, ascend and sit
- पत्ये (*patye*)—to your husband
- वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)—as you go
- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—deathless
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—the world of the gods
- स्योनं (*syonaṃ*)—agreeable
- कृणुष्ट्व (*kṛṇuṣṭva*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sūryā, ascend and sit in the chariot made of the excellent kiṃśuka and śalmali trees, having many forms, golden ornaments, an excellent covering and excellent wheels. As you go to your husband, make the deathless world of the gods agreeable.

##### English translation
Ascend, Surya; the chariot made of good kimshuka wood and of shalmali, multiform, decorated with gold, well-covered, well-wheeled; prepare the happy world of the immortals, yonr marriage procession to your husband.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the Nirukta for this Ṛk:

सुकाशनं शन्नमलं सर्वरूपं । अपि वोपमार्थे स्यात् । सुकिंशुकमिव शल्मलिमिति । किंशुकं क्रंशतेः । प्रकाशयतिकर्मणः । शल्मलिः सुशरो भवति। शरवान्वा । आरोह सूर्ये अमृतस्य लोकमुदकस्य सुखु पत्ये वहतुं कुरुष्ट । सविता सूर्यं प्रायच्छत् सोमाय राजे प्रजापतये वा इति च ब्राह्मणं ॥ (*sukāśanaṃ śannamalaṃ sarvarūpaṃ | api vopamārthe syāt | sukiṃśukamiva śalmalimiti | kiṃśukaṃ kraṃśateḥ | prakāśayatikarmaṇaḥ | śalmaliḥ suśaro bhavati| śaravānvā | āroha sūrye amṛtasya lokamudakasya sukhu patye vahatuṃ kuruṣṭa | savitā sūryaṃ prāyacchat somāya rāje prajāpataye vā iti ca brāhmaṇaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 12-8)

When describing the chariot in which the goddess Sūryā is to ascend and sit, the seer describes it with words such as सुकिंशुकं (*sukiṃśukaṃ*).

### Printed p. 400

सुकिंशुकं (*sukiṃśukaṃ*)—सुष्टु काशनं दीपनं लोकानां । (*suṣṭu kāśanaṃ dīpanaṃ lokānāṃ |*) Shining well, exceedingly resplendent.

शल्मलिं (*śalmaliṃ*)—शन्नमलं व्यपगतमलं । (*śannamalaṃ vyapagatamalaṃ |*) Free from stain, without dirt, pure, clean.

विश्वरूपं (*viśvarūpaṃ*)—सर्वरूपं । (*sarvarūpaṃ |*) Of many kinds, that is, having variegated forms, having various ornaments.

Or the words सुकिंशुकं शल्मलिं (*sukiṃśukaṃ śalmaliṃ*) may be explained also as a comparison. शल्मलि (*śalmali*) means the पालाश (*pālāśa*) tree. किंशुक (*kiṃśuka*) means a flower that has just sprouted. Therefore, for the words सकिंशुकं शल्मलिं (*sakiṃśukaṃ śalmaliṃ*) a comparison is given for the chariot: a chariot that looks like a पालाश (*pālāśa*) tree shining thickly with many red flowers. In this sense the word किंशुक (*kiṃśuka*) is derived from the root क्रंशति (*kraṃśati*), meaning "to shine, to look brilliant", क्रंशकेः प्रकाशयतिकर्मणः । (*kraṃśakeḥ prakāśayatikarmaṇaḥ |*) The word शल्मलि (*śalmali*) is derived from the root शृ (*śṛ*) (हिंसायां (*hiṃsāyāṃ*)), meaning "to injure", शल्मलिः सुशरो भवति शरवान्वा (*śalmaliḥ suśaro bhavati śaravānvā*); it is understood as a tree with thorns.

The meaning of the Ṛk is: O goddess Sūryā, ascending and sitting in such an excellent and comfortable chariot, depart towards the heaven, the world of water (the atmosphere). The author of the Nirukta has quoted the Brāhmaṇa sentence सविता सूर्यां प्रायच्छत् सॊमाय राजे प्रजापतये वा (*savitā sūryāṃ prāyacchat sòmāya rāje prajāpataye vā*). According to this, in the Nirukta view it is expressed that जोत्स्नां सोमाय ददाति (*jotsnāṃ somāya dadāti*), he gave light (moonlight) to Soma (the moon); and in the historical view that उषसं वा मध्यस्थानाय प्रजापतये ददाति (*uṣasaṃ vā madhyasthānāya prajāpataye dadāti*), he gave the goddess Uṣas to Prajāpati (the Sun), the deity of the middle region.

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदी॒र्ष्वातः॒ पति॑वती॒ ह्ये॒३॒॑षा वि॒श्वाव॑सुं॒ नम॑सा गी॒र्भिरी॑ळे।  
> अ॒न्यामि॑च्छ पितृ॒षदं॒ व्य॑क्तां॒ स ते॑ भा॒गो ज॒नुषा॒ तस्य॑ विद्धि ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ईर्ष्व । अतः । पतिवती । हि । एषा । विश्ववसुं । नमसा । गीर्भिः । ईळे ।  
> अन्यां । इच्छ । पितृसदं । विअक्तां । सः । ते । भागः । जनुषा । तस्य । विद्दि ॥ २१ ॥

### Printed p. 401

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अभिनृणां विवाहः स्तूयते । हे विश्वावसो अतः स्थानात्कन्यासमीपादुदीर्ष्ट । उत्तिष्ठ । एषा कन्या पतिवती हि संजाता । आत उदीर्ष्टेति वातः शब्दो
> योज्यः । विश्वावसुमेतन्नामानं गंधर्वं नमसा नमस्कारेण गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिश्चेळे ।
> सौमि । तर्ह्येनां विहाय कां स्वीकरोमीति यदि ब्रूषे तर्ह्यन्यां पितृषदु
> पितृकुले स्थितां व्यक्तामनूढेति परिस्फुटां निगतांजनां वा । स्तनोद्गमादिराहित्येनाप्रौढामित्यर्थः । स तादृशः पदार्थस्ते तव भागः कल्पितः । तस्य तं भागं
> विद्दि जानीहि जनुषा जन्मना । लभस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The marriage of men is praised here. O Viśvāvasu, rise from this place, from beside the maiden, for this maiden has now become one who has a husband. The word "wind" is to be connected with "rise" **NOTE**. I praise Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva of this name, with homage and with hymns. **NOTE**. If you ask, "Leaving her, whom shall I take?", then take another maiden, one who stays in her father's family, who is plainly unmarried, or one without collyrium; the meaning is one not yet mature, without the signs such as the budding of the breasts. Such a thing is your allotted portion; know it by birth, that is, obtain it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from this place
- उदीर्घ (*udīrgha*)—rise up
- एषा (*eṣā*)—this maiden
- पतिवती हि (*pativatī hi*)—(because) she has a husband
- विश्वावसुं (*viśvāvasuṃ*)—the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with reverence
- गीर्भि: (*gīrbhi:*)—with hymns
- ईळे (*īḷe*)—I praise (I pray)
- पितृषदं (*pitṛṣadaṃ*)—one who dwells in her father's house
- व्यक्तां (*vyaktāṃ*)—one who is plainly shown not to be married
- अन्यां (*anyāṃ*)—another maiden
- इच्छॆ (*icchè*)—desire
- सः (*saḥ*)—such a thing
- ते भागः (*te bhāgaḥ*)—is the thing allotted to you
- तस्य (*tasya*)—that thing
- जनुषा (*januṣā*)—by nature
- विद्दि (*viddi*)—know it to be yours

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

"O Viśvāvasu, this maiden has been married and has her husband. Therefore leave this place and rise up." Thus I pray, praising with reverence and with hymns the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu. Know that only the maiden who is unmarried in her father's house is the portion that belongs to you.

##### English translation
Rise up from hence, for this (damsel) has a husband; I worship Vishwavasu with reverence and with hymns; O Viswavasu, seek for another maiden still dwelling in her father's house, decorated with ornaments ; that is your portion, know this (to be your portion, take it) from your birth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk and in the next, the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu is prayed to go away from the neighbourhood of the newly married bride. In this same sūkta, in the Ṛk

### Printed p. 402

सोमः प्रथमो विविदे गंधर्वो विविद उत्तरः । तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ॥ (*somaḥ prathamo vivide gaṃdharvo vivida uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo agniṣṭe patisturīyaste manuṣyajāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-40)

it is said thus: For the maiden who lives in her father's house in the state of maidenhood, Soma is first the lord, then the Gandharva, then Agni, and last the human being, that is, the bridegroom who marries her. All of these, one after another, are her lord; that is, the maiden is regarded as subject to them. At the beginning, that is, when the girl is very small, she is under Soma's authority. Then, when she approaches marriageable age, she is under the Gandharvas' authority. At the time of the marriage she is under Agni's control. After the marriage she is under the control of the human being (the bridegroom). Therefore here, after the marriage, the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu is addressed: O Gandharva Viśvāvasu, until now this maiden was under your authority. Now that this maiden has been married and has to go to her husband's house, go away from her side to another place, that is, to the other maidens who are in their father's house and not yet married. Such maidens are the ones who should come to your share; so the prayer is made.

Formerly, when the Śyena bird was bringing the Soma plants from heaven, the Gandharva named Viśvāvasu barred the way, seized those plants and kept them with himself. Then, while the gods were thinking how to bring those Soma plants back from him, the goddess Vāk spoke to them: "Why do you worry about this?" स्त्रीकामा वै गंधर्वाः स्त्रिया निष्क्रिणामेति ते वाचग्स् स्त्रियमेकहायिनीं कृत्वा तया निरक्रीणन् । (*strīkāmā vai gaṃdharvāḥ striyā niṣkriṇāmeti te vācags striyamekahāyinīṃ kṛtvā tayā nirakrīṇan |*) — To be attached to women, that is, to have desire for women, is the very nature of the Gandharvas. They have a great longing for women. Therefore I shall become a beautiful woman. Sell me to that Gandharva and in exchange buy the Soma plants that he has stolen. When she said this, the gods did so. Afterwards the goddess Vāk, in the form of a red doe, escaped from the Gandharva and ran to the gods. This story is told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1).

A little explanation concerning the Gandharvas is necessary.

As already stated, in connection with the Apsarases there is a male, Gandharva, or a male race, the Gandharvas. In the Ṛgveda, of the twenty places where it occurs, only three times is it in the plural. In the Atharvaveda, of the thirty-two, half are in the plural. From this it appears that at first there was only one, and that gradually the number increased. In the other Vedas the Gandharvas, like the gods, the Pitṛs and the Asuras, are a class (A. Ve. 11-5-2 **NOTE**; Tai. Saṃ. 7-8-25-2). In the Yajurveda their number is twenty-seven; in the Atharvaveda it becomes about 6333 (A. Ve. 11-5-2). From the beginning their character and nature

### Printed p. 403

are not determined; no support for it is found in the Ṛgveda. In this connection it is also an important matter in which maṇḍalas these expressions are found. In maṇḍalas two to seven it occurs altogether only once, and in the eighth twice, in opposition to Indra. Or it appears that this word may be taken as an epithet. Sometimes it is used together with the word Viśvāvasu (9-86-36; 10-139-4,5; A. Ve. 2.2.4; Vā. Saṃ. 2-3). In one passage the word Viśvāvasu is used to indicate the Gandharva (10-85-21,22; compare 10-85 40, 41). In the other Saṃhitās, the Brāhmaṇas and the Purāṇas and the like, Viśvāvasu is the name of a Gandharva.

According to the Ṛgveda the Gandharva dwells in the atmosphere, or in the highest region of the sky. He is the measurer in the sky (10-139.5); he dwells in the unfathomable regions of the atmosphere (8-66-5); he is of divine nature and stands erect in the middle region (10-123-7). It is on him that the Apsaras smiles (10-123-5). His dwelling is in heaven (A. Ve. 2-2.1.2), and the virtuous live with the Gandharvas (A. Ve. 4.34.3). In some passages it is said that the Gandharvas have some connection with heavenly light. He is associated with the sun, Varuṇa's messenger with golden wings (10-123.6), with the sun-bird (10-177-2), with the sun-horse (1-163.2), and with Soma, who is like the sun (9-85-12). Moreover, a connection is assumed with the twenty-seven constellations on the moon's path (Vā. Saṃ. 9-7), and especially with the constellation Rohiṇī (A. Ve. 13.1-23). In the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Vā. Saṃ. 18.38) the Gandharva is regarded as a deity together with Agni, the sun, the moon and the wind. In the Purāṇas and the like, gandharvanagara (the city of the Gandharvas) is a name of the mirage.

The name of the Gandharvas is mentioned especially in the ninth maṇḍala, together with Soma. They guard the place of Soma and the lineage of the gods (9-83-4; compare 1-22-14). They stand in the firmament, watching all the states of the Soma juice (9.85.12). Together with Parjanya and the daughter of the sun, the Gandharvas increase the Soma juice (9-113.3). It is from the mouth of the Gandharva that the gods drink Soma (A. Ve. 7,73-3). It is said that the Gandharvas guarded the Soma for the gods, but allowed it to be stolen, and that as a punishment the drinking of Soma was forbidden to the Gandharvas (Mai. Saṃ. 3-8.10). In connection with this Soma juice it is said that the Gandharvas know the plants (A. Ve. 4-4-1). The Gandharva who was devoted to guarding the Soma incurs Indra's displeasure and is pierced by him in the atmosphere

### Printed p. 404

(8-66 5). And for this very reason the hymns praise Indra, asking him to defeat him (8-1 11). In another place (Tai. Saṃ. 1-2.9-1) Soma is also told to come in the form of a Śyena, in order to escape from the Gandharva Viśvāvasu. It is said that the Soma juice was in the midst of the Gandharvas, or was stolen by the Gandharva Viśvāvasu; that the gods gave the goddess Vāk as the price to the Gandharvas, who were fond of women, and obtained the Soma from the Gandharvas (Ai. Brā. 1-27; Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-5; Mai. Saṃ. 3-7-3). Kṛśānu, who shoots an arrow at the Śyena that is carrying off the Soma, must also be a Gandharva. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 1-9-3) it is stated clearly that Kṛśānu too is a Gandharva.

The Gandharvas have a connection with water. The Gandharva in the water and the Apsaras of watery form are said to be the parents of Yama and Yamī (10-10-4). The Soma juice poured into water is called the Gandharva of the water (9-86-36). The Gandharvas, who are united with the Apsarases, also live in the water (A. Ve. 2.2-3; 4-37-12).

The union of the Gandharva and the Apsaras is suggestive of marriage. Therefore a connection is assumed between the Gandharvas and the marriage ceremony. The unmarried maiden belongs to the Gandharva, Soma and Agni (10-85-40,41). In the first days of the marriage, Viśvāvasu is a rival to the bridegroom (10-85-22). The Gandharva's love for women is well known in the other Vedas (Mai. Saṃ. 3-7-3). The Gandharvas and the Apsarases are the presiding deities of fertility, and those who desire offspring praise them (Saṃ. Brā. 19-3-2 **NOTE**).

That the Gandharvas are celestial singers has become famous in the Purāṇas and the like, but there is no support for it anywhere in the Ṛgveda (compare 10-177-2; 10-11-2).

Only in one or two places is there a reference to their bodies and the like. For them the wind is the hair (3-38-6), and they have shining weapons (10-123-7). In this matter the Atharvaveda is clearer (A. Ve. 4-3-7; 8-6-1 especially). Here it is said that they are hairy, that they have bodies like half-animals, and that they are harmful to human beings in many ways; in other places again it is said that they are beautiful (Śa. Brā. 13-4-4-7,8). In the Ṛgveda it is said that the Gandharvas wear fragrant garments (10-123-7), and in the Atharvaveda that fragrance from the earth reaches the Gandharvas (A. Ve. 12-1-23).

From this it may be said that the word gandharva is derived from gandha (fragrance). Even if this is the correct derivation, the nature or characteristics of the Gandharva are not thereby understood. From the descriptions seen above, the Gandharva is a radiant divine person who lives in the water with his companion, the Apsaras

### Printed p. 405

— this much alone can be said with certainty. Various scholars have expressed various opinions on this matter: that they are abstract persons belonging to the wind, the rainbow, the moon, Soma, the rising sun, or a deity presiding over the clouds, and so on.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उदी॒ष्वातो॑ विश्वावसो॒ नम॑सेळामहे त्वा ।  
> अ॒न्यामि॑च्छ प्रफ॒र्व्यं१॒॑१ सं जा॒यां पत्या॑ सृज ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ईर्ष्व । अतः । विश्वावसो इति विश्ववसो । नमसा । ईळामहे । त्वा ।  
> अन्यां । इच्छ । प्रफर्व्यं । सं । जायां । पत्या । सृज ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अतोऽस्माच्छयनाद्धे विश्वावसो कन्यास्वामिन्गंधर्व उदीर्ष्व । उद्दच्छ ॥
> ईर गत् आदादिकः । अनुदात्तेत् । तस्य लोटि रूपं ॥ विश्वावसुर्नाम गंधर्वः
> कन्यानामधिपतिर्यतः । लभामि तेन कन्यामिति हि मंत्रः । स तादृश देव त्वां
> नमसा नमस्कारेणेळामहे । स्तुमः । स त्वमन्यां प्रफर्व्यं बृहन्नितंबां
> कन्यामिच्छ । जायां मां पत्या सह पुनः सं सृज ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From this couch, O Viśvāvasu, Gandharva, lord of the maiden, rise up; go away. Viśvāvasu is a Gandharva, the overlord of maidens; hence there is the mantra, "By him I obtain a maiden." O god of such a kind, we praise you with homage, with reverence. You, then, desire another maiden, one with large hips. Unite me, the wife, again with my husband.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वावसो (*viśvāvaso*)—O Viśvāvasu
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with reverence
- ईळामहे (*īḷāmahe*)—we praise and pray to you
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from this place
- उदीर्ष्व (*udīrṣva*)—rise up
- प्रफर्व्यं (*prapharvyaṃ*)—one with fully developed hips
- अन्यां (*anyāṃ*)—another maiden
- इच्छ (*iccha*)—desire
- जायां (*jāyāṃ*)—me, who am the wife of another
- पत्या (*patyā*)—to be with my husband
- सं सृज (*saṃ sṛja*)—give up

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Viśvāvasu, with reverence we praise you and pray to you. Rise up from this place. Desire another maiden with fully developed hips. Give me, the wife of another, up to be with my husband.

### Printed p. 406

##### English translation
Rise up from hence, Vishwavasu; we worship you with reverence. seek another maiden, one with large hips; leave the bride with her husband

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒न्य॒क्ष॒रा ऋ॒जवः॑ संतु॒ पंथा॒ येभिः॒ सखा॑यो॒ यंति॑ नो  ॒
> वरेयं ।  
> सम॑र्य॒मा सं भगो॑ नो निनीया॒त्सं जा॑स्प॒त्यं सु॒यम॑मस्तु देवाः ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अन्यक्षराः । ऋजवः । संतु । पंथाः । येभिः । सखायः । यंति । नः । वरेयं ।  
> सं । अर्यमा । सं । भगः । नः । निनीयात् । सं । जाःपत्यं । सुयमं । अस्तु ।  
> देवाः ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देवाः पंथाः पंथानो मार्गा अनृक्षराः । ऋक्षरः कंटक उच्यते ।
> कंटकरहिता यजवोऽकुटिलाश्च संतु येभिर्यैः पथिभिनोस्माकं सखायो
> वरप्रेषिता वरेयं वरैर्याचितव्यं पितरु प्रति यंति गच्छंति ते पंथा इति ।
> किंचार्यमा देवो नोऽस्मान् सं निनीयात् । सम्यक् प्रापयेत् । तथा भगो
> देवः सं निनीयात् । हे देवाः आसंगतमस्तु पतिकुलमिति शेषः तथेदं जास्पत्यं
> जायापत्योर्युगलं सुयममस्तु । सुमिथुनमस्तु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O gods, may the paths, the roads, be free of thorns and not crooked, by which our friends, sent by the suitors, go to the father to ask for the bride. Further, may the god Aryaman lead us rightly, that is, bring us well to our goal; and likewise may the god Bhaga lead us. O gods, may the husband's family be well joined to us (this is the word to be supplied). So may this pair, the wife and the husband, be well yoked, that is, may they be a good couple.

- अनृक्षराः (*anṛkṣarāḥ*)—free of thorns
- ऋजवः (*ṛjavaḥ*)—and without crookedness
- संतु (*saṃtu*)—may they be
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- सं निनीयात् (*saṃ ninīyāt*)—may he lead rightly
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—Bhaga
- सं (*saṃ*)—may he show the way rightly
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—O gods
- जास्पत्यं (*jāspatyaṃ*)—the mutual relation of the married pair
- सुयमं (*suyamaṃ*)—having an excellent bond
- अस्तु (*astu*)—may it be

### Printed p. 407

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the paths by which our friends go to the father of the maiden who is asked for by the suitors be free of thorns and without crookedness. May the god Aryaman lead us rightly. May Bhaga show us the right way. O gods, may the mutual relation of the married pair be excellently joined.

##### English translation
Smooth and straight be the paths by which our friends repair to the bride's father ; may Aryaman, may Bhaga conduct us, and may the union of the wife and husband be easily accomplished, O gods.

#### Ṛk 24

> ऋ॒तस्य॒ योन्सौ॑ सुकृ॒तस्य॑ लो॒केऽरि॑ष्टां त्वा स॒ह पत्या॑ दधामि ॥

> सुशेवः ।  
> ऋतस्य । योन्सौ । सुकृतस्य । लोके । अरिष्टां । त्वा । सह । पत्या । दधामि ॥ २४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पत्न्या योक्रविमोचने प्र त्वा मुंचामित्येषा । सूत्रितं च : अथास्या
> योक्रं विच्यतेत्प त्वा मुंचामि वरुणस्य पाशात् । आ. १-११ । इति ॥
> जातं प्राणिनं सवित्रा प्रेरितो वरुण आत्मपाशैर्बध्नाति । तस्माद्वरुणस्य
> पाशात् हे वधु त्वा त्वां प्र मुंचामि येन त्वा त्वां सविता वरुणस्य प्रेरकः
> सुशेवः सुखोऽबध्नात् बंधनं कृतवान् । यज्ञांगपक्षे पत्नीं योक्रेण बध्नाति ।
> बंधनस्य वरुणोऽभिमानी । अतो वरुणपाशाद्योक्रात्र्य मुंचामि येन
> योक्रेण सविता कर्मणामनुज्ञाता देव ऋत्विक्पाशेनाबध्नात् । तं मोचयित्वा

### Printed p. 408

> चर्तस्य यज्ञस्य योन्सौ स्थाने यागभूमौ सुकृतस्य लोके कर्मक्षेत्रे भूलोके
> चारिष्टामहिंसितां त्वां पुत्राद्यर्थं पत्या सह दधामि । स्थापयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is used for loosening the wife's yoke-cord, and it is laid down in the sūtra that when her yoke-cord is loosened, the verse beginning "I release you from the noose of Varuṇa" is recited (Ā. 1-11). Varuṇa, impelled by Savitṛ, binds a born creature with his own nooses. Therefore, O bride, I release you from the noose of Varuṇa, with which Savitṛ, the impeller of Varuṇa, the gracious one, bound you, that is, made a bond for you. As a limb of the sacrifice, the wife is bound with the yoke-cord, and Varuṇa presides over binding; so I release you from the Varuṇa-noose, the yoke-cord, with which the god Savitṛ, who gives leave for the rites, bound you with the noose of the priest. Having released it, in the seat of the sacrifice, that is, on the sacrificial ground, in the world of good deeds, that is, in the field of rites, the earth, I place you, unharmed, with your husband, for the sake of sons and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—by which noose
- सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*)—the giver of excellent happiness
- सविता (*savitā*)—the god Savitṛ
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- अबध्नात् (*abadhnāt*)—had bound, of such a kind
- वरुणस्य (*varuṇasya*)—of Varuṇa
- पाशात् (*pāśāt*)—from the bond
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- प्र मुंचामि (*pra muṃcāmi*)—I release
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for the sacrifice
- योन्सौ (*yonsau*)—the seat
- सुकृतस्य (*sukṛtasya*)—for excellent action
- लोके (*loke*)—in the earth, which is the field
- अरिष्टां त्वा (*ariṣṭāṃ tvā*)—you, who are free from harm
- पत्या सह (*patyā saha*)—together with your husband
- दधामि (*dadhāmi*)—I establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, I release you from the bond of Varuṇa, with which the god Savitṛ, the giver of excellent happiness, had bound you. On the earth, which is the seat of the sacrifice and the field of excellent action, I establish you, free from harm, together with your husband.

##### English translation
I set you free from the noose of Varuna, wherewith the adorable Savitri had bound you; in the place of sacrifice in the world of good deeds I unite you, unharmed, with your husband.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अथास्या योक्त्रं विच्यतेत्प्र ता मुंचामि वरुणस्य पाशात् (*athāsyā yoktraṃ vicyatetpra tā muṃcāmi varuṇasya pāśāt*) (Ā. 1-11), which says that when the rope of darbha grass called the yoke-cord, tied round the wife's waist, is untied, the Ṛk प्र त्वा मुंचामि (*pra tvā muṃcāmi*) is to be recited.

Varuṇa, impelled by the god Savitṛ, binds with his noose all creatures, those now born and those to be born. Therefore he had bound the bride mentioned here earlier, that is, at the time of her birth. Now, after this marriage, the assurance is stated here: I untie the noose of that Varuṇa, so that you may be able to live happily with your husband, and I establish you near your husband.

> प्रेतो मुं॒चामि॒ नामुतः॑ सुब॒द्धा म॒मुत॑स्करं ।

> यथेयमिंद्र विढ्वः सुपुत्रा सुभगासति ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । इतः । मुंचामि । न । अमुतः । सुबद्धां । अमुतः । करं ।  
> यथा । इयं । इंद्र । माढ्वः । सुपुत्रा ! सुभगा । असति ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इतः पितृकुलात्प्र मुंचामि त्वां नामुतो भर्तृगृहात्प्रमुंचामि । अमुतो
> भर्तृगृहे सुबद्धां करं । यथेयं कन्या हे इंद्र मीढ्वः सेक्तः सुपुत्रा सुभगा
> सुष्टु भाग्या वासति भवति तथा कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

From here, from the father's family, I release you; I do not release you from there, from the husband's house; there, in the husband's house, I make you well bound. O Indra, the showerer, the sprinkler, act so that this maiden may become the mother of good sons and fortunate, that is, blessed with good fortune.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from the father's family
- प्र मुंचामि (*pra muṃcāmi*)—I release you
- अमुतः (*amutaḥ*)—from the husband's house
- न (*na*)—I do not release
- अमुतः (*amutaḥ*)—in the husband's house
- सुबद्धां (*subaddhāṃ*)—so that you are firmly established
- अकरं (*akaraṃ*)—I make
- मीड्वः (*mīḍvaḥ*)—showerer of desires
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what way
- इयं (*iyaṃ*)—this maiden
- सुपुत्रा (*suputrā*)—possessed of excellent sons
- सुभगा (*subhagā*)—possessed of good fortune
- आसति (*āsati*)—will become, in that way favour (her)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, I release you from your father's family. I do not release you from your husband's house. I make you firmly established in your husband's house. O Indra, showerer of desires, favour her so that this maiden may become the mother of excellent sons and possessed of good fortune.

##### English translation
I set you free from thence, not from hence; I place you here firmly bound; grant, Indra, showerer, that this (damsel) may have excellent children, and be very fortunate.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इतः प्र मुंचामि (*itaḥ pra muṃcāmi*), न अमुतः (*na amutaḥ*), अमुतः सुबद्धां करं (*amutaḥ subaddhāṃ karaṃ*) — O bride, since you are now married, I release the connection with your father's house. But I do not release the connection with your husband's house; not only that, I shall make you live there permanently. So it is said. Here it is described how the maiden, who before the marriage was in her father's house, now leaves it and goes to her husband's house. After the marriage the married girl has no connection at all with her father's house. All the connection that was there has been given up. Whatever connection there is from now on is with her husband's house alone. That connection alone is to be understood as permanent from now on. O Indra, grant that this maiden, becoming the mother of sons and fortunate, may live in permanent happiness in her husband's house; thus Indra is prayed.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पू॒षा त्वे॒तो न॑यतु हस्त॒गृह्या॒श्विना॑ त्वा॒ प्र व॑हतां॒ रथे॑न ।  
> गृ॒हान्ग॑च्छ गृ॒हप॑त्नि॒ यथासो॑ व॒शिनी॒ त्वं वि॒दथ॒मा व॑दासि ॥

> गृहान् । गच्छ । गृहपत्नि । यथा । असः । वशिनी । त्वं । विदथं । आ । वदासि ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विवाहानंतरभाविनि प्रयाणे पूषा त्वेतो नयत्वित्यनया रथादियानमारोहयेत् । सूत्रितं च । पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्येति यानमारोहयेत् । अ. गृ. १-८.१ ॥
> हस्तगृह्य ग्राह्यहस्तः पूषा त्वामितो नयतु । प्रापयतु । अश्विनाश्विन्
> त्वा त्वां रथेन प्र वहतां । प्रगमयतां । गृहान्‌ भर्तृसंबंधिनो गच्छ त्वं
> गृहपत्नि यथासः भवसि स्वगृहस्वामिनी भवसि । वशिनी सर्वेषां गृहगतानां वशं
> प्रापयित्रि प्रत्युर्वशे वर्तमाना वा विदथं पतिगृहमा वदासि । आवदसि । गृहस्थितं
> भृत्यादिजनमावद ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

On the journey that comes after the marriage, with this Ṛk, "May Pūṣan lead you hence", one should make her mount a vehicle such as a chariot. It is laid down in the sūtra: with "May Pūṣan lead you hence, taking you by the hand" she should mount the vehicle (A. Gṛ. 1-8.1 **NOTE**). May Pūṣan, holding your hand, lead you hence, that is, bring you. May the two Aśvins convey you forward in a chariot, make you go forward. Go to the houses connected with your husband, so that you become the mistress of your house, mistress of your own household. Be one who brings all those who are in the house under her control, or one who lives under her husband's control; speak to the household, that is, address the servants and others who stay in the house.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हस्तगृह्य (*hastagṛhya*)—taking your hand
- पूषा (*pūṣā*)—the god Pūṣan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इतः (*itaḥ*)—from here
- नयतु (*nayatu*)—may he lead
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin gods
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- रथेन (*rathena*)—in a chariot
- प्र वहतां (*pra vahatāṃ*)—may they carry away
- यथा (*yathā*)—in what manner

### Printed p. 411

- गृहपत्नि असः (*gṛhapatni asaḥ*)—as you may become the guardian of your husband's house
- गृहान् (*gṛhān*)—to your husband's house
- गच्छ (*gaccha*)—go
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वशिनी (*vaśinī*)—submissive to your husband
- विदथं (*vidathaṃ*)—to the people of that house
- आ वदासि (*ā vadāsi*)—go on giving direction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, may the god Pūṣan take your hand and lead you from here. May the Aśvin gods carry you away in a chariot. Go to your husband's house and be the guardian of your husband's house there. Living under your husband's control, go on giving proper direction to the servants and others of that house.

##### English translation
May Pushan lead you hence, taking you by the hand; may the Ashwins convey you away in their car, go to the dwelling (of your husband) as you are the mistress of the house; you, submissive (to your husband) give orders to his household.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

After the marriage, when the bride sets out for her husband's house and sits in a chariot or the like (a cart), she is to be made to mount and sit in the cart with the Ṛk beginning पूषा त्वेतो नयतु (*pūṣā tveto nayatu*); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra, पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्येति यानमारोहेत् (*pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyeti yānamārohet*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8 1 **NOTE**).

After the marriage, as the bride goes to her husband's house, the assurance is stated here that the new bride, going to her husband's house and becoming the mistress there, carrying out the household duties, being helpful in her husband's work and affairs, and behaving respectfully towards the household members in the house, the children younger than herself, the servants and so on, and making them obedient to her, may live happily.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इह प्रियमित्येषा वध्वा गृहप्रवेशनी । सूत्रितं च । इह प्रियं प्रजया ते
> समृध्यतामिति गृहं प्रवेशयेत् । अ. गृ. १-८.८ । इति ॥
> हे वधु ते तवेहास्मिन्सतिकुले प्रियं प्रजया सह समृध्यतां । अस्मिन्गृहे

> गृहमा वदाथः । अभिमुख्येन वदतं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is the bride's entry into the house. It is laid down in the sūtra: with "Here may what is dear to you increase with offspring" she should be made to enter the house (A. Gṛ. 1-8.8). O bride, here in this your husband's family let what is dear to you increase together with offspring. In this house be awake, be alert, for the mistress-ship of the household, that is, for being the lady of the house. With this husband unite your own body; be joined with him. Then, as an aged wife and husband, you two shall speak in the household, that is, speak facing it, addressing it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—to you
- इह (*iha*)—here in this husband's house
- प्रजया (*prajayā*)—with sons and the like
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—affection
- समृध्यतां (*samṛdhyatāṃ*)—may it grow fully
- अस्मिन् गृहे (*asmin gṛhe*)—in this house
- गार्हपत्याय (*gārhapatyāya*)—to be the guardian of the house
- जागृहि (*jāgṛhi*)—be watchful
- एना पत्या (*enā patyā*)—with this your husband
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—your body
- सं सृजस्व (*saṃ sṛjasva*)—join together
- अध (*adha*)—after some time
- जीवी (*jīvī*)—you two, grown old
- विदथं (*vidathaṃ*)—to the sons and others who are in your house
- आ वदार्थः (*ā vadārthaḥ*)—you will give direction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, in this husband's house may the affection that is joined with sons and the like grow in you. Be watchful in order to be the guardian of this house. Joining with your husband, attain oneness with him. After some time, grown old, you two will give direction to the sons and others who are in your house.

##### English translation
In this your (husband's family) may affection increase with ofspring, be watchful over the domestic fire in this house; unite your person with this your husband ; and both growing old together govern your household.

### Printed p. 413

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk इह प्रियं (*iha priyaṃ*) is to be recited when the new bride enters her husband's house is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra, इह प्रियं प्रजया ते समृध्यतामिति गृहं प्रवेशयेत् (*iha priyaṃ prajayā te samṛdhyatāmiti gṛhaṃ praveśayet*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-8 **NOTE**).

O bride, enter this husband's house. Here may things dear to you, wealth and the like, and offspring such as sons grow. Being the mistress of this house, look after the management of the house with care. Joining with this husband of yours, obtain bodily happiness and beget offspring such as sons. In this way the wish is expressed that you, husband and wife, may live and thrive in this house for a long time in happiness and joy, and at the end may both grow old together.

The pronominal words ayā and enā are used when such a woman or such a man is being indicated. The word ayā is used with regard to women, and the word enā with regard to men and to neuter words. For example:

अया ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम । इति स्त्रियाः ॥ (*ayā te agne samidhā vidhema | iti striyāḥ ‖*)

In this Vedic sentence the word ayā is used in connection with the feminine word samidhā.

एना वो अग्निं नमसा । इति नपुंसकस्य ॥ (*enā vo agniṃ namasā | iti napuṃsakasya ‖*)

In this sentence the word enā is used in connection with the neuter word namasā.

एना पत्या तन्वं संसृजस्व ! इति पुंसः ॥ (*enā patyā tanvaṃ saṃsṛjasva ! iti puṃsaḥ ‖*)

In this sentence the word enā is used in connection with the masculine word patyā (Ni. 3-21).

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नी॒ल॒लो॒हि॒तं भ॑वति कृ॒त्यास॒क्तिर्व्य॑ज्यते ।  
> एधं॑ते अस्या ज्ञा॒तयः॒ पति॑र्बं॒धेषु॑ बध्यते ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नील्यलोहितं । भवति । कृत्या । आसक्तिः । वि । अज्यते ।  
> विधंते । आस्त्याः । ज्ञातयः । पतिः । बंधेषु । बध्यते ॥ २८ ॥

### Printed p. 414

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कृत्याभिचाराभिमानिनी देवता नीललोहितं भवंति । नीलं च लोहितं च
> तस्या रूपं भवतीत्यर्थः । सा कृत्यासक्तिरासक्तास्यां संबद्धा व्यज्यते । त्यज्यत इत्यर्थः ।
> तस्यां कृत्यायामपगतायामस्या वध्वा ज्ञातय विधंते वर्धंते । पतिर्बंधेषु
> सांसारिकेषु बध्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The deity presiding over Kṛtyā, the magical act of harm, becomes blue and red; that is, blue and red is her form. That Kṛtyā, attached, joined to her, is cast off, that is, abandoned. When that Kṛtyā has gone away, the kinsmen of this bride prosper, grow. The husband is bound in worldly bonds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कृत्या (*kṛtyā*)—the deity named Kṛtyā, presiding over magical harm (the deity possessed of magical power)
- नीललोहिता (*nīlalohitā*)—becoming blue and red in colour
- भवति (*bhavati*)—she is
- आसक्तिः (*āsaktiḥ*)—that Kṛtyā clinging to her
- व्यज्यते (*vyajyate*)—is abandoned
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—of this bride
- ज्ञातयः (*jñātayaḥ*)—kinsmen
- विधंते (*vidhaṃte*)—prosper
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—her husband
- बंधेषु (*baṃdheṣu*)—in worldly bonds
- बध्यते (*badhyate*)—is bound, restrained

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The deity named Kṛtyā, who possesses magical power, is blue and red in colour. That Kṛtyā clinging to this bride is abandoned. After that the kinsmen of this bride prosper. Her husband is restrained in worldly bonds.

##### English translation
Blue and red is (her form) ; Kritya devoted (to her) is left behind ; her kinsmen prosper, the husband is bound in bonds.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परा॑ देहि शामु॒ल्यं॑ ब्र॒ह्मभ्योः॒ वि भ॑जा॒ वसु॑ ।  
> कृ॒तैषा प॒द्वती॑ भू॒त्वा जा॒या वि॑शते॒ पतिं॑ ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परा । देहि । शामुल्यं । ब्रह्मभ्यः । वि । भज । वसु ।  
> कृत्या । एषा । पत्त्ववती । भूत्वी । आ । जाया । विशते । पतिं ॥ २९ ॥

### Printed p. 415

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> शामुल्यं । शामलमित्यर्थः । शमलं शारीरं मलं । शरीरावच्छन्नस्य मलस्य
> धारकं वस्त्रं परा देहि । परात्यज । धृतप्रायश्चित्यार्थं ब्रह्मभ्यो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो
> वसु धनं वि भज । प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः । किमर्थं वधूवासःपरित्याग इति चेत् उच्यते ।
> निषा कृत्या पद्वर्ती पादवती सती जाया भूत्वा भूत्वा पतिं विशते । कृत्यारूपवासःप्रवेशात् कृत्या जाया भूत्वा विश्वत इत्युपचर्यते । अतस्तत्परित्यागे कृत्यैव
> त्यक्ता भवतीत्यर्थः । यदि वधूवासः स्वयं निधत्ते तदैवं भवतीति वधूवासःसंस्पर्शनं निंदायुक्तं ii

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Śāmulya means the same as śāmala; śamala is the dirt of the body. Give away, cast off, the garment that holds the dirt covering the body. For the expiation of having worn it, distribute wealth to the Brahmins; that is, give it. If it is asked why the bride's garment is to be abandoned, the answer is: this Kṛtyā, having become endowed with feet, having become the wife, enters the husband. Since Kṛtyā enters in the form of the bride's garment, it is said figuratively that Kṛtyā, having become the wife, enters. Therefore, when the garment is abandoned, Kṛtyā herself is abandoned. If the husband himself puts on the bride's garment, then this happens; so touching the bride's garment is blameworthy.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शामुल्यं (*śāmulyaṃ*)—the garment soiled by the dirt of the body
- परा वेहि (*parā vehi*)—throw far away
- ब्रह्मभ्यः (*brahmabhyaḥ*)—to those who know the Veda
- वसु (*vasu*)—wealth
- वि भज (*vi bhaja*)—distribute
- एषा कृत्या (*eṣā kṛtyā*)—this goddess named Kṛtyā
- पद्वती (*padvatī*)—having become possessed of feet
- जाया भूत्वी (*jāyā bhūtvī*)—having attained the relation of a wife
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—your husband
- आ विशते (*ā viśate*)—enters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, throw far away the garment soiled by the dirt of the body. Distribute wealth to those who know the Veda. This goddess named Kṛtyā, having become possessed of feet and having taken the form of a wife, enters your husband.

##### English translation
Put away the garment soiled by the body; give wealth to the Brahmins; this Kritya having become endowed with feet, enters the husband's heart as his wife.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the bride is directed to cast far away her garment soiled by dirt. For if the bride's soiled garment touches the husband's body, there is a possibility that a sinful deity named Kṛtyā, of blue and red form, will enter the husband's body. Therefore it is said that, so that that sinful deity may go far away, the bride should throw away her soiled garment. For this very reason it is said that touching the bride's garment is blameworthy.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒श्री॒रा त॒नूर्भ॑वति॒ रुश॑ती पा॒पया॑मु॒या ।  
> पति॒र्यद्व॒ध्वो॒३॒॑ ३ वास॑सा॒ स्वमंग॑मभि॒धित्स॑ते ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्रीरा । तनूः । भवति । रुशती । पापया । अमुया ।  
> पतिः । यत् । वध्वः । वाससा । स्वं । अंगं । अभिधित्सते ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रापि वधूवासःसंस्पर्शनिंदोच्यते ! तनूर्वरस्य संबंधिन्यश्रीरश्रीका
> भवति । कथं स्यादिति उच्यते । रुशती । रुशदिति वर्णनाम । दीप्तयामुयानया
> पापरूपया कृत्यया युक्ता चेत्तनूः । तदेवाह । पतियद्यदि वध्वो वाससा
> स्वमंगमभिधित्सते परिधातुमिच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here too the blame of touching the bride's garment is stated. The body belonging to the bridegroom becomes without beauty. How this comes about is told: ruśat is a name for colour. If the body, though bright, is joined with this sinful Kṛtyā, that is the case; and this very thing he says: if the husband wishes to cover his own limb with the bride's garment, that is, wishes to put it on.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—the bridegroom
- वध्वः (*vadhvaḥ*)—of the bride
- वाससा (*vāsasā*)—with the garment
- स्वं अंगं (*svaṃ aṃgaṃ*)—his own body
- अभिधित्सते (*abhidhitsate*)—wishes to cover, then
- अमुया पापया (*amuyā pāpayā*)—by contact with this most sinful goddess Kṛtyā
- रुशती (*ruśatī*)—shining
- तनूः (*tanūḥ*)—his body
- अश्रीराः (*aśrīrāḥ*)—without lustre
- भवति (*bhavati*)—becomes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the husband wishes to cover his own body with the bride's garment, then, by contact with this most sinful goddess Kṛtyā, his shining body becomes without lustre.

##### English translation
The (bridegroom's) body is lacking in beauty; shining with this wicked (Kritya), when he wishes to clothe his own limbs with his wife's garments.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk too the blame of touching the bride's garment is stated. If the husband should once cover himself with the bride's garment, then the colour and lustre of his body are lost and the body becomes

### Printed p. 417

without beauty. Therefore even now it is the custom that men wear women's garments and the like **NOTE**. A man who wishes to be possessed of health, radiance and strength should never wear garments and the like that women have used.

> पुन॒स्तान्य॒ज्ञिया॑ दे॒वा नयं॑तु॒ यत॒ आग॑ताः ॥ ३१ ॥
