> ये । वध्वः । चंद्रं । वहतुं । यक्ष्याः । यंति । जनात् । अनु ।  
> पुनरिति । तान् । यज्ञियाः । देवाः । नयंतु । यतः । आगताः ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वध्वश्चंद्रं हिरण्यरूपं वहतुं ये यक्ष्या व्याधयोऽनु यंति प्राप्नुवंति
> जनादस्मद्विरोधिनः सकाशात् । यद्वा । जनाद्यमाख्यात् । तान्सुनर्नयंतु
> प्रापयंतु यज्ञिया यज्ञार्हा देवा इंद्रादयः । यत आगता यस्मात्ते
> यक्ष्या आगताः तत्र तान्नयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those diseases, the yakṣmas, which follow, that is, reach, the bride's "candra", golden in form, which is to be carried, from a person, an adversary of ours; or else from the one called Yama: may the gods worthy of sacrifice, Indra and the others, lead them back, bring them, to the place from which those diseases came; let them lead them there.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञियाः (*yajñiyāḥ*)—worthy of sacrifice
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- जनात् (*janāt*)—from people who are our enemies
- ये यक्ष्माः (*ye yakṣmāḥ*)—those diseases which
- वध्वः (*vadhvaḥ*)—of the bride
- चंद्रं (*caṃdraṃ*)—golden in form
- वहतुं (*vahatuṃ*)—splendour
- अनुयंति (*anuyaṃti*)—enter and make lustreless
- तान् (*tān*)—them
- यत आगताः (*yata āgatāḥ*)—to the place from which they came
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- नयंतु (*nayaṃtu*)—may they send back

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the gods send back again, to the place from which they came, those diseases which, from our enemies, enter the golden-formed body of the bride and make it lustreless.

##### English translation
May the adorable gods drive back again to the place whence they came the diseases which follow from (other) people the wife's golden bridal procession.

### Printed p. 418

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the present Ṛk the assurance is stated that if diseases such as yakṣma come from enemies or from Yama, all of them, by the grace of the gods Indra and the others, go back and go to the enemies; that is, they afflict the enemies themselves.

Candram means golden: the body of the bride, shining like the lustre of gold. Two kinds of meaning can be given to the word candra. सर्वेषामाह्लादकश्चंद्रसदृशो भवति । (*sarveṣāmāhlādakaścaṃdrasadṛśo bhavati |*) When describing a thing, a thing that shines like the radiance of the moon, which gives delight to all, is described by the word candra. This meaning follows the explanation of the Nirukta. In the Nirukta it is said, चंद्रश्चंदतेः कांतिकर्मणः । (*caṃdraścaṃdateḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ |*) (Ni. 11-5), that is, the word candra is formed from the root cand, which means to shine with lustre, to look lovely. Therefore the word candra is used when describing an agreeable thing.

#### Ṛk 32

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मा वि॑दन्परिपं॒थिनो॒ य आ॒सीदं॑ति॒ दंप॑ती ।  
> सु॒गेभि॑र्दु॒र्गमती॑ता॒मप॑ द्रां॒त्वरा॑तयः ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मा । विदन् । परिपंथिनः । ये । आसीदंति । दंपती इति दंपती ।  
> सुगेभिः । दुर्गं । आशि । इतां । अप । द्रांतु । अरातयः ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वध्वाः प्रयाणे मा विदन्नित्येषा याज्या । सूत्रितं च । कल्याणेषु देशवृक्षचतुष्पथेषु मा विदन्परिपंथिन इति जपेत् । अ. गृ. १-८.६ । इति ॥
> परिपंथिनः पर्यवस्थातारः शत्रवो मा विदन् मा प्रापयन् ये
> परिपंथिनो दंपती आसीदंति अभिगच्छंति । सुगेभिः सुगैर्मार्गैर्दुर्गं दुःखेन
> गंतुं शक्यं दुर्गमं देशमतीतां । अतिगच्छतां । आरातयोऽदात्तारः शत्रवोऽप
> द्रांतु । अपगच्छंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is the yājyā for the bride's journey. It is laid down in the sūtra: at auspicious places, such as a region, a tree or a crossroads, one should mutter "May the waylayers not find" (A. Gṛ. 1-8.6 **NOTE**). May the waylayers, those who stand about, the enemies, not find, not reach, those who come upon the married couple. By easy roads let them pass beyond a hard place, that is, a region difficult to go through. May the enemies, those who give nothing, go away, depart.

### Printed p. 419

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये परिपंथिनः (*ye paripaṃthinaḥ*)—which waylayers, the robbers who guard the road
- दंपती (*daṃpatī*)—this newly married couple
- आसीदंति (*āsīdaṃti*)—those who come confronting them
- मा विदन् (*mā vidan*)—let them not come near these two
- दुर्गं (*durgaṃ*)—the difficult road
- सुगेभिः (*sugebhiḥ*)—by a pleasant journey
- अशीतां (*aśītāṃ*)—may they cross
- अरातयः (*arātayaḥ*)—enemies
- अप द्रांतु (*apa drāṃtu*)—may they run far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the robbers who guard the road and come confronting this newly married couple not come near them. May these two cross safely and pleasantly the region where their road is difficult. May their enemies run far away.

##### English translation
Let not the robbers who approach the husband and wife reach them ; may they by easy roads pass the difficulty ; may enemies keep aloof.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time when the bride travels to the house of her husband, this Ṛk beginning मा विदन् (*mā vidan*) is to be recited. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra, कल्याणेषु देशवृक्ष चतुष्पथेषु मा विदन् परिपंथिन इति जपेत (*kalyāṇeṣu deśavṛkṣa catuṣpatheṣu mā vidan paripaṃthina iti japeta*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-6 **NOTE**).

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सु॒मं॒ग॒लीरि॒यं व॒धूति॒मां स॒मेत॒ पश्य॑त ॥  
> सौभा॑ग्यमस्मै द॒त्वायाथास्तं॒ वि परे॑तन ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुमंगलीः । इयं । वधूः । इमां । संएत । पश्यत ।  
> सौभाग्यं । अस्यै । दत्त्वाय । अथ । अस्तं । वि । परा । इतन ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इयं वधूः सुमंगलीः शोभनमंगला । अत इमां सर्व आशीःकर्तारः
> समेत । संगच्छत । तां पश्यत च । तां संगताश्च दृष्ट्वा स्या ऊढायै सौभाग्यं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This bride is of excellent auspiciousness. Therefore all of you, who are givers of blessings, come together, that is, assemble, and look upon her; and having assembled and seen her, give good fortune to her, the bride,

### Printed p. 420

> दत्त्वा य दत्त्वाथास्तं । गृहनामैतत् । स्वस्वसंबंधिनं वि परेतन । विविधं
> परागच्छत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

and then go each to your own house: अस्तं (*astaṃ*) is a name for a house. Depart in various directions, that is, go away in different ways. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इयं वधूः (*iyaṃ vadhūḥ*)—this bride
- सुमंगलीः (*sumaṃgalīḥ*)—she who is of auspicious form
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—her (O elders)
- समेत (*sameta*)—approach
- पश्यत (*paśyata*)—look upon with a gracious eye
- अस्यै (*asyai*)—to her
- सौभाग्यं (*saubhāgyaṃ*)—the word of blessing
- दत्वाय (*datvāya*)—having given
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to your own several houses
- वि परेतन (*vi paretana*)—go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O elders, this bride is of auspicious form. Approach her and bestow blessings upon her. Then set out for your own several houses.

##### English translation
Fortunate is this bride, approach, behold her; having given her your congratulations, depart to your several homes.

#### Ṛk 34

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तृ॒ष्णमे॒तत्कटु॑कमे॒तद॑पा॒ष्ठव॑द्वि॒षव॒न्नैतदत्त॑वे ॥  
> सू॒र्यां यो ब्र॒ह्मा वि॒द्यात्स इद्वाधू॑यमर्हति ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तृप्तं । एतत् । कटुकं । एतत् । अपाप्यवत् । विषवत् । न । एतत् । अत्तवे ।  
> सूर्यां । यः । ब्रह्मा । विद्यात् । सः । इत् । वाधूयं । अर्हति ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनयापि वधूवस्त्रपरित्यागः प्रतिपाद्यते । एतद्वस्त्रं तृष्टं दाहजनकं ।
> तथैतत्कटुकं । तथापाष्ठवत् । अपाष्ठमपस्थितमृजीषं । तद्वत् । कथा विषवत् ॥
> नैतद्वस्त्रमत्तवे । अत्तव्यं । अनुपयोग्यं । यो ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणः सूर्यामिदानीं
> प्रस्तुतां देवीं विद्यात् सम्यग्ज्ञानीयात् स इत्स एव वाधूयं वधूवस्त्रमर्हति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk too the abandoning of the bride's garment is set forth. This garment is burning, that is, it causes burning; likewise it is pungent; likewise it is like apāṣṭha, that is, ṛjīṣa that has been set aside, like that; and also like poison **NOTE**. This garment is not to be eaten, that is, it is of no use. The Brahman, the Brāhmaṇa, who knows Sūryā, the goddess now under discussion, rightly, he alone is worthy of the bride's garment.

### Printed p. 421

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एतत् (*etat*)—this garment
- तृष्टं (*tṛṣṭaṃ*)—is burning, causing heat
- एतत् (*etat*)—this
- कटुकं (*kaṭukaṃ*)—is of an astringent nature
- अपाष्ठवत् (*apāṣṭhavat*)—is like old Soma called ṛjīṣa
- विषवत् (*viṣavat*)—is like poison
- एतत् (*etat*)—this
- अत्तवे न (*attave na*)—is not fit for use
- यः ब्रह्मा (*yaḥ brahmā*)—the man who knows the mantras, who
- सूर्यां (*sūryāṃ*)—the goddess Sūryā
- विद्युत् (*vidyut*)—knows
- स इत् (*sa it*)—he alone
- वाधूयं (*vādhūyaṃ*)—this garment of the bride
- अर्हति (*arhati*)—becomes worthy to receive

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This garment is burning. It is of an astringent nature. It is like old Soma called ṛjīṣa. It is like poison. It is not fit for use. Only the Brāhmaṇa who knows the nature of the goddess Sūryā becomes worthy to receive this garment of the bride.

##### English translation
This (garment) is inflaming , it is pungent ; it is like stale Soma ; it is like poison ; it is not fit to eat ; the Brahman, who knows Surya, verily desires the bridal (garment).

#### Ṛk 35

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒ शस॑नं वि॒शस॑न॒मथो॑ अधिवि॒कर्त॑नं ।  
> सू॒र्यायाः॑ पश्य रू॒पाणि॒ तानि॑ ब्र॒ह्मा तु शुं॑धति ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आशसनं i विशसनं । अथो इति । अधिविकर्तनं ।  
> सूर्यायाः । पश्य । रूपाणि । तानि । ब्रह्मा । तु । शुंधति ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आशसनं तूषाधानं । तच्चान्यवर्णं भवति । विशसनं शिरसि निधीयमानं ।
> तादृशं दशांते निधीयमानमधिविकर्तनं यत्त्रिधा वासो विकृंतंति । तान्याशसनादीनि वासांस्यवस्थितानि सूर्याया रूपाणि भवंति । तानि पश्य । एवंभूतान्याशसनादीनि पुरा सूर्यास्वशरीरे स्थितान्यमंगलानि वासांसि विधत्ते । तानि रूपाणि
> सूर्याविद्ब्रह्मातु ब्राह्मण विव तस्माद्वाससः सकाशाच्छुंधति । अपनयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The āśasana is the तूषाधानं (*tūṣādhānaṃ*) **NOTE**, and that is of another colour. The viśasana is that which is placed on the head. The adhivikartana is of the same kind, placed at the end of the cloth, one which they cut into three parts as cloth. These cloths, the āśasana and the others, as they are arranged, are the forms of Sūryā. Look at them. Such cloths, the āśasana and the others, inauspicious, which formerly stood on Sūryā's own body, he prescribes **NOTE**. The Brahman, that is the Brāhmaṇa who knows Sūryā, removes those forms from that garment, takes them away.

### Printed p. 422

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरायाः (*sūrāyāḥ*)—of the goddess Sūryā
- आशसनं (*āśasanaṃ*)—the one called āśasana, which lies at the side
- विशसनं (*viśasanaṃ*)—the one called viśasana, which is placed on the head
- अधिविकर्तनं (*adhivikartanaṃ*)—the one called adhivikartana, which is of the nature of a division
- रूपाणि (*rūpāṇi*)—the three forms (garments)
- पश्य (*paśya*)—look
- तानि (*tāni*)—them
- ब्रह्मा तु (*brahmā tu*)—the man who knows the mantras, alone
- शुंधति (*śuṃdhati*)—removes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Look at the three forms (garments) of the goddess Sūryā: the one called āśasana, which lies at the side, the one called viśasana, which is placed on the head, and the one called adhivikartana, which is of the nature of a division. Only the man who knows the mantras removes them.

##### English translation
Beheld the forms of Surya, the ashasana (border-cloth), the Vishasana (head-cloth), the adhivikartana (divided skirt); of these the Brahman relieves her.

#### Ṛk 36

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गृ॒भ्णामि॑ ते सौभग॒त्वाय॒ हस्तं॒ मया॒ पत्या॑ ज॒रद॑ष्टि॒र्यथासः॑ ।  
> भगो॑ अर्य॒मा स॑वि॒ता पुरं॑धि॒र्मह्यं॑ त्वादु॒र्गार्ह॑पत्याय  ॒
> देवाः । ३६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गृभ्वामि । ते । सौभगत्वाय । हस्तं । मया । पत्या । जरत् अष्टिः । यथा । असः ।  
> भगः । अर्यमा । सविता । पुरंथिः । मह्यं । त्वा । अदुः । गार्हपत्याय देवाः॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विवाहे कन्याहस्तग्रहणे गृभ्नामीत्येषा। सूत्रितं च। गृभ्नामि ते सौभगत्वाय
> हस्तमित्यंगुष्ठमेव गृह्णीयात् । आ. गृ.. १-७-३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the marriage, in taking the hand of the maiden, the Ṛk गृभ्नामि (*gṛbhnāmi*) is used. It is laid down in the sūtra: गृभ्नामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तमित्यंगुष्ठमेव गृह्णीयात् (*gṛbhnāmi te saubhagatvāya hastamityaṃguṣṭhameva gṛhṇīyāt*), that is, with this he should take the thumb only (Ā. Gṛ. 1-7-3 **NOTE**).

### Printed p. 423

> हे वधु ते तव हस्तमहं गृभ्णामि । गृह्णामि । किमर्थं । सौभगत्वाय
> सौभाग्याय । मया पत्या त्वं यथा जरदष्टिः प्राप्तवार्धक्यासः भवसि । भगोऽर्यमा सविता पुरंधिः पूषा एते देवास्त्वा त्वां मह्यमदुः । दत्तवंतः । किमर्थं
> गार्हपत्याय । यथाहं गृहपतिः स्यामिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bride, I take your hand, I grasp it. For what purpose? For good fortune. So that you, with me as husband, may become jaradaṣṭi, one who has reached old age. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Purandhi, that is Pūṣan, these gods have given you to me. For what purpose? For the mastership of the house, so that I may be master of the house.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ते (*te*)—your
- हस्तं (*hastaṃ*)—hand
- सौभगत्वाय (*saubhagatvāya*)—for the accomplishment of welfare
- गृभ्णामि (*gṛbhṇāmi*)—I take
- यथा (*yathā*)—by this very relation
- पत्या मया (*patyā mayā*)—with me, your husband
- जरदष्टिः असः (*jaradaṣṭiḥ asaḥ*)—you will attain old age
- गार्हपत्याय (*gārhapatyāya*)—that I may become the protector of the house
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods who are of divine nature
- भगः (*bhagaḥ*)—Bhaga
- अरमा (*aramā*)—Aryaman
- सविता (*savitā*)—Savitṛ
- पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—the god Pūṣan
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—to me
- अदुः (*aduḥ*)—have given

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I take your hand for the accomplishment of welfare. By this very relation, remain with me, your husband, until you attain old age. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Pūṣan, who are of divine nature, have given you to me, that I may become master of the house (a householder).

##### English translation
I take your hand for good fortune, that you may attain old age with me as your husband ; the gods Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitri, Pnrandhi have given you to me, that I may be the master of a household-

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the time of marriage, while taking the hand of the maiden, this Ṛk beginning गृभ्णामि (*gṛbhṇāmi*) is to be recited. This is set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra, गृभ्णामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तमित्यंगुष्ठमेव गृह्णीयात् (*gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastamityaṃguṣṭhameva gṛhṇīyāt*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-7-3 **NOTE**).

गृभ्नामि ते सौभगत्वाय हस्तं (*gṛbhnāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ*)—"O bride, for the sake of all prosperity and for the attainment of welfare, at this time of marriage I take your hand," thus the bridegroom says, addressing the bride, and he acts accordingly.

मया पत्या जरदृष्टिः यथा असः (*mayā patyā jaradṛṣṭiḥ yathā asaḥ*)—"O bride, with me, your husband, for a long time, that is, until we both become old, that is, until the body grows slack with old age, carry on your life in the world and live happily."

भगो आर्यमा सविता पुरंधिः देवाः त्वां मह्यं गार्हपत्याय अदुः (*bhago āryamā savitā puraṃdhiḥ devāḥ tvāṃ mahyaṃ gārhapatyāya aduḥ*)—

### Printed p. 424

"O bride, the gods Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, Pūṣan and the others have given you to me, that we both may perform the duties of action in the householder's stage of life," thus the bridegroom says, addressing the bride.

#### Ṛk 37

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तां पू॑षञ्भा॒वत॑मा॒मेर॑यस्व॒ यस्यां॒ बीजं॑ मनु॒ष्या॒३॒॑ ३  ॑
> वपंति ।  
> या न॑ ऊ॒रू उ॑श॒ती वि॒श्रया॑ते॒ यस्या॑मु॒शंतः॑ प्र॒हरा॑म॒  ॑
> शेषं ॥ ३७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तां । पूषन् । शिवतमां । आ । ईरयस्व । यस्यां । बीजं । मनुष्याः । वपंति ।  
> या । नः । ऊरू इति । उशती । विश्रयाते । यस्यां । उशंतः । प्रहराम ।  
> शेषं ॥ ३७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पूषन्नोषकैतन्नामक देव शिवतमामत्यंतमंगलभूतां तामेरयस्व । आ ईरय । सर्वतः प्रेरय । यस्यामूरौ बीजं रेतोलक्षणं मनुष्या
> वपंति आदधते । या नोऽस्माकमूरू उशती कामयमाना विश्रयाते । यस्यामूरावुशंतः कामयमाना वयं शेषं स्पर्शनयोग्यं पुंसृजननं प्रहराम ।
> ऊरौ व्यंजनसंबंधं करवामेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pūṣan, god of that name, the nourisher, send, urge on from all sides her, the most auspicious one, in whose thigh men sow seed, of the nature of semen. She who, desiring us, spreads her thighs; in whom we, desiring, shall insert the शेषं (*śeṣaṃ*), that which is fit for touching, the male generative organ: that is, let us bring about the contact of the organs with the thighs.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पूषन् (*pūṣan*)—O god Pūṣan
- यस्यां (*yasyāṃ*)—in whom
- बीजं (*bījaṃ*)—the seed in the form of semen
- मनुष्याः (*manuṣyāḥ*)—men
- वपंति (*vapaṃti*)—they establish
- या (*yā*)—she who
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊरू (*ūrū*)—union
- उशती (*uśatī*)—desiring
- विश्रयाते (*viśrayāte*)—she welcomes
- यस्यां (*yasyāṃ*)—in whom
- उशंतः (*uśaṃtaḥ*)—wishing for sons
- शेषं (*śeṣaṃ*)—the seed that produces sons (the male organ)
- प्रचराम (*pracarāma*)—we shall establish
- शिवतमां तां (*śivatamāṃ tāṃ*)—her, who brings good fortune
- एरयस्व (*erayasva*)—urge her to love us

### Printed p. 425

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Pūṣan, urge her to love us: her in whom men establish the seed in the form of semen, who desires our union and receives us, and in whom we, wishing for sons, shall establish the seed that produces sons (the male organ).

##### English translation
Pushan, inspire her who is most aaspicious, in whom men may sow seed, who most affectionate may be devoted to us, and in whom animated by desire we may beget progeny.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the word शेषं (*śeṣaṃ*) in the sentence यस्यामुशंतः प्रहराम शेषं (*yasyāmuśaṃtaḥ praharāma śeṣaṃ*), which is the last pāda of this Ṛk, Yāska has stated the explanation in this way:

शेपो वैतस इति पुंस्प्रजननस्य । शेषः शपतॆः स्मृशतिकर्मणः वैतसो वितस्तं भवति । यस्मामुशंतः प्रहराम शेषं । त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेन इत्यपि निगमौ भवतः ॥ (*śepo vaitasa iti puṃsprajananasya | śeṣaḥ śapatèḥ smṛśatikarmaṇaḥ vaitaso vitastaṃ bhavati | yasmāmuśaṃtaḥ praharāma śeṣaṃ | triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasena ityapi nigamau bhavataḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-21) **NOTE**

The two words शेपः (*śepaḥ*) and वैतसः (*vaitasaḥ*) both denote the organ of generation of the man, that is, the male member. The word शेपः (*śepaḥ*) is formed from the root meaning to touch, to feel; for with this organ the man touches the woman (the woman's yoni). वैतस (*vaitasa*) means the part of the male member that is like a rod (penis); for when there is no contact with a woman it is वितस्तं (*vitastaṃ*), that is, it lies in a dormant state without excitement. Therefore it is called वैतस (*vaitasa*). Yāska has given as examples two Śruti sentences in which these words are used.

यस्यामुशंतः प्रहराम शेषं । (*yasyāmuśaṃtaḥ praharāma śeṣaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.85.37)

This sentence stands in the last pāda of the present Ṛk. The chief meaning of this sentence is: O Pūṣan, urge to love us that woman we love, in whom (or in whose yoni) we place our male member.

त्रिः स्म माह्नः श्नथयो वैतसेन (*triḥ sma māhnaḥ śnathayo vaitasena*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-5)

In this sentence Urvaśī, addressing Purūravas, speaks thus: O Purūravas, on three days you have beaten me (the region of my yoni) with the rod of your male member. This is the chief meaning of this sentence. वैतस (*vaitasa*) means the part of the male member that is like a rod.

#### Ṛk 38

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तुभ्य॒मग्रे॒ पर्य॑वहन्सू॒र्यां व॑ह॒तुना॑ स॒ह ।  
> पुनः॒ पति॑भ्यो जा॒यां दा अ॑ग्ने प्र॒जया॑ स॒ह ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यं । अग्रे । परि । अवहन् । सूर्यां । वहतुना । सह ।  
> पुनरिति । पतिभ्यः । जायां । दाः । अग्ने । प्रजया । सह ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गंधर्वा हे अग्ने तुभ्यमग्रे पर्यवहन् । प्रायच्छन्नित्यर्थः । कां ।
> सूर्यां । केन सह । वहतुना सह। वहतुना सह । त्वं च तां सूर्यां वहतुना
> सह सोमाय प्रायच्छः । तद्वदिदानीमपि हे अग्ने पुनः पतिभ्योऽस्मभ्यं जायां
> प्रजया सह दाः । देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Gandharvas, O Agni, offered to you first, that is, gave. Whom? Sūryā. With what? With the वहतुना (*vahatunā*). And you gave that Sūryā with the वहतुना (*vahatunā*) to Soma **NOTE**. As then, so now also, O Agni, give back to us, the husbands, the wife together with offspring.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- अग्रे (*agre*)—first
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- सूर्यां (*sūryāṃ*)—Sūryā
- वहतुना सह (*vahatunā saha*)—together with ornaments
- पर्यवहन् (*paryavahan*)—the Gandharvas gave
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—now
- पतिभ्यः (*patibhyaḥ*)—to us, who are men
- जायां (*jāyāṃ*)—the wife
- प्रजया सह (*prajayā saha*)—together with offspring
- दाः (*dāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, first the Gandharvas gave Sūryā to you together with ornaments. Now give to us, who are of human form, a wife fit for offspring.

##### English translation
(The Gandharvas) gave Surya to you, Agni, with her bridal ornaments ; do you, Agni, give (us) husbands our wife back again with male offspring.

#### Ṛk 39

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुनः॒ पत्नि॑म॒ग्निर॑ददा॒दायु॑षा स॒ह वर्च॑सा ।

### Printed p. 427

> दीर्घायुरस्या यः पति जीवाति शरदः शतं ॥ ३९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुनरिति । पत्नीं । अग्निः । अदात् । आयुषा । सह । वर्चसा ।  
> दीर्घआयुः । अस्त्याः । यः । पतिः । जीवाति । शरदः । शतं ॥ ३९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनः स्वगृहीतां पत्निमग्निरायुषा सह वर्चसा सहादात् । प्रायच्छत् ।
> अस्या अग्निदत्ताया यः पतिः पुमान् स दीर्घायुः सञ्वरदः शतं शतसंवत्सरं
> जीवाति । जीवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni gave back the wife whom he had taken, together with life and lustre. Of her, given by Agni, whoever is the husband, the man, let him live a hundred years, long-lived.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—after obtaining the wife
- पत्निं (*patniṃ*)—her
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- आयुषा सह (*āyuṣā saha*)—together with long life
- वर्चसा (*varcasā*)—and with lustre
- अदात् (*adāt*)—gave (to the man)
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—of her
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—becomes the husband, he
- दीर्घायुः (*dīrghāyuḥ*)—being long-lived
- शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*)—for a hundred years
- जीवाति (*jīvāti*)—lives

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After obtaining the wife, Agni gave to the man the wife together with long life and lustre. He who becomes her husband, being long-lived, lives a hundred years (may he live).

##### English translation
Agni gave the wife back agaia with life and splendour : may he who is her husband enjoying long-life live a hundred years.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk it is said पुनः पत्नीं अग्निः अदात् (*punaḥ patnīṃ agniḥ adāt*): after the marriage Agni gave the wife again to the bridegroom. What is the propriety of the use of the word पुनः (*punaḥ*) here? It is this. As is said in the Ṛk

सोमोददद्दंधर्वाय गंधर्वोऽददग्नये । रयिं च पुत्रांश्चादग्निर्मह्यमथो इमां ॥ (*somodadaddaṃdharvāya gaṃdharvo 'dadagnaye | rayiṃ ca putrāṃścādagnirmahyamatho imāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-55.41 **NOTE**)

### Printed p. 428

Soma gave the maiden who was in his power to the Gandharva. The Gandharva gave that bride to Agni. Afterwards Agni gave the maiden whom he had received again to the bridegroom, a man **NOTE**. Because the maiden is thus given from one to another, that is, because she is given more than once, पुनः (*punaḥ*) is said here.

Besides, when Soma gives the maiden into the power of the Gandharva, and when the Gandharva gives her into the power of Agni, only the maiden (without any other things) is given from one to another. But Agni does not give back to the man the maiden who has come into his power in that same state. He gives her joined with long life and lustre. Therefore in the present Ṛk it is said आयुषा सह वर्चसा (*āyuṣā saha varcasā*). The words आयुषा (*āyuṣā*) and वर्चसा (*varcasā*) may apply both to the maiden and to her husband. But in the latter half of this Ṛk the matter of long life applies to the bridegroom only. In the sentence दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जिवाति शरदः शतं (*dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjivāti śaradaḥ śataṃ*) there is the assurance that the bridegroom who is the husband of this bride, that is, of this bride who at the time of marriage has been consecrated with Agni first, may live a hundred years, and Agni delivers the bride into the power of the bridegroom together with long life. This very matter is set forth in the present Ṛk by the sentence पुनः पत्निमग्नि रदात् (*punaḥ patnimagni radāt*).

For the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) in this Ṛk Yāska has stated the explanation शरच्छता अस्यानोषधयो भवंति । शीर्णा आप इति वा (*śaracchatā asyānoṣadhayo bhavaṃti | śīrṇā āpa iti vā*) (Ni. 4-25). In the autumn season, after the creepers, trees, herbs and plants, the whole vegetable kingdom, have dropped their fruits and the like, the leaves and the like also fall; or, because fruits ripen in this season, the season has the name śarat; or, in this season the water in rivers and other reservoirs becomes less. As there is no rain of the rainy season, the water of the reservoirs dries up and only a little water remains. Therefore this season has the name śarat. शरद्दि दुर्जिवा रोगभूयस्त्वात् : आत एवमाशास्त्रते शरच्छतं जीवत्विति । (*śaraddi durjivā rogabhūyastvāt : āta evamāśāstrate śaracchataṃ jīvatviti |*) In the autumn, because of the change of the atmosphere, many kinds of diseases and ailments befall men. Therefore it is hard to pass through this autumn season. If one autumn is passed, one can be happy for a year. And since the autumn comes only once in a year, it is the custom in the Vedas to use the word śarat to indicate the measure of a year. जीवाति शरदः शतं (*jīvāti śaradaḥ śataṃ*) means: he lives for a hundred years.

For the words शरदः शतं (*śaradaḥ śataṃ*) in the sense 'a hundred years', many examples of sentences can be given, such as

पश्येम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतं नंदाम शरदः शतं मोदाम शरदः शतं भवाम शरदः शतग्ं शृणवाम शरदः शतं प्रब्रवाम शरदः शतं अजीतास्स्याम शरदः शतं ॥ (*paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ naṃdāma śaradaḥ śataṃ modāma śaradaḥ śataṃ bhavāma śaradaḥ śatagṃ śṛṇavāma śaradaḥ śataṃ prabravāma śaradaḥ śataṃ ajītāssyāma śaradaḥ śataṃ ‖*) (Tai. Ā. 4-41-6) **GLOSS**

#### Ṛk 40

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमः॑ प्रथ॒मो वि॑विदे गंध॒र्वो वि॑विद॒ उत्त॑रः ।  
> तृ॒तीयोः॑ अ॒ग्निष्टे॒ पति॑स्तु॒रीय॑स्ते मनुष्य॒जाः ॥ ४० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमः । प्रथमः । विविदे । गंधर्वः । विविदे । उत्तरः ।  
> तृतीयः । अग्निः । ते । पतिः । तुरीयः । ते । मनुष्यजाः ॥ ४० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जातां कन्यां सोमः प्रथमभावी सन् विविदे । लब्धवान् । गंधर्व
> उत्तरः सन् विविदे । लब्धवान् । अग्निस्तृतीयः पतिस्ते तव । पश्चान्मनुष्यजाः
> पतिस्तुरीयश्चतुर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being the first, obtained, won, the maiden once born. The Gandharva, being the next, obtained her. Agni is your third husband; afterwards the husband born of man is the fourth, the turīya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—first
- विविदे (*vivide*)—obtained the maiden
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—afterwards
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—the Gandharva
- विविदे (*vivide*)—obtained (O maiden)
- ते (*te*)—to you
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- तृतीयः पतिः (*tṛtīyaḥ patiḥ*)—the third husband
- ते (*te*)—to you (afterwards)
- मनुष्यजाः (*manuṣyajāḥ*)—the husband born among men
- तुरीयः (*turīyaḥ*)—the fourth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O maiden, Soma obtained you first. Afterwards the Gandharva obtained you. Agni is your third husband. The husband who is a man is the fourth.

##### English translation
Soma first obtained the bride; the Gandharva obtained her next ; Agni was your third husband ; your fourth (husband) is born of man.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the sentence तृतीयो आगिष्टे पतिः (*tṛtīyo āgiṣṭe patiḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has stated the Nirukta explanation.

### Printed p. 430

सेनेव सृष्टामं दधात्यस्तुर्न दिद्युत्वेषप्रतीका । यनो ह जातो यमो जनित्वं जारः कनीनां पतिर्जनीनां ॥ (*seneva sṛṣṭāmaṃ dadhātyasturna didyutveṣapratīkā | yano ha jāto yamo janitvaṃ jāraḥ kanīnāṃ patirjanīnāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-66-4) **GLOSS**

When giving the Nirukta explanation of this Ṛk, he explains the relation between Agni and the maiden. There, for the sentence जारः कनीनां पतिर्जनीनां (*jāraḥ kanīnāṃ patirjanīnāṃ*) he has said जारः कनीनां जरयिता कन्यानां पतिर्जनीनां पालयिता जायानां । तत्पधाना हि यज्ञसंयोगेन भवंति ॥ (*jāraḥ kanīnāṃ jarayitā kanyānāṃ patirjanīnāṃ pālayitā jāyānāṃ | tatpadhānā hi yajñasaṃyogena bhavaṃti ‖*) Agni is the beloved of maidens and the one who changes their condition, that is, who brings them from the state of maidenhood to the state of a mature woman. How? Before marriage the maiden is ordinarily in childhood. After marriage, by the rites in the presence of Agni (homa and the like), she is regarded as a mature woman and as fit for the enjoyment of her husband. Since in this way she passes from one state to another, the age of the maiden is passed over; the age of maturity is greater than the age of maidenhood. That Agni is the cause of this passing over of age is described by जरयिता कन्यानां (*jarayitā kanyānāṃ*): one who makes the age of the maiden wear out, that is, pass away. Besides, for the words पतिर्जनीनां (*patirjanīnāṃ*) he has said पालयिता जायानां (*pālayitā jāyānāṃ*), the protector of wives. What is meant by Agni being the protector of wives? After marriage the wife, together with her husband, has to perform in the fire the aupāsana and other rites, vows and the like, and the attendance on the fire. The author of the Nirukta has made this clear by the explanation

तं वश्चराथा चरंत्या पश्वाहुत्या वसत्या च निवसंत्यौषधाहुत्यास्तं यथा गाव आप्नुवंति तथाप्यनुयामेद्धं समिद्धं भोगैः ॥ (*taṃ vaścarāthā caraṃtyā paśvāhutyā vasatyā ca nivasaṃtyauṣadhāhutyāstaṃ yathā gāva āpnuvaṃti tathāpyanuyāmeddhaṃ samiddhaṃ bhogaiḥ ‖*) (Ni. 10-21)

That is: in order to perform the acts of attendance, such as offering moving things such as animals into the fire (sacrificial rites and the like) and offering with kindling sticks and the like of the unmoving herbs and trees, one should approach the blazing fire, as cows approach their house (the cowshed), and serve it with ghee and other substances that are means of enjoyment. By such attendance on the fire, Agni, pleased, becomes the giver of enjoyment and the like to the wife and also to the husband. Because there is such a relation, that is, because he is the bestower of favour, Agni is called the protector of the wife. That such an Agni, O bride, is your husband, that is, your protector, is the chief meaning of the sentence तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिः (*tṛtīyo agniṣṭe patiḥ*) in the third pāda of the present Ṛk.

#### Ṛk 41

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमो॑ ददद्गंध॒र्वाय॑ गंध॒र्वो द॑दद॒ग्नये॑ ।  
> र॒यिं च॑ पु॒त्रांश्चा॑दा॒ग्निर्मह्य॒मथो॑ इ॒मां ॥ ४१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमः । ददत् । गंधर्वाय । गंधर्वः । ददत् । अग्नये ।  
> रयिं । च । पुत्रान् । च । अदात् । अग्निः । मह्यं । अथो इति । इमां ॥ ४१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोमो गंधर्वाय प्रथदुं ददत् । प्रादात् । गंधर्वोऽग्नये प्रादात् ।
> अथो अपि चाग्निरिमां कन्यां रयिं धनं पुत्रांश्च मह्यमदात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma gave to the Gandharva first **NOTE**; he gave, offered. The Gandharva offered to Agni. And then Agni gave to me this maiden, wealth and sons.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- गंधर्वाय (*gaṃdharvāya*)—to the Gandharva
- ददत् (*dadat*)—first gave the maiden
- गंधर्वः (*gaṃdharvaḥ*)—the Gandharva
- अग्नये ददत् (*agnaye dadat*)—afterwards gave to Agni
- अथो (*atho*)—afterwards
- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Agni
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—this maiden
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- पुत्रांश्च (*putrāṃśca*)—and sons
- मह्यं (*mahyaṃ*)—to me
- अदात् (*adāt*)—gave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

First Soma gave this maiden to the Gandharva. Afterwards the Gandharva gave her to Agni. In the end Agni gave me her, and together with her wealth and sons.

##### English translation
Soma gave her to the Gandharva ; the Gandharva gave her to Agni; Agni has given her to me and wealth and sons.

> क्रीळं॑तौ पु॒त्रैर्नप्तृ॑भि॒र्मोद॑मानौ॒ स्वे गृ॒हे ॥ ४२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इह । एव । स्तं । मा । वि । यौष्टं । विश्वं । आयुः । वि । अश्नुतं ।  
> क्रीळंतौ । पुत्रैः । नप्तृभिः । मोदमानौ । स्वे । गृहे ॥ ४२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इहैव स्तं । इहैवास्मिंल्लोके स्तं । भवतं। मा वि यौष्टं । मा पृथग्भूतं।
> विश्वमायुर्व्यश्नुतं । प्राप्तुतं । किंच पुत्रैर्नप्तृभिः पौत्रैः सह स्वे गृहे
> मोदमाना भवतमिति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Remain here itself, in this world: be. Do not be separated. Attain the whole span of life. And further, with sons and नप्तृभिः (*naptṛbhiḥ*), that is, grandsons, be rejoicing in your own house: the word "be" is the remainder to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इहैव स्तं (*ihaiva staṃ*)—(O maiden) let us be in this world itself
- मा वियौष्टं (*mā viyauṣṭaṃ*)—let us not be separated
- स्वे गृहे (*sve gṛhe*)—in our own house
- पुत्रैः (*putraiḥ*)—with sons
- नप्तृभिः (*naptṛbhiḥ*)—with grandsons
- क्रीळंतौ (*krīḷaṃtau*)—playing
- मोदमानौ (*modamānau*)—experiencing joy
- विश्वं आयुः (*viśvaṃ āyuḥ*)—the full span of life
- व्यश्नुतं (*vyaśnutaṃ*)—let us enjoy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O maiden, let us be in this world itself; let us not be separated; in our own house, with sons and with grandsons, playing and experiencing joy, let us enjoy the full span of life.

##### English translation
Abide here together; may you never be separated; live together all your lives, sporting with sons and grand-sons, happy in your own home

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the sentence अर्थवंतः शॆब्दसामान्यात् (*arthavaṃtaḥ śèbdasāmānyāt*) Yāska has spoken thus. As a rule, the meaning that words have in common use is the very meaning to be stated in each context. Only in some special contexts do words have both a general meaning and a special meaning. In this matter he cites

एतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियामाणमृग्यजुर्वाभिवदतीति च ब्राह्मणं । क्रीळंतौ पुत्रैर्नप्तृभिरिति ॥ (*etadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyāmāṇamṛgyajurvābhivadatīti ca brāhmaṇaṃ | krīḷaṃtau putrairnaptṛbhiriti ‖*) (Ni. 1.16)

### Printed p. 433

as a Brāhmaṇa sentence. Its meaning is this. When a rite is performed in a sacrifice and the like, the mantra relating to it has to be recited. The mantra recited on that occasion must accord with that rite, that is, it must be related to the matter stated in that rite. When there is such a mutual relation between the mantra and the rite, it is called समृद्ध (*samṛddha*) or रूपसमृद्ध (*rūpasamṛddha*). रूपसमृद्ध (*rūpasamṛddha*) means that, in accordance with the form of the rite, the mantra recited, whether a Ṛk or a Yajus, must be related to that very rite. Only so is that rite duly completed and the appointed fruit obtained. If there is no mutual relation between the rite performed and the mantra recited, it cannot be called समृद्ध (*samṛddha*) or रूपसमृद्ध (*rūpasamṛddha*).

Another kind of meaning also is in use for the word समृद्ध (*samṛddha*). On this occasion समृद्ध (*samṛddha*) means the abundant attainment of the means of worldly happiness, such as food, wealth, house, sons and the like. These are called समृद्धि (*samṛddhi*) or समृद्ध (*samṛddha*). To explain a meaning of this kind Yāska has given as an example the sentence क्रीळंतौ पुत्रैर्नप्तृभिर्मोदमानौ स्वे गृहे (*krīḷaṃtau putrairnaptṛbhirmodamānau sve gṛhe*) in the present Ṛk. In this sentence the bridegroom, addressing the bride, says: O bride, let us both, enjoying happiness and delight with the sons we shall obtain in the future and with grandsons, dwell in a house of our own. The word समृद्ध (*samṛddha*) here denotes both the obtaining of offspring such as sons and grandsons, and dwelling with them in a house of one's own with happiness, delight and the like, without the experience of sorrow and the like.

#### Ṛk 43

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नः॑ प्र॒जां ज॑नयतु प्र॒जाप॑तिराजर॒साय॒ सम॑नक्त्यर्य॒मा।  
> अदु॑र्मंगलीः पतिलो॒कमा वि॑श॒ शं नो॑ भव द्वि॒पदे॒ शं  ॑
> चतुष्पदे ॥ ४३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । प्रजां । जनयतु । प्रजापतिः । आजरसाय । सं । अनक्तु । अर्यमा ।  
> अदुःमंगलीः । पतिलोकं । आ । विश । शं । नः । भव । द्विपदे । शं । चतुःपदे॥

### Printed p. 434

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गृहप्रवेश आ नः प्रजां जनयत्वित्याद्याश्चतस्रो होमार्थाः । सूत्रितं च ।
> आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिरिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा । अ. गृ. १-८-९ । इति ॥
> प्रजापतिर्देवो नोऽस्माकं प्रजामा जनयतु । अर्यमा चाजरसाय
> जरापर्यंतं जीवनाय समनक्तु! संगमयतु । सा। त्वमदुर्मंगलीर्दुमंगलरहिता सुमंगली । यद्वा । या मंगलाचारान्सूषयति सा दुर्मंगली ।
> ततोऽन्यादुर्मंगली । तादृशी सती पतिलोकं पतिसमीपमा विश । प्राप्नुहि ।
> नोऽस्माकं द्विपदे शं भव । तथा च शं चतुष्पदे भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

At the house-entry the four Ṛks beginning आ नः प्रजां जनयतु (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu*) are for the homa. It is laid down in the sūtra: आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिरिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatiriti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcaṃ hutvā*) (A. Gṛ. 1-8-9 **NOTE**). May the god Prajāpati beget offspring for us. And may Aryaman bring us together for life up to old age. You, अदुर्मंगलीः (*adurmaṃgalīḥ*), free from inauspiciousness, are a sumaṅgalī. Or else: she who spoils **NOTE** auspicious observances is durmaṅgalī; the other is adurmaṅgalī. Being such, enter, reach, your husband's abode, that is, the neighbourhood of your husband. Be a source of welfare to our bipeds, and likewise a source of welfare to our quadrupeds.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रजापतिः (*prajāpatiḥ*)—Prajāpati
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- प्रजां (*prajāṃ*)—sons
- आ जनयतु (*ā janayatu*)—may he bestow
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—Aryaman
- आजरसाय (*ājarasāya*)—to live until old age
- समनक्तु (*samanaktu*)—may he keep us together (O maiden)
- अदुर्मंगलीः (*adurmaṃgalīḥ*)—without marks that cause ruin
- पतिलोकं (*patilokaṃ*)—your husband's house
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- द्विपदे (*dvipade*)—to sons and the like
- शं भव (*śaṃ bhava*)—be a bringer of good fortune
- चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*)—to cattle and the like
- शं (*śaṃ*)—be a bringer of happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Prajāpati bestow sons upon us. May Aryaman favour us so that we remain together up to old age. O maiden, enter your husband's house without marks that cause ruin. Bring good to our sons and the like, and to our cattle and the like.

##### English translation
May Prajapati grant us progeny, may Aryaman unite us together until old age ; free from all evil omens enter your husband's abode, be the bringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the house-entry homa performed at the time of marriage, the four Ṛks beginning आ नः प्रजां जनयतु (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu*) are to be recited and the principal oblation offered, as set forth by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana-gṛhya-sūtra आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिरिति चतसृभिः प्रत्यृचं हुत्वा (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatiriti catasṛbhiḥ pratyṛcaṃ hutvā*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-9 **NOTE**).

### Printed p. 435

आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिः (*ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatiḥ*)—प्रजापतिर्देवोऽस्माकं प्रजां जनयतु । (*prajāpatirdevo 'smākaṃ prajāṃ janayatu |*) May Prajāpati, the lord of all, bring about offspring and the like for us, the newly wedded couple: thus the husband, or the newly married couple, desire, or they pray to Prajāpati.

आजरसाय सं अनक्तु अर्यमा (*ājarasāya saṃ anaktu aryamā*)—देवोऽर्यमा च जरापर्यंतं जीवनाय संगमयतु । (*devo 'ryamā ca jarāparyaṃtaṃ jīvanāya saṃgamayatu |*) May the god called Aryaman also grant that we, the couple, do not part from each other until we grow old through the slackening of the body, that is, as long as we live.

अदुर्मंगलीः पतिलोकं आ विश (*adurmaṃgalīḥ patilokaṃ ā viśa*)—Here two kinds of meaning can be given for the word अदुर्मंगलीः (*adurmaṃgalīḥ*). मंगल (*maṃgala*) means good, welfare, what is auspicious. दुर्मंगल (*durmaṃgala*) means what is not मंगल (*maṃgala*), what is inauspicious. दुर्मंगलीः (*durmaṃgalīḥ*) means a woman who is not auspicious, not propitious, of bad disposition; अदुर्मंगलीः (*adurmaṃgalīḥ*) means one who is not दुर्मंगली (*durmaṃgalī*), not of bad disposition, not inauspicious, that is, a woman of good disposition, who brings welfare, auspicious or bestowing auspiciousness, a sumaṅgalī, a virtuous wife. Or else, मंगलाचारान् दूषयति सा दुर्मंगली । ततोऽन्या अदुर्मंगलीः (*maṃgalācārān dūṣayati sā durmaṃgalī | tato 'nyā adurmaṃgalīḥ*): she who disparages, or hates, or has no interest in, or does not practise, excellent and auspicious good acts such as worship of the gods is called दुर्मंगली (*durmaṃgalī*). A woman of the opposite disposition is called अदुर्मंगलीः (*adurmaṃgalīḥ*); that is, a woman with good qualities, such as good conduct and the practice of auspicious rites, is called अदुर्मंगलि (*adurmaṃgali*) or sumaṅgalī. In this sentence the meaning is stated: O bride, you, endowed with the good qualities spoken of above and a sumaṅgalī, go to the place where your husband is, that is, come into your husband's nearness.

शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे (*śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade*)—Here द्विपदे (*dvipade*) means men, who have two feet; चतुष्पदे (*catuṣpade*) means animals such as cows, which have four feet. O bride, after you have reached your husband's house, be agreeable, speaking good words, to your husband's kinsmen there, the brother-in-law, mother-in-law, father-in-law and the like, and to the servants and the rest of the household; and in regard to the animals in the house, the cows, horses and the like, behave with kindness and compassion and look after their welfare properly: this is the chief meaning of this sentence.

#### Ṛk 44

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अघो॑रचक्षु॒रप॑तिघ्न्येधि शि॒वा प॒शुभ्यः॑ सु॒मनाः॑ सु॒वर्चाः॑ ।  
> वी॒र॒सूर्दे॒वका॑मा स्यो॒ना शं नो॑ भव द्वि॒पदे॒ शं चतु॑ष्पदे॥

### Printed p. 436

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अघोरचक्षुः । अपतिघ्नी । विधि । शिवा । पशुभ्यः । सुमनाः । सुवर्चाः ।  
> वीरसूः । देवकामा । स्नोना । शं । नः । भव । द्विपदे । शं । चतुःपदे ॥४४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वधु त्वमघोरचक्षुः क्रोधादभयंकरचक्षुरेधि । भव । तथापतिघ्नी
> भव । तथा पशुभ्यः शिवा हितकरी भव । सुमनाः सुवर्चाश्च भव । वीरसूः पुत्राणामेव प्रसवित्रि देवकामा स्कोना सुखिकरा च भव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bride, be one whose eye is not terrible, whose eye is not fearful through anger. Likewise be not a slayer of your husband. Likewise be auspicious, beneficial, to the cattle. Be well-minded and of good lustre. Be वीरसूः (*vīrasūḥ*), the bearer of sons only, be devoted to the gods, and be स्कोना (*skonā*) **NOTE**, a giver of happiness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—(O bride) you
- अघोरचक्षुः (*aghoracakṣuḥ*)—without a terrible look
- विधि (*vidhi*)—approach your husband
- अपतिघ्नी (*apatighnī*)—do not wish your husband harm
- पशुभ्यः (*paśubhyaḥ*)—to the cattle
- शिवा (*śivā*)—be beneficial
- सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*)—be pleasant-faced
- सुवर्चाः (*suvarcāḥ*)—be of good lustre
- वीरसूः (*vīrasūḥ*)—one who bears heroic sons
- देवकामा (*devakāmā*)—one devoted to the worship of the gods
- स्कोना (*skonā*)—and be a bringer of happiness

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, approach your husband without a terrible look (a cruel glance). Do not wish your husband harm. Be beneficial to the cattle, pleasant-faced and full of lustre. Bear heroic sons, be devoted to the worship of the gods, and be a bringer of happiness.

##### English translation
(Look upon your husband) with no angry eye, be not hostile to your lord, be tender to animals, be amiable, be very glorious; be the mother of males, be devoted to the gods, be the bestower of happiness, be the bringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds,

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

आघोरचक्षुः (*āghoracakṣuḥ*)—It is desired that the bride's look be gentle and not cruel through anger and the like, and that the bride be of a smiling countenance. Whether women or men, the expression of the face depends on the eyes. If there are anger, grief and the like in the mind, they show in the eyes and spoil the very beauty of the face. If, on the other hand, there are joy in the mind and friendliness, kindness and a helpful spirit towards others, the eyes are gentle and agreeable and increase the beauty of the face. Therefore it is said here that the bride should be of a gentle look.

### Printed p. 437

अपतिघ्नी (*apatighnī*)—It is desired that she do no harm to her husband, that is, do no act that is not beneficial to her husband.

शिवा पशुभ्यः (*śivā paśubhyaḥ*)—Towards cattle and the other animals: the meaning is that she should look after them well, put down grass, water and the like at the proper times, and be watchful in guarding them.

सुमनाः, सुवर्चाः (*sumanāḥ, suvarcāḥ*)—Being of good mind means that she should not wish harm to anyone even in her mind, but should also be endowed with courtesy and modesty in speech, speaking only kind words and always wishing that all may fare well. This kind of conduct is called सुमनाः (*sumanāḥ*). सुवर्चाः (*suvarcāḥ*) means that to be adorned with clean clothes, ornaments and the like and to be devoted to works for the good of others is what is called splendour. It is desired that she be endowed with such splendour.

वीरसू (*vīrasū*)—The chief duties of a wife are to serve her husband, to assist him in the performance of good rites, and to bear excellent sons. In those days the Āryas had often to fight against the dark people called Dasyus, the inhabitants of this country, and so the need for heroic sons was very great. Therefore, even when praying to the gods, it is the custom of the seers to pray many times that heroic sons, grandsons and the like be given. Here too it is desired that the new bride bear heroic sons.

देवकामाः (*devakāmāḥ*)—It is desired that she be devoted to the duties owed to the gods, that is, to good rites such as sacrifices, and that she be a helper to her husband in them.

स्येना शं नो भव द्विपदे शं चतुष्पदे (*syenā śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade*)—To us, that is, to us the bride's relatives, to the household and the servants and the rest, she is assured that she will not only bring happiness with affection and respect, but also, behaving with compassion and sympathy towards other people and towards cows and the other animals, will bring happiness to all by her conduct.

> दशा॑स्यां पु॒त्राना धे॑हि॒ पति॑मेकाद॒शं कृ॑धि ॥ ४५ ॥

> दश । अस्क्यां । पुत्रान् । आ । धेहि । पतिं । एकादशं । कृधि ॥ ४५ ॥
