##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वमिमां वधूं सुपुत्रां सुभगां च कृणु । कृधि । अस्यां वध्वां
> दश पुत्राना धेहि । पतिमेकादशं कृधि । दश पुत्राः पतिरेकादशो यथा स्यात्तथा
> कृधि । कृणु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, make this bride one with good sons and fortunate. Place in her ten sons. Make her husband the eleventh: make it so that the ten sons are there and the husband is the eleventh.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मीढ्वः (*mīḍhvaḥ*)—O showerer of desires
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this bride
- सुपुत्रां (*suputrāṃ*)—as one having excellent sons
- सुभगां (*subhagāṃ*)—as one who brings good fortune
- कृणु (*kṛṇu*)—make
- अस्यां (*asyāṃ*)—in her
- दश पुत्रान् (*daśa putrān*)—ten sons
- आ धेहि (*ā dhehi*)—cause to be born
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—her husband
- एकादशं (*ekādaśaṃ*)—as the eleventh
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of desires, make this bride the mother of excellent sons and bring her good fortune. Cause ten sons to be born in her. Make her husband himself the eleventh.

##### English translation
Indra, showerer, make her the mother of sons, pleasing (to her husband **NOTE**); give her ten sons; make her husband the eleventh.

#### Ṛk 46

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒म्राज्ञे॒ श्वशु॑रे भव स॒म्राज्ञे॑ श्व॒ाश्यां भ॑व ।  
> ननां॑दरि स॒म्राज्ञे॑ भव स॒म्राज्ञे॒ अधि॑ दे॒वृषु॑ ॥ ४६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> संराज्ञे । श्वशुरे । भव । संराज्ञे । श्वाश्रा० । भव ।  
> ननांदरि । संराज्ञे । भव । संराज्ञे । अधि । देवृषु ॥ ४६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वधु श्वशुरादिसु त्वं सम्राज्ञी भव । देवृषु । देवरेष्टित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O bride, be a queen among your father-in-law and the others. देवृषु (*devṛṣu*) means among the husband's brothers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O bride) श्वशुरे (*śvaśure*)—towards your father-in-law
- संराज्ञी भव (*saṃrājñī bhava*)—behave like a queen who gives delight
- श्वश्रावां (*śvaśrāvāṃ*)—towards your mother-in-law also
- संराज्ञी भव (*saṃrājñī bhava*)—conduct yourself as a giver of joy
- ननांदरि (*nanāṃdari*)—towards the husband's sisters

### Printed p. 439

- संराज्ञॆ (*saṃrājñè*)—behave like an excellent queen
- आधि देवृषु (*ādhi devṛṣu*)—towards the husband's brothers also
- संराज्ञॆ (*saṃrājñè*)—exercise authority that gives joy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O bride, behave towards your father-in-law like a queen who gives delight. Towards your mother-in-law also conduct yourself as a giver of joy. In respect of your husband's sisters and brothers also, exercise authority as one who brings them gladness.

##### English translation
Be a queen to your father-in law, be a queen to your mother-in-law, be a queen to your husband's sister, be a queen to your husband's brothers-

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To explain the meaning of the word देवरं (*devaraṃ*), Yāska took Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-40-2 as an example and gave the Nirukta:

क्व स्विद्रात् भवतः, क्व दिवा, क्वापिप्राप्तिं कुरुथः, क्व वसथः, को वा शयने विधवेव देवरं । देवरः कस्मात् द्वितीयो वर उच्यते । विधवा विधातृका भवति । विधावनाद्वा । विधवनाद्वेति प्रचर्मशिराः। आपि ना धव इति मनुष्यनाम तद्वियोगाद्विधवा । देवरो दीव्यतिकर्मा । मर्यो मनुष्यो मरणधर्मा । योषा यौतेः । आकुरुते सहस्थाने ॥ (*kva svidrāt bhavataḥ, kva divā, kvāpiprāptiṃ kuruthaḥ, kva vasathaḥ, ko vā śayane vidhaveva devaraṃ | devaraḥ kasmāt dvitīyo vara ucyate | vidhavā vidhātṛkā bhavati | vidhāvanādvā | vidhavanādveti pracarmaśirāḥ| āpi nā dhava iti manuṣyanāma tadviyogādvidhavā | devaro dīvyatikarmā | maryo manuṣyo maraṇadharmā | yoṣā yauteḥ | ākurute sahasthāne ‖*) (Ni. 3-15)

The woman Ghoṣā, the seer of this sūkta, questions the Aśvins thus while praising them: O Aśvins, where are you at night? Where are you by day? Where do you do your work (such as bathing and eating)? Where do you dwell? In the sacrificial house of which sacrificer who performs a sacrifice are you honoured by him, as a widow seats her husband's younger brother facing her on her bed (at night), and as a wife, in solitude, seats her husband facing her and takes her pleasure?

How is the word देवर (*devara*) formed? What is देवर (*devara*)? देवर (*devara*) means the second husband. For a woman the husband she is married to is the first husband. If that husband dies before children are born (as was the custom of that time), the husband's younger brother, that is, the brother-in-law, may have intercourse with that woman for the begetting of a son; therefore that brother-in-law is the woman's second husband, that is, the meaning of the word देवर (*devara*) is brother-in-law.

### Printed p. 440

For the word विधवा (*vidhavā*): (1) its meaning is विधातृका (*vidhātṛkā*). After the husband has died there is no one to support her, that is, to maintain her by giving food, clothing and the like; therefore a woman without a husband is called विधवा (*vidhavā*). (2) Or विधवनाद्वा (*vidhavanādvā*): because she is grieved by her husband's death and trembles with sorrow, a woman without a husband is called विधवा (*vidhavā*). (3) Or विधावनाद्वा (*vidhāvanādvā*): because, scorched with grief by her husband's death, she wanders from here to there with no one's restraint, a woman bereft of her husband is called विधवा (*vidhavā*); this is the opinion of the teacher called Carmaśiras. (4) Or the word धव (*dhava*) means a man; therefore a woman who has lost her husband (वि धव (*vi dhava*)) is called विधवा (*vidhavā*).

देवरः दीव्यतिकर्मा (*devaraḥ dīvyatikarmā*). The word देवर (*devara*) is formed from the root दीव्यति (*dīvyati*), which means to sport. Here the meaning is one who is eager to take his pleasure in amorous sport with his brother's wife.

#### Ṛk 47

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समं॑जंतु॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः समापो॒ हृद॑यानि नौ ।  
> सं मा॑त॒रिश्वा॒ सं धा॒ता समु॒ देष्ट्री॑ दधातु नौ ॥ ४७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । अंजंतु । विश्वे । देवाः । सं । आपः । हृदयानि । नौ ।  
> सं । मातरिश्वा । सं । धाता । सं । ऊं इति । देष्ट्री । दधातु । नौ ॥ ४७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समंजंत्येषा वरस्य दधिप्राशने वधूवरयोर्हृदयस्पर्शने वा
> विनियुक्ता । तथा च सूत्रितं । समंजंतु विश्वे देवा इति दध्नः प्राश्य प्रतिप्रयच्छेदाज्यशेषेण वानक्ति हृदये । आ. गृ. १-८.९ ! इति ॥
> विश्वे देवाः सर्वॆ देवा नौ हृदयानि मानसानि समंजंतु । सम्यगंजंतु ।
> अपगतदुःखादिक्लेशानि कृत्वा लौकिकवैदिकविषयेषु प्रकाशयुक्तानि कुर्वंत्यर्थः ।
> आपश्च समंजंतु । तथा मातरिश्वा नौ हृदयानि सं दधातु । अवयोर्बुद्धीः
> परस्परानुकूलाः करोत्वित्यर्थः । धाता च सं दधातु । देष्ट्री दात्री फलानां ।
> सरस्वतीत्यर्थः । सा च सं दधातु । संधानं करोतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk is applied at the bridegroom's eating of curds, or at the touching of the hearts of the bride and bridegroom; and so the sūtra has it **NOTE**: after eating of the curds he gives it to her in turn, or anoints the heart with the remainder of the ghee. All the gods anoint our two hearts, that is, they unite them well: having removed sorrow and other afflictions, they make them bright in worldly and Vedic matters. The waters also unite them. Likewise Mātariśvan unites our hearts: the meaning is that he makes the minds of us two favourable to each other. Dhātṛ also unites them. देष्ट्री (*deṣṭrī*) is the giver of fruits, that is, Sarasvatī; she also unites, she brings about the union.

### Printed p. 441

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- नौ हृदयानि (*nau hṛdayāni*)—the hearts of us both
- समंजंतु (*samaṃjaṃtu*)—let them unite
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the deities of the waters
- सं अंजंतु (*saṃ aṃjaṃtu*)—let them make them one
- मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—the wind (Mātariśvan)
- सं दधातु (*saṃ dadhātu*)—let him make our minds beneficial to each other
- देष्ट्री (*deṣṭrī*)—Sarasvatī, the giver of fruit
- धाता (*dhātā*)—Dhātṛ also
- नौ (*nau*)—our hearts
- सं (दधातु) (*saṃ (dadhātu)*)—let him make one

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May all the gods together make our hearts one. May the deities of the waters also unite us. May Mātariśvan make our minds beneficial to each other. May Sarasvatī, the giver of fruit, make our hearts one.

##### English translation
May the universal gods unite both our hearts; may the waters unite them ; may Matarishvan, Dhatri and the bountiful (Saraswati) unite both our hearts.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

That this Ṛk beginning समंजंतु (*samaṃjaṃtu*) is to be recited at the time of marriage when the bridegroom eats the curds, and when the bride and bridegroom touch their hearts, is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra समंजंशु निश्वेदेवा इति दध्नः प्राश्य प्रतियच्छेदाज्यशेषेण वानक्ति हृदये (*samaṃjaṃśu niśvedevā iti dadhnaḥ prāśya pratiyacchedājyaśeṣeṇa vānakti hṛdaye*) (Ā. Gṛ. 1-8-9).

हृदयानि समंजंतु (*hṛdayāni samaṃjaṃtu*)—अपगतदुःखादिक्लेशानि कृता लौकिकवैदिकविषयेषु प्रकाशयुक्तानि कुर्वंत्यर्थः ॥ (*apagataduḥkhādikleśāni kṛtā laukikavaidikaviṣayeṣu prakāśayuktāni kurvaṃtyarthaḥ ‖*). O all gods, remove the sorrows, afflictions and troubles that may befall us, the newly wedded pair, and grant that the minds of us both may act in the same manner, without difference of opinion, in worldly household duties and in Vedic good rites such as sacrifices; this is the meaning.

Although the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) ordinarily means the wind that blows in the atmosphere, its etymological meaning is given with reference to Agni:

मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति प्राणिति सूर्यरूपेण चेष्टत इति मातरिश्वा । (*mātaryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti prāṇiti sūryarūpeṇa ceṣṭata iti mātariśvā |*)

or else मातर्यरण्यां श्वसिति निवसतीति मातरिश्वा (*mātaryaraṇyāṃ śvasiti nivasatīti mātariśvā*). That is, the sun moving in the atmosphere shines, giving life to all living beings. Since this sun is only a changed form of the fire that is in the heaven-world, the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) may be said to mean Agni in the form of the Āditya. Or else,

### Printed p. 442

since fire is produced by churning in the aranis (pieces of wood), the aranis stand in the place of mothers to Agni. Since Agni dwells in such aranis, मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) means Agni: this is another kind of derivation. For the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) Yāska has given the explanation मातरिश्वा वायुर्मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति मार्तर्याश्वनितीति वा (*mātariśvā vāyurmātaryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti mārtaryāśvanitīti vā*) (Ni. 7-26). मातरि (*mātari*) means in the atmosphere; श्वसिति (*śvasiti*) moves. Therefore the meaning in one way is the wind that moves in the atmosphere. Or else, because he goes (अनिति (*aniti*), that is, गच्छति (*gacchati*)) swiftly in the atmosphere, the wind is called Mātariśvan: this is another meaning. That is, the meaning given to the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) is a deity that moves in the atmosphere. It is not the wind alone that moves in the atmosphere; the sun also moves in the atmosphere, and so the sun too is called Mātariśvan. Since the sun too is a changed form of the fire that is in the heaven-world, Agni is described here by the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*).

मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)—मातरिश्वा वायुर्मातर्यंतरिक्षे श्वसिति मातराश्वनितीति वा (*mātariśvā vāyurmātaryaṃtarikṣe śvasiti mātarāśvanitīti vā*). Because he breathes or moves in the atmosphere, the name Mātariśvan has come to the wind. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-4 they take this word to mean Agni, and in 1-141-3 to mean the sacrificer. But except in one or two such places, everywhere else मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) means the wind.

अन्यं मातरश्वा दिव आ जभार (*anyaṃ mātaraśvā diva ā jabhāra*)—The unearthly manifestation and the earthly origin of Agni, who is sacrifice itself, are described in many ways. Agni is the banner of sacrifices, the means of the vidatha, the father of sacrifices and the like, and the king of the adhvaras (see the descriptions in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-3; 3-11-2; 4-2-3 and others). That the manifestation of Agni first came to the wind in the form of lightning is praised in the Ṛks of the Ṛk-saṃhitā

त्वमग्ने प्रथमो मातरिश्वन आर्भिव सुक्रतूया विवस्वते । (*tvamagne prathamo mātariśvana ārbhiva sukratūyā vivasvate |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-3)

स जायमानः परमे व्योमन्याविरग्नि रभवन्मातरिश्वने । (*sa jāyamānaḥ parame vyomanyāviragni rabhavanmātariśvane |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-43-2)

and others. There are many Vedic statements that this wind brought Agni, who was hidden in a very distant region, for Bhṛgu and for Manu, the sacrificers, and helped them. For example—

### Printed p. 443

द्विजन्मानं रयिमिव प्रशस्तं रातिं भरद्भृगवे मातरिश्वा । (*dvijanmānaṃ rayimiva praśastaṃ rātiṃ bharadbhṛgave mātariśvā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-60-1)

यं मातरिश्वा मनवे परावतो देवं भाः परावतः । (*yaṃ mātariśvā manave parāvato devaṃ bhāḥ parāvataḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-128-2)

ऐनं नयन्मातरिश्वा परावतो देवेभ्यो मथितं परि । (*ainaṃ nayanmātariśvā parāvato devebhyo mathitaṃ pari |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-5)

आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः । (*ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4)

ईळेन्यं प्रथमं मातरिश्वा देवास्त्रत्कुर्मनवे यजत्रं । (*īḷenyaṃ prathamaṃ mātariśvā devāstratkurmanave yajatraṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-46-9)

In these and many other Ṛks it is well known from the Veda that Mātariśvan, for the benefit of the sacrificers Bhṛgu and Manu, brought to the earth the Agni who lay hidden in a distant region, and thereby did good to all the people on earth.

मातरिश्वा मथित् (*mātariśvā mathit*)—For the explanation of the word मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*), see the Special Topics of the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-6. The commentator explains the word विभृतः (*vibhṛtaḥ*) with कीदृशः मातरिश्वा । विभृतः । प्राणिसु प्राणापानादि पंच वृत्तिरूपेण विहृतो विभज्य स्थितः । (*kīdṛśaḥ mātariśvā | vibhṛtaḥ | prāṇisu prāṇāpānādi paṃca vṛttirūpeṇa vihṛto vibhajya sthitaḥ |*), that is, one who pervades living beings divided into five parts, prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna and samāna; and of these, for the present context, he explains मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) as व्यानवृत्तिरूपेणावस्थितो मुख्यप्राणः । (*vyānavṛttirūpeṇāvasthito mukhyaprāṇaḥ |*), that is, the wind who is the chief breath, existing in the form of vyāna. To support the view that the wind in this form alone is capable of kindling fire and performed this task, he cites in praise of the wind in the form of vyāna the passage of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad अथ यः प्राणापानयोः संधिः स व्यानः । अतो यान्यन्यानि वीर्यवंति कर्माणि यथाग्नेर्मंथनमाजेः सरणं दृढस्य धनुष आयमनमप्राणन्न नपानंस्तानि करोति । (*atha yaḥ prāṇāpānayoḥ saṃdhiḥ sa vyānaḥ | ato yānyanyāni vīryavaṃti karmāṇi yathāgnermaṃthanamājeḥ saraṇaṃ dṛḍhasya dhanuṣa āyamanamaprāṇanna napānaṃstāni karoti |*) The purport of this passage is that all deeds of valour that exceed the power of prāṇa and apāna, such as the kindling of fire, can be done only by the wind in the form of vyāna. (Chā. U. 1.3.3-5)

There is an ancient story about the kindling of fire. As it says, सर्वमिदमंधंतम असीत् । अथ मातरिश्वाकाशे सूक्ष्ममग्निपश्यत् । तममथ्नात् । मथित्वा चानयदिति । (*sarvamidamaṃdhaṃtama asīt | atha mātariśvākāśe sūkṣmamagnipaśyat | tamamathnāt | mathitvā cānayaditi |*) Formerly the whole world was covered with pitch darkness. Then Mātariśvan perceived the subtle Agni in the sky and churned it. Afterwards he brought it to the earth so as to be useful for the sacrifice. This well-known story is told in the Ṛk-saṃhitā too, in a subtle way, in many places. For example—

### Printed p. 444

अन्यं दिवो मातारिश्वा जभारामथ्नादन्यं परि श्योनो अद्रेः । (*anyaṃ divo mātāriśvā jabhārāmathnādanyaṃ pari śyono adreḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.93.6)

आ दूतो अग्निमभरद्विवस्वतो वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वा परावतः । (*ā dūto agnimabharadvivasvato vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvā parāvataḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-8-4)

In these Ṛks also the praise of Agni is set out together with the context of the old story, just as it is praised here. The meaning is that it was only after Mātariśvan had brought him that Agni shone in the sacrificial house.

**General description of the deity Mātariśvan**

There is no sūkta that praises this deity alone. The name occurs twenty-seven times. It is understood that Mātariśvan and Agni are one, or that Mātariśvan produces Agni. Mātariśvan is a name of Agni itself (3-5-9; 3-26-2; 1-96-4). The address in (9-88-19) also must be applied to Agni. In another place Agni is named तनूनपात् (*tanūnapāt*) in his heavenly, atomic form; after his birth he is called नराशंस (*narāśaṃsa*); when he arises in the form of Mātariśvan, he himself becomes the swift-moving wind (3-29-11). The wise call the one by many names; they speak of Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan and so on (1-164-46). The name Bṛhaspati, which is said many times to be equal to Agni, belongs to Mātariśvan too. "That Bṛhaspati himself became Mātariśvan at the time of the sacrifice" (1-190-2).

In some other places Agni and Mātariśvan are said to be different. He (Agni), born very high in heaven, appeared to Mātariśvan (1-143-2). In the beginning Agni appeared to Mātariśvan and Vivasvat (1-31-3). Because he is the greatest among the luminous bodies, Agni with his flames is the support of the sky; Mātariśvan made the hidden bearer of oblations blaze up (3-5-10). From the sky Mātariśvan brought one (Agni); the hawk brought another (Soma) from the mountain (1-93-6). Mātariśvan brought Agni, the revered priest, the dweller in heaven (3-2-13). The gods made Agni, born from Bhṛgu, the first priest for men (10-46-9). The deity Mātariśvan brought him (Agni) from very far away for the sake of man (1-128-2). Mātariśvan, the messenger of Vivasvat, brought Vaiśvānara Agni from very far away; the mighty ones seized him in the water (6-8-4). Mātariśvan brought from very far away the hidden Agni, who had been raised by the kindling of the araṇi (3-9-5). Mātariśvan churned the hidden Agni and produced him (1-141-3). Churned by Mātariśvan, Agni was established in the dwellings of men

### Printed p. 445

(1-71-4, 1-148-1). Indra, having released the cows for Trita from the grip of the serpent, gave the cow-stalls to Dadhyañc and Mātariśvan (10-48-2).

In some sūktas of the later part of the Ṛgveda, although Mātariśvan is mentioned, nothing is learnt about his nature, qualities and the like. In two places (9-67-31; 10-114-1) it is said that he purified Soma and drank it. In another place (Vāla. 4-2) the name occurs among the group of the fathers; there Indra sits by his side and drinks Soma. Once Indra is compared to him as to an excellent craftsman (10-105-6). In the sūkta relating to marriage, when Mātariśvan is prayed, together with the other gods, to enter the hearts of the two lovers, this skill may be what is meant. Lastly, in one place Mātariśvan is said to be boundless and wandering (10-109-1). Both these qualities support the view that Mātariśvan means the wind.

Thus Mātariśvan may be called the embodied heavenly Agni; moreover it is he who brought Agni from heaven to the earth. Lightning may be called the origin of Mātariśvan. Just as Agni is the messenger between these two worlds, so Mātariśvan came from heaven to earth as the messenger of Vivasvat. In the Atharvaveda also Mātariśvan is a name of Agni (A.Ve. 10-8-39 and 40) **NOTE**; but in the Brāhmaṇas and the like Mātariśvan means the wind itself. The basis for this view has already been stated (3.29-11). Agni, who in the atmosphere was like a hissing serpent, is described in another place as the wind rushing with force (1-79.1).

The word मातरिश्वर् (*mātariśvar*) may mean one who grows in the mother, one who has taken shape. The root शु (*śu*) means to increase, to become larger in size. From it words such as शिशु (*śiśu*) are formed. Like Mātariśvan, Agni too grows in the mothers (1-141-5). When applied to Mātariśvan, the mother may be the lower part of the araṇi, or the cloud. Since Mātariśvan comes from the atmosphere, it can be said that the cloud is his mother. In the view of Yāska, Mātariśvan means the wind; मातरि (*mātari*) means in the atmosphere, and श्वन् (*śvan*) means one who breathes, or आशु आन् (*āśu ān*), one who breathes quickly; that is, it means the wind.

### Printed p. 446

वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेश तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । (*vedārthasya prakāśeśa tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan |*)

पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*)

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्येष्टमाष्टके तृतीयोऽध्यायः समाप्तः (*iti śrīmadrājādhirājaparameśvaravaidikamārgapravartaka śrīvīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣyeṣṭamāṣṭake tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ*)

Here the third chapter in the eighth Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, together with the Bhāṣya of Śrī Sāyaṇa and with a translation into the Karnāṭaka language, is concluded.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्राहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrāhīnaṃ tu yadbhavet |*)

तत्सर्वं क्षम्य तां देववागीश्वर नमोस्तु ते ॥ (*tatsarvaṃ kṣamya tāṃ devavāgīśvara namostu te ‖*)

शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*)

Auspiciousness.

श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे . (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame .*)

यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्चसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । (*yasya niścasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat |*)

निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ |*)

तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*)

प्राज्ञः श्रीसायणाचार्यो वाख्याय चरमेष्टके । (*prājñaḥ śrīsāyaṇācāryo vākhyāya carameṣṭake |*)

स्पुटं तृतीयमध्यायं चतुर्थं वक्तुमुद्यतः । (*spuṭaṃ tṛtīyamadhyāyaṃ caturthaṃ vaktumudyataḥ |*)

Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the Bhāṣya of Sāyaṇa.

अष्टमाष्टके चतुर्थोऽध्यायः (*aṣṭamāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ*)

The fourth chapter in the eighth Aṣṭaka.

## Sūkta 86 (Maṇḍala 10)

The eighty-sixth sūkta in the tenth Maṇḍala.

**Introduction**

It is said that the seer of this sūkta is Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra. This sūkta is a dialogue among three: Indra, Indrāṇī, and Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra. Yāska has given the following etymology of the word वृषाकपि (*vṛṣākapi*)—

वृषाकपिः । अथ यद्रश्मिभिरभिप्रकुपयन्नेति तद्वृषाकपिर्भवति वृषाकंपन । (*vṛṣākapiḥ | atha yadraśmibhirabhiprakupayanneti tadvṛṣākapirbhavati vṛṣākaṃpana |*) (Ni. 12-27)

### Printed p. 448

He has explained, with reference to the Sun, that the one who makes everything tremble with his rays is called Vṛṣākapi. To support this, he has given as an example the Ṛk of the present sūkta

पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै । (*punarehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai |*)

य एष स्वप्ननंशनोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*ya eṣa svapnanaṃśano 'stameṣi pathā punarviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-21)

The word स्वप्ननंशनः (*svapnanaṃśanaḥ*) in this Ṛk he has explained as the Sun, who by his rising brings to an end, that is, destroys, the sleep of living beings. Sāyaṇa has said that Vṛṣākapi is of the nature of the Sun. Although the meaning "the Sun" fits the word वृषाकपि (*vṛṣākapi*), the Vṛṣākapi spoken of in the present sūkta must be understood to be the son of Indra. Moreover, when speaking of Indrāṇī, the wife of Indra, Yāska

cites the Ṛk

नाहमिंद्राणि रारण सख्युवृषाकपेयुते । (*nāhamiṃdrāṇi rāraṇa sakhyuvṛṣākapeyute |*)

यस्येदमप्यं हविः प्रियं देवेषु गच्छति विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*yasyedamapyaṃ haviḥ priyaṃ deveṣu gacchati viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-12)

and Indra addresses Indrāṇī as his wife and as the mother of Vṛṣākapi (Ni. 11-39). Besides—

वृषाकपायी । वृषाकपायी वृषाकपेः पत्न्यैवाभिसृष्टकालतमा ॥ (*vṛṣākapāyī | vṛṣākapāyī vṛṣākapeḥ patnyaivābhisṛṣṭakālatamā ‖*)

He has said that Vṛṣākapāyī means the wife of Vṛṣākapi (Indra), and that Vṛṣākapi means the Sun.

वृषाकपिः (*vṛṣākapiḥ*)

It is not easy to state precisely the nature of the Vṛṣākapi who is indicated in the present sūkta. Roughly seen, Vṛṣākapi may be called a monkey dear to Indra. When this Vṛṣākapi, on one occasion, caused distress to the mind of Indrāṇī, the wife of Indra, the conversation that took place between Indra and Indrāṇī, and the taking part of Vṛṣākapi too in the middle of this conversation, is the subject of this sūkta. In it the meaning of the first Ṛk is given in two ways. According to one view it is the speech of Indra, according to the other the speech of Indrāṇī.

According to the first explanation it is understood that Indra declares: although Vṛṣākapi drank the Soma assigned to me and deprived me of that delight, I myself am the lord of the whole world. And secondly—

### Printed p. 449

One purport is that Indrāṇī says: Vṛṣākapi drank the Soma assigned to my husband Indra and deprived my husband of this delight; yet my husband Indra is the lord of the whole world. Who this Vṛṣākapi is, and whether there is a basis for stating precisely the relation between Indra and Vṛṣākapi, and the like, must be examined in the present context.

The Nirukta and the statements of the Bṛhaddevatā explain the nature of Vṛṣākapi to some extent. The author of the Nirukta gives the etymology of this word.

यद्रश्किभिरभिप्रकंपयन्नेति तद्वृषाकपिर्भवति, वृषाकंपनः ॥ (*yadraśkibhirabhiprakaṃpayanneti tadvṛṣākapirbhavati, vṛṣākaṃpanaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 12-26)

He has stated the purport that the one who by his rays makes everything tremble is Vṛṣākapi. Further, citing the Ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā

पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै । (*punarehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai |*)

य एष स्वप्ननंशनोस्तमेषि पथा पुनर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*ya eṣa svapnanaṃśanostameṣi pathā punarviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-5-21) **NOTE**

he has explained the purport of the word वृषाकपि (*vṛṣākapi*) used in this Ṛk and the action of Vṛṣākapi. The purport of this Ṛk is as follows. O Vṛṣākapi, you are the destroyer of dreams. You must come again to travel by this path. Please come again. Let us both together perform the auspicious rite. The explanation of the author of the Nirukta, as to who is meant by Vṛṣākapi in the Ṛk that gives this purport, is as follows—

पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुप्रसूतानि वः कर्माणि कल्पयावहै । य एष स्वप्नदर्शनः स्वप्नान् नाशयसि आदित्य उदयेन सोऽस्तमेषि यथा पुनः । (*punarehi vṛṣākape suprasūtāni vaḥ karmāṇi kalpayāvahai | ya eṣa svapnadarśanaḥ svapnān nāśayasi āditya udayena so 'stameṣi yathā punaḥ |*)

सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद् ब्रूम आदित्यं : (*sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametad brūma ādityaṃ :*) (Si.: 3-28) **NOTE**

O Vṛṣākapi, you are the destroyer of dreams; that is, since at your rising in the morning the sleep of all is destroyed, you are the Sun. In accordance with your duty you must rise again. After your rising again, let us both together perform the auspicious rite. Addressing the Sun, who has the form of Indra, they say this same praise; thus it is declared that Vṛṣākapi and Indra are both special manifestations of the Sun. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā too have indicated Vṛṣākapi as a deity belonging to the world of the Sun.

### Printed p. 450

वृषाकपायीं सूर्यस्य तामेवाहुस्तु निम्रुचि । (*vṛṣākapāyīṃ sūryasya tāmevāhustu nimruci |*)

तस्याश्रये सरण्यूश्च भगः पूषा वृषाकपिः ॥ (*tasyāśraye saraṇyūśca bhagaḥ pūṣā vṛṣākapiḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-10)

Vṛṣākapāyī, Sūryā and Uṣas are the wives of the Sun. At sunset the relation between the Sun and Vṛṣākapāyī is the closer. The passage gives details that confirm the purport of the author of the Nirukta, that Saraṇyū, Bhaga, Pūṣan and Vṛṣākapi all belong to the Sun's shelter. Then the etymology of this word runs as follows.

वृषैव कपिलो भूत्वा यन्नाकमधिरोहति । (*vṛṣaiva kapilo bhūtvā yannākamadhirohati |*)

वृषाकपिरसौ तेन विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः । (*vṛṣākapirasau tena viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ |*)

रश्मिभिः कंपयन्नेति वृषा वर्षिष्ठ एव सः ॥ (*raśmibhiḥ kaṃpayanneti vṛṣā varṣiṣṭha eva saḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-67)

Because the bull of tawny colour climbs up to the firmament (नाक (*nāka*)), it is called Vṛṣākapi. Therefore the Vṛṣākapi described in the sūkta that contains the sentence विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः (*viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ*) must be the Sun himself, who makes things tremble.

सायाह्नकाले भूतानि स्वापयन्नस्तमेति यत् । (*sāyāhnakāle bhūtāni svāpayannastameti yat |*)

वृषाकपिरितो वा स्यादिति मंत्रेषु दृश्यते ॥ (*vṛṣākapirito vā syāditi maṃtreṣu dṛśyate ‖*) (Bṛ. De 2.68)

Moreover, at evening he sets, having made all beings sleep. From the mantra धन्व च यत्कृंतत्रं (*dhanva ca yatkṛṃtatraṃ*) up to the mantra यदुदंचो वृषाकपे (*yadudaṃco vṛṣākape*) (20-22) there is a precise indication of Indra with regard to Vṛṣākapi. Thus it is understood from the above details that Vṛṣākapi is a deity who belongs to the world of the Sun and reflects a part of the Sun.

According to some, Vṛṣākapi belongs to the class of animals, from the word मृग (*mṛga*) in sentences such as चकार हरितो मृगः (*cakāra harito mṛgaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-3). But the word मृग (*mṛga*) also has been explained as referring to the Sun. The author of the Nirukta makes this matter clear by citing the Ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā

यदुदंचो वृषाकपे गृहमिंद्राजगंतन । (*yadudaṃco vṛṣākape gṛhamiṃdrājagaṃtana |*)

क्वंस्य पुल्वघो मृगः कमगंजनयोपनो विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ (*kvaṃsya pulvagho mṛgaḥ kamagaṃjanayopano viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-22)

and, with त एतद्वः ब्रूम आदित्यं (*ta etadvaḥ brūma ādityaṃ*) (Ni. 13-3), he has explained it here also as referring to the Sun. Durgācārya, explaining the word मृग (*mṛga*) here

### Printed p. 451

(Ni. 13-2), explains the qualifying word पुल्वघः (*pulvaghaḥ*) in order to show how a meaning referring to the Sun is possible for this word. The author of the Nirukta himself has said that पुल्वघः (*pulvaghaḥ*) means one who eats much (बह्वादी (*bahvādī*)), that is, one who devours abundantly. How is that? बह्वसौ अत्ति सर्पप्राणिष्टवस्थितः— (*bahvasau atti sarpaprāṇiṣṭavasthitaḥ—*)सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥ (*sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1). Since, as described in this sentence, the Sun himself pervades the self of all living beings, and since Upaniṣadic sentences such as अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि (*adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni*) explain the devouring nature of the supreme Brahman who is in the form of the Sun, here also पुल्वघः मृगः (*pulvaghaḥ mṛgaḥ*) has been explained as the Sun.

It has already been said that in this sūkta a dialogue of Indra, Indrāṇī and Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra, is told. That dialogue itself is briefly set out here—

(1) Indra—I am the greatest of the whole world, higher than all. Yet the priests, commanded by me, praised in the Soma sacrifice they performed my son Vṛṣākapi alone. In that sacrifice he gained satisfaction from drinking Soma. In that sacrifice the Soma juice was not pressed and prepared for me, and I was not praised.

(2) Indrāṇī (the wife of Indra)—O Indra, your mind, in its distress, always runs towards Vṛṣākapi. You never go anywhere else to drink Soma.

(3) O Indra, what helpful service has that Vṛṣākapi, who is just like a beast, done for you? Even if he does nothing, you generously provide him with wealth and food, do you not?

(4) O Indra, may a hunting dog seize and devour this Vṛṣākapi, your son, whom you wish to protect with so much love, as a hunting dog bites a wild boar by the ear, kills it and eats it.

(5) This wicked monkey has spoiled and ruined the oblation mixed with ghee that the sacrificers had prepared for me in the sacrifice. I shall cut off its head. I never wish to bring happiness to those who do evil.

(6) There is no other woman more fortunate than I. There is no woman other than I who has good sons. There is no woman other than I who follows her husband, agrees with him and fulfils his wishes.

### Printed p. 452

(7) Vṛṣākapi—O mother, let everything be fulfilled quickly just as you have said. May my father Indra gain happiness through your company. When you are with your husband may he be happy. Like the song of the cuckoo and other birds, may my father experience delight through your loving words.

(8) Indra (addressing Indrāṇī)—O fair-limbed one, you are the wife of a hero, your arms are tender, your fingers are beautiful. Your masses of hair are long and black. Your hips are broad. Why do you, being such, become angry with our son Vṛṣākapi?

(9) Indrāṇī—This wicked beast speaks with contempt, considering me as one who has no protection of men. For me the hero Indra is the husband, for me there are heroic sons. The heroic Maruts too are my friends.

(10) This Indrāṇī (I), the maker of truth, who has heroic sons, the wife of the heroic Indra, being prayed to by the singers and in order to favour them, goes to the battle they wage or to the sacrificial ground.

(11) Indra (addressing Indrāṇī)—I have heard that among fortunate women this Indrāṇī is the most fortunate. For Indra, the husband of this Indrāṇī, is the greatest of all. Unlike ordinary people he does not fall under the power of death through old age.

(12) O Indrāṇī, if my son Vṛṣākapi, who is like a friend to me, is not with me, I have no joy. The pure oblation prepared by that Vṛṣākapi and refined with water is most dear to the gods.

(13) Vṛṣākapi—O Vṛṣākapāyī (Indrāṇī), who are the mother (of me, Vṛṣākapi), you are rich, you have excellent sons and good daughters-in-law. May you eat the animals (the flesh of animals), the oblation which you offer lovingly for your husband Indra and which is dear to Indra.

(14) Indra—The sacrificers, impelled by my wife Indrāṇī, cook for my satisfaction fifteen or twenty bulls (ox or bull), that is, their flesh. I eat them and grow strong. They fill both sides of my belly, and the sacrificers fill my belly with Soma juice. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 453

(15) Indrāṇī—O Indra, as a bull with sharp horns rejoices, bellowing in a herd of cows, so may the Soma juice that I press and prepare for your delight satisfy you and be a giver of joy.

(16) O Indra, the man whose organ of generation hangs between the two thighs, only in a sleeping state and powerless, such a man is not able to perform the act of union with a woman, that is, to enjoy a woman. But the man whose organ of generation is able to stand straight in the state of excitement, such a man alone is capable of performing the act of love with a woman.

(17) Indra—O Indrāṇī, what you say is not right. The man whose male organ, lying in the sleeping state, stands upright in the state of excitement is not able to enjoy a woman; the man whose organ of generation hangs powerless between the two thighs, such a man alone is capable of union with a woman.

(18) Indrāṇī—Let this Vṛṣākapi take a dead animal that is not his own. Let him get ready a sharp knife to cut it, a ladle to cook it, a new pan, and a cartload of firewood to boil it.

(19) Indra—O Indrāṇī, I shall come there watching the sacrificial rite of the sacrificers who are performing the sacrifice. I shall learn which of them are Dāsas (Dasyus, the dark-coloured people) and which are Āryas. I shall drink only the Soma of those who prepare Soma juice for me with a good mind. And I shall look with a gracious mind upon the excellent sacrificer.

(20) O Vṛṣākapi, between our house and this place there is a forest and a barren region. How far does it extend? There may be enemies in it. Therefore set out from here, go to our house and go near the sacrificial house there.

(21) O Vṛṣākapi, come back to our house. I and Indrāṇī intend to do only what is good for you. Therefore you, who are in the form of the Sun, who by his rising disturbs the sleep of living beings, come home by the straight path.

(22) Indrāṇī—O Vṛṣākapi, O Indra, rise, come home. Where has that ruinous wretched beast gone?

### Printed p. 454

(23) Vṛṣākapi—O arrow released by Indra, the daughter of Manu, the girl named पर्शु (*parśu*), bore twenty children at one time. May there be good fortune to that woman who bore twenty children at one time in her womb.

On the use of this sūkta, the Ṛgvidhāna, a work spoken by Śaunaka, says as follows.

इंद्राण्याः कृतसंवादं स्नाने सूक्तं प्रयोजयेत् । (*iṃdrāṇyāḥ kṛtasaṃvādaṃ snāne sūktaṃ prayojayet |*)

नववर्गोत्तमयुतं पतिसौभाग्यपुत्रदं ॥ (*navavargottamayutaṃ patisaubhāgyaputradaṃ ‖*)

जलपुष्पोत्करयुते चित्रकुंभसमावृते । (*jalapuṣpotkarayute citrakuṃbhasamāvṛte |*)

कर्तव्योऽत्र तथा यागः सोमगंधर्ववह्निनां ॥ (*kartavyo 'tra tathā yāgaḥ somagaṃdharvavahnināṃ ‖*)

भगायाप्सरसां चैव यक्षाधिपतयेऽपि च । (*bhagāyāpsarasāṃ caiva yakṣādhipataye 'pi ca |*)

इंद्राण्यै देवपत्नीनां रतिप्रद्युम्नयोस्तथा ॥ (*iṃdrāṇyai devapatnīnāṃ ratipradyumnayostathā ‖*)

नदीसलिलसंपूर्णैः पंचगव्यसमावृतैः । (*nadīsalilasaṃpūrṇaiḥ paṃcagavyasamāvṛtaiḥ |*)

हुत्वाग्निं स्नापयेत्कन्यां स्थितां देशे तु दक्षिणे ॥ (*hutvāgniṃ snāpayetkanyāṃ sthitāṃ deśe tu dakṣiṇe ‖*)

प्रियंगुवटनागानां कषायोद्धृष्टकेसरं । (*priyaṃguvaṭanāgānāṃ kaṣāyoddhṛṣṭakesaraṃ |*)

संपाताभिहुतं कृत्वा सर्वौषधिसमन्वितं ॥ (*saṃpātābhihutaṃ kṛtvā sarvauṣadhisamanvitaṃ ‖*)

अभिमंत्र्येह सूक्तांते नवभिस्तु वि हीति वै । (*abhimaṃtryeha sūktāṃte navabhistu vi hīti vai |*)

स्थेयाभिरद्भिः पूर्णेन अभिषिंचेदुपोषितां ॥ (*stheyābhiradbhiḥ pūrṇena abhiṣiṃcedupoṣitāṃ ‖*)

याः पतिघ्न्यस्सि यस्तन्वः शाम्यंते तास्त्वनेन वै । (*yāḥ patighnyassi yastanvaḥ śāmyaṃte tāstvanena vai |*)

स्नापयेदाहनस्याभिर्विद्याद्यां विप्रवाजिनीं ॥ (*snāpayedāhanasyābhirvidyādyāṃ vipravājinīṃ ‖*)

सूक्तामपोद्धरेदेनं न सेश इति तु दृचं । (*sūktāmapoddharedenaṃ na seśa iti tu dṛcaṃ |*)

उपदिष्टोऽयमेकेषां पुंसः कर्मणि पौरुषे ॥ (*upadiṣṭo 'yamekeṣāṃ puṃsaḥ karmaṇi pauruṣe ‖*) (Mugvidhāna. A. 3-120 to 127) **NOTE**

This sūkta, which contains the dialogue that took place with Indra and Indrāṇī, should be recited at the time of bathing. By this women obtain good fortune, a husband, sons and the like. One should set up a variegated pot, fill it with water, put in sprouts, leaves and flowers, invoke Soma and the other deities in it, and perform a sacrifice. In that offering, one should make oblations in the fire addressed to Soma, Gandharva, Agni, Bhaga, the Apsarases, the lord of the Yakṣas, Indrāṇī, the wives of the gods, Rati and Pradyumna. One should consecrate the pañcagavya together with river water. After the oblation in the fire, one should seat the girl in the southern direction and have her bathed with the water of the pot. With the juice prepared from priyaṅgu and other herbs one should sprinkle the girl while reciting the mantras of this sūkta, and after the recitation of the sūkta have her bathed with the water of the pot. If this is done, the spirits and other beings and the diseases that have entered the woman's body

### Printed p. 455

are removed, and long life and health increase. If men, on instruction, mutter the two Ṛks of this sūkta, the 16th and the 17th, beginning with न सेशे (*na seśe*), the lost manhood will be regained.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अष्टमाष्टकस्य चतुर्थोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्र वि हीति त्रयोविंशत्यृचं
> द्वितीयं सूक्तं । वृषाकपिर्नामेंद्रस्य पुत्रः । स चेंद्राणींद्रश्चैते त्रयः
> संहताः संविवादं कृशवंतः ! तत्र विहि सोतोरसृक्षत किं सुबाहो स्वंगुर
> इंद्राणीमासु नारिष्टिति द्वे उक्षो हि मेऽयमेमीति चतस्र इत्येता नवर्च
> इंद्रवाक्यानि । अतस्तासामिंद्र ऋषिः । परा हींद्रेति पंचावीरामिति द्वे वृषभो
> न तिग्मशृंग इत्याद्याश्चतस्र इत्येकादशर्च इंद्राण्या वाक्यानि । अतस्तासामिंद्राण्यृषिः ।
> उवे अंब वृषाकपायि रेवति पर्शुर्ह नामोति तिस्रो वृषाकपेर्वाक्यानि ।
> आतस्तासां वृषाकपिर्यषिः । सर्व० सूक्तमैंद्रं पंचपदापंक्तिच्छंदस्कं । तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । वि हि त्र्यधिकॆंद्रो वृषाकपिरिंद्राणींद्रश्च समूदिरे सांकृतमिति ॥
> षष्ठेऽहनि ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्तशस्त्र एतसूक्तं ! सूक्तं च । अथ वृषाकपिं
> शंसेद्यथा होताज्याद्यां चतुर्थे : आ. ८-३ । इति ॥ यदि षष्ठेऽहन्युक्थस्तोत्राणि
> द्विपदासु न स्तुवीरन्नामगा यदि वेदमहरग्निष्टोमः स्यात्तदानीं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी
> माध्यंदिने सवन आरंभणीयाभ्य ऊर्ध्वमेतसूक्तं शंसेद्विश्वजित्यपि । तथा च
> सूत्रितं । सुकीर्तिं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी वृषाकपिं च पंक्तिशंसं । आ. ८-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fourth chapter of the eighth Aṣṭaka begins. In it the second sūkta, वि हि (*vi hi*), has twenty-three Ṛks. Vṛṣākapi is the son of Indra. He, Indrāṇī and Indra, these three, together carry on a dispute. Of these, वि हि सोतोरसृक्षत (*vi hi sotorasṛkṣata*) (1), किं सुबाहो स्वंगुरे (*kiṃ subāho svaṃgure*) (8), the two Ṛks इंद्राणीमासु नारिषु (*iṃdrāṇīmāsu nāriṣu*), the four beginning उक्ष्णो हि मे (*ukṣṇo hi me*) and आयमेमि (*āyamemi*) (14, 19-22), these nine Ṛks are speeches of Indra; therefore Indra is their seer. The five beginning परा हींद्र (*parā hīṃdra*), the two beginning अवीरां (*avīrāṃ*), and the four beginning वृषभो न तिग्मशृंगः (*vṛṣabho na tigmaśṛṃgaḥ*), these eleven Ṛks are speeches of Indrāṇī; therefore Indrāṇī is their seer. उवे अंब (*uve aṃba*), वृषाकपायि रेवति (*vṛṣākapāyi revati*) and पर्शुर्ह नाम (*parśurha nāma*) are speeches of Vṛṣākapi; therefore Vṛṣākapi is their seer. The whole sūkta is addressed to Indra and is in the metre पंचपदापंक्ति (*paṃcapadāpaṃkti*). So the Anukramaṇī says: वि हि त्र्यधिकेंद्रो वृषाकपिरिंद्राणींद्रश्च समूदिरे (*vi hi tryadhikeṃdro vṛṣākapiriṃdrāṇīṃdraśca samūdire*). On the sixth day (of the sacrifice) the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites this sūkta in the ukthya śastra. A sūtra says: let him recite the Vṛṣākapi sūkta as the Hotṛ does, the first Ṛk and so on in the fourth (Ā. 8-3). If on the sixth day the uktha-stotras are not sung on dvipadā Ṛks, or if the Sāman singers have recited इदमहः (*idamahaḥ*) (the Agniṣṭoma being the Viśvajit day), then the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites this sūkta after the Ārambhaṇīyā Ṛks at the midday pressing. So it is formulated in the sūtra: the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin recites the Sukīrti and the Vṛṣākapi, a Paṅkti recitation (Ā. 8-4).

Translation: In the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā the explanation of the fourth chapter of the eighth Aṣṭaka is now begun. The sūkta वि हि (*vi hi*), with which this chapter begins, is the second sūkta in the seventh Anuvāka. It has twenty-three Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra. In this sūkta a dialogue of three, Vṛṣākapi, Indra and Indrāṇī, is contained. In this sūkta, वि हि सोतोरसृक्षत (*vi hi sotorasṛkṣata*) (1), किं सुबाहो स्वंगुरे (*kiṃ subāho svaṃgure*) (8), the two Ṛks इंद्राणीमासु नारिषु (*iṃdrāṇīmāsu nāriṣu*) (11-12), उक्ष्णो हि मे (*ukṣṇo hi me*) (14), and the four Ṛks आयमेमि (*āyamemi*) (19-22), in all nine Ṛks, contain the speeches of Indra. Therefore Indra himself is the seer of these Ṛks; the five Ṛks परा हींद्र (*parā hīṃdra*) (2.6), the two Ṛks अवीरां (*avīrāṃ*) (9.10), and the four Ṛks वृषभो न तिग्मशृंगः (*vṛṣabho na tigmaśṛṃgaḥ*) (15-18), in all eleven Ṛks, are the speeches of Indrāṇī; therefore Indrāṇī is the seer of these. The Ṛks उवे अंब (*uve aṃba*) (7), वृषाकपायि रेवति (*vṛṣākapāyi revati*) (13) and पर्शुहर्नाम (*parśuharnāma*) (23) are speeches of Vṛṣākapi. Therefore Vṛṣākapi himself is the seer of these Ṛks. For the whole sūkta Indra is the deity. The Ṛks of the sūkta are in the metre called पंचपदापंक्तिः (*paṃcapadāpaṃktiḥ*). In the Anukramaṇī it is said: वि हि त्र्यधिकेंद्रो वृषाकपिरिंद्राणींद्रश्च समूदिरे (*vi hi tryadhikeṃdro vṛṣākapiriṃdrāṇīṃdraśca samūdire*) पांक्तं (*pāṃktaṃ*)

### Printed p. 456

as it says. The use of this sūkta for the ukthya-śastra mantras to be recited on the sixth day of the sacrifice by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अथ वृषाकपिं शंसेद्यथा होताज्याद्यां चतुर्थे (*atha vṛṣākapiṃ śaṃsedyathā hotājyādyāṃ caturthe*) (Ā. 8-3). If on the sixth day the uktha-stotras are not praised with Ṛks of the dvipadā metre, or if the Sāman singers recite the mantra इदमहः (*idamahaḥ*) on the day called विश्वजित् (*viśvajit*) of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, then the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin should recite this sūkta at the time of the midday pressing after the opening mantras. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, सुकीर्ति० ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी वृषाकपिं च पंक्तिशंसं (*sukīrti0 brāhmaṇācchaṃsī vṛṣākapiṃ ca paṃktiśaṃsaṃ*) (A. 8-4). **NOTE**

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 86. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 1, 2, 3, 4. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 23. Seer: वृषाकपिरैंद्र इंद्राणींद्रश्च समूदिरे (*vṛṣākapiraiṃdra iṃdrāṇīṃdraśca samūdire*); Ṛks 1, 8, 11-12, 14, 19-22: Indra; 2-6, 9-10, 15-18: Indrāṇī; 7, 13, 23: Vṛṣākapi. Deity: Indra. Metre: Paṅkti.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि हि सोतो॒रसृ॑क्षत॒ नेंद्रं॑ दे॒वम॑मंसत ।  
> यत्राम॑दद्वृ॒षाक॑पिर॒र्यः पु॒ष्टेषु॒ मत्स॑खा॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । हि । सोतोः । असृक्षत । न । इंद्रं । देवं । अमंसत ।  
> यत्र । अमदत् । वृषाकपिः । अर्यः । पुष्टेषु । मत्त्सखा । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोतोः सोमाभिषवं कर्तुं व्यसृक्षत । यागं प्रति मया विसृष्टा
> अनुज्ञाताः स्तोतारो वृषाकपेय्यष्टारः । हीति पूरणः । तत्र देवं द्योतमान-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सोतोः (*sotoḥ*) means: to perform the pressing of Soma. The praisers, who are the sacrificers of Vṛṣākapi, were sent forth and permitted by me for the sacrifice (व्यसृक्षत (*vyasṛkṣata*)); हि (*hi*) is a filler. There देवं (*devaṃ*) means shining

### Printed p. 457

> मिंद्रं मां नामंसत । मया प्रेरिताः संतोऽपि ते स्तोतारो न स्तुतवंतः ।
> किंतु मनु पुत्रं वृषाकपिमेव स्तुतवंतः । यत्र येषु पुष्टेषु सोमेन
> प्रवृद्धेषु यागेऽवर्यः स्वामी वृषाकपिर्मम पुत्रो मत्सखा मनु सखिभूतः
> सन्नमदत् सोमपानेन हृष्टोऽभूत् । यद्यस्येवं तथापींद्रोऽहं विश्वस्मात्सर्वस्माज्जगत उत्तरः । उत्कृष्टतरः ॥ माधवभट्टास्तु वि हि सोतोरित्येषर्गिंद्राण्या
> वाक्यमिति मन्यंते । तथा च तद्वचनं । इंद्राणै कल्पितं हविः कश्चिन्मगोऽदूदुषदिंद्रपुत्रस्य वृषाकपीर्विषये वर्तमानः । तत्रेंद्रमिंद्राणी वदति तस्मिन्पक्षे
> त्वस्या ऋचोऽयमर्थः । सोतोः सोमाभिषवं कर्तुं वि ह्यसृक्षत । उपरतसोमाभिषवा आसन्यजमाना इत्यर्थः । किंच मम पतिमिंद्रं देवं नामंसत ।
> स्तोतारो न स्तुवंति । कुत्रेति अत्राह । यत्र यस्मिन्वेशे पुष्टेषु प्रवृद्धेषु
> धनेऽवर्यः स्वामी वृषाकपिरमदत् । मत्सखा मत्तियश्चेंद्रो विश्वस्मात्सर्वस्माज्जगत उत्तरः । उत्कृष्टतरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*) is me. They did not praise me. Although sent forth by me, those praisers did not praise me, but praised my son Vṛṣākapi alone **NOTE**. यत्र (*yatra*): in those sacrifices that were fortified with Soma, the lord Vṛṣākapi, my son, my friend, being as it were a companion, rejoiced, that is, was delighted by drinking Soma. Although this is so, I, Indra, am above the whole world, more excellent. The followers of Mādhavabhaṭṭa, however, think that this Ṛk वि हि सोतोः (*vi hi sotoḥ*) is the speech of Indrāṇī; and they cite his statement: some animal, being in the sphere of Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra, spoiled the oblation prepared for Indrāṇī; there Indrāṇī speaks to Indra. According to that view the meaning of this Ṛk is as follows. The sacrificers have left off pressing Soma, that is, they have stopped the Soma-pressing. Moreover, they do not praise my husband, the god Indra. Where? Where, in which place, when the wealth was increased, the lord Vṛṣākapi rejoiced. And Indra, the friend, is above the whole world, more excellent. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुष्टेषु (*puṣṭeṣu*)—those that have grown by Soma juice
- यत्र (*yatra*)—in which sacrifices
- मत्सखा (*matsakhā*)—my friend
- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—and lord
- वृषाकपिः (*vṛṣākapiḥ*)—Vṛṣākapi (my son)
- अमदत् (*amadat*)—rejoiced; there
- सोतोः (*sotoḥ*)—to press Soma for the sacrifice
- व्यसृक्षत (*vyasṛkṣata*)—the priests were appointed by me myself
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the shining one
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—and the lord, me alone
- न अमंसत (*na amaṃsata*)—(although) they did not praise
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In those sacrifices enriched by Soma, in which Vṛṣākapi, my friend, lord and son, rejoiced, the priests were appointed by me myself to press Soma for the sacrifice. Yet they did not praise me alone, the shining one and the lord. Even so, Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indra speaks : ] They have neglected the pressing of the Soma, they have not praised the divine Indra at the cherished (sacrifices), at which the noble Vrishakapi becoming my friend rejoiced: (still) I, Indra, am above all (the world).

### Printed p. 458

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

वि हि सोतोः अस्पृक्षत न इंद्रं देवं अमंसत (*vi hi sotoḥ aspṛkṣata na iṃdraṃ devaṃ amaṃsata*)—this is the speech of Indra.

वृषाकपेय्र्यष्टारो स्तोतारो मया अनुज्ञाताः संतोऽपि तद्यज्ञे देवं इंद्रं मां न अमंसत । मया प्रेरिताः संतोऽपि ते स्तोतारो न स्तुतवंतः । किंतु मम पुत्रं वृषाकपिमेव स्तुतवंतः ॥ (*vṛṣākapeyryaṣṭāro stotāro mayā anujñātāḥ saṃto 'pi tadyajñe devaṃ iṃdraṃ māṃ na amaṃsata | mayā preritāḥ saṃto 'pi te stotāro na stutavaṃtaḥ | kiṃtu mama putraṃ vṛṣākapimeva stutavaṃtaḥ ‖*) Vṛṣākapi is my son. The priests who took part in the sacrifice he was performing were commanded by me myself to press the Soma juice. Yet they did not praise me, who am the chief leader of the sacrifice and the god. Instead of that they praised my son Vṛṣākapi alone.

यत्र पुष्टेषु अर्यः वृषाकपि मत्सखा अमदत् इंद्रः विश्वस्मात् उत्तरःसोमेन प्रवृद्धेषु येषु यागेषु स्वामी वृषाकपि सखिभूतः मम पुत्रः सोमपानेन हृष्टोऽभूत् यद्यस्येवं तथापि इंद्रः अहं सर्वस्माज्जगतः उत्कृष्टतरः ॥ (*yatra puṣṭeṣu aryaḥ vṛṣākapi matsakhā amadat iṃdraḥ viśvasmāt uttaraḥsomena pravṛddheṣu yeṣu yāgeṣu svāmī vṛṣākapi sakhibhūtaḥ mama putraḥ somapānena hṛṣṭo 'bhūt yadyasyevaṃ tathāpi iṃdraḥ ahaṃ sarvasmājjagataḥ utkṛṣṭataraḥ ‖*) In the sacrifice performed by Vṛṣākapi the pressing of the Soma went on as much as desired. My son Vṛṣākapi, who is like a friend to me, drank Soma abundantly in that sacrifice and became delighted. Even so, I, Indra, am greater than the whole world.

The main purport is this: I, Indra, am greater than the whole world; there is no one who surpasses me. Yet when the priests, commanded by me myself, performed the pressing of the Soma in the sacrifice that my son Vṛṣākapi was performing, they did not praise me, the chief leader of the sacrifice; they praised Vṛṣākapi alone. Indra has expressed his sorrow that this is highly improper.

One called Mādhavabhaṭṭa (Peṅkaṭamādhava **NOTE**, who lived before Sāyaṇa and who also wrote a commentary on the Ṛgveda) has indicated his opinion that the statement made in this Ṛk is not made by Indra but is the speech of Indrāṇī, in the following way—

इंद्राण्यै कल्पितं हविः कश्चिन्मृगोऽदूदुषदिंद्रस्य वृषाकपेर्विषये वर्तमानः । तत्रेंद्रमिंद्राणी वदति । तस्मिन्पक्षे त्वस्या ऋचोऽयमर्थः । सोतोः सोमाभिषवं कर्तुं वि ह्यसृक्षत । उपरतसोमाभिषवा आसन् यजमाना इत्यर्थः । किंच मम पतिमिंद्रं देवं नामंसत स्तोतारो न स्तुवंति । कुत्रॆति अत्राह । यत्र यस्मिन् जनपदे पुष्टेषु प्रवृद्धेषु धनेष्वर्यः स्वामी वृषाकपिरमदत् । मत्सखा मत्र्ययश्चेंद्रो विश्वस्मात्सर्वस्माज्जगत उत्तरः उत्कृष्टतरः ॥ (*iṃdrāṇyai kalpitaṃ haviḥ kaścinmṛgo 'dūduṣadiṃdrasya vṛṣākaperviṣaye vartamānaḥ | tatreṃdramiṃdrāṇī vadati | tasminpakṣe tvasyā ṛco 'yamarthaḥ | sotoḥ somābhiṣavaṃ kartuṃ vi hyasṛkṣata | uparatasomābhiṣavā āsan yajamānā ityarthaḥ | kiṃca mama patimiṃdraṃ devaṃ nāmaṃsata stotāro na stuvaṃti | kutrèti atrāha | yatra yasmin janapade puṣṭeṣu pravṛddheṣu dhaneṣvaryaḥ svāmī vṛṣākapiramadat | matsakhā matryayaśceṃdro viśvasmātsarvasmājjagata uttaraḥ utkṛṣṭataraḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 459

Formerly, at one time, an animal living in the realm of Vṛṣākapi, the son of Indra, spoiled and ruined the oblation prepared for the goddess Indrāṇī. What Indrāṇī said to Indra on that occasion is stated in this Ṛk. The sacrificers who had engaged in the work of pressing Soma juice in the sacrifice were resting after pressing the Soma juice. At that time a wicked animal spoiled the Soma juice that had been pressed. And in that sacrifice the priests and sacrificers did not praise my husband Indra at all. All this took place in the realm of Vṛṣākapi, which was abundant in every kind of wealth. Vṛṣākapi was the lord of such a country and lived there happily. Indra, who is like a friend to me and is dear to me, is no ordinary person. He is greater than the whole world. The main purport is that there is none greater or more excellent than he.

For this Ṛk Yāska, in the Pariśiṣṭa chapter, having said अथेमा अतिस्तुतय इत्याचक्षते (*athemā atistutaya ityācakṣate*), that is, "we shall explain some mantras that indicate a meaning different from the ordinary meaning", has given an etymological explanation of this Ṛk. It refers to the Sun. Therefore I shall explain it here—

व्यसृक्षत हि प्रसवाय न चेंद्रं देवममंसत यत्रा माद्यत् वृषाकपिरर्य ईश्वरः पुष्टेषु पोषेषु मत्सखा मनु सखा मदनसखा ये नः सखायस्मै सहेति ना सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूम आदित्यं ॥ (*vyasṛkṣata hi prasavāya na ceṃdraṃ devamamaṃsata yatrā mādyat vṛṣākapirarya īśvaraḥ puṣṭeṣu poṣeṣu matsakhā manu sakhā madanasakhā ye naḥ sakhāyasmai saheti nā sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūma ādityaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 13-4)

We shall first set out the commentary written on this by Durgācārya, the commentator of the Nirukta, and then give the meaning in translation—

व्यसृक्षत यदादित्यो रश्मीनहन्यहनि सोतोः सर्वभूतप्रसवाय, अभ्यनुज्ञानाय, तत्प्रकाशितलोकस्य सर्वकर्मोपपत्तेः । तदा किं ? इति । तदा ते रश्मयः सर्वकर्मण्यनुगमनात् नेंद्रं देवममंसत तमेवेंद्रमादित्यं येन विसृष्टाः तमेतमात्मनो दीपयितारं न मन्यंते स्वमहिम्मेव दीप्यामह इति मन्यंते । (*vyasṛkṣata yadādityo raśmīnahanyahani sotoḥ sarvabhūtaprasavāya, abhyanujñānāya, tatprakāśitalokasya sarvakarmopapatteḥ | tadā kiṃ ? iti | tadā te raśmayaḥ sarvakarmaṇyanugamanāt neṃdraṃ devamamaṃsata tameveṃdramādityaṃ yena visṛṣṭāḥ tametamātmano dīpayitāraṃ na manyaṃte svamahimmeva dīpyāmaha iti manyaṃte |*)

कदा ? यत्र यदा अमदत् वृषाकपिः अर्यः स्वामिा रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति पुष्टेषु एकीभूतेषु मध्यंदिने । मत्सखा मम सखा इति मंत्रदृगाह। अथवा सर्व एव मन्यते ममायं सखा ममायं सखा इति । अथवा मदनसखा हर्षसखेत्यर्थः । अथवा ये नः सखायः रश्मयः तै सहेति । विश्वस्मात् इति उक्तार्थः । (*kadā ? yatra yadā amadat vṛṣākapiḥ aryaḥ svāmiā raśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati puṣṭeṣu ekībhūteṣu madhyaṃdine | matsakhā mama sakhā iti maṃtradṛgāha| athavā sarva eva manyate mamāyaṃ sakhā mamāyaṃ sakhā iti | athavā madanasakhā harṣasakhetyarthaḥ | athavā ye naḥ sakhāyaḥ raśmayaḥ tai saheti | viśvasmāt iti uktārthaḥ |*) (Niru. Bhā. 13.4) **NOTE**

In this Ṛk the meaning referring to the rays of the Sun is explained. Here the Sun, who is the cause of the act of raining, is called Vṛṣākapi. वि हि सोतोरसृक्षत (*vi hi sotorasṛkṣata*)—that is, the one who is the cause of the birth of all living beings

### Printed p. 460

is the Sun. Such a Sun sent forth his rays, that is, spread them, scattered them over the whole world, for the birth of all living beings, or for the activities of the whole world illumined by him to go on. But although those rays, or beams, went out from the Sun, they did not know him, who is their cause and lord (the Sun himself). That is, forgetting that they shine by the greatness of the Sun, they fell into the delusion that they shine by their own greatness. When is this? अमदत् (*amadat*) वृषाकपि (*vṛṣākapi*) आर्यः पुष्टेषु (*āryaḥ puṣṭeṣu*)—when this Sun, the lord of the whole world, shines concentrating all his power, that is, at midday. At midday the light of the Sun is very intense. Here the meaning of the word मत्सखा (*matsakhā*) is this: the seer who saw the sūkta has called the Sun मत्सखा (*matsakhā*), "my friend", in the highest affection; or मत्सखा (*matsakhā*) means मदनसखा (*madanasakhā*), a friend who produces joy. Or ये नः सखायः तै सहेति (*ye naḥ sakhāyaḥ tai saheti*): it can also be said that the meaning is the Sun accompanied by those rays that are beneficial to me like friends. The purport of the etymology is that such a Sun shines unequalled (supreme) in the whole world.

In the last quarter of every Ṛk of this sūkta the qualifying sentence विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः (*viśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ*), praising Indra, is recited again and again like a refrain.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परा॒ हीं॑द्र॒ धाव॑सि वृ॒षाक॑पे॒रति॒ व्यथिः॑ ।  
> नो अह॒ प्र विं॑दस्य॒न्यत्र॒ सोम॑पीतये॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒ उत्त॑रः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परा । हि । इंद्र । धावसि । वृषाकपेः । अति । व्यथिः ।  
> नो इति । अह । प्र । विंदसि । अन्यत्र । सोमपीतये । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वमत्यत्यंतं व्यथिश्चलितो वृषाकपेवृषाकपिं परा धावसि ।
> प्रतिगच्छसि । अन्यत्र सोमपीतये सोमपानाय नो अह नैव च प्र विंदसि ।
> प्रगच्छसीत्यर्थः । सोऽयमिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you, greatly agitated (व्यथिः (*vyathiḥ*), moved), run towards Vṛṣākapi, that is, go to him. And you do not at all go to another place to drink Soma (सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*), for Soma-drinking); the meaning of प्र विंदसि (*pra viṃdasi*) is that you go forth. This Indra is above all.

### Printed p. 461

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अति व्यथि (*ati vyathi*)—very distressed in mind
- वृषाकपेः परा (*vṛṣākapeḥ parā*)—towards Vṛṣākapi
- धावसि (*dhāvasi*)—you run
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for drinking Soma
- अन्यत्र (*anyatra*)—to another place
- नो अह प्र विंदसि (*no aha pra viṃdasi*)—you certainly do not go at all
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, greatly distressed in mind, you run towards Vṛṣākapi. You do not go to another place to drink Soma. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indrani speaks: ] You, Indra, much annoyed, hasten towards Vrishakapi; and yet you find no other place to drink the Soma; Indra is above all (the world).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> किम॒यं त्वां वृ॒षाक॑पिश्च॒कार॒ हरि॑तो मृ॒गः ।  
> यस्मा॑ इर॒स्यसीदु॒ नृ १ १॒॑र्यो वा॑ पुष्टि॒मद्वसु॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒द्रिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> किं । अयं । त्वां । वृषाकपिः । चकार । हरितः । मृगः ।  
> यस्मै । अरस्यसि । इत् । ऊं इति । नु ! अर्यः । वा । पुष्टिमत् । वसु । विश्वस्यात् ।  
> इंद्रः । उत्तरः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वां प्रति हरितो हरितवर्णो मृगो मृगभूतोऽयं वृषाकपिः ।
> मृगजातिर्हि वृषाकपिः । किं प्रियं चकार । अकार्षित् । यस्मै वृषाकपये
> पुष्टिमत्पोषयुक्तं वसु धनमर्यो वोदार इव स त्वं नु क्षिप्रमिरस्य सीत्
> प्रयच्छस्येव । य इंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this Vṛṣākapi, the green (हरित (*harita*)) animal, has become an animal in relation to you; for Vṛṣākapi belongs to the class of animals. What pleasing thing has he done, did he do? To that Vṛṣākapi you give nourishing wealth as a generous lord would; you quickly give it. This Indra is above all.

- पुष्टिमत् (*puṣṭimat*)—that which is a means of nourishment

- अर्यो न (*aryo na*)—like a generous giver
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- इरस्यसीत् (*irasyasīt*)—you gave; to such

- मृगः (*mṛgaḥ*)—the one of animal form

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, what good has that green-coloured Vṛṣākapi, of animal form, to whom you gave nourishing wealth like a generous giver, done to you? Indra is more excellent than the whole world.

##### English translation
What (favour) has this tawny dear Vrishakapi done to you that you should, like a liberal (banefactor), bestow upon him wealth and nourish ment ? Indra is above all (the world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

O Indra, what service has that green-coloured animal Vṛṣākapi done to you? Why do you give him wealth and nourishing food like a generous giver? This is the main purport.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यमि॒नं त्वं वृ॒षाक॑सिं प्रि॒यमिं॑द्राभि॒रक्ष॑सि ।  
> श्वा न्व॑स्य जंभिष॒दपि॒ कर्णे॑ वराह॒युर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒ उत्त॑रः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । इमं । त्वं । वृषाकपिं । प्रियं । इंद्र । अभिरक्षसि ।  
> श्वा । नु । अस्य । जंभिषत् । अपि । कर्णे । वराहयुः । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः।  
> उत्तरः ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 463

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं प्रियमिष्टं पुत्रं यमिमं वृषाकपिमभिरक्षसि परिपालयसि
> अस्यैनं वृषाकपिं । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी । वराहयुर्वराहमिच्छञ्वा नु क्षिप्रं
> उंभिषत् । भक्षयतु । अपि च कर्णे गृह्ण्णात्विति शेषः । श्वानो हि वराहमिच्छंति ।
> सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this Vṛṣākapi, your dear, beloved son, whom you protect and cherish: अस्य (*asya*) stands for the sixth case in the sense of the second, that is, this Vṛṣākapi. May a dog that desires a boar (वराहयुः (*varāhayuḥ*)) quickly devour (उंभिषत् (*uṃbhiṣat*)) him, that is, eat him; "and let it seize him by the ear" is to be supplied. For dogs desire a boar. The rest is established. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—dear to you
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom
- इमं वृषाकपिं (*imaṃ vṛṣākapiṃ*)—this Vṛṣākapi
- अभिरक्षसि (*abhirakṣasi*)—you protect
- अस्य (*asya*)—such this Vṛṣākapi
- वराहयुः (*varāhayuḥ*)—desirous of catching a boar
- श्वा (*śvā*)—a dog
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- कर्णे (*karṇe*)—seizing by the ear
- जंभिषत् (*jaṃbhiṣat*)—may it swallow
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may a dog desirous of catching a boar quickly seize by the ear this Vṛṣākapi, dear to you, whom you protect, and swallow him. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
This Vrishakapi whom you, Indra, cherish as your dear (son)—may the dog which chases the boar (seize) him by the ear (and) devour him ; Indra is above all (the world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Indrāṇī, disgusted with regard to Vṛṣākapi, speaks thus: O Indra, I cannot bear to see this Vṛṣākapi whom you protect with so much pride. As a hunting dog chases a wild boar and brings it, holding it by the ear, so may a dog quickly bite this Vṛṣākapi and eat him up.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रि॒या त॒ष्टानि॑ मे क॒पिव्य॑क्ता॒ व्य॑दूदुषत् ।  
> शिरो॒ न्व॑स्य राविषं॒ न सु॒गं दु॒ष्कृते॑ भुवं॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 464

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रिया । तष्टानि । मे । कपिः । विअक्ता । वि । अदूदुषत् ।  
> शिरः । नु । अस्य । राविषं । न । सुगं । दुःकृते । भुवं । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मह्यमिंद्राण्यै तष्टानि यजमानैः कल्पितानि प्रिया प्रियाणि व्यक्ता
> व्यक्तान्याज्यैर्विशेषेणाक्तानि हवींषि कश्चिद्वृषाकपीर्विषये वर्तमानः कपिर्व्यदूदुषत् । दूषयामास । ततोऽहमस्य तत्कपिस्वामिनो वृषाकपेः शिरो नु क्षिप्रं
> राविषं। लुनीयां । दुष्कृते दुष्टस्यकर्मणः कर्त्रे वृषाकपयेऽस्मै सुगं सुखं
> न भुवं । अहं न भवेयं । आस्मै सुखप्रदात्रि न भवामीत्यर्थः । अस्या मम
> पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मे (*me*): for me, Indrāṇī, the oblations (तष्टानि (*taṣṭāni*)) prepared by the sacrificers, dear (प्रिया (*priyā*)) and specially anointed (व्यक्ता (*vyaktā*)) with ghee: some ape (कपिः (*kapiḥ*)) living in the realm of Vṛṣākapi has spoiled them (व्यदूदुषत् (*vyadūduṣat*)), that is, defiled them. Therefore I shall quickly cut off (राविषं (*rāviṣaṃ*)) the head of Vṛṣākapi, the master of that ape. To this Vṛṣākapi, the doer of an evil deed, I shall not be (न भुवं (*na bhuvaṃ*)) a giver of happiness (सुगं (*sugaṃ*)). My husband Indra is above all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—addressed to me (Indrāṇī)
- तप्पानि (*tappāni*)—prepared by the sacrificers
- प्रिया (*priyā*)—beneficial
- व्यक्ता (*vyaktā*)—filled with ghee, the oblation
- कपिः (*kapiḥ*)—this wicked ape in the country of this Vṛṣākapi
- व्यदूदुषत् (*vyadūduṣat*)—has spoiled (therefore)
- अस्य (*asya*)—of Vṛṣākapi, the master of this wicked ape
- शिरो नु (*śiro nu*)—the head
- राविषं (*rāviṣaṃ*)—I shall cut off
- दुष्क, ते (*duṣka, te*)—to one who does an evil deed
- सुगं (*sugaṃ*)—happiness
- न भुवं (*na bhuvaṃ*)—I shall not give the opportunity to be produced
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This ape has spoiled the oblation, prepared by the sacrificers for me, Indrāṇī, beneficial to me and filled with ghee. I shall cut off its head. I shall not give an opportunity for happiness to one who does an evil deed. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
The ape has spoiled the beloved ghi-adorned (oblations) made to me (by worshippers); let me quickly cut off his head, let me not be the giver of happiness to one who works evil; Indra is above all (the world).

### Printed p. 465

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Kapiḥ: the commentator explains this word as वृषाकर्पेर्विषये वर्तमानः कश्चित् कपिः (*vṛṣākarperviṣaye vartamānaḥ kaścit kapiḥ*), that is, some wicked ape living in the realm of Vṛṣākapi. And with अस्य शिरो नु क्षिप्रं राविषं—तत्कपिस्वामिनो वृषाकपेः शिरः लुनीयां । (*asya śiro nu kṣipraṃ rāviṣaṃ—tatkapisvāmino vṛṣākapeḥ śiraḥ lunīyāṃ |*) he means: therefore I shall cut off the head of this Vṛṣākapi, who is the master of that ape, says Indrāṇī. This too is seen in worldly practice. It is the custom to punish the owner of an animal for the evil deed done by the animal. For example, if a cow or a dog does harm to another person, it is common to bring the owner of that animal to punishment.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> न मत्स्यी सु॑भ॒सत्त॑रा॒ न सु॒याशु॑तरा भुवत् ।  
> न मत्प्रति॑च्यवीयसी॒ न सक्थुद्य॑मीयसी॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । मत् । स्त्री । सुभसत्९तरा । न । सुयाशु९तरा । भुवत् ।  
> न । मत् । प्रतिच्यवीयसी । न । सक्ति । उत्९यमीयसी । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्९तरः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मन्मत्तोऽन्या स्त्री नारी सुभसत्तरातिशयेन सुभगा न भुवत् । न भवति ।
> नास्तित्यर्थः । किंच मत्तोऽन्या स्त्री सुयाशुतरातिशयेन सुसुखातिशयेन सुपुत्रा
> वा न भवति । तथा च मंत्रांतरं । ददाति मह्यं यादुरी याशूनां भोज्या
> शता । ऋ. १-१२६-६ । इति । किंच मन्मत्तोऽन्या प्रतिच्यवीयसी पुमांसं प्रति
> शरीरस्यात्यंतं च्यावयित्रि नास्ति । किंच मत्तोऽन्या स्त्री सक्तुद्यमायसी
> संभोगेऽत्यंतमुत्कृष्टेनास्ति । न मत्तोऽन्या काचिदपि नारी मैथुनेऽनुगुणं
> सक्तुद्यच्छतीत्यर्थः । मम पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः । उत्कृष्टः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Another woman than I, स्त्री (*strī*), is not सुभसत्तरा (*subhasattarā*), exceedingly fortunate: there is none. Further, no other woman than I is exceedingly happy, सुयाशुतरा (*suyāśutarā*), or else the mother of good sons. In this sense another mantra says ददाति मह्यं यादुरी याशूनां भोज्या शता (*dadāti mahyaṃ yādurī yāśūnāṃ bhojyā śatā*) (Ṛ. 1-126-6) **GLOSS**. Further, no other woman than I is प्रतिच्यवीयसी (*praticyavīyasī*), one who, in relation to a man, exceedingly causes the body to be moved. Further, no other woman than I is सक्तुद्यमायसी (*saktudyamāyasī*), one who is exceedingly excellent in union; that is, no other woman at all offers her thigh in a manner suited to the union. My husband Indra is above all, superior. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मत् (*mat*)—than me
- सुभसत्तरा (*subhasattarā*)—possessing greater good fortune
- स्त्री (*strī*)—woman!
- न भुवत् (*na bhuvat*)—there is none at all
- सुयाशुतरा (*suyāśutarā*)—a greater giver of happiness
- न (*na*)—there is none that exceeds me

### Printed p. 466

- मत् (*mat*)—than me
- प्रतिच्यवीयसी (*praticyavīyasī*)—one who agrees with her husband
- न (*na*)—there is no other
- सक्षि (*sakṣi*)—when husband and wife are together
- उद्यमीयसी (*udyamīyasī*)—one of greater compliance than I
- न (*na*)—there is no other
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is the most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

There is no woman more fortunate than I. There is none who gives more happiness. There is no other woman beyond me who agrees with her husband and, when husband and wife are together, follows her husband's wish. Indra is the most excellent, above the whole world.

##### English translation
There is no woman more amiable than I am, nor one who bears fairer sons than I ; nor one more tractable nor one more ardent; Indra is above all (the world),

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒वे अं॑ब सुलाभिके॒ यथे॑वां॒ग भ॑वि॒ष्यति॑ ।  
> भ॒सन्ने॑ अंब॒ सक्ति॑ मे॒ शिरो॑ मे॒ वी॑व हृष्यति॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उवे । अंब । सुलाभिके : यथा इव । अंग । भविष्यति ।  
> बसत् । मे । अंब । सक्ति । मे । शिरः । मे । विइव । हृष्यति । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवमिंद्राण्या शप्पो वृषाकपिर्ब्रवीति । उवे इति संबोधनार्थो निपातः ।
> हे अंब मातः सुलाभिके शोभनलाभे त्वया यथैव येन प्रकारेणैवोक्तं
> तथैव तदंग क्षिप्रं भविष्यति । भवतु । किमनेन त्वदनुप्रीतिकारिणा ग्रहेण मम
> प्रयोजनं । किंच मे मम पितुस्त्वदीयो भसद्भग उपयुज्यतां । किंच मम

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Thus addressed by Indrāṇī in anger, Vṛṣākapi speaks. उवे (*uve*) is a particle in the sense of address. O mother (अंब (*aṃba*)), सुलाभिके (*sulābhike*), one of fair gain: in just the manner in which you have spoken, so it will quickly (अंग (*aṃga*)) be. Let it be so; what use have I of this seizing of yours that works your pleasure? Further, let your भसद्भग (*bhasadbhaga*) be put to use for my father, and your सक्कि (*sakki*) be put to use as well.

### Printed p. 467

> पितुस्त्वदीयं सक्कि चोपयुज्यतां । किंच मे मम पितरमिंद्रं त्वदीयं शिरश
> प्रियालापेन वीव यथा कोकिलादिः पक्षी तद्वद्धृष्यति। हर्षयतु। मम पितेंद्रो
> विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Further, your head delights, हृष्यति (*hṛṣyati*), my father Indra with pleasing speech, as a cuckoo or other such bird does (वीव (*vīva*)); let it delight him. My father Indra is above all, superior. **NOTE**

- उवे अंब (*uve aṃba*)—O mother
- यथैव (*yathaiva*)—just as you have said
- अंग (*aṃga*)—quickly
- भविष्यति (*bhaviṣyati*)—let it come to pass
- अंब (*aṃba*)—mother
- सक्ति (*sakti*)—while you are with your husband
- मे (*me*)—my father Indra
- भसत् (*bhasat*)—let him enjoy happiness with you
- वीव (*vīva*)—like a bird
- शिरः (*śiraḥ*)—your head
- मे (*me*)—my father Indra
- हृष्यति (*hṛṣyati*)—let it delight
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is the most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mother, who bestow favour with ease, let it be fulfilled quickly just as you have said. While you are with your husband, let my father Indra enjoy happiness with you. Let your head delight my father Indra like a bird. Indra is the most excellent, above the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Vrishakapi speaks ] : O mother, who are easy of access, it wil quickly be as (you have said) ; may my (father) and you, mother, be uni- ted ; may it delight my (father) and your head like a bird : Indra is above all (the world).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra pacifies her who is angry. O fair-armed one (सुबाहो (*subāho*)), O fair-fingered one (स्वंगुरे (*svaṃgure*)), O you of a broad mass of hair (पृथुष्टो (*pṛthuṣṭo*)), O broad-hipped one (पृथुजघने (*pṛthujaghane*)), O wife of a hero (शूरपत्नि (*śūrapatni*)), O Indrāṇī: why are you angry (अभ्यमीषि (*abhyamīṣi*)) with our Vṛṣākapi? The word किं (*kiṃ*) is one only. I, Indra, whose father I am, am above all, superior.

- किं अभ्यमीषि (*kiṃ abhyamīṣi*)—why are you angry
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—I, the lord of the world

- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—am the most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indrāṇī, you of excellent arms, of fine fingers, of a full mass of hair, of broad hips, wife of a hero: why are you angry with my son Vṛṣākapi? I, the lord of the world, am the most excellent, above the whole world.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)
