> मम पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indrāṇī again speaks to Indra. This शरारुः (*śarāruḥ*), a destructive beast, Vṛṣākapi, regards (अभि मन्यते (*abhi manyate*)), that is, takes me, Indrāṇī, as if one without a hero. And I am Indra's wife (इंद्रपत्नी (*iṃdrapatnī*)), I am वीरिणी (*vīriṇī*), one who has sons, and I am मरुत्सखा (*marutsakhā*), joined with the Maruts. My husband Indra is above all, superior.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शरारुः (*śarāruḥ*)—this Vṛṣākapi, a destructive beast
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this
- मां (*māṃ*)—me
- अवितां इव (*avitāṃ iva*)—as one without the protection of a hero (thinking)
- अभि मन्यते (*abhi manyate*)—speaks with contempt
- उत (*uta*)—in truth
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- इंद्रपत्नि (*iṃdrapatni*)—am the wife of Indra, the hero
- वीरिणी (*vīriṇī*)—and have heroic sons
- मरुत्सखा (*marutsakhā*)—and am joined with the Maruts
- अस्मि (*asmi*)—am
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—my husband Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Vṛṣākapi, a wicked beast, thinks of me as one without the protection of a hero and speaks with contempt. But Indra, the hero, is my husband. I have heroic sons. The heroic Maruts are my friends. My husband Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
Indrani speaks : ] This savage beast (Vrishakapi) despises me as one who has no male (protector), and yet I am the mother of male off-spring, the wife of Indra, the friend of the Maruts; Indra is above all (the world).

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं॒हो॒त्रं स्म॑ पु॒रा नारी॒ सम॑नं॒ वाव॑ गच्छति ।  
> वे॒धा ऋ॒तस्य॑ वी॒रिणेंद्र॑पत्नी महीयते॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒ उत्त॑रः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> संहोत्रं । स्म । पुरा । नारी । समनं । वा । अव । गच्छति ।

### Printed p. 470

> वेधाः । ऋतस्य । वीरिणी । इंद्रपत्नी । महीयते । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ १८ ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नारी स्त्रैतस्य सत्यस्य वेधा विधात्रि वीरिणी पुत्रवतींद्रपत्नींद्रस्य भार्येंद्राणी संहोत्रं स्म समीचीनं यज्ञं खलु समनं वा संग्रामं । समनमिति
> संग्रामनामसु पाठात् । अव प्रति पुरा गच्छति । महीयते । स्तोतृभिः स्तूयते
> च । तस्या मम पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The woman, नारी (*nārī*), Indrāṇī, is the maker (वेधा (*vedhā*)) of this truth, वीरिणी (*vīriṇī*), one who has sons, and इंद्रपत्नी (*iṃdrapatnī*), the wife of Indra. She goes (गच्छति (*gacchati*)) forward (पुरा (*purā*)) to the संहोत्रं (*saṃhotraṃ*), a good sacrifice, and to the समनं (*samanaṃ*), battle, since समनमिति संग्रामनामसु पाठात् (*samanamiti saṃgrāmanāmasu pāṭhāt*), the word samana is read among the names of battle. She is honoured (महीयते (*mahīyate*)), that is, praised by the praisers. My husband Indra is above all, superior.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—of truth
- विधात्रि (*vidhātri*)—the maker
- वीरिणी (*vīriṇī*)—one who has heroic sons
- इंद्र पत्नि (*iṃdra patni*)—who is also the wife of Indra
- नारी (*nārī*)—Indrāṇī
- संहोत्रं स्म (*saṃhotraṃ sma*)—to a good sacrifice
- समनं वा (*samanaṃ vā*)—or to battle
- अव (*ava*)—facing
- पुरा (*purā*)—before all
- गच्छति (*gacchati*)—goes
- महीयते (*mahīyate*)—there is praised by the praisers
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indrāṇī, the maker of truth, mother of heroic sons and wife of Indra, goes before all, whether to a good sacrifice or to battle. There she is praised by the praisers. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
The mother who is the institutress of the ceremony, the mother of male offspring, the wife of Indra, goes first to the united sacrifice, to battle (and) is honoured (by the praisers); Indra is above all (the world).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इं॒द्रा॒णीमा॒सु नारि॑षु सु॒भगा॑म॒हम॑श्रवं ।  
> न॒ह्य॑स्या अप॒रं च॒न ज॒रसा॒ मर॑ते॒ पति॒र्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒ उत्त॑रः ॥११॥

### Printed p. 471

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राणीं । आसु । नारिषु । सुभगां । अहं । अश्रवं ।  
> नहि । आस्त्याः । अपरं । चन । जरसा । मरते । पतिः । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः । उत्तरः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथेंद्राणीमिंद्रः स्तौति । आसु सौभाग्यवत्तया प्रसिद्धासु नारीषु स्त्रीषु
> स्त्रीणां मध्य इंद्राणीं सुभगां सौभाग्यवतीमहमिंद्रोऽश्रवं । अशौषं ।
> किंचास्या इंद्राण्याः पतिः पालको विश्वस्मादुत्तर उत्कृष्टतर इंद्रोऽपरं चनान्यद्भूतजातमिव जरसा वयोहान्या न हि मरते । न खलु म्रियते । यद्वा ।
> इदं वृषाकपीर्वाक्यं । तस्मिन्पक्षे त्वहमिति शब्दो वृषाकपिपरतया योज्यः ।
> अन्यत्समानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Indra praises Indrāṇī. Among these women (नारीषु (*nārīṣu*)), famed for good fortune, I, Indra, have heard (अश्रवं (*aśravaṃ*), that is, अशौषं (*aśauṣaṃ*)) that Indrāṇī is fortunate (सुभगां (*subhagāṃ*)), possessed of good fortune. Further, her husband, her protector Indra, who is above all, more excellent, does not die of old age (जरसा (*jarasā*), by loss of vigour) like any other creature. Or else this is the speech of Vṛṣākapi; on that view the word अहं (*ahaṃ*) is to be applied to Vṛṣākapi. The rest is the same.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आसु नारिषु (*āsu nāriṣu*)—among all these women
- इंद्राणीं (*iṃdrāṇīṃ*)—Indrāṇī alone
- सुभगां (*subhagāṃ*)—as a most excellent fortunate woman
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अश्रवं (*aśravaṃ*)—have heard
- अस्याः (*asyāḥ*)—her
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—protector
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is the most excellent
- अपरं च न (*aparaṃ ca na*)—not like other people
- जरसा (*jarasā*)—by old age
- न हि मरते (*na hi marate*)—does not die

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have heard that among all these women Indrāṇī is the most excellent and fortunate. Indra, who is greater than the whole world, is her husband. He does not die of old age like other people.

##### English translation
[ Indra speaks:] I have heard that Indrani is the most fortunate among these women, for her lord Indra, who is above all (the world), does not die of old age like other (men).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk Yāska has given the Nirukta: इंद्राणी इंद्रस्य पत्निः तस्यैषा भवति । इंद्राणीमासु नारिषु सुभगामहमश्रवं । न ह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ इंद्राणीमासु नारिषु सुभगामहमशृणवं न्य ह्यस्या अपरामपि समां जरया म्रियते पतिः सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूमः ॥ (*iṃdrāṇī iṃdrasya patniḥ tasyaiṣā bhavati | iṃdrāṇīmāsu nāriṣu subhagāmahamaśravaṃ | na hyasyā aparaṃ cana jarasā marate patirviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖ iṃdrāṇīmāsu nāriṣu subhagāmahamaśṛṇavaṃ nya hyasyā aparāmapi samāṃ jarayā mriyate patiḥ sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūmaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 11-38)

### Printed p. 472

Indrāṇī means the wife of Indra. In the Ṛk that follows there is mention of Indrāṇī. I have heard that Indrāṇī, the wife of Indra, is endowed with the greatest good fortune of all other women. For, however many years may pass, her husband Indra never at any time dies of old age. The main purport of the Nirukta is that Indra is the most excellent one, greater than the whole world.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नाहमिं॑द्राणि रारण॒ सख्यु॑र्वृ॒षाक॑पेर्यु॒ते ।  
> यस्ये॒नमष्यं॑ ह॒विः प्रि॒यं दे॒वेषु॒ गच्छ॑ति॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । अहं । इंद्राणि । ररण । सख्युः । वृषाकपेः । ऋते ।  
> यस्य । इदं । अप्यं । हविः । प्रियं । देवेषु । गच्छति । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्कतरः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्राणि अहमिंद्रः सख्युर्मम सखिभूताद्वृषाकपेर्यते प्रियं
> वृषाकपिं विना न रराण । न रमे । अप्यमप्पु भवमद्भिर्वा सुसंस्कृतं प्रियं
> प्रीतिकरमिदमुपस्थितं हविर्देवेषु देवानां मध्यॆ यस्य ममेंद्रस्य सकाशं
> गच्छति । यश्चाहमिंद्रः सर्वस्मादुत्तरः । यद्वा । अयमर्थः । हे इंद्राणि
> वृषाकपेः सख्युरिंद्रादृतेऽहं वृषाकपिर्न रराण । न रमे । अन्यत्समानं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indrāṇī, I, Indra, do not delight (रराण (*rarāṇa*): न रमे (*na rame*)) without वृषाकपेः (*vṛṣākapeḥ*), my friend (सख्युः (*sakhyuḥ*)), the dear Vṛṣākapi. अप्यं (*apyaṃ*) is that which is born in the waters or that which is well prepared with waters; this dear, pleasing oblation, now present, goes among the gods to me, Indra. And I, Indra, am above all, more excellent. Or else this is the meaning: O Indrāṇī, without Vṛṣākapi's friend Indra, I, Vṛṣākapi, do not delight. The rest is the same.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्राणि (*iṃdrāṇi*)—O Indrāṇī
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- सख्युः (*sakhyuḥ*)—of my son Vṛṣākapi
- ऋते (*ṛte*)—without Vṛṣākapi
- न ररण (*na raraṇa*)—am not delighted
- अप्यं (*apyaṃ*)—prepared with water
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—and dear to me
- इदं हविः (*idaṃ haviḥ*)—this oblation
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- यस्य (*yasya*)—to whomever, to me
- गच्छति (*gacchati*)—comes
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—I, the lord
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—am the more excellent

### Printed p. 473

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indrāṇī, without my friend Vṛṣākapi I have no joy. I, the lord, towards whom this oblation, prepared with water and dear to me, comes among the gods, am more excellent than the world. **NOTE**

##### English translation
I am not happy, Indrani, without my friend Vrishakapi: whose acceptable oblation here, purified with water, proceeds to the gods; Indra is above all (the world)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given the Nirukta of this Ṛk in this way: नाहमिंद्राणि रमे सख्युर्वृषाकपेर्ऋते यस्येदमप्यं हविरप्सु शृतमद्भिः संस्कृतमिति ना प्रियं देवेषु निगच्छति सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूमः ॥ (*nāhamiṃdrāṇi rame sakhyurvṛṣākaperṛte yasyedamapyaṃ havirapsu śṛtamadbhiḥ saṃskṛtamiti nā priyaṃ deveṣu nigacchati sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūmaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 11-39). In this Ṛk Indra addresses Indrāṇī and speaks thus: O Indrāṇī, if Vṛṣākapi, my friend and son, is not with me, I have no joy. The oblation that is cooked with water, that is, prepared by the use of water, gives pleasure to the gods and approaches them.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वृषा॑कपायि॒ रेव॑ति॒ सुपु॑त्र॒ आदु॒ सुस्नु॑षे ।  
> घस॑त्त॒ इंद्र॑ उ॒क्षणः॑ प्रि॒यं का॑चित्क॒रं ह॒विर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषाकपायि । रेवति । सुपुत्रे। आत् । ऊं इति । सुस्नुषे ।  
> घसत् । ते । इंद्रः । उक्षणः । प्रियं । काचित्सरं । हविः । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 474

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषाकपायि। कामानां वर्षकत्वादभीष्टदेशग नाच्चेंद्रो वृषाकपिः
> तस्य पत्नि । यद्वा । वृषाकपेर्मम मातरित्यर्थः । रेवति धनवति सुपुत्रे शोभनपुत्रे सुस्नुषे शोभनस्नुषे हे इंद्राणि ते तवायमिंद्र उक्षणः सेचनसमर्था
> नाद्वनंतरमेव। शीघ्रमेवेत्यर्थः । पशून्फसत् । प्राश्नातु । किंच काचित्करं ।
> कं सुखं। तस्याचित् संघः। तत्करं हविः प्रियमिष्टं कुर्विति शेषः। किंच ते पतिरिंद्रो
> विश्वस्मादुत्तरः । तथा च यास्कः । वृषाकपायि रेवति सुपुत्रे मध्यमेन सुस्नुषे
> माध्यमिकया वाचा । स्नुषा साधुसादिनीति वा साधुसानिनीति वा । प्रियं कुरुष्ट
> सुखाचयकरं हविः सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरः । नि. १२-९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O वृषाकपायि (*vṛṣākapāyi*): Indra is Vṛṣākapi because he rains down desires and goes to the places desired; his wife is Vṛṣākapāyī. Or else it means Vṛṣākapi's, that is my, mother. O wealthy one (रेवति (*revati*)), O mother of a good son (सुपुत्रे (*suputre*)), O one with a good daughter-in-law (सुस्नुषे (*susnuṣe*)), O Indrāṇī: let this your Indra, उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*), who is able to sprinkle, immediately thereafter, that is, quickly, eat (घसत् (*ghasat*)) the animals. Further, the oblation that produces happiness (काचित्करं (*kācitkaraṃ*), ka being happiness): make it dear, that is, desired; this is the word to be supplied. Further, your husband Indra is above all. Likewise Yāska says: मध्यमेन सुस्नुषे माध्यमिकया वाचा (*madhyamena susnuṣe mādhyamikayā vācā*); स्नुषा साधुसादिनीति वा साधुसानिनीति वा (*snuṣā sādhusādinīti vā sādhusāninīti vā*); प्रियं कुरुष्ट सुखाचयकरं हविः (*priyaṃ kuruṣṭa sukhācayakaraṃ haviḥ*) (Ni. 12-9). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषाकपायि (*vṛṣākapāyi*)—O mother of Vṛṣākapi
- रेवति (*revati*)—possessed of wealth
- सुपुत्रे (*suputre*)—having excellent sons
- सुस्नुषे (*susnuṣe*)—having an excellent daughter-in-law (O Indrāṇī)
- ते (*te*)—your husband
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*)—powerful bulls
- आदु (*ādu*)—immediately
- घसत् (*ghasat*)—let him eat
- काचित्करं हविः (*kācitkaraṃ haviḥ*)—the oblation that gives happiness
- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—make it agreeable to Indra
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than all the worlds
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indrāṇī, mother of Vṛṣākapi, possessed of wealth, having excellent sons and an excellent daughter-in-law: let your husband Indra eat the flesh of powerful bulls. Make the oblation that gives happiness agreeable to Indra. Indra is more excellent than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Vrishakapi speaks : ] O mother of Vrishakapi, wealthy, possessing excellent sons, possessing excellent daughters-in-law, let Indra eat your bulls, (give him) the beloved and most delightful ghi; Indra is above all (the world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining the word वृषाकपाया (*vṛṣākapāyā*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has, as an example, given the explanation of this Ṛk in this way: वृषाकपायी वृषाकपेः पत्न्येष्टैवाभिसृष्टकालतमा । तस्येषा भवति । वृषाकपायी रेवति सुपुत्र आ सुस्नुषे घसत्त इंद्र उक्षणः प्रियं (*vṛṣākapāyī vṛṣākapeḥ patnyeṣṭaivābhisṛṣṭakālatamā | tasyeṣā bhavati | vṛṣākapāyī revati suputra ā susnuṣe ghasatta iṃdra ukṣaṇaḥ priyaṃ*)

### Printed p. 475

काचित्करं हविर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ वृषाकपायि रेवति सुपुत्रे मध्यमेन सुस्नुषे माध्यमिकया वाचा । स्नुषा साधुसादिनीति वा साधुसानिनीति वा स्वपत्यं तत्सनोतीति वा ॥ प्राश्नातु त इंद्र उक्षण एतान्याध्यमिकान् संस्तायान् । उक्षण उक्षतेर्वृद्धि कर्मणः उक्षंत्युदकेनेति वा प्रियं कुरुष्ट सुखाचयकरं हविः सुखकरं हविः सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूम आदित्यं ॥ (*kācitkaraṃ havirviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖ vṛṣākapāyi revati suputre madhyamena susnuṣe mādhyamikayā vācā | snuṣā sādhusādinīti vā sādhusāninīti vā svapatyaṃ tatsanotīti vā ‖ prāśnātu ta iṃdra ukṣaṇa etānyādhyamikān saṃstāyān | ukṣaṇa ukṣatervṛddhi karmaṇaḥ ukṣaṃtyudakeneti vā priyaṃ kuruṣṭa sukhācayakaraṃ haviḥ sukhakaraṃ haviḥ sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūma ādityaṃ ‖*) (Ni. 12-9)

Vṛṣākapāyi means the wife of Vṛṣākapi, that is, the wife of Āditya; Vṛṣākapi means the Sun. Sūryā, the wife of that Sun, after some time is called by the name Vṛṣākapāyi. In the Ṛk beginning वृषाकपायि रेवति (*vṛṣākapāyi revati*) (the present Ṛk) this matter is mentioned. O Vṛṣākapāyi (wife of Āditya), you are रेवति (*revati*), that is, possessed of wealth; here wealth is wealth in the form of water. सुपुत्रे (*suputre*): having an excellent son; here the son is Indra, the deity of the middle region (the atmosphere), the excellent son. सुस्नुषे (*susnuṣe*): having an excellent daughter-in-law; here the deity of Speech of the middle region is the excellent daughter-in-law. Three derivations of the word स्नुषा (*snuṣā*) are stated here. साधुसादिनीति वा स्नुषा (*sādhusādinīti vā snuṣā*): because she sits well, that is, dwells steadily in the house of the mother-in-law, the daughter-in-law is called snuṣā. Or साधु सानिनीति वा स्नुषा (*sādhu sāninīti vā snuṣā*): because she works in the house of the mother-in-law and helps in the work of maintaining the livelihood, the daughter-in-law is called snuṣā. Or स्वपत्यं तत्सनोतीति वा स्नुषा (*svapatyaṃ tatsanotīti vā snuṣā*): because, living in the house of her husband, she increases the offspring of her husband, the daughter-in-law is called snuṣā.

The word उक्षणः (*ukṣaṇaḥ*) is formed from the root ukṣ in the sense of growing; or the root ukṣ may also mean to sprinkle water. Therefore ukṣaṇaḥ can be explained as the clouds that sprinkle water. घसत्त इंद्र उक्षणः (*ghasatta iṃdra ukṣaṇaḥ*) means: let Indra eat, that is, destroy, these water-sprinkling clouds, let him strike them with the thunderbolt. Therefore make this oblation, offered to this Indra, that is, to the Sun, agreeable to him. This is the main purport of the Nirukta.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒क्ष्णो हि मे॒ पंच॑दश सा॒कं पचं॑ति विंश॒तिं ।  
> उ॒ताहम॑द्मि॒ पीव॒ इदु॒भा कु॒क्सी पृ॑णंति मे॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑

> इंद्रः । उत्तरः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथेंद्रो ब्रवीति । मे मदर्थं पंचदश पंचदशसंख्याकान् विंशतिं
> विंशतिसंख्याकांश्चोक्ष्णो वृषभान् साकं सह मम भार्ययेंद्राण्या प्रेरिता
> यष्टारः पचंति । उतापि चाहमद्मि । तान्भक्षयामि । जग्त्वा चाहं पीव इत् स्कूल
> एव भवामीति शेषः । किंच मे मनोभोभौ कुक्षि पृणंति । सोमेन पूरयंति
> यष्टारः । सोऽहमिंद्रः सर्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Indra speaks. For me (मे (*me*)), on my behalf, the sacrificers, impelled by my wife Indrāṇī, cook together (साकं (*sākaṃ*)) fifteen (पंचदश (*paṃcadaśa*)) and twenty (विंशतिं (*viṃśatiṃ*)) bulls (उक्ष्णः (*ukṣṇaḥ*)). And I eat (अद्मि (*admi*)) them, and I become stout (पीव इत् (*pīva it*)). Further, the sacrificers fill both my sides of the belly (कुक्षी (*kukṣī*)) with Soma. I, that Indra, am above all, more excellent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—for me
- पंचदश (*paṃcadaśa*)—fifteen in number
- विंशतिं (*viṃśatiṃ*)—and twenty in number
- उक्ष्णः (*ukṣṇaḥ*)—bulls
- साकं (*sākaṃ*)—together
- पचंति (*pacaṃti*)—the sacrificers cook
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I
- अद्मि (*admi*)—eat them
- पवीत् (*pavīt*)—grow stout
- मे (*me*)—my
- उभा कुक्षि (*ubhā kukṣi*)—both sides of the belly
- पृणंति (*pṛṇaṃti*)—fill
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—I, the lord
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—am more excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers cook fifteen and twenty bulls for me and offer them. I eat them and grow stout. They fill both sides of my belly. I, the lord, am more excellent than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indra speaks : ] The worshippers dress for me fifteen (and) twenty bulls : I eat them and (become) fat, they fill both sides of my belly; Indra is above all (the world).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मं॒थस्त॑ इंद्र॒ शं हृ॒दे यं ते॑ सु॒नोति॑ भाव॒युर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒ उत्त॑रः ॥ १५ ॥

> मंथः । ते । इंद्र । शं । हृदे । यं । ते । सुनोति । भावयुः । विश्वस्मात् ।  
> इंद्रः । उत्तरः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथेंद्राणी ब्रवीति । तिग्मशृंगस्तीक्ष्णशृंगो वृषभो न यथा वृषभो
> यूथेषु गोसंघेष्टंतर्मध्यॆ रोरुवच्छब्दं कुर्वन् गा अभिरमयति तथा
> हे इंद्र त्वं मामभिरमयेति शेषः । किंच हे इंद्र ते तव हृदे हृदयाय
> मंथो दध्नो मथनवेलायां शब्दं कुर्वञ्यं शंकरो भवत्त्विति शेषः । किंच ते
> तुभ्यं यं सोमं भावयुर्भावमिच्छंतींद्राणी सुनोति अभिषुणोति सोऽपि
> शंकरो भवत्त्यर्थः । मम पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Indrāṇī speaks. As (न (*na*)) a bull with sharp horns (तिग्मशृंग (*tigmaśṛṃga*)) roars (रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)) among the herds of cows and delights the cows, so, O Indra, may you delight me; this is the word to be supplied. Further, O Indra, for your heart (हृदे (*hṛde*)) may the मंथः (*maṃthaḥ*), the sound made at the time of churning curds, be a source of happiness; this is the word to be supplied. Further, the Soma which Indrāṇī, desiring bhāva (भावयुः (*bhāvayuḥ*)), presses (सुनोति (*sunoti*)) for you, may that too be a source of happiness. My husband Indra is above all, more excellent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यूथेषु अंतः (*yūtheṣu aṃtaḥ*)—in the herd of cows
- रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)—making a sound
- तिग्मृंगः (*tigmṛṃgaḥ*)—having sharp horns
- वृषभो न (*vṛṣabho na*)—like a bull that experiences delight
- ते (*te*)—for you
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- भावयुः (*bhāvayuḥ*)—I who desire your delight
- सुनोति (*sunoti*)—press
- ते (*te*)—your
- हृदे (*hṛde*)—in the heart
- मंथः (*maṃthaḥ*)—making the sound of churning
- शं (*śaṃ*)—may it be a source of happiness
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—you, the lord
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—are more excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, as a bull with sharp horns experiences delight roaring among the herd of cows, so the Soma which I, desiring your happiness, press for you, may it, making the sound of churning in your heart,

### Printed p. 478

be a source of happiness. You, the lord, are more excellent than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indrani speaks : ] Like a sharp-horned bull roaring amongst the herds, so may your libation please your heart, Indra, (your libation) which she who desires to please you is expressing for you; Indra is above all (the world).

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सेदी॑शे॒ यस्य॑ रोम॒शं नि॑षे॒दुषो॑ वि॒जृंभ॑ते॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> न । सः । ईशे । यस्य । रंबते । अंतरा । सक्था । कपृत् ।

> सः । इत् । ईशे । यस्य । रोमशं । निषेदुषः । विजृंभते । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स जनो नेशे मैथुनं कर्तुं नेष्टे न शक्योति यस्य जनस्य
> कपृच्छेपः सक्ता सक्तिनी अंतरा रंबते लंबते । सेत् स एव स्त्रीजन ईशे मैथुनं
> कर्तुं सक्कोति यस्य जनस्य निषेदुषः शयानस्य रोमशमुपस्थं विजृंभते विवृतं
> भवति । यस्य च पतिरिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, that man is not able (नेशे (*neśe*): न शक्योति (*na śakyoti*)) to perform union, in whose case the कपृत् (*kapṛt*), the organ, hangs (रंबते (*raṃbate*): लंबते (*laṃbate*)) between the thighs (सक्ता (*saktā*)). That very person (स्त्रीजन (*strījana*)) is able (ईशे (*īśe*)) to perform union, in whose case, when he sits down or lies down, the hairy (रोमशं (*romaśaṃ*)) private part gapes (विजृंभते (*vijṛṃbhate*)), that is, becomes open. And of whom Indra is the husband is above all, more excellent. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which man
- कपृत् (*kapṛt*)—the generative organ
- सक्ष्या (*sakṣyā*)—of the thighs
- अंतरा (*aṃtarā*)—in the middle
- रंबते (*raṃbate*)—hangs without strength (in the sleeping state)
- सः जनः (*saḥ janaḥ*)—that man
- न ईशे (*na īśe*)—is not able to carry out the act of union with a woman, that is, to have intercourse
- यस्य (*yasya*)—of which man
- निषेदुषः (*niṣeduṣaḥ*)—who is in the sleeping state
- रोमशं (*romaśaṃ*)—the male organ (or the shaft of the organ)
- विजृंभते (*vijṛṃbhate*)—stands in an excited state
- सः इत् (*saḥ it*)—such

### Printed p. 479

- man alone
- ईशे (*īśe*)—is able to have intercourse with a woman
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is most excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the man whose organ of generation hangs between the two thighs and, being only in the sleeping state, is without strength, such a man is not able to perform the act of union with a woman, that is, to have intercourse with a woman. But the man whose organ is able to stand erect straight in the state of excitement, such a man alone is capable of performing the act of love with a woman. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
The man who is impotent begets not progeny, but he who is endowed with vigour; Indra is above all (the world).

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That man is not able (नेशे (*neśe*)) to perform union, in whose case, when he sits down or lies down (निषेदुषः (*niṣeduṣaḥ*): शयानस्य (*śayānasya*)), the hairy (रोमशं (*romaśaṃ*)) private part gapes (विजृंभते (*vijṛṃbhate*)), that is, becomes open. That very man is able (ईशे (*īśe*)) to perform union, in whose case the कपृत् (*kapṛt*), the organ of generation, hangs (रंबते (*raṃbate*): लंबते (*laṃbate*)) between the thighs. The rest is established. The difference from what was said before is to be seen here: in the previous Ṛk Indrāṇī speaks to Indra, while here Indra speaks to Indrāṇī; thus there is no contradiction. **NOTE**

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indrāṇī, what you say is not right. The man whose male organ, in the sleeping state, stands straight in the state of excitement is not capable of intercourse with a woman; the man whose organ of generation hangs without strength between the two thighs, such a man alone is capable of union with a woman. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indra speaks : ] He who is endowed with vigour begets not progeny, but he who is impotent ; Indra is above all (the world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

What Indra has said in this Ṛk is quite different from what Indrāṇī said in the previous Ṛk. Although what Indrāṇī said in the previous Ṛk, being eager for union, was in accord with nature, Indra, who has no desire for union, has deliberately expressed an opinion contrary to nature.

> अ॒यमिं॑द्र वृ॒षाक॑पिः॒ पर॑स्वंतं ह॒तं वि॑दत् ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अयं वृषाकपिः परस्वंतं परस्वमात्मनो विषयेऽवर्तमानं
> हतं हिंसितं विदत् । विंदतु । तथा हतस्य विशसनायासिं शस्त्रं सूनामुद्धानं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, let this Vṛṣākapi find (विदत् (*vidat*)) a slain (हतं (*hataṃ*)), injured animal that is परस्वंतं (*parasvaṃtaṃ*), one not belonging to himself. Likewise, for cutting up the slain animal, let him find a knife (असिं (*asiṃ*), a weapon), a सूनां (*sūnāṃ*) for cooking, a new (नवं (*navaṃ*)), fresh vessel (चरुं (*caruṃ*)), and afterwards a cart (अनः (*anaḥ*)) full (अचितं (*acitaṃ*)) of firewood. My husband Indra is above all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- आयं वृषाकपिः (*āyaṃ vṛṣākapiḥ*)—this Vṛṣākapi
- परस्वंतं (*parasvaṃtaṃ*)—not his own
- हतं (*hataṃ*)—and killed; this animal
- विदत् (*vidat*)—let him obtain
- असिं (*asiṃ*)—a sword (to cut it up)
- सूनां (*sūnāṃ*)—a ladle for cooking
- नवं चरुं (*navaṃ caruṃ*)—a new cooking pot
- आत् (*āt*)—afterwards
- विधस्य अचितं (*vidhasya acitaṃ*)—full of firewood
- अनः (*anaḥ*)—let him also obtain a cart
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let this Vṛṣākapi obtain a dead animal that is not his own. To cut it up, let him obtain a sword, to cook it a ladle, a new cooking pot, and a cart full of firewood. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indrani speaks : ] Let this Vrishakapi, Indra, take a dead wild ass, (let him take) a knife (to cut it up), a fire place (to cook it), a new saucepan, and a cart full of fuel ; Indra is above all (the world).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यमे॑मि वि॒चाक॑शद्विचि॒न्वन्नास॒मायं॑ ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयं । एमि । विचाकशत् । विचिन्वन् । दासं । आर्यं ।  
> पिबामि । पाक्स्यसुत्वनः । अभि । धीरं । अचाकशं । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः । उत्तरः ॥

**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अथेंद्रो ब्रवीति । विचाकशत् पश्यन्यजमानान् दासमुपक्षपयितारमसुरमार्यमपि च विचिन्वन् पृथक्कुर्वन्नयमहमिंद्र एमि । यज्ञं प्रति गच्छामि ।
> यज्ञं गत्वा च पाकसुत्वनः । पचतीति पाकः । सुनोतीति सुत्वा ! हविषां पक्तुः
> सोमस्याभिषोतुर्यजमानस्य पाकेन विपक्वेन मनसा सोमस्याभिषोतुर्वा
> यजमानस्य संबंधिनं सोमं पिबामि! तथा धीरं धीमंतं यजमानमभ्यचाकशं।
> अभिपश्यामि । योऽहमिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Now Indra speaks. Looking at (विचाकशत् (*vicākaśat*)) the sacrificers, and separating (विचिन्वन् (*vicinvan*): पृथक्कुर्वन् (*pṛthakkurvan*)) the दास (*dāsa*), the destroyer, the Asura, and also the Ārya, I, this Indra, come (एमि (*emi*)), I go towards the sacrifice. Having gone to the sacrifice, I drink the Soma belonging to the sacrificer who cooks the oblations and presses Soma (पाकसुत्वनः (*pākasutvanaḥ*)), or to the one who presses Soma with a ripened mind (पाकेन विपक्वेन मनसा (*pākena vipakvena manasā*)). Likewise I look upon (अभ्यचाकशं (*abhyacākaśaṃ*)) the wise (धीरं (*dhīraṃ*)), intelligent sacrificer. I am that Indra who is above all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विचाकतत् (*vicākatat*)—looking upon the rite of the sacrificer
- दासं (*dāsaṃ*)—the Dāsa who is without rites
- आर्यं (*āryaṃ*)—the Ārya devoted to rites
- विचिन्वन् (*vicinvan*)—dividing
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—I, the lord
- एमि (*emi*)—come to the sacrifice
- पाकसुत्वनः (*pākasutvanaḥ*)—the Soma of one who presses with a ripened mind
- पिबामि (*pibāmi*)—I drink
- धीरं (*dhīraṃ*)—the wise sacrificer
- अभ्यचाकशं (*abhyacākaśaṃ*)—I look upon with favour
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—I, the lord
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—am more excellent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Looking upon the rite of the sacrificer, and separating the Dāsa who is without rites from the Ārya devoted to rites, I, the lord, come to the sacrifice. I drink the Soma of him who presses and offers it with a ripened mind. I look with favour upon the wise sacrificer. I, the lord, am more excellent than the whole world.

##### English translation
[ Indra speaks ] Here I come to the (sacrifice) looking upon (the worshippers), distinguishing the Dasa and the Arya; I drink the (Soma)

### Printed p. 483

of the (worshipper), who effuses (the Soma) with mature (mind); I look upon the intelligent (sacrifice); Indra is above all (the world).

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धन्व॑ च॒ यत्क्॒यंतत्र॑ च॒ कति॑ स्वि॒त्ता वि योज॑ना ।  
> नेदी॑यसो वृषाक॒पेस्त॒मेहि॑ गृ॒हा उप॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धन्व । च । यत् । कृंतत्रं । च । कति । स्वित् । ता । वि । योजना ।  
> नेदीयसः । वृषाकपे । अस्तं । आ । इहि । गृहान् । उप । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धन्व निरुदकोऽरण्यरहितो देशः । कृंतत्रं कर्तनीयमरण्यं । यद्यच्च धन्व
> च कृंतत्रं च भवति । मृगोद्वासमरण्यमेवंविधं भवति न त्वत्यंतविपिनं । तस्य
> शत्रुनिलयस्यास्मदीयगृहस्य च मध्ये कति स्वित्ता तानि योजना योजनानि स्थितानि ।
> नात्यंतदूरे तद्भवतीत्यर्थः । अतो नेदीयसोऽतिशयेन समीपस्थाच्छत्तुनिलयात् हे वृषाकपे त्वमस्तमस्कां गृहं वैहि । विशेषेणागच्छ । अगत्य च
> गृहान्यज्ञगृहानुपगच्छ । यतोऽमिंद्रः सर्वस्मादुत्कृष्टः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

धन्व (*dhanva*) is a waterless region without forest; कृंतत्रं (*kṛṃtatraṃ*) is a forest to be cut. A forest from which the deer have been driven away is of this kind, both dhanva and kṛntatra, but not an extremely thick forest. Between that dwelling of the enemy and our house, how many (कति स्वित्ता (*kati svittā*)) leagues (योजना (*yojanā*)) stand? It is not extremely far. Therefore, O Vṛṣākapi, from the exceedingly near (नेदीयसः (*nedīyasaḥ*)) dwelling of the enemy, you come in particular (व्येहि (*vyehi*): विशेषेणागच्छ (*viśeṣeṇāgaccha*)) to our house (अस्तं (*astaṃ*)). And having come, go to the houses (गृहान् (*gṛhān*)) of the sacrifice. For I, Indra, am more excellent than all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—whichever region
- धन्व च (*dhanva ca*)—is both a desert
- कृंतत्रं च (*kṛṃtatraṃ ca*)—and full of violence; from that forest to our house
- कति स्वित् ता योजना (*kati svit tā yojanā*)—there are only a few leagues
- वृषाकपे (*vṛṣākape*)—O Vṛṣākapi
- नेदीयसः (*nedīyasaḥ*)—from this forest that is near
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to our house
- व्येहि (*vyehi*)—set out
- गृहान् उप (*gṛhān upa*)—go also to the house of the sacrifice
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The region that is both a desert and full of violence: from that forest to our house there are only a few leagues. O Vṛṣākapi, set out from this near forest to our house. Go also to the house of the sacrifice. Indra is greater than the whole world.

### Printed p. 484

##### English translation

> कर्माणि कल्पयावहै । इंद्राण्यहं चावामुभौ पर्यालोच्य कुर्याव । किंच
> यः स्वप्ननंशन उदयेन सर्वस्य प्राणिनः स्वप्नानां नाशयितादित्यः स एष त्वं पथा
> मार्गेणास्तमात्मीयमावासं पुनरेषि । गच्छसि । यतोऽहमिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः।
> तथा च यास्कः । सुप्रसूतानि वः कर्माणि कल्पयावहै य एष स्वप्ननंशनः
> स्वप्नान्नाशयस्यादित्य उदयेन सोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनः । नि. १२-२८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra speaks to Vṛṣākapi who has gone and come back. O Vṛṣākapi, come again (पुनरेहि (*punarehi*)); come to us. When you have come, we two, Indrāṇī and I, having considered the matter, will do (कल्पयावहै (*kalpayāvahai*)) the good deeds (सुविता (*suvitā*)), that is, the auspicious deeds that please your mind. Further, you, who are the Āditya, स्वप्ननंशनः (*svapnanaṃśanaḥ*), the destroyer of the dreams of every creature by your rising, go again (एषि (*eṣi*)) by the path to your own abode, the setting (अस्तं (*astaṃ*)). For I, Indra, am more excellent than all. Likewise Yāska says: सुप्रसूतानि वः कर्माणि कल्पयावहै य एष स्वप्ननंशनः स्वप्नान्नाशयस्यादित्य उदयेन सोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनः । (*suprasūtāni vaḥ karmāṇi kalpayāvahai ya eṣa svapnanaṃśanaḥ svapnānnāśayasyāditya udayena so 'stameṣi pathā punaḥ |*) (Ni. 12-28) **GLOSS** **NOTE**

- वृषाकपे (*vṛṣākape*)—O Vṛṣākapi
- पुनः एहि (*punaḥ ehi*)—come back to the house
- सुविता (*suvitā*)—the deeds that are dear to you
- कल्पयावहै (*kalpayāvahai*)—I and Indrāṇī will do
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- स्वप्ननंशनः (*svapnanaṃśanaḥ*)—in the form of Āditya, the destroyer of sleep
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—such as you are
- पथ (*patha*)—by an excellent path
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—to our house
- पुनः एषि (*punaḥ eṣi*)—come back again
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—is greater

### Printed p. 485

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vṛṣākapi, come back home. I and Indrāṇī will do the deeds that are dear to you. You who are the destroyer of sleep, in the form of Āditya, come back to our house by the excellent path. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
Come back, Vrishakapi, that we may do what is agreeable to you; you, who are the destroyer of sleep come home again by the road: Indra is above all (the world).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In explaining the etymology of the word Vṛṣākapi, Yāska has given the Nirukta on this Ṛk—

वृषाकपिः । अथ यद्रश्मिभिरभिप्रकंपयन्नेति तद्वृषाकपिर्भवति वृषाकंपनः । तस्यैषा भवति । पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुविता कल्पयावहै । य एष स्वप्ननंशनोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनर्विश्वस्मादिंद्र उत्तरः ॥ पुनरेहि वृषाकपे सुप्रसूतानि यः कर्माणि कल्पयावहै य एष स्वप्ननंतनः स्वप्नान्नाशयत्यादित्य उदयेन सोऽस्तमेषि पथा पुनः सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूम आदित्यं (*vṛṣākapiḥ | atha yadraśmibhirabhiprakaṃpayanneti tadvṛṣākapirbhavati vṛṣākaṃpanaḥ | tasyaiṣā bhavati | punarehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai | ya eṣa svapnanaṃśano 'stameṣi pathā punarviśvasmādiṃdra uttaraḥ ‖ punarehi vṛṣākape suprasūtāni yaḥ karmāṇi kalpayāvahai ya eṣa svapnanaṃtanaḥ svapnānnāśayatyāditya udayena so 'stameṣi pathā punaḥ sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūma ādityaṃ*) (Ni. 12-28)

Vṛṣākapi means Āditya. For this Āditya, when he rises with his rays, makes everything tremble; or the sun, accompanied by his rays, when he sets, makes all beings tremble. After the sun has sunk, darkness spreads. Many are frightened by the darkness and tremble; or, after darkness has come, because the heat of the sun is absent, people tremble with cold. Therefore, because the sun is of a nature to make people or beings tremble, he has the name Vṛṣākapi. This matter is alluded to in the following Ṛk.

O Vṛṣākapi (Āditya), since you rise and destroy the sleep of beings (people), you are the destroyer of people's dreams. Such as you are, rise again. After your rising we shall engage in the duties that we have to perform. Because you sink, darkness spreads and, there being no heat, people tremble with cold. As soon as you rise, the sleep of the people is destroyed, they wake up and engage in their respective tasks. Therefore, O Vṛṣākapi (Āditya), rise and come this day also: this is the main import of the Nirukta statement.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यदुदं॑चो वृषाकपे गृ॒हमिं॒द्राज॑गंतन ।  
> क्व१॒॑ १ स्य पु॑ल्व॒घो मृ॒गः कम॑गञ्जन॒योप॑नो॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिंद्र॒  ॑
> उत्तरः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । उदंचः । वृषाकपे । गृहं । इंद्र । अजगंतन ।  
> क्व । स्यः । पुल्वघः । मृगः । कं । अगन् । जन्योपनः । विश्वस्मात् । इंद्रः ।  
> उत्तरः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गत्वा पुनरागतं वृषाकपिमिंद्रः पृच्छति । हे इंद्र परमैश्वर्यवन्
> हे वृषाकपे यूयमुदंच उद्गामिनः संतो मद्गृहमजगंतन । आगच्छ ।
> एकस्यापि बहुवचनं पूजार्थं । तत्र भवतः संबंधी पुल्वघो बहूनां भौमरसानामत्ता स्य स मृगः क्वाभूत् । जनयोपनो जनानां मोदयिता मृगः कं वा
> देशमगन् . अगच्छत् । सोऽहमिंद्रो विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥ यद्वा इंद्राणेवाक्यमिदं!
> अत्र यास्क? । यदुदंचो वृषाकपे गृहमिंद्राजगमत क्व स्य पुल्वघो मृगः
> क्व स बह्वादी मृगः । मृगो माष्टेर्गतिकर्मणः । कमगमद्देशं जनयोपनः ।
> नि. १३-३ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra questions Vṛṣākapi, who has gone and returned. "O Indra, possessed of supreme lordship", and "O Vṛṣākapi, you, going upward (उदंच (*udaṃca*): rising), come to my house": the plural is used for a single person out of respect. "Your associate Pulvagha, the eater of many earthly juices, that deer, where has it been? And Janayopana, the delighter of people, the deer, to what region has it gone? I, Indra, am superior to all." Or else this verse is the speech of Indrāṇī. Here Yāska explains: where is that deer that eats much; मृग (*mṛga*) comes from a root of motion; to what region has Janayopana gone (Ni. 13-3).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O one endowed with wealth
- वृषाकपे (*vṛṣākape*)—O Vṛṣākapi
- गृहं उदंचः (*gṛhaṃ udaṃcaḥ*)—rising towards my house
- अजगंतन (*ajagaṃtana*)—come
- पुल्वघः (*pulvaghaḥ*)—the one that sucks the juice
- स्यः मृगः (*syaḥ mṛgaḥ*)—that famed deer
- क्व (*kva*)—where
- जनयोपनः (*janayopanaḥ*)—that deer, the delighter of people
- कु अगन् (*ku agan*)—to what region has it gone **NOTE**
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- विश्वस्मात् (*viśvasmāt*)—than the whole world
- उत्तरः (*uttaraḥ*)—greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Vṛṣākapi, endowed with wealth, rise towards my house and come. Where is that famed deer that sucks the juice? To what region has that deer, the delighter of people, gone? Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
Rise up and come home, Vrishakapi and Indra; where is that destructive beast, to what (region) has (that beast), the exhilarator of men gone? Indra is above all (the world)

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Yāska has given an etymology of this Ṛk from the standpoint of Āditya—

यदुदंचो वृषाकपे गृहमिंद्राजगमत क्व स्यः पुल्वघो मृगः क्व स बह्वादी मृगः! मृगो माष्टेर्गतिकर्मणः । कमगमद्देशं जनयोपनः सर्वस्माद्य इंद्र उत्तरस्तमेतद्दूम आदित्यं ॥ (*yadudaṃco vṛṣākape gṛhamiṃdrājagamata kva syaḥ pulvagho mṛgaḥ kva sa bahvādī mṛgaḥ! mṛgo māṣṭergatikarmaṇaḥ | kamagamaddeśaṃ janayopanaḥ sarvasmādya iṃdra uttarastametaddūma ādityaṃ ‖*)

Here उदंचः (*udaṃcaḥ*) means being in the northern direction, that is, going round by way of the northern direction; गृह (*gṛha*) means one's own region, the region in which we dwell; पुल्वघः (*pulvaghaḥ*) means puru plus agha, one who eats much of everything, that is, Agni who devours everything. Since Agni is also in the form of Āditya, Āditya is here said to be the one who eats greatly, existing in the form of the digestive fire of all beings. The word मृग (*mṛga*) is formed from the root मार्ष्टि (*mārṣṭi*), which denotes motion. Since the sun pervades everywhere by his rays, the sun is said to be denoted by the word मृग (*mṛga*). Therefore the main import of this Ṛk is: O Vṛṣākapi, that is, O Āditya, come again to our earth, going round by way of the northern direction, so that we may see you. Where did you go until now (during the night)? In the form of fire you are the devourer of all, and by your rays you are pervading everywhere. Such as you are, where have you gone until now? Rise and come quickly to illumine this earth, which is called our home. Such is the main import of the Ṛk.

After rising in the eastern direction, the sun by day goes round by way of the southern direction and sets in the western direction. All of us see this every day. Afterwards, in the evening, after the sun has set, we cannot see the course of the sun. Therefore the seer questions Āditya as to where he was until now, and states the answer to it. O Āditya, by day you go round by way of the southern direction. Therefore, at night, going round by way of the northern direction, rise again in the eastern direction as usual and come: thus he has said. Here the earth on which we dwell is called a home out of excess of respect. The earth on which we dwell, here, is only that earth on which the light of the sun falls by day. Since the course of the sun is not seen at night, the region on which the light of the sun falls at that time the seer has

### Printed p. 488

not taken into account. Therefore the seer expresses wonder as to where the sun was after he had set, until the sunrise again.

Hiraṇyakaśyapa Samudri describes this same matter, saying—

क्वे ३ दानीं सूर्यः कश्चिकेत कतमां द्यां रश्मिरस्या ततान ॥ (*kve 3 dānīṃ sūryaḥ kaściketa katamāṃ dyāṃ raśmirasyā tatāna ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-7) **NOTE**

Who can know where the sun is now (at night)? Into what other region does he spread his rays and shine? No one knows this: thus he has expressed wonder.

> मनोर्दुहितेयं विंशतिं विंशतिसंख्याकान्सुत्रान् साकं सह ससूव । अजीजनत् ।

> उदरमामयत् गर्भस्थैर्विंशतिभिः पुत्रैः पुष्टमासीत् । मम पितेंद्रो
> विश्वस्मादुत्तरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this mantra Vṛṣākapi blesses the arrow being discharged by Indra. "O भल (*bhala*), arrow discharged by Indra": the root भल (*bhala*) has the sense of piercing. पर्शुः नाम (*parśuḥ nāma*) is a female deer; ह (*ha*) is an expletive. This daughter of Manu bore twenty, that is, twenty sons, together at one birth. May good fortune, such as is to be enjoyed, befall her whose belly was swollen, that is, filled, with twenty sons in the womb. Indra, my father, is above all. **NOTE**

- ससूव (*sasūva*)—she bore
- भल (*bhala*)—O arrow discharged by Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This female deer, the daughter of Manu, named Parśu, bore twenty children together. O arrow discharged by Indra, may good fortune befall her whose belly was filled with these twenty embryos. Indra is greater than the whole world.

##### English translation
The daughter of Manu, Parshu by name, bore twenty children at once ; may good fortune, O arrow of Indra, befall her whose belly was so prolific ; Indra is above all (the world).

## Sūkta 87 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Pīṭhikā**

The deity of this sūkta is Rakṣohāgni. Although matter concerning Rakṣohāgni occurs here and there in many Ṛks, the sūktas that chiefly praise this deity are three. Rakṣohāgni is the deity of the three sūktas कृणुष्टपाजः (*kṛṇuṣṭapājaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4), रक्षोहणं वाजिनं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ vājinaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-87) and अग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणं (*agne haṃsi nyatriṇaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-118). It is customary to recite the sūktas that praise Rakṣohāgni so that no obstruction by the troops of Rakṣas may arise in sacrifices and the like. At the time of churning fire, if fire is not produced from the araṇis, it is regarded that the cause is the obstruction by the troop of Rakṣas, and the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says, in the context of the fire-churning, that the Rakṣas-destroying sūkta अग्ने हंसि (*agne haṃsi*) in the Gāyatrī metre should be recited. We have mentioned this matter when describing the act of fire-churning. In the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104, Indra, Soma and others are called destroyers of Rakṣas, and that sūkta also is called a Rakṣoghna sūkta. The epithet रक्षोहाः (*rakṣohāḥ*) applies sometimes to Soma also: रक्षोहा विश्वचर्षणिः (*rakṣohā viśvacarṣaṇiḥ*) (9-1-2) and so on. Since in the present sūkta there is matter concerning Agni in the form of Jātavedas, Rakṣohāgni, the troops of Rakṣas, bhūtas, piśācas and yātudhānas, a detailed account of these is necessary.

### Printed p. 490

Jātavedas:—This word has been explained by the authors of the Nirukta as जातानि वेद, जातानि नैनं विदुः जातेजाते विद्यत इति वा, जातविद्यो जातधनः जातविद्यो जातप्रज्ञानः यत्तज्जातः पशूनविंदतेति तज्ञातवेदसो जातवेदस्त्वं इति ब्राह्मणं (*jātāni veda, jātāni nainaṃ viduḥ jātejāte vidyata iti vā, jātavidyo jātadhanaḥ jātavidyo jātaprajñānaḥ yattajjātaḥ paśūnaviṃdateti tajñātavedaso jātavedastvaṃ iti brāhmaṇaṃ*) **GLOSS**

The nature of Jātavedas is stated thus in the Bṛhaddevatā—

इहाग्निभूतस्तृषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः । जातवेदाः स्तुतो मध्यॆ स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि (*ihāgnibhūtastṛṣibhirloke stutibhirīḷitaḥ | jātavedāḥ stuto madhyè stuto vaiśvānaro divi*) (Bṛ. De. 1.67)

This verse says that the seers call the Agni that is on the earth Jātavedas, and the Agni that is in the heavenly world Vaiśvānara; and, continuing the same explanation—

वैश्वानरं श्रितोह्यग्निरग्निं वैश्वानरः श्रितः । अनयोर्जातवेदास्तु तथैते जातवेदसि ॥ (*vaiśvānaraṃ śritohyagniragniṃ vaiśvānaraḥ śritaḥ | anayorjātavedāstu tathaite jātavedasi ‖*) (Bṛ. Ve. 1-97) **NOTE**

It is explained that Agni is contained in Vaiśvānara and Vaiśvānara in Agni, that Jātavedas is contained in both these forms, and that these two forms are different parts of Jātavedas. Having thus stated the stations of Jātavedas in the first chapter, the etymology of the nature of Jātavedas is given in the second chapter thus—

भूतानि वेद यज्ञातो जातवेदाथ कथ्यते । यच्चैष जातविद्योऽभूत् नित्तं जातोऽधिनेत्ति वा ॥ (*bhūtāni veda yajñāto jātavedātha kathyate | yaccaiṣa jātavidyo 'bhūt nittaṃ jāto 'dhinetti vā ‖*) (Bṛ. Je. 2-30) **NOTE**

विद्यते सर्वभूतैर्हि यद्वा जातः पुनःपुनः । तेनैष मध्यभागेंद्रो जातवेदा इति स्तुतः ॥ (*vidyate sarvabhūtairhi yadvā jātaḥ punaḥpunaḥ | tenaiṣa madhyabhāgeṃdro jātavedā iti stutaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 2-31)

The Bṛhaddevatā gives the etymology that Agni is praised as Jātavedas, like Indra who dwells in the middle world, because he knows everything the moment he is born, or because knowledge arose in him, or because the moment he is born he knows and possesses all wealth, or because every time he is born again he is known by all beings. In the same way, explaining the nature of this Agni, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says thus—

यः संवत्सरं जातः स्यात्पाणो वा अग्निस्तमेतद्बिभर्त्यथ ह वै रेतः सिक्तं प्राणोऽन्ववरोहति तद्विंदते तद्यज्जातं जातं विंदते तस्माच्चातवेदाः ॥ (*yaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ jātaḥ syātpāṇo vā agnistametadbibhartyatha ha vai retaḥ siktaṃ prāṇo 'nvavarohati tadviṃdate tadyajjātaṃ jātaṃ viṃdate tasmāccātavedāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 9-5-16-8)

### Printed p. 491

Since Agni in the form of Prāṇa pervades by his power all the beings that are born, it is said that he is called Jātavedas. This very Jātavedas, who is worshipped in the sacrificial house, is described in the Upaniṣads as Brahman, the Self of the universe.

विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपंतं ॥ (*viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapaṃtaṃ ‖*) (Pra. U. 1-8) **NOTE**

In the Praśna Upaniṣad it is said that the Sun rises, who is of universal form, has a thousand rays, is omniscient, is the support of the whole world, is known by the wise, and is the inner self of all beings; and in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad—

अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः । दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ॥ (*araṇyornihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ | dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhirhaviṣmadbhirmanuṣyebhiragniḥ ‖*) (Ka. U. 1-4-8) **NOTE**

The Kaṭha Upaniṣad describes that Jātavedas, who, abiding between the two araṇis in the adhiyajña, enjoys all the oblations, whom the yogis meditate upon, holding him in their hearts as the Supreme Person, as pregnant women with affection nourish and bring up their embryos, and towards whom, as the worshipful Agni, the sacrificers offer oblations, is the Supreme Brahman, the Self of the universe. In the same sequence, the matter described in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-29.2 is also told in the Kaṭha. Thus all the Śrutis praise him, saying that because he is omniscient, all-pervading, the support of all, and supremely excellent, he is called Jātavedas.

The deity of this sūkta is अग्नी रक्षोहा (*agnī rakṣohā*), that is, Agni who destroys the troops of Rakṣas, the bhūtas, piśācas and the like that obstruct sacrifices. Yāska, explaining the word रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*), says—

रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मात् । रहसि क्षणोतीति वा । रात्रौ नक्षत इति वा ॥ (*rakṣo rakṣitavyamasmāt | rahasi kṣaṇotīti vā | rātrau nakṣata iti vā ‖*) (Ni. 4-18)

and thus has given the etymology. That is, the troop of beings called Rakṣas devours men. From this our body has to be protected. Because it has to be protected from them, they are called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Or because they injure (men) in a deserted place where no one is, or in the dark, they are called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Or because they move about at night, they are called रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). Thus he has stated three kinds of meaning. There is a difference between the word रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*) and the word rākṣasa. Rākṣasas are individual beings of human form or of other fearful form visible to the eye. They are of wicked nature, always causing injury to good men, and bringing obstruction

### Printed p. 492

to good rites. The word रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*) denotes the bhūtas, daivas, piśācas and the like that are not visible to the eye: Demons, evil spirits &c; it is their nature to cause injury to men and to cause obstruction to good rites such as sacrifices. It is customary to pray to Agni, in sacrifices and in other rites, to remove their trouble and protect. The Agni who removes this kind of trouble is called Rakṣohāgni.

The piśācas or bhūtas who are on the earth are the enemies of men. The word that denotes them as a class is रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*). This word has occurred more than fifty times in the singular and the plural. Ordinarily it comes in connection with some deity, either as a prayer in the form "destroy the rākṣasa", or as praise in the form "he has slain the rākṣasa". In the sūktas 7-104 and 10-87 the very subject of these beings is present. Here the words रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*), यातु (*yātu*), यातुधान (*yātudhāna*) and others indicate them. Since रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*) is the name for evil deities, piśācas and all these, it may be understood as the word for the class, and यातु (*yātu*) as the word for the sub-class.

These piśācas or bhūtas have the forms of dogs, vultures, owls and other birds (7-104-20 to 22). In the form of birds they fly about at night (7-104-18). Assuming the form of a brother, a husband or a lover, they approach women and wish to destroy their children (10-162-5). In the form of a dog or a monkey they lie in wait to fall upon women (A. Ve. 4-37-11) **NOTE**. Therefore pregnant women and children are troubled by them (A. Ve. 8-6). At the time of marriage they move about around the bride, in order to pierce their eyes. They shoot small arrows into the sky (Mā. Gṛ. Sū. 1-10) **NOTE**. The description of their form and so on is found in the Atharvaveda itself. They especially assume human form. Mention is made of their limbs, such as head, eyes and heart; but some deformity is always present: three heads, two mouths, four eyes, five feet, no fingers, feet turned backward, or horns on the hand, and so on (A. Ve. 8-6; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2 3-7) **NOTE**. Blue, yellow or green piśācas are also mentioned (A. Ve. 19-22-4, 5). Among them also there are males and females, households and kings (A. Ve. 5-22-12; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-7); they also are subject to death (A. Ve. 6-32-2: and so on).

The Yātudhānas eat the flesh of men and of horses, and drink cow's milk (10.86.16, 17). To satisfy their craving for blood and flesh the Rākṣasas attack men. This attack is ordinarily by entering into them. There is a prayer to Agni to keep the Rākṣasas from entering those who sustain (the rite) (8-48.20) **NOTE**. Hither and thither

### Printed p. 493

flying, a piśāca that presides over disease enters men (A. Ve. 7-76-4). These bhūtas and pretas ordinarily enter us through our mouth when we eat or drink (A. Ve. 5-29.6 to 8); they also enter by other doors (Ta. Ve. 8.6.3) **NOTE**. Having entered within, they tear and eat the flesh of man and cause disease **NOTE** (A. Ve. 5-29.5, 10). They cause madness and destroy the power of speech (A. Ve. 6.101.3; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 1-15.5). They invade the dwelling houses of men (Kau. Sū. 135.9) **NOTE**. Some bhūtas, in the evening, go about around the houses dancing and braying like donkeys **NOTE**, or go about in forests, or keep laughing loudly or drinking from skulls (A. Ve. 8-6-10, 11, 14; Hi. Gṛ. Sū. 2-3-3). Their time of moving about is night or evening (7-104.8). In the eastern direction their sport does not go on at all; the sun rising there drives them away (Tai. Saṃ. 1.6.6 3). A falling meteor is believed to be the form of a bhūta (Kau. Sū. 125-9). Just as the pitch darkness of the new-moon night is suitable for the movement of the pretas, so for the bhūtas also it is the favourable time (A. Ve. 1-16 1; 4.36.3).

Nothing is so perilous to sacrifices as they are. In sacrifices that are fit for the gods the piśācas cause defects and omissions, and the Yātus scatter the oblations that have been offered, in disorder (7-104-18, 21). They cannot bear the sight of a hymn of praise (10-182-3). There is a prayer to Agni to burn up the bhūtas and the like, so that no curse may touch the sacrifice (1-76-3). There is a mantra that makes an enemy's sacrifice unproductive by the magic of the Yātudhānas and the troops of Rakṣas (A. Ve. 7-70-2. They come as obstructions, in the form of pretas, to the food and water that are offered as oblations to the dead (A. Ve. 18-2-28; compare Vā. Saṃ. 2-29). In the Purāṇas it is commonly said that these troops of Rakṣas (referred to as rākṣasas) trouble the yogis.

Between Agni, who dispels darkness and is the lord of the sacrifice, and them there is an implacable hatred. Hence the prayer is made to Agni himself: burn them, drive them away or destroy them (10-87-3, 6 and so on). It is from this very work that Agni and some other deities have received the name रक्षोहा (*rakṣohā*). These bhūtas are not only harmful by nature but also do harm when impelled by others. रक्षोयजः (*rakṣoyajaḥ*) (those who impel the Rākṣasas) is found (6-62-9). And there are bhūtas and Yātus of the practisers of mantras here and there (7-104.23; 8.60.20). One who has come under the affliction of a bhūta sent by an enemy can drive them away by making an offering to Yaviṣṭhāgni

### Printed p. 494

(Tai. Saṃ. 2.2-3-2), and there is a command to those bhūtas themselves: swallow the very one who impels you (A. Ve. 2.2-4).

In the sense of bhūtas the word रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*) is used in both the masculine and the feminine. In the neuter it also has the meaning "danger". It may be रक्ष् (*rakṣ*) from the root रक्ष् (*rakṣ*) (to trouble) (ऋक्षा (*ṛkṣā*), dangerous); but this usage is very rare. It may also be from the ordinary रक्ष् (*rakṣ*), to protect. In this context रक्ष् (*rakṣ*) would mean that which has to be escaped.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रक्षोहणमिति पंचविंशत्यचं तृतीयं सूक्तं । पायुर्नाम भारद्वाज
> ऋषिः । द्याविंशाद्याश्चतस्रोऽनुष्टुभः। शिष्टा एकविंशतिस्त्रिष्टुभः । रक्षोहाग्निर्देवता।
> तथा चानुक्रांतं । रक्षोहणं पंचाधिकापायुराग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं चतुरनुष्टुबंतमिति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥ अंगाराभिविहरणे परि त्वाग्नि इत्येषा जप्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । धिष्टावतामित्यादिना परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्यंतेन । आ. ५-१३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning रक्षोहणं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ*) is the third sūkta and has twenty-five Ṛks. The seer is Pāyu of the Bharadvāja line. The four Ṛks beginning with the twenty-second are in the Anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining twenty-one are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The deity is Rakṣohāgni. So it is stated in the Anukramaṇī: रक्षोहणं पंचाधिकापायुराग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं चतुरनुष्टुबंतमिति (*rakṣohaṇaṃ paṃcādhikāpāyurāgneyaṃ rākṣoghnaṃ caturanuṣṭubaṃtamiti*). The use of the sūkta has been stated. At the angārābhivihara the Ṛk परि त्वाग्नि (*pari tvāgni*) is to be muttered. It is also prescribed in the sūtra धिष्टावतामित्यादिना परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयमित्यंतेन (*dhiṣṭāvatāmityādinā pari tvāgne puraṃ vayamityaṃtena*) (Ā. 5-13).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta रक्षोहणं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ*) is the third sūkta in the seventh Anuvāka. It has twenty-five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Pāyu of the Bharadvāja gotra. From the twenty-second Ṛk of this sūkta the next four Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭup metre; the remaining twenty-one Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre. Rakṣohāgni is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said—रक्षोहणं पंचाधिका पायुराग्नेयं राक्षोघ्नं चतुरनुष्टु बंतं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ paṃcādhikā pāyurāgneyaṃ rākṣoghnaṃ caturanuṣṭu baṃtaṃ*). The use of the sūkta has been stated before. At the angārābhivihara the twenty-second Ṛk of this sūkta, परित्वाग्ने (*paritvāgne*), is to be muttered: this is prescribed by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, धिष्टावतामित्यादिना परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयं (*dhiṣṭāvatāmityādinā pari tvāgne puraṃ vayaṃ*) (Ā. 5-13).

Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 87. Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 25. Seer: पायुः (*pāyuḥ*). Deity: अग्नी रक्षोहा (*agnī rakṣohā*). Metre: 1-21 Triṣṭup; 22-25 Anuṣṭup.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रक्षोहणं रक्षसां हंतारं वाजिनं बलवंतमन्नवंतं वाग्निमा जिघर्मि ।
> धृतेनाजुहोमि । किंच मित्रं यजमानानां सखायं प्रथिष्टं पृथुतमं शर्म
> गृहमुप यामि । उपगच्छामि । सोऽयमग्निः शिशानो ज्वालास्तीक्ष्णीकुर्वन्

> रिषो हिंसकाद्रक्षसः पातु । रक्षतु । सोऽग्निर्नक्तं रात्र्य चास्मान्रक्षसः पातु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

I offer ghee to Agni, the slayer of the Rakṣas, who is powerful or possessed of food. And I approach the friend of the sacrificers, the most spacious refuge, that is, the house. This Agni, sharpening his flames, is kindled, set ablaze, by men intent on ritual. And may that Agni protect us by day from the Rakṣas who injure, and may that Agni protect us from the Rakṣas by night.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रक्षोहणं (*rakṣohaṇaṃ*)—the destroyer of the Rākṣasas
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—to Agni, who is endowed with strength
- आ जिघर्मि (*ā jigharmi*)—I offer an oblation of ghee
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—the friend of the sacrificers
- प्रथिष्टं (*prathiṣṭaṃ*)—the sturdy one
- शर्म (*śarma*)—Agni, who gives shelter like a house
- उप यामि (*upa yāmi*)—I approach
- अग्नि: (*agni:*)—Agni
- शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*)—sharp with flame
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—becomes kindled
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- दिवा (*divā*)—by day
- रिषः (*riṣaḥ*)—from the enemies who injure
- पातु (*pātu*)—may he protect
- सः (*saḥ*)—Agni
- नक्तं (*naktaṃ*)—may he protect by night also

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I offer an oblation of ghee to Agni, the destroyer of the Rākṣasas and endowed with strength. I approach Agni, the friend of the sacrificers, the sturdy one, who gives shelter like a house. Agni, sharp with his flame, is kindled by men intent on ritual. May that same Agni protect us by day and by night.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, he who has acquired wealth or has acquired knowledge, you, kindled, well blazing, are अयोदंष्ट्रः (*ayodaṃṣṭraḥ*), having teeth of iron, that is, having become sharp-toothed. Touch the Yātudhānas, the Rākṣasas, with your flame, that is, burn them up. And seize with your tongue, that is, your flame, the मूरदेवान् (*mūradevān*), the foolish gods, the Rākṣasas whose business is killing: that is, kill them. And having killed them, cut up the flesh-eating Rākṣasas and put them in your mouth; cover them. **NOTE** **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni named Jātavedas
- अयोदंष्ट्रः (*ayodaṃṣṭraḥ*)—you who have jaws as sharp as steel
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—blazing
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with your flame
- यातुधानान् (*yātudhānān*)—the Rākṣasas
- उप स्पृश (*upa spṛśa*)—destroy
- मूरदेवान् (*mūradevān*)—the Asuras of violent activity
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with the flame
- आ रभस्व (*ā rabhasva*)—annihilate
- क्रव्यादः (*kravyādaḥ*)—the Asuras who eat flesh
- वृक्त्वी (*vṛktvī*)—cutting
- आसन् (*āsan*)—into the mouth
- अपि धत्स्व (*api dhatsva*)—stuff in

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni named Jātavedas, you whose jaws are as sharp as steel, blazing, destroy the Rākṣasas with your flame. Annihilate with your flame the Asuras of violent activity. Cut up the flesh-eating Asuras and stuff them into your mouth.

> त्वमंतरिक्षे स्थितान्राक्षसान्परि याहि । परिगच्छ । परिगण्य च तान्यातुधानान्नाक्षसाङ्जंभैर्भक्षणसाधनभूताभिर्दंष्ट्राभिरभि सं धेहि! संयोजय भक्षयेत्यर्थः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Ubhayāvin, Agni endowed with both jaws, you are हिंस्रः (*hiṃsraḥ*), the harmer of the Rākṣasas. Sharpening both jaws, fix them on the Rākṣasas who deserve to be killed. And protect the world, the lower and the higher. And further, O king, blazing Agni, go round the Rākṣasas who stand in the sky; having gone round them, join the Yātudhānas, the Rākṣasas, with the जंभैः (*jaṃbhaiḥ*), the jaws that are the means of eating: that is, make them eat them.

- परं च (*paraṃ ca*)—and protect the world above
- उत (*uta*)—and
- राजन् (*rājan*)—O Agni, endowed with radiance
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—against the Asuras who dwell in the sky
- परि याहि (*pari yāhi*)—set out
- यातुधानान् (*yātudhānān*)—those Rākṣasas
- जंभैः (*jaṃbhaiḥ*)—with sharp tusks
- अभि सं धेहि (*abhi saṃ dhehi*)—swallow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who have two jaws, you the harmer of the Rākṣasas, sharpen both your jaws and apply them on the Rākṣasas. Protect this world and the world above. O Agni, endowed with radiance, confront the Asuras who dwell in the sky. Swallow those Rākṣasas with your sharp tusks.

##### English translation

> ताभि॑र्विध्य॒ हृद॑ये यातु॒धाना॑न्प्रति॒चो बा॒हून्प्रति॑  
> भज्येषां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यज्ञैः । इषूः । संनममानः । अग्ने । वाचा । शल्यान् । अशनिभिः । दिहानः ।  
> ताभिः । विध्य । हृदये । यातुधानान् । प्रतीचः । बाहून् । प्रति । भज्य । एषां॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं यज्ञैरस्मदीयैर्बलकरैर्यागैर्वाचास्मदीयया स्तुत्या
> चेषूर्वक्रान्पाणान् संनममानः संनमयन् शल्यांस्तासां शल्यानशनिभिर्दिप्तिबिर्दिहानस्तीक्ष्मीकुर्वन् ताभिरिशुभिर्यातुधानानाक्षसान्हृदये विध्य । तत एषां
> यातुधानानां संबंधिनः प्रतीचो युद्धाय त्वां प्रतिगतान्पाहून्प्रति भज ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, by our sacrifices that give strength and by our speech, our praise, bending the arrows, and sharpening their shafts with splendours, pierce with those arrows the Yātudhānas, the Rākṣasas, in the heart. Then, of these Yātudhānas, break and crush the arms of those who have come against you for battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यज्ञैः (*yajñaiḥ*)—by sacrifices
- वाचा (*vācā*)—and by praises
- इषू: (*iṣū:*)—your arrows
- संनममानः (*saṃnamamānaḥ*)—bending them to shoot at the Asuras
- शल्यान् (*śalyān*)—your javelins

### Printed p. 499

- आशनिभिः (*āśanibhiḥ*)—with flames
- दिहानः (*dihānaḥ*)—sharpening
- ताभिः (*tābhiḥ*)—with them
- यातुधानान् (*yātudhānān*)—the Asuras
- हृदये (*hṛdaye*)—striking them in the heart
- विध्य (*vidhya*)—cleave
- प्रतीचः (*pratīcaḥ*)—who oppose you
- एषां बाहून् (*eṣāṃ bāhūn*)—their arms
- प्रति भंगि (*prati bhaṃgi*)—cut off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, bending your arrows by sacrifices and praises to shoot at the Asuras, and sharpening your javelins with flames, strike the Asuras with them in the heart and cleave them. Cut off the arms of those who oppose you.

##### English translation
Agni, bending your arrows by means of our sacrifices and praise, and sharpening the javelins with your splendours, pierce with them the Yatudhanas to the heart, break their arms when raised against you-

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अग्ने॒ त्वचं॑ यातु॒धान॑स्य भिंधि हिं॒स्राशनि॒र्हर॑सा हंतेनं ।  
> प्र पर्वा॑णि जातवेदः शृणीहि क्र॒व्यात्क्र॑वि॒ष्णुर्वि चि॑नोतु  ॒
> वृक्लं ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आग्ने । त्वचं । यातुधानस्य । भिंधि । हिंस्रा । अशनिः । हरसा । हंतु । एनं ।  
> प्र । पर्वाणि ! जातवेदः । शृणीहि । क्रव्यआत् । कृविष्णुः : वि । चिनोतु । वृक्लं ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेदो जातधन जातप्रज्ञ वाग्ने त्वं यातुधानस्य राक्षसस्य त्वचु
> भिंधि । दारय । एनं भिन्नत्वचं यातुधानं हिंसा हिंसनशीलं तवाशनिर्वज्रं
> हरसा तापेन हंतु । हिनस्तु । हतस्य राक्षसस्य पर्वाणि शरीरपर्वाणि च प्र शृणीहि ।
> छिंद्दीत्यर्थः । छिन्नेषु च शरीरसंबंधिसु सत्सु वृक्षं छिन्नसंधिमेनु यातुधानु
> क्रविष्णुर्मांसमिच्छन् क्रव्यान्मांसभक्षको वृकादिर्वि चिनोतु । भक्षयतित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, Agni, he who has acquired wealth or has acquired knowledge, split, tear apart, the skin of the Yātudhāna, the Rākṣasa. May your thunderbolt, which is given to harming, destroy with its heat this Yātudhāna whose skin is split. And break the joints of the body of the slain Rākṣasa. When the parts joined to the body have been cut, let the flesh-desiring, flesh-eating wolves and the like devour the Yātudhāna whose joints are cut. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 500

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni, who know everything
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यातुधानस्य (*yātudhānasya*)—of the Asura
- त्व चं (*tva caṃ*)—the skin
- भिंधि (*bhiṃdhi*)—strip off
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—him
- हिंस्रा (*hiṃsrā*)—that causes pain
- अशनिः (*aśaniḥ*)—the thunderbolt
- हरसा (*harasā*)—with its flame
- हंतु (*haṃtu*)—let it destroy
- पर्वाणि (*parvāṇi*)—the joints of the body
- प्र शृणीहि (*pra śṛṇīhi*)—cut off
- वृक्षं (*vṛkṣaṃ*)—this one whose body has been cut up
- क्रविष्णुः (*kraviṣṇuḥ*)—that which desires flesh
- क्रव्यात् (*kravyāt*)—wicked animals such as wolves, that eat flesh
- वि चिनोतु (*vi cinotu*)—let them tear and eat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, omniscient, strip off the skin of the Asura. May the thunderbolt that causes pain destroy him with its flame. Cut off the joints of his body. May the flesh-eating wolves and the like tear and eat him whose body has been cut up.

##### English translation
Agni Jatavedas, cut through the skin of the Yatudhana, let your destructive thunderbolt destroy him with its fire ; sever his joints, may the flesh-desiring flesh-eater devour his mutilated body.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्रे॒दानीं॒ पश्य॑सि जातवेद॒स्तिष्ठं॑तमग्न उ॒त वा॒ चरं॑तं ।  
> यद्वां॒तरि॑क्षे प॒थिभिः॒ पतं॑तं॒ तमस्ता॑ विध्य॒ शर्वा॒ शिशा॑नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत्र । इदानीं । पश्यसि । जातवेदः । तिष्ठंतं । अग्ने । उत । वा । चरुतं ।  
> यत् । वा । अंतरिक्षे । पथिभिः । पतंतं । तं । अस्ता । विध्य । शर्वा । शिशानः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे जातवेद उत्पन्नप्रज्ञाग्ने त्वं यत्र पृथिव्यां तिष्ठंतमुतापि च चरंतं
> यद्वांतरिक्षे पथिभिराकाशमार्गैः पतंतं गच्छंतं यातुधानमिदानीं संप्रति

### Printed p. 501

> पश्यसि तं यातुधानमस्ता शराणां क्षेप्ता त्वं शिशानः शरांस्तीक्ष्णीकुर्वञ्चा
> शरेण विध्य ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Jātavedas, Agni, in whom knowledge has arisen, wherever you now see on the earth a Yātudhāna, a Rākṣasa, standing, or moving, or going in the sky by the paths of the air, you, the hurler of arrows, sharpening your arrows, pierce him with an arrow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni in the form of Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तिष्ठंतं (*tiṣṭhaṃtaṃ*)—let that Asura be standing
- उत वा (*uta vā*)—or
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—let him be moving
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—or
- अंतरिक्षे पथिभिः (*aṃtarikṣe pathibhiḥ*)—on the paths of the sky
- पतंतं (*pataṃtaṃ*)—let him be flying: such a Yātudhāna
- इदानीं (*idānīṃ*)—now
- यत्र पश्यसि (*yatra paśyasi*)—in whatever region you see him
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- अस्ता (*astā*)—you who shoot arrows
- शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*)—having sharpened your weapon
- शर्वा (*śarvā*)—with an arrow
- विध्य (*vidhya*)—cleave

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni in the form of Jātavedas, whether that Yātudhāna is standing, or moving, or flying on the paths of the sky, in whatever region you now see him, destroy him with the shooting of your sharp arrow.

##### English translation
Wherever you now behold him, Agni Jatavedas, whether standing or moving, or passing along the paths in the firmament, you, O shooter, sharpening (your arrows), transfix him with your shaft.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒ताल॑ब्धं स्पृणुहि जातवेद आलेभा॒नादृ॒ष्टिभि॑र्यातु॒धाना॑त् ।  
> अग्ने॒ पूर्वो॒ नि ज॑हि॒ शोशु॑चान आ॒मादः॒ क्विंका॒स्तम॑दं॒तैनीः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उते । आलब्धं । स्पृणिहि । जातवेदः । आलेभानात् । ऋष्टिभिः । यातुधानात् ।  
> अग्ने । पूर्वः । नि । जहि । शोशुचानः । आमअदः । क्विंकाः । तं । अदंतु । एनीः ॥

### Printed p. 502

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतापि च हे जातवेदोऽग्ने त्वमालब्धं हंतुं हस्ताभ्यामारब्धं साधुं
> मां स्तोतारं यष्टारं वालेभानादालभमानाद्यातुधानाद्राक्षसादृष्टिभिरात्मीयैरायुधविशेषैः स्पृणुहि । पारय । रक्षेत्यर्थः । किंच पूर्वो मुख्यस्त्वं
> शोशुचानः प्रज्वलन्नि जहि । मां हंतुमुद्युक्तं यातुधानं मारय । किंच तं
> यातुधानमामादोऽपक्वस्य मांसस्य भक्षकाः क्विंकाः शब्दकारिण्यः॥ टुक्षु शब्दे ॥
> यद्वा । क्विंका नाम पक्षिविशेषाः । एनीर्गंत्रोदंतु । भक्षयंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And, O Jātavedas, Agni, me who am आलब्धं (*ālabdhaṃ*), seized, begun upon by hands in order to be killed, a good man, a praiser or a sacrificer, from the Yātudhāna, the Rākṣasa who seizes me, deliver and protect with your own special weapons. And you, the foremost, blazing, slay the Yātudhāna who is bent on killing me. And let the Kviṅkās, the eaters of uncooked flesh, the noise-makers, devour that Yātudhāna; or else the Kviṅkās are a special kind of birds. Let the एनीः (*enīḥ*) eat, devour him. **NOTE** **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—O Agni in the form of Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- आलब्धं (*ālabdhaṃ*)—me, who have striven for the destruction of the enemy
- आलेभानात् (*ālebhānāt*)—from the one who confronts me and falls upon me
- यातुधानात् (*yātudhānāt*)—the Rākṣasa
- ऋष्टिभिः (*ṛṣṭibhiḥ*)—with your weapons
- स्पृणुहि (*spṛṇuhi*)—protect
- पूर्वः (*pūrvaḥ*)—you who are foremost
- शोशुचानः (*śośucānaḥ*)—blazing
- नि जहि (*ni jahi*)—destroy the enemy
- आमादः (*āmādaḥ*)—that eat flesh
- क्ष्वॆंकाः (*kṣvèṃkāḥ*)—that make noise
- एनीः (*enīḥ*)—cruel birds that fly about
- तं अदंतु (*taṃ adaṃtu*)—let them eat him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni in the form of Jātavedas, protect me, who have striven for the destruction of the enemy, from the Rākṣasa who falls upon me. You, the foremost, blazing, destroy the enemy. May the cruel birds that eat flesh and make noise eat him.

##### English translation
And defend me, Jatavedas, with your darts when I am seized, (defend me) from the Yatudhana who has seized me; anticipating him you, Agni, blazing fiercely, slay him; may the swift-flying vultures, the flesh-eaters, devour him.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ह प्र ब्रू॑हि यत॒मः सो अ॑ग्ने॒ यो या॑तु॒धानो॒ य ॒ ॒॑
> इ॒दं कृ॒णोति॑ ।  
> तमा र॑भस्व स॒मिधा॑ यविष्ठ नृ॒चक्ष॑स॒श्चक्षु॑षे रंधय्यनं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इह । प्र । ब्रूहि । यतमः । सः । अग्ने । यः । यातुधानः । यः । इदं ।  
> कृणोति ।  
> तं । आ । रभस्व । संइधा । यविष्ठ । नृचक्षसः । चक्षुषे । रंधय । एनं ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये यविष्ठ युवतमाग्ने यो यातुधानो राक्षसोऽस्मद्यज्ञविघ्नकारी
> यश्चान्योऽपि पिशाचादिरिदं यज्ञदूषणादि करोति स यतमः ॥ तमबवधारणार्थ० ॥ इहास्मिंत्वद्विषययागकर्मणि वर्तमानाय मह्यं प्र ब्रूहि ।
> तं पापकारिणं समिधा स्वकीयेन तेजसा रभस्व। हंतुं प्रारभस्व । तत एनं पापिष्ठं
> नृचक्षसो नृणां द्रष्टुस्तव चक्षुषे तेजसे रंधय । वशं नय । तेजसा
> संदहेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Yaviṣṭha, youngest Agni, whichever Yātudhāna, Rākṣasa, is an obstructer of our sacrifice, and whichever other, a Piśāca or the like, does this defilement of the sacrifice, he is यतमः (*yatamaḥ*), "whichever" (the suffix तम (*tama*) is in the sense of determination). Tell me, who am present here in the rite that is directed to you. Begin to kill that evildoer with your own radiance. Then subject this most sinful one to the radiance of you, the beholder of men: bring him under control; the meaning is: burn him up with radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यविष्ठ (*yaviṣṭha*)—O extremely young one
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः यातुधानः (*yaḥ yātudhānaḥ*)—whichever Rākṣasa
- यः (*yaḥ*)—or whichever Piśāca
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—to our sacrifice, an obstruction
- करोति (*karoti*)—does
- सं यतमः (*saṃ yatamaḥ*)—whoever he may be
- इह (*iha*)—here
- प्र ब्रूहि (*pra brūhi*)—announce his name
- तं (*taṃ*)—that evildoer
- समिधा (*samidhā*)—with your flame
- अरभस्व (*arabhasva*)—try to destroy
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—this Asura
- नृचक्षसः (*nṛcakṣasaḥ*)—who can see the doings of men
- चक्षसः (*cakṣasaḥ*)—to your radiance
- रंधय (*raṃdhaya*)—make him subject

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, extremely young, whichever Rākṣasa, or whichever Piśāca, causes obstruction to our sacrifice, whoever he may be, announce his name here. Destroy that evildoer with your flame. Make him subject to your flame.

##### English translation
Agni, youngest of the gods, announce (to me present) at this (your sacrifice), which is your Yatudhana who does this; destroy him with your kindled flame; beholder of men, consume him with your brilliance.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अग्ने त्वं तीक्ष्णेन तिग्मेन चक्षुषा तेजसा यज्ञमस्मदीयं यागं रक्ष ।
> पालय । किंच हे प्रचेतः प्रकृष्टज्ञानाग्ने प्रांचं प्रांचितारं यज्ञं वसुभ्यो
> वसूनामर्थाय प्रणय । प्रकर्षेण नय । किंच हे नृचक्षो नृणां द्रष्टरग्ने
> रक्षांसि हिंस्रं हिंसनशीलमभि शोशुचानमभिप्रदीप्तं त्वा त्वां यातुधाना राक्षसा
> मा दभन् । हिंसिषुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Agni, protect, guard, our sacrifice with your sharp radiance. And, O Pracetas, Agni of excellent knowledge, lead forward the sacrifice, the one that goes forward, for the sake of riches, for the sake of the Vasus. And, O Agni, beholder of men, may the Yātudhānas, the Rākṣasas, not harm you, who are given to harming the Rākṣasas and are blazing forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- तीक्ष्णेन (*tīkṣṇena*)—that burns
- चक्षुषा (*cakṣuṣā*)—with your radiance
- यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—our sacrifice
- रक्ष (*rakṣa*)—protect
- प्रचेतः (*pracetaḥ*)—O Agni, who have excellent knowledge
- प्रांचं (*prāṃcaṃ*)—our sacrifice that goes forward
- वसुभ्यः (*vasubhyaḥ*)—for the sake of wealth
- प्र णय (*pra ṇaya*)—make it advance fully
- नृचक्षः (*nṛcakṣaḥ*)—O Agni, who can see men
- हिंस्रं (*hiṃsraṃ*)—that causes injury
- रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)—the Rākṣasas
- अभि शोशुचानं (*abhi śośucānaṃ*)—who burn
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- यातुधानाः (*yātudhānāḥ*)—the Asuras
- मा दभन् (*mā dabhan*)—let them not injure

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, protect our sacrifice with your burning radiance. O Agni, who have excellent knowledge, make our sacrifice complete for the sake of wealth. May the injuring Asuras not injure you, who destroy them.

##### English translation
Protect this sacrifice, Agni, with your sharp glance; lead it sage (Agni) forward to (the acquisition of) riches; let not the Yatudhanas harm you, beholder of men, the destroyer of Rakshasas blazing fiercely.

> हे अग्ने नृचक्षा नृणां द्रष्टा त्वं विक्षु मनुष्येषु हिंसकत्वेन वर्तमानं
> रक्षो राक्षसं परि पश्य । सर्वतोऽवलोकय । अवलोक्य च तस्य रक्षसस्त्रीण्यग्राग्राणि

> मूलं पादं वृश्च । छिद्धि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, who is the beholder of men, is told to look all around at the Rākṣasa who lives among men as a harmer. Having looked, he is to cut off the three topmost heads of that Rākṣasa. Then he is to destroy with his own radiance the Rākṣasas who stand at the side of that Rākṣasa. In the same way he is to cut off, in a threefold manner, the foot of that Yātudhāna Rākṣasa. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—you who can see the doings of men
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among men, harmful
- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the Asura
- परिपश्य (*paripaśya*)—find out
- तस्य (*tasya*)—his
- त्रीणि ग्रा (*trīṇi grā*)—the three heads **NOTE**
- प्रति शृणीहि (*prati śṛṇīhi*)—cut off
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of that same Asura
- पृष्टीः (*pṛṣṭīḥ*)—those at his side
- हरसा (*harasā*)—with your radiance
- शृणीहि (*śṛṇīhi*)—destroy
- यातुधानस्य (*yātudhānasya*)—of the Asura
- त्रेधा (*tredhā*)—threefold
- मूलं (*mūlaṃ*)—the foot
- वृश्च (*vṛśca*)—cut off

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, you who can see the doings of men, find out the Asura who among men is a harmer. Cut off all his three heads. Destroy with your radiance those who are at the side of that same Asura. Cut off also the threefold foot of the Asura.

##### English translation
Regard, beholder of men, the Rakshasa among the people; cut off his three heads; cut off his flanks with your might; cut off the triple foot of the Yatudhana.

> हे जातवेदो जातप्रज्ञाग्ने ते त्वदीयं प्रसितिं ज्वालाप्रबंधनं
> यातुधानो राक्षसस्त्रिस्त्रीन्वारानेतु । गच्छतु । त्रिबद्धं यत्तत्सुबद्धं भवति हि ।

> वर्जय वृकेण ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Jātaveda, Agni of wisdom, is addressed: let the Yātudhāna Rākṣasa come three times into your prasiti, the binding of your flames; what is bound threefold is well bound. Further, the Yātudhāna Rākṣasa who strikes truth with untruth: crushing him with your own radiance (the root sphūrj here has the sense of crushing), restrain that Yātudhāna in plain view before me, who make praise, and keep him away, वृकेण (*vṛkeṇa*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जातवेदः (*jātavedaḥ*)—you who are Jātavedas
- अग्ने (*agne*)—O Agni
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Rākṣasa who
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—truth
- अनृतेन (*anṛtena*)—with untruth
- हंति (*haṃti*)—defiles
- यातुधानः (*yātudhānaḥ*)—that same Asura
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्रसितिं (*prasitiṃ*)—in the mass of flames
- त्रिः (*triḥ*)—three times
- एतु (*etu*)—let him be caught
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with your radiance
- स्फूर्जयन् (*sphūrjayan*)—crushing
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—him
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—of the praiser
- समक्षं (*samakṣaṃ*)—in plain view
- नि वृजि (*ni vṛji*)—destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, who are Jātavedas, may the Rākṣasa who defiles truth with untruth be caught three times in your mass of flames. Crushing him with your radiance, destroy him in the plain view of the praiser.

##### English translation
Agni, Jatavedas, let the Yatudhana, who defeats your truth with falsehood, come thrice into the confinement of your flames; crushing him with your might, drive him from the presence of (me) your worshipper.

> येन चक्षुषा शफारुजं शफाभ्यामारुजंतं शफसदृशैनर्खैः साधूनामाभिमुख्येन
> भंजकं यातुधानं राक्षसं पश्यसि । किंच सत्यं धूर्वंतमसत्येन हिंसंतमचितमज्ञानं दैव्येन दिवि भवेन ज्योतिषा तेजसाथर्ववन्नोष । नितरां दह। दध्यज्जथर्वा
> रक्षसां हंतेति प्रागुक्तं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni is told to cast that eye, that radiance, upon the roaring Rākṣasa, the eye with which he sees the Yātudhāna Rākṣasa who is śaphārujam, one who with nails like hoofs breaks the pious by assailing them. Further, he is to burn down thoroughly, as Atharvan did, with divine radiance, the ignorant one who harms truth with untruth. Sāyaṇa adds that this was said before: दध्यज्जथर्वा रक्षसां हंतेति प्रागुक्तं (*dadhyajjatharvā rakṣasāṃ haṃteti prāguktaṃ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- येन (*yena*)—with which eye

- पश्यसि (*paśyasi*)—you see
- तत् चक्षुः (*tat cakṣuḥ*)—that same eye
- रेभे (*rebhe*)—upon the Asura who makes a noise
- प्रति धेहि (*prati dhehi*)—direct
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—truth
- धूर्वतं (*dhūrvataṃ*)—who harms with untruth **NOTE**
- अचितं (*acitaṃ*)—the ignorant one
- दिव्येन ज्योतिषा (*divyena jyotiṣā*)—with his own divine light
- अथर्वसत् (*atharvasat*)—as Atharvan destroys **NOTE**
- न्यूष (*nyūṣa*)—burn the Asuras completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, with whatever eye you look at the Rākṣasa whose nails are harmful like hoofs, direct that same eye upon the Asura who makes a noise. Burn completely, with your divine light, the ignorant one who harms truth with falsehood, as Atharvan destroys the Asuras.
