> किंच यज्ञयानां यज्ञसंपादिनां देवानां मायामु प्रज्ञामेवैतां मन्यंते
> कवय इति शेषः । यत्प्रजानन् प्रज्ञायमानः सूर्यस्तर्णिस्वरमाणः

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Vaiśvānara Agni at night (नक्तं (*naktaṃ*)) becomes the head (मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*)), that is, the chief like a head, of all beings (भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)), because at night the light of all creatures depends on him. Then (ततः (*tataḥ*)), after the night, Sūrya is born rising in the morning; that is, by day that same Vaiśvānara Agni becomes Sūrya. Further, of the gods who accomplish the sacrifice, the seers (the word "seers" is to be supplied) consider this to be wisdom, मायामु (*māyāmu*). As for that which, becoming known, Sūrya

### Printed p. 550

> सन्नपोऽंतरिक्षं कर्म वा चरति । तथा च यास्कः । मूर्धा मूर्तमस्मिन्द्धीयते
> मूर्धा यः सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूर्यो जायते
> प्रातरुद्यंत्स एव प्रज्ञां त्वेतां मन्यंते यज्जियानां देवानां यज्ञसंपादिनामपो यत्कर्म चरति प्रजानंत्सर्वाणि स्थानान्यनुसंचरति त्वरमाणः ।
> नि. ७-२७ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Being knowing, he moves through the atmosphere, or he moves in action. Accordingly Yāska (Ni. 7-27) says: he explains मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*) as that in which the solid (mūrta) is placed; that which becomes the head of all beings at night is Agni; then Sūrya is born, rising in the morning; he indeed is the one whom they consider as wisdom, of the gods worthy of sacrifice who accomplish the sacrifice; he, knowing, moves through the atmosphere, or through action, and hastening goes about to all the places.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अग्निः (*agniḥ*)—Vaiśvānara Agni
- नक्तं (*naktaṃ*)—at night
- भुवः (*bhuvaḥ*)—for all the worlds
- मूर्धा (*mūrdhā*)—as the chief illuminator
- भवति (*bhavati*)—he is
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—after the night
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—the sun
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—in the morning
- उद्यन् (*udyan*)—appearing
- जायते (*jāyate*)—becomes visible
- यत् (*yat*)—by which greatness
- प्रजानन् (*prajānan*)—the sun who has become visible
- तूर्णिः (*tūrṇiḥ*)—moving swiftly
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—throughout the atmosphere
- चरति (*carati*)—moves; that
- यज्ञियानां (*yajñiyānāṃ*)—of the gods worthy of sacrifice
- एतां मायामु (*etāṃ māyāmu*)—the wise understand as wisdom itself

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Vaiśvānara Agni is the chief illuminator of all the worlds at night. After the night the sun appears in the morning and becomes visible. By whatever greatness the sun, who has become visible to all, moves swiftly throughout the atmosphere, that, those who know say, is the wise action of the gods worthy of sacrifice.

##### English translation
Agni is the head of all beings by night; then the sun rising early is born ; (the wise know) this to be the wisdom of the adorable gods, that the swift-moving sun being intelligent moves through the firmament.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For the explanation of the etymology that Yāska has written for this Ṛk, see what is written in the introduction to this sūkta (pages 537-538).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दृ॒शेन्नो॒ यो म॑हि॒ना समि॒द्धोऽरो॑चत दि॒वियो॑निर्वि॒भावाः॑  
> तस्मि॑न्न॒ग्नौ सू॑क्तवा॒केन॑ दे॒वा ह॒विर्विश्व॒ आजु॑हवुस्तनू॒पाः ॥७॥

### Printed p. 551

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दृशेन्यः । यः । महिना । संइद्धः । आरोचत । दिवियोनिः । विभावा ।  
> तस्मिन् । अग्नौ । सूक्तवाकेन । देवाः । हविः । विश्वे । आ । अजुहवुः । तनूपाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यो वैश्वानरोग्निर्महिना महत्त्वेन दृशेन्वः सर्वदर्शनीयः समिद्धः
> सम्यग्नीप्तो दिवियोनिर्दुस्थानो विभावा दीप्तिमांश्च सन्नरोचत दीप्यते
> तस्मिन्वैश्वानरेग्नौ तनूपाः शरीराणां रक्षका विश्वे सर्वॆ देवाः सूक्तवाकेनेदं
> द्यावापृथिवी इत्यादिवाक्येन स्तोत्राणां वचनेन वा हविराजुहवुः । अभिमुख्येन
> जुहुवुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Vaiśvānara Agni who by his greatness (महिना (*mahinā*) means "by greatness") is visible to all (दृशेन्यः (*dṛśenyaḥ*)), well kindled (समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)), having his station in heaven (दिवियोनिः (*diviyoniḥ*)) and endowed with brilliance (विभावा (*vibhāvā*)), shines (अरोचत (*arocata*) means "he shines"). In that Vaiśvānara Agni all the gods, the protectors of bodies (तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)), offered the oblation, facing him, with the sūktavāka, that is, with a sentence such as "idam dyāvāpṛthivī", or with the recitation of hymns of praise.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Vaiśvānara Agni
- महिना (*mahinā*)—by his own greatness
- दृशेन्यः (*dṛśenyaḥ*)—visible to all
- समिद्धः (*samiddhaḥ*)—blazing
- दिवियोनिः (*diviyoniḥ*)—having heaven as his station
- विभावा (*vibhāvā*)—endowed with splendour
- अरोचत (*arocata*)—he shines
- तस्मिन् आग्नौ (*tasmin āgnau*)—in that same Vaiśvānara Agni
- तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)—the protectors of bodies
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- सूक्तवाकेन (*sūktavākena*)—with words of praise
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- आजुहवुः (*ājuhavuḥ*)—offered in the form of an oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Vaiśvānara Agni who by his own greatness shines, visible to all, blazing, having heaven as his station and endowed with splendour—in that same Vaiśvānara Agni all the gods, the protectors of bodies, offered the oblation in the form of an offering with words of praise.

##### English translation
He who shines visible to all through his greatness radiant, having his station in the sky, resplendent in him, Agni, the universal gods, the guardians of men's bodies, have presented an oblation with the voice of praise.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सू॒क्त॒वा॒कं प्र॑थ॒ममादिद॒ग्निमादिद्द॒विर॑जनयंत दे॒वाः ।

### Printed p. 552

> स एषां यज्ञो अभवत्तनूपास्तं द्यौर्वेद तं पृथिवी  
> तमापः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सूक्तवाकं । प्रथमं । आत् । इत् । अग्निं । आत् । इत् । हविः। अजनयंत। देवाः।  
> सः । एषां । यज्ञः । अभवत् । तनूपाः । तं । द्यौः । वेद । तं । पृथिवी । तं ।  
> आपः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रथमं पूर्वं सूक्तवाकमिदं द्यावापृथिवी इत्यादि वाक्यं मनसा
> निरूपयंति । आदिदनंतरमेवाग्निं मथनेनोत्पादयंति । आदिदनंतरमेव देवा
> हविरजनयंत । स वैश्वानरोऽग्निरेषां देवानां यज्ञो यष्टव्योऽभवत् ।
> भवति । स तनूपाः शरीराणां रक्षिता च भवति । तमग्निं द्यौर्द्युलोको वेद ।
> जानाति । तमग्निं पृथिवी भूमिरपि च जानाति । तमग्निमापोऽंतरिक्षं च जानाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods first (प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)) ponder in the mind the sūktavāka, the sentence beginning "idam dyāvāpṛthivī". Immediately after (आदित् (*ādit*)) they produce Agni by churning. Immediately after that the gods produced the oblation. That Vaiśvānara Agni became the sacrifice, that is, the one to be sacrificed to, of these gods; and he is also the protector of bodies (तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)). Heaven knows that Agni; earth also knows him; the waters, that is, the atmosphere, also know him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)—first
- सूक्तवाकं (*sūktavākaṃ*)—the words of praise of the deity
- आदित् (*ādit*)—afterwards
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- आदित् (*ādit*)—after that
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- अजनयंत (*ajanayaṃta*)—they produced
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Vaiśvānara Agni
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—for these gods
- यज्ञः (*yajñaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- अभवत् (*abhavat*)—has become
- तनूपाः (*tanūpāḥ*)—the protector of bodies
- तं (*taṃ*)—that Agni
- द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)—the world of heaven
- वेद (*veda*)—knows
- तं (*taṃ*)—that same Agni
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth also knows
- तं (*taṃ*)—him
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the atmosphere also knows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods produced first the words of praise such as "idam dyāvāpṛthivī", then Agni, and after that the oblation. Vaiśvānara Agni is for the gods worthy of worship and the protector of bodies. Heaven and earth and the atmosphere know this Agni fully.

##### English translation
The gods first generated the words of the hymn, then Agni, hent the oblation ; he is the (object of the) sacrifice of these deities, the protector of the body ; him the heaven knows, him the earth and the waters know.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यं दे॒वासोऽज॑नयंता॒ग्निं यस्मि॒नाजु॑हवु॒र्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ ।  
> सो आ॒र्चिषा॑ पृथि॒वीं द्यामु॒तेनामृ॑जू॒यमा॑नो अतपन्महि॒त्वा ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यं । देवासः । अजनयंत । अग्निं । यस्मिन् । आ । अजुहवुः । भुवनानि । विश्वा ।  
> सः । अर्चिपा । पृथिवीं । द्यां । उत । इमां । ऋजुयमानः। अतपत् । महित्वा॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यं वैश्वानरमग्निं देवासो देवा अजनयंत उत्पादितवंतः यस्मिंश्चोत्सन्ने वैश्वानरेऽग्नौ विश्वा विश्वानि भुवनानि भूतान्याजुहवुः अभिमुख्येन
> जुहवुः सर्वमेधे स वैश्वानरोऽग्निरर्चिषा तेजसा पृथिवीमंतरिक्षं । आपः
> पृथिवीत्यंतरिक्षनामसु पाठात् । द्यां दिनं चोतापि चेमां भूमिं चर्जूयमान
> ऋजुगमनो महित्वा महत्वेनातपत् । सर्वं तपति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Vaiśvānara Agni whom the gods produced (अजनयंत (*ajanayaṃta*) means "they produced"), and in whom, when he was produced, all beings offered oblations, facing him, in the sarvamedha. That Vaiśvānara Agni, with his radiance (अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*) means "with brilliance"), warmed (अतपत् (*atapat*)) the earth, which here is the atmosphere, since the waters and the earth are read among the names of the atmosphere, and heaven, and also this earth; going straight (ऋजुयमानः (*ṛjuyamānaḥ*) means "straight-going"), with greatness (महित्वा (*mahitvā*)) he heats everything.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं अग्निं (*yaṃ agniṃ*)—which Vaiśvānara Agni
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- अजनयंत (*ajanayaṃta*)—produced
- यस्मिन् (*yasmin*)—in which Agni
- विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all the worlds
- आ अजुहवुः (*ā ajuhavuḥ*)—offered oblations
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Vaiśvānara Agni
- ऋजुयमानः (*ṛjuyamānaḥ*)—having a straight course
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—endowed with greatness
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—by his radiance
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the atmosphere
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the world of heaven
- उत (*uta*)—and
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—this earth
- आतपत् (*ātapat*)—has caused to be possessed of heat

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Vaiśvānara Agni whom the gods produced, in whom all the worlds offered oblations, that same Vaiśvānara Agni, having a straight course, by his own radiance endowed with greatness **NOTE**, has caused the atmosphere, the world of heaven and also the earth to be possessed of heat.

### Printed p. 554

##### English translation
Agni whom the gods, generated, in whom all beings have offered oblations—he, the straight-going, has warmed by his radiance, by his might, the earth and this heaven.

#### Ṛk 10
**NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्तोमे॑न॒ हिदि॒वि दे॒वासो॑ अ॒ग्निमजी॑जन॒ञ्क्ति॑भी रोदसि॒प्रां।  
> तमू॑ अकृण्वन् त्रे॒धा भु॒वे कं स ओष॑धीः पचति वि॒श्वरू॑पाः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> स्तोमेन । हि । दिवि । देवासः । अग्निं । अजीजनन् । शक्तिभिः । रोदसिप्रां ।  
> तं । ऊं इति । अकृण्वन् । त्रेधा । भुवे । कं । सः । ओषधीः । पचति । विश्वरूपाः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवासो देवाः शक्तिभिः कर्मभी रोदसिप्रां द्यावापृथिव्योरापूरयितारमग्निं सूर्यात्मकं दिवि द्युलोके स्तोमेन हि स्तुत्या खल्वजीजनन् ।
> उत्पादितवंतः । अपि च तमु तमेव कं सुखकरमग्निं यज्ञे त्रेधा भुवे
> त्रेधाभावायाकृण्वन् । कुर्वंति । पृथिव्यां वर्तमानो विश्वरूपाः सर्वरूपा
> ओषधीर्वीह्र्याद्यास्तेन तेनोपकारेण पचति । अत्र यास्कः । स्तोमेन यं हि दिवि
> देवासोऽग्निमजनयञ्क्तिभिः कर्मभिद्यावापृथिव्योः पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधा.
> भावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः । यदस्य दिवि तृतीयं तदसावादित्य
> इति हि ब्राह्मणं । नि. ७-२८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods (देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)) by powers, that is, by deeds (शक्तिभिः (*śaktibhiḥ*)), produced in heaven, by praise, Agni of the nature of Sūrya, who fills heaven and earth (रोदसिप्रां (*rodasiprāṃ*)). Moreover, that same Agni, the giver of happiness, they made in the sacrifice for threefold being (त्रेधा भुवे (*tredhā bhuve*)). He, being on earth, ripens by that benefit the plants of all forms (विश्वरूपाः (*viśvarūpāḥ*)), rice and the like. Here Yāska (Ni. 7-28) says: the Agni whom the gods in heaven produced by praise, by powers, that is, by deeds, they made him the filling of heaven and earth, for threefold being, on earth, in the atmosphere and in heaven, says Śākapūṇi. "What is his third in heaven, that is that Āditya": so says a Brāhmaṇa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—the gods
- शक्तिभिः (*śaktibhiḥ*)—by their great deeds
- रोदसिप्रां (*rodasiprāṃ*)—who fills heaven and earth
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni of the form of Sūrya
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- स्तोमेन (*stomena*)—with praise
- आजीजनन् (*ājījanan*)—produced
- कं तमु (*kaṃ tamu*)—that same Agni, the giver of happiness
- त्रेधा भुवे (*tredhā bhuve*)—so that he shines in three forms in the three worlds
- अकृण्वन् (*akṛṇvan*)—have made
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- विश्वरूपाः (*viśvarūpāḥ*)—possessing many forms
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the plants
- पचति (*pacati*)—ripens

### Printed p. 555

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, by their great deeds, produced in the world of heaven, with praise, the Agni of the form of Sūrya, who fills all of heaven and earth. That same giver of happiness, Agni, they have made to shine in three forms in the three worlds. That same Agni on earth ripens the many forms, the plants.

##### English translation
The gods have by praise engendered Agni in the sky, who fills heven and earth by his functions, they appointed the joy-bestowing Agni to his three-fold condition, he brings the manifold plants to maturity.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य॒देदे॑न॒मद॑धुर्य॒ज्ञिया॑सो दि॒वि दे॒वाः सूर्य॑मादिते॒यं।  
> य॒दा च॑रि॒ष्णू मि॑थु॒नावभू॑ता॒मादित्पप्रप॑श्य॒न्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यदा । इत् । एनं । अदधुः । यज्ञियासः । दिवि । देवाः । सूर्यं । आदितेयं ।  
> यदा । चरिष्णू इति । मिथुनौ । अभूतां । आत् । इत् । प्र । अपश्यन् । भुवनानि ।  
> विश्वा ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यदेद्यदैव प्रातरादितेयमदितेः पुत्रं सूर्यमेनमग्निं च यज्जि
> यासो यज्ञार्हा देवा दिवि द्युलोकेऽदधुः धृतवंतः । यदा चेमा चरिष्णू
> चरणशील् सूर्यवैश्वानरौ मिथुनावभूतां प्रादुरभूतां । आदिदनंतरमेव
> विश्वा विश्वानि भुवनानि भूतजातानि प्रापश्यन् । तौ पश्यंति ॥ अत्र यास्कः !
> यदैनमदधुर्यज्जियाः सर्वे दिवि देवाः सूर्यमदितेः पुत्रं यदा चरिष्णू

### Printed p. 556

> मिथुनौ प्रादुरभूतां सर्वदा सहचारिणावुषाश्चादित्यश्च । मिथुनौ कस्मान्मिनोतिः
> श्रयतिकर्मा थु इति नामकरणस्थकारो वा नयतिः परो वनिर्वा समाश्रितावन्योन्यं नयतो वनुतो वा । मनुष्यमिथुनावप्येतस्मादेव मेथंतावन्योन्यं
> वनुत इति वा । नि. ७-२९ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When, in the morning, the gods worthy of sacrifice placed in heaven Sūrya, the son of Aditi (आदितेयं (*āditeyaṃ*)), and this Agni; and when these two moving ones (चरिष्णू (*cariṣṇū*)), Sūrya and Vaiśvānara, became a pair (मिथुनौ (*mithunau*)) and appeared; immediately after (आदित् (*ādit*)) all the worlds, all beings, saw them. Here Yāska (Ni. 7-29) says: when all the gods worthy of sacrifice in heaven placed him, Sūrya, the son of Aditi, and when the pair of moving ones appeared, always going together, Uṣas and Āditya. Why a pair? He derives मिथुनौ (*mithunau*) from roots meaning to resort to, to lead and to win, because the two, resorting to each other, lead or win each other; human pairs too delight in each other, or win each other, from this very root **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यदेत् (*yadet*)—when
- आदितेयं (*āditeyaṃ*)—the son of Aditi
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—Agni
- यज्ञियासः (*yajñiyāsaḥ*)—worthy of sacrifice
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the world of heaven
- अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*)—established
- यदा (*yadā*)—and when
- चरिष्टू (*cariṣṭū*)—these two, the sun and Vaiśvānara Agni, who are given to moving about
- मिथुना (*mithunā*)—joined together as one
- आदित् (*ādit*)—immediately thereafter
- विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—all the worlds
- प्रापश्यन् (*prāpaśyan*)—saw these two

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the gods worthy of sacrifice established in the world of heaven the sun, the son of Aditi, and Agni, and when these two, the sun and Agni, who are given to moving about, joined together as a pair, immediately thereafter all the worlds saw these two.

##### English translation
When the adorable gods placed him and Surya, the son of Aditi, in heaven; when the swift-moving pair (Agni and Vishwanar) appeared, then all beings beheld them,

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The gods, Indra and the others, made the Vaiśvānara Agni, who is beneficial to all men, the indicator of the days, for the sake of the whole world. He is the one who spreads out the shining dawns in manifold ways. Moreover, this same Agni, moving along, drives away the darkness, the gloom, with his radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—the Vaiśvānara Agni who

- आ ततान (*ā tatāna*)—causes to spread out, such a one
- वैश्वानरं अग्निं (*vaiśvānaraṃ agniṃ*)—Agni who has the form of Vaiśvānara
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods, Indra and the others
- विश्वस्मै भुवनाय (*viśvasmai bhuvanāya*)—for the welfare of all the worlds
- अह्नां केतुं (*ahnāṃ ketuṃ*)—as the indicator of the days
- अकृण्वन् (*akṛṇvan*)—made (this same Agni)
- यन् (*yan*)—moving everywhere
- तमः (*tamaḥ*)—the darkness
- अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)—with his own radiance
- अपो ऊर्णोति (*apo ūrṇoti*)—destroys

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The gods, Indra and the others, made this Agni, who has the form of Vaiśvānara and who caused the shining dawns to spread out by his lustre, the indicator of the days, for the welfare of all the worlds as well. This same Agni, moving everywhere, destroys the darkness with his radiance.

##### English translation
The gods made Agni Vaishwanara, the indicator of days, for the sake of the whole world, who stretched out the radiant dawns, and as he moves along scatters the darkness with his light.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wise ones, the gods who are worthy of sacrifice or who accomplish the sacrifice, brought forth the Vaiśvānara Agni, who is free from old age or cannot be harmed, who is benevolent to all men and has the nature of the sun. This Agni, brought forth by the gods, overcame the nakṣatra, that is Kṛttikā and the rest, the ancient, the moving one. The root yakṣ here has the sense of worship, as is seen in the usage prayakṣam and the like (Ṛ. 2.5-1). He is the overseer, the manifest lord, of the worshipful god (यक्षस्य (*yakṣasya*)), the grown, the great and mighty. He injured it, that is, he overcame it with his splendour.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्जियासः (*yajjiyāsaḥ*)—worthy of sacrifice

- जुर्यं (*juryaṃ*)—the one free from decay

- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- अजनयन् (*ajanayan*)—brought forth (this same Agni)
- प्रत्नं (*pratnaṃ*)—the ancient
- चरिष्णु (*cariṣṇu*)—the one of the nature of movement
- यक्षस्य (*yakṣasya*)—of the worshipful host of gods
- अध्यक्षं (*adhyakṣaṃ*)—the chief (the lord)
- तविषं (*taviṣaṃ*)—the grown
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—the one possessed of greatness
- नक्षत्रं (*nakṣatraṃ*)—the host of stars
- अभिनत् (*abhinat*)—destroyed by his own splendour **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wise gods, worthy of sacrifice, brought forth Agni, who is free from decay and is called Vaiśvānara. This same Agni destroyed by his splendour the host of stars, the ancient, the moving, the chief (lord) of the worshipful host of gods, the grown, the great.

##### English translation
The wise and adorable gods engendered the imperishable Agni Vaishwanara ; he overcame (with his light) the ancient swift-moving Nakshatra, the overseer of the adorable (deity), mighty and great.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the Pitṛs and the gods, and also of mortals, that is, men, I have heard two paths, called the way of the gods and the way of the Pitṛs. The whole of this world which is between the father, heaven, who is a father by being the protector, and the mother, earth, who is a mother by being the supporter, being purified by Agni, goes moving to the world of the gods and the world of the Pitṛs, and proceeds by those two paths, the way of the gods and the way of the Pitṛs. Those two paths were shown by the Blessed One (Bha. Gī. 8-24, 25, 26) **NOTE**: fire, light, day, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern course; going there, the men who know Brahman reach Brahman. Smoke, night, likewise the dark fortnight, the six months of the southern course; going there the yogi attains the lunar light and returns. These bright and dark paths are held to be the eternal two of the world; by the one he goes to non-return, by the other he returns again. Knowing these two paths, O Pārtha, no yogi is deluded.

- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—for the gods

- मर्त्यानां (*martyānāṃ*)—for men
- द्वे स्रुती (*dve srutī*)—that there are two paths, called the way of the gods and the way of the Pitṛs
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—

- अंतरा (*aṃtarā*)—which is between
- यत् इदं विश्वं (*yat idaṃ viśvaṃ*)—this whole world, which it is, that
- एजत् (*ejat*)—moving
- ताभ्यां (*tābhyāṃ*)—only between these two paths
- सं एति (*saṃ eti*)—moves about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I have heard that for the Pitṛs, for the gods and also for men there are two paths, called the way of the gods and the way of the Pitṛs. This whole world, which lies between the world of heaven and the world of earth, moving, goes about only on these two paths.

##### English translation
I have heard that there are two paths for Pitris, gods and mortals ; all this universe which is between the paternal (heaven) and the maternal (earth) proceeds on its way by these two (paths).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Upaniṣads the words devayāna and pitṛyāna have a technical meaning. But in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā the word devayāna simply means the path along which the gods travel. Only in some places is the spiritual import described in the Upaniṣads also indicated.

By the words devayāna and pitṛyāna in the Upaniṣads two paths are well known, along which, after the death of a man, when his body has become ashes, the eternal ātman travels. Of the paths along which one goes to enjoy the fruit of good works, one is devayāna and the other pitṛyāna. One is the path of the gods; the other is the path of the Pitṛs. Those who know the Pañcāgni-vidyā and place their faith in truth alone set out on the path of the gods and reach the Supreme Brahman. After their death the ātman enters the flame, and through it the day, the bright fortnight, the northern course, the year, the sun and the lightning, and through them, with the help of the non-human person, obtains the Supreme Brahman. This matter is described in the Upaniṣads in this way:

ते य एवमेतद्विद्युरेचामि अरण्ये श्रद्धां सत्यमुपासते तेऽर्चिरभिसंभवंत्यर्चिषोऽहरह्न आपूर्यमाणपक्षमापूर्यमाणपक्षाद्यान्पण्हासान्नुदज्जादित्य एति मासेभ्यो देवलोकं देवलोकादादित्यमादित्याद्वैद्युतं तान्‌वैद्युतान्पुरुषो मानस एत्य ब्रह्मलोकान्नमयति (*te ya evametadvidyurecāmi araṇye śraddhāṃ satyamupāsate te 'rcirabhisaṃbhavaṃtyarciṣo 'harahna āpūryamāṇapakṣamāpūryamāṇapakṣādyānpaṇhāsānnudajjāditya eti māsebhyo devalokaṃ devalokādādityamādityādvaidyutaṃ tānvaidyutānpuruṣo mānasa etya brahmalokānnamayati*)

### Printed p. 562

तेषु ब्रह्मलोकेषु पराः परावशो वसंति तेषां न पुनरावर्तितिः ॥ (*teṣu brahmalokeṣu parāḥ parāvaśo vasaṃti teṣāṃ na punarāvartitiḥ ‖*)

(Bṛ. U. 2-6-12)

Having thus told that those who have reached the world of Brahman have no return, it then describes the nature of the pitṛyāna and the order of that path.

अथ ये यज्ञेन दानेन तपसा लोकाञ्चयंति ते धूममभिसंभवंति धूमाद्रात्रिं रात्रेरपक्षीयमाणपक्षमपक्षीयमाणपक्षाद्यान्नष्टा सान्दक्षिणादित्य एति मासेभ्यः पितृलोकं पितृलोकाच्चंद्रं ते चंद्रं प्राप्तान्नं भवंति तांस्तत्र देवा यथा सोमं राजानमाप्याय............ते पृथीवीं प्राप्तान्नं भवंति ते पुनः पुरुषाग्नौ हूयंते..................एवमेवानुपरिवर्तंते ॥ (*atha ye yajñena dānena tapasā lokāñcayaṃti te dhūmamabhisaṃbhavaṃti dhūmādrātriṃ rātrerapakṣīyamāṇapakṣamapakṣīyamāṇapakṣādyānnaṣṭā sāndakṣiṇāditya eti māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokaṃ pitṛlokāccaṃdraṃ te caṃdraṃ prāptānnaṃ bhavaṃti tāṃstatra devā yathā somaṃ rājānamāpyāya............te pṛthīvīṃ prāptānnaṃ bhavaṃti te punaḥ puruṣāgnau hūyaṃte..................evamevānuparivartaṃte ‖*)

(Bṛ. U. 6-2-16)

Those who satisfy the world merely by sacrifice and by gifts and the like, that is, who without knowing the Pañcāgni-vidyā are devoted only to good works, travel after death by a different path. After the body has been burnt, the ātman unites with smoke, and then goes to the night, through it to the dark fortnight, through that to the southern course, then to the world of the Pitṛs and at last to the world of the moon. That is their final place. Having fully enjoyed in that world the fruits that correspond to their good works and having lived with the Pitṛs, as soon as the impression of their works is exhausted they return again to the earth by the same path of smoke. This is the nature of the devayāna and pitṛyāna described in the Upaniṣads.

What we have to consider in the present context is this: whether the whole import described in the Upaniṣads, as explained above, is fully indicated by the word devayāna used in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, or whether it means merely the physical path along which the gods travel. In the same way, what meaning the word pitṛyāna described in the Upaniṣads has must also be examined in the present context.

The word devayāna is used in all thirteen times in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. [1-72-7; 1-162-4: 1-18-3-6; 1-184-6; 4-37-1; 5-43-6; 7-38-8; 7-76-2; 10-18-1; 11 51-2; 10-51-5; 10.98-11; 10-181-3.] **NOTE** In all these contexts Sāyaṇa has given mainly only two meanings. According to his explanation, it means first the path along which the human sacrificers go with their oblations to approach the gods, and second the path along which the gods come to the earth to receive their oblations.

### Printed p. 563

The word pitṛyāna is used only once in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. The context in which it is used is this:

यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्टा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान । पंथामनु प्रविद्वान् पितृयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहि ॥ (*yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna | paṃthāmanu pravidvān pitṛyāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhi ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-2.7)

In this Ṛk it is prayed that Agni, who was kindled by heaven and earth, by the waters, by the creator and by Tvaṣṭṛ, and who has fully known the nature of the pitṛyāṇa, shine forth as soon as he is kindled. For this word, which stands in the third pāda of the Ṛk, the explanation of Sāyaṇa is पितृयाणं पितरो येन मार्गेण गच्छंति तं (*pitṛyāṇaṃ pitaro yena mārgeṇa gacchaṃti taṃ*): the path along which the Pitṛs travel is the meaning. The English scholars also accept and explain this same meaning.

If devayāna is thus taken as the path along which the gods come for the oblation, and pitṛyāna as the path along which the Pitṛs travel, then, if it is asked how the spiritual import described in the Upaniṣads can be possible in these contexts, the import of the Ṛks cited below must be considered, and it must be decided whether this idea is expressed by those mantras.

प्र मे पंथा देवयाना अदृश्रन्नमर्धंतो वसुभिरिष्कृतासः । अभूदु केतुरुषसः पुरस्तात्प्रतीच्यागादधि हर्मेभ्यः ॥ (*pra me paṃthā devayānā adṛśrannamardhaṃto vasubhiriṣkṛtāsaḥ | abhūdu keturuṣasaḥ purastātpratīcyāgādadhi harmebhyaḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-76.2)

को मा ददर्श कतमः स देवो यो मे तन्नो बहुधा पर्यपश्यत् । क्वाह मित्रावरुणा क्षियंत्यग्निर्विश्वाः समिधो देवयानीः ॥ ( (*ko mā dadarśa katamaḥ sa devo yo me tanno bahudhā paryapaśyat | kvāha mitrāvaruṇā kṣiyaṃtyagnirviśvāḥ samidho devayānīḥ ‖ (*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-51-2)

एहि मनुर्देवयुर्यज्ञकामोऽरंकृत्या तमसि क्षेप्यग्ने । सुगान्पथः कृणुहि देवयानान्वह हव्यानि सुमनस्यमानः ॥ (*ehi manurdevayuryajñakāmo 'raṃkṛtyā tamasi kṣepyagne | sugānpathaḥ kṛṇuhi devayānānvaha havyāni sumanasyamānaḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-51-5)

Of these Ṛks, the devayāna described in the first half of the first Ṛk has two attributes. First it is amardhantaḥ (not injuring), and second vasubhiḥ iṣkṛtāsaḥ (prepared by splendours). By these two attributes the nature of the devayāna is described. These attributes tell that it is a path that is not injured and that it is full of splendour. In the second half of the second mantra, when Agni questions Mitra and Varuṇa, who among the gods has known the endless form of Agni, which is full of splendour and which has the form of the devayāna

### Printed p. 564

he asks; and in the third mantra Agni is prayed to make the devayāna, which carries the oblation to the gods, full of splendour.

On these grounds the devayāna described in the Ṛk-saṃhitā is not merely a path for travelling. It may be said to be a path that is also fit to be travelled. The path of the Pitṛs is that which lacks these qualities and is opposed to it; this is known from the sentences of the Upaniṣads. Another question is whether the point stated in the Upaniṣads, that the ātman which has obtained fitness to travel by this devayāna does not, after reaching the world of Brahman, undergo return and come back to the earth, is also indicated in the sentences of the Ṛk-saṃhitā. That point can be understood clearly from the descriptions in the mantras cited below.

परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पंथां यस्ते स्व इततो देवयानात् । चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान् ॥ (*paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi paṃthāṃ yaste sva itato devayānāt | cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-18-1)

एतान्यग्ने नवतिं सहस्रा सं प्र यच्छ वृष्ण इंद्राय भागं । विद्वान् पथ ऋतुशो देवयानानप्यौलानं दिवि देवेषु धेहि ॥ (*etānyagne navatiṃ sahasrā saṃ pra yaccha vṛṣṇa iṃdrāya bhāgaṃ | vidvān patha ṛtuśo devayānānapyaulānaṃ divi deveṣu dhehi ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-11)

विद्वा अग्ने वयुनानि क्षितीनां न्यानुषक्भुरुधो जीवसे धाः । अंतर्विद्वा अध्वनो देवयानानतंद्रो दूतो अभवो हविर्वाट् ॥ (*vidvā agne vayunāni kṣitīnāṃ nyānuṣakbhurudho jīvase dhāḥ | aṃtarvidvā adhvano devayānānataṃdro dūto abhavo havirvāṭ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-7)

Of these mantras, the first is a prayer addressed to Death. It is clear here that the path of Death is one thing and the path of devayāna another. By the sentence यः त्वे स्वः देवयानात् इतरः (*yaḥ tve svaḥ devayānāt itaraḥ*) it is described that the path of Death is different from devayāna. Therefore, since devayāna and Death are opposed, the meaning is suggested that all who travel by devayāna become free from death and reach the eternal world of Brahman.

In the second mantra, addressing the Agni who knows the nature of devayāna, it is prayed that the man called Aulāna Śantanu be brought to the gods. The idea described elsewhere, that after death the ātman, entering within the flame of Agni, reaches the world of the gods, is indicated here. In the third mantra too this same point is clearly indicated.

On these grounds it is understood that devayāna and pitṛyāṇa are different paths that carry the ātman after death. If these ideas are to be understood still more clearly, they can be understood in the respective contexts when the import of the words गातु (*gātu*),

### Printed p. 565

रजस् (*rajas*) and स्रुती (*srutī*) is explained. For example:

द्वे स्तुती अशृणवं पित्यणामहु देवनामुत मर्त्यानां । ताभ्यामिदं विश्वमेजत्समेति यदंतरा पितरं मातरं च ॥ (*dve stutī aśṛṇavaṃ pityaṇāmahu devanāmuta martyānāṃ | tābhyāmidaṃ viśvamejatsameti yadaṃtarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-15)

आ कृष्णेण रजसा वर्तमानो निवेशयन्नमृतं मर्त्यं च । हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् ॥ (*ā kṛṣṇeṇa rajasā vartamāno niveśayannamṛtaṃ martyaṃ ca | hiraṇyayena savitā rathenā devo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35.-2)

In mantras of this kind the difference between the two paths is shown. This matter will be explained still more clearly later, in the respective contexts. This same devayāna is also called in the Upaniṣads the path beginning with light. That for the virtuous who have reached the world of Brahman by this path after death there is no return, as is described in the sentences of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad cited above, this point is stated in other Upaniṣads also.

तत्पुरुषोऽमानवः स एनाब्रह्म गमयत्येष देवपथो ब्रह्मपथ एतेन प्रतिपद्यमाना इमं मानवमावर्तं नावर्तंते ॥ (*tatpuruṣo 'mānavaḥ sa enābrahma gamayatyeṣa devapatho brahmapatha etena pratipadyamānā imaṃ mānavamāvartaṃ nāvartaṃte ‖*)

(Chā. U. 4-15-5)

सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयांति यत्रामृतः सः पुरुषोऽह्यव्ययात्मा ॥ (*sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayāṃti yatrāmṛtaḥ saḥ puruṣo 'hyavyayātmā ‖*)

(Mu. U. 2-11) **NOTE**

Sentences of this kind, describing the door of the sun, praise the greatness of devayāna.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> समाची संगते द्वे द्यावापृथिव्यौ चरंतं गच्छंतं शीर्षतः शिरसो
> जातमुत्पन्नं । तथा च निगमांतरं । उत मन्येऽहमेनमनयोर्हि शिरस्तोऽयं
> प्रातर्जायत इति । यद्वा । सर्वशिरोभूतादादित्याज्ञातमित्यर्थः । मनसा ।
> मन्यतिरर्चतिकर्मा । अर्चनीयया स्तुत्या विमृष्टं शोधितं संस्कृतमग्निं
> बिभृतः । धारयतः । सोऽप्रयुच्छन्नप्रमाद्यंस्तरणिः क्षिप्रकारी भ्राजमानो दीप्यमानोऽग्निर्विश्वानि भुवनानि प्रत्यज्जभिमुखस्थौ । तिष्ठति । तथा च श्रूयते ।
> तस्मात्सर्व एव मन्यंते मां प्रत्युदगादिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two, heaven and earth, joined together, bear Agni, who moves and is born from the head. Another Nigama passage says: "I think this one is born from the head of these two, in the morning." Or else the sense is that he is born from the Āditya, who is the head of all. The word मनसा (*manasā*) comes from the root meaning worship: Agni is purified and refined by praise that is worthy of worship. Heaven and earth bear him. That Agni, unremitting, not neglectful, swift in action, shining, stands facing all the worlds. And so it is heard: "therefore all think that he has risen towards me."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- समीची (*samīcī*)—joined together
- द्वे (*dve*)—heaven and earth
- चरंतं (*caraṃtaṃ*)—him whose nature is movement
- शीर्षतः (*śīrṣataḥ*)—from the head
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—born
- मनसा (*manasā*)—by praise
- विमृष्टं (*vimṛṣṭaṃ*)—and refined, Agni
- विभृतः (*vibhṛtaḥ*)—bear
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni
- अप्रयुच्छन् (*aprayucchan*)—without sloth
- तरणिः (*taraṇiḥ*)—swift-going
- भ्राजमानः (*bhrājamānaḥ*)—shining
- विश्वा भुवनानि (*viśvā bhuvanāni*)—to all the worlds
- प्रत्यज् (*pratyaj*)—facing
- तस्थौ (*tasthau*)—has been established

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Heaven and earth, in mutual union, bear Agni, who is of the nature of movement, born from the head and refined by praise. That same Agni, without sloth in his work, swift-going and shining, is established facing all the worlds.

##### English translation
The associated two (heaven and earth) support (Agni) moving, born from the head, sanctified by praise; diligent, rapid, radiant, he appears in the presence of all beings.

> सधमादं यज्ञमा शेकुः । कर्तुं शक्नुवंति । तथा यज्ञं नक्षंत अश्नुवतेऽनुतिष्ठंति

> विवादस्य निर्णयरूपं वाक्यं वि वोचत् । ब्रवीति । माध्यमिकमिममग्निं ब्रवीति ॥
> तथा च यास्कः । यत्र विवदेते देव्या होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः कतरो
> नौ यज्ञे भूयो वेदेत्याशक्नुवंति तत्सहमदनं समानख्याना ऋत्विजस्तेषां
> यज्ञं समश्नुवानानां को न इदं विनक्ष्यति । नि. ७-३० । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the terrestrial Agni, the divine hotṛ, who is the lower, and the one in the middle, Vāyu, who is the upper, both dispute, that is, quarrel, as to which of the two of us, the leaders of the sacrifice, knows the sacrifice more; then the friends, the priests of the same renown, are able to accomplish the sacrifice that is a common delight, and they attain it and carry it out. Among these learned ones who attain the sacrifice, which learned performer will pronounce the sentence that settles this dispute? He declares it of this Agni of the middle region. Yāska says accordingly (Ni. 7-30): where the two divine hotṛs dispute, this Agni and that middle one, which of the two of us knows more in the sacrifice; the priests of the same renown are able to accomplish that common delight; which of those who attain the sacrifice will declare this to us?

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यज्ञन्नोः (*yajñannoḥ*)—of the two leaders of the sacrifice
- नौ (*nau*)—among us
- कतरः (*kataraḥ*)—who
- वि वेद (*vi veda*)—is the greater knower, thus
- यत्र (*yatra*)—when
- अवरः (*avaraḥ*)—the terrestrial Agni
- परश्च (*paraśca*)—and Vāyu of the middle region
- वदेते (*vadete*)—speak in the form of a question, then
- सखायः (*sakhāyaḥ*)—their friends, the priests
- सधमादं (*sadhamādaṃ*)—the sacrifice
- आ शेकुः (*ā śekuḥ*)—are able to carry out
- यज्ञं नक्षंत (*yajñaṃ nakṣaṃta*)—also carry out the sacrifice (at the time of this sacrifice)
- कः (*kaḥ*)—who
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—the settlement of this dispute
- विवोचत् (*vivocat*)—can declare, having known it

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When a dispute arose between the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the middle region in the form of Vāyu, "Among us, the leaders of the sacrifice, who is the greater knower?", his friends, the priests, carry out the sacrifice with ability. At the time of this sacrifice, who can know and declare the settlement of this dispute?

##### English translation
When the lower and upper (fire) disputed " which of us twin leaders of sacrifice knows the work best ? " then the friends (the priests) were

### Printed p. 568

competent (to offer) sacrifice, they came to the sacrifice; who declares this ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

यत्र विवदेते देव्यौ होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः कतरो नौ यज्ञे भूयो वेदेत्याशक्नुवंति सत्सहमदनं समानख्याना ऋत्विजस्तेषां यज्ञं समश्नुवानानां को न इदं विवक्ष्यतीति ॥ (*yatra vivadete devyau hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ kataro nau yajñe bhūyo vedetyāśaknuvaṃti satsahamadanaṃ samānakhyānā ṛtvijasteṣāṃ yajñaṃ samaśnuvānānāṃ ko na idaṃ vivakṣyatīti ‖*)

(Ni. 7-30)

The seer has praised with this Ṛk, accepting this Vaiśvānara Agni as the terrestrial Agni. Of the lower and the upper fires who know the matter of the sacrifice, who knows more? Who is capable of deciding and settling this matter?

दैवौ होतारौ (*daivau hotārau*) means hotṛs who are of the nature of deities, the Agni named Hotṛ who invokes the gods in the sacrifice. Since the word होतारौ (*hotārau*) is here in the dual, the two deities are the terrestrial Agni (the sacrificial fire) established on the earth, and Vāyu or the lightning fire that stands in the middle region. Since both are only different forms of Agni, they are addressed by the dual word होतारौ (*hotārau*). अवरः परश्च (*avaraḥ paraśca*) means the lower and the upper. The lower is to be understood as the terrestrial Agni in the region of the earth, and परः (*paraḥ*) as the Agni (lightning) in the region of the middle. Which of these two has the greater understanding? Among the priests who take equal shares, that is the chief parts, in rites such as the sacrifice and who know the matter of the sacrifice well, which priest is capable of deciding this matter?

दैव्या होतारा—देवसंबंधिनौ होतारौ। आयं च मध्यमस्थानश्च इत्युभौ (*daivyā hotārā—devasaṃbaṃdhinau hotārau| āyaṃ ca madhyamasthānaśca ityubhau*) **NOTE** Sāyaṇa has explained this as the two forms of Agni, the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere, both related to the gods and both hotṛs. Some modern scholars have given different meanings and have shown differences of opinion among themselves. The scholar Geldner has explained them as the hotṛ who is the sacrificer and his Agni, Haug as the hotṛ and the adhvaryu, Oldenberg as the hotṛ and his assistant Maitrāvaruṇa. None of these is reasonable.

That the chief duty of these hotṛs is to perform the sacrifice is said in the Ṛks 1-13-8 and 1-188-7 by यज्ञं नो यक्षतामिमं (*yajñaṃ no yakṣatāmimaṃ*) and in the Ṛk 2-3-7 by देवान्यजंतावृतुथा (*devānyajaṃtāvṛtuthā*). This statement of duty must apply to the human hotṛ, and Agni is addressed figuratively.

### Printed p. 569

The explanation of Yāska concerning the word दैव होतारा (*daiva hotārā*) is:

दैन्व्या होतारा दैव्या होतारावयं चाग्निरसौ च मध्यमः (*dainvyā hotārā daivyā hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasau ca madhyamaḥ*)

That is, this word indicates Agni. Since Agni invokes the gods, Agni is the mediator between the gods and men; an example has been given on this matter.

दैन्व्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै । प्रचोदयंता विधथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशंता ॥ (*dainvyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai | pracodayaṃtā vidhatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśaṃtā ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-7)

The commentary composed by Durgācārya on this is:

यावेत् दैवौ होतारौ । देवेषु भवौ देव्यौ देवानेव देव्यौ । स्वार्थे एव तद्धितः । मनुष्यहोतारौ अपेक्ष्य । दैवौ होतारौ होतृमैत्तावरुणौ इति विशेषणं। होतारा होतारौ आह्वातारौ देवानां वाय्वग्नी। प्रथमा प्रथमौ मुख्यौ मनुष्यहोतारावपेक्ष्य । सुवाचा । सुवाचौ । प्रशस्तवाचौ । सुस्तुतौ । मिमाना यज्ञं यज्ञनिर्मातारौ नित्यं। मनुषः मनुष्यस्य यजध्यै यजनाय । प्रचोदयंता प्रचोदयमानौ । विदधेषु यज्ञेषु । कारू कर्तारौ । (*yāvet daivau hotārau | deveṣu bhavau devyau devāneva devyau | svārthe eva taddhitaḥ | manuṣyahotārau apekṣya | daivau hotārau hotṛmaittāvaruṇau iti viśeṣaṇaṃ| hotārā hotārau āhvātārau devānāṃ vāyvagnī| prathamā prathamau mukhyau manuṣyahotārāvapekṣya | suvācā | suvācau | praśastavācau | sustutau | mimānā yajñaṃ yajñanirmātārau nityaṃ| manuṣaḥ manuṣyasya yajadhyai yajanāya | pracodayaṃtā pracodayamānau | vidadheṣu yajñeṣu | kārū kartārau |*) इत्यादि (*ityādi*)

The main meaning of this is: for the gods, Agni and Vāyu are well known as the hotṛs, and for men the priests called Hotṛ and Maitrāvaruṇa are the hotṛs. Since Agni, or Agni and Vāyu, standing between the gods and men, establish a connection between them, Agni is said to be the middle one. The name of the deities दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) is read, apart from the Āprī hymns, in only two Ṛks:

त्वष्टारं वायुमृभवो य ओहते दैव्या होतारा उषसं स्वस्तये । (*tvaṣṭāraṃ vāyumṛbhavo ya ohate daivyā hotārā uṣasaṃ svastaye |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-10)

दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा पुरोहित ऋतस्य पंथामन्वेमि साधुया । (*daivyā hotārā prathamā purohita ṛtasya paṃthāmanvemi sādhuyā |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66-13)

In the Ṛk 7-2-7 they are called जातावेदसा (*jātāvedasā*) and in the Ṛk 10-70-7 पुरोहितौ (*purohitau*). And since the words मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै (*mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai*), यज्ञेषु मानुषेसु कारू (*yajñeṣu mānuṣesu kārū*) and प्रचोदयंता विदथेषु कारू (*pracodayaṃtā vidatheṣu kārū*) in the Ṛks mentioned above say that these deities conduct the sacrifices that men perform, it is natural that they are called purohitas.

### Printed p. 570

Where among the gods the hotṛs are Agni and Vāyu, among men the Hotṛ and his assistant priest Maitrāvaruṇa are called the hotṛs. This Maitrāvaruṇa commands the other priests by the Praiṣa mantras to perform their respective acts. In the Yajurveda (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1) it is said: मैत्तावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्भो वाचं विभजति (*maittāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigbho vācaṃ vibhajati*).

Thus, although some attributes are common to the two hotṛs and indicate the duty of the human hotṛ, there are other attributes which, though they too are common to both, describe only the duties of Agni, the divine hotṛ. For example:

दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा नृंजे सप्त पृक्षासः स्वधया मदंति । यतं शंसंत ऋतमित्त आहुरनु व्रतं व्रतपा दीध्यानाः ॥ (*daivyā hotārā prathamā nṛṃje sapta pṛkṣāsaḥ svadhayā madaṃti | yataṃ śaṃsaṃta ṛtamitta āhuranu vrataṃ vratapā dīdhyānāḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-4-7)

In this Ṛk there is no doubt that the attribute प्रथमा (*prathamā*) refers only to Agni, the divine hotṛ. In 1-13-4 होता मनुर्हितः (*hotā manurhitaḥ*) is an attribute of Agni. The precise difference that holds between these two hotṛs is stated in the Praiṣa-sūkta in this way:

होता यक्षद्वैव्या होतारा मंद्रा पोतारा कवी प्रचेतसा । स्विष्टमद्यान्यः करदिषा स्वभिगूर्तमन्य ऊर्जा सतवसेमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धत्तां वीतामाज्यस्य होतरज ॥ (*hotā yakṣadvaivyā hotārā maṃdrā potārā kavī pracetasā | sviṣṭamadyānyaḥ karadiṣā svabhigūrtamanya ūrjā satavasemaṃ yajñaṃ divi deveṣu dhattāṃ vītāmājyasya hotaraja ‖*)

(Śrī. Brā. 3 6-2-2) **NOTE**

In this sentence it is indicated that one hotṛ should make the sacrifice acceptable by the oblation in the form of food, and the other should establish this sacrifice among the gods in heaven. This exchange of functions shows the difference between the human hotṛ and Agni, the divine hotṛ. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

दैव्या होतार यजति प्राणापान् वैद्यैवा, होतारा प्राणापानावेव तत्णाति प्राणापान् यजमाने दधाति । (*daivyā hotāra yajati prāṇāpān vaidyaivā, hotārā prāṇāpānāveva tatṇāti prāṇāpān yajamāne dadhāti |*)

(Ai. Brā. 2-4)

having stated the identity of these hotṛs with prāṇa and apāna, it says that he who recites this mantra secures for the sacrificer a good state of prāṇa and apāna. In the Nirukta:

दैव्या होतारा दैव्या होतारावयं चाग्निरस्च मध्यमः । (*daivyā hotārā daivyā hotārāvayaṃ cāgnirasca madhyamaḥ |*)

(Ni. 8-12)

it is said, by the supporting passages that bear out Sāyaṇa's meaning, that they are the terrestrial Agni and the Agni of the atmosphere. The Bṛhaddevatā also, approving this same meaning,

### Printed p. 571

दैन्व्याविति तु होतारावग्नी पार्थिवमध्यमौ । दिव्यादग्निर्हि जज्ञाते दैप्सौ तेनेह जन्मना ॥ (*dainvyāviti tu hotārāvagnī pārthivamadhyamau | divyādagnirhi jajñāte daipsau teneha janmanā ‖*)

(Bṛ. De. 3.11)

says that these two hotṛs are the terrestrial and the middle (atmospheric) fires.

> नोप॒स्पिजं॑ वः पितरो वदामि पृ॒च्छामि॑ वः कवयो वि॒द्मने॒  
> कं ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कति । अग्नियः । कति । सूर्यासः । कति । उषसः । कति । ऊं इति । स्वित् । आपः ।  
> न । उपस्पिजं । वः । पितरः । वदामि । पृच्छामि । वः । कवयः । विद्मने । कं ॥१८।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एवं विवदमानावग्निवायू पित्थन्प्रश्नमेयितुः । तत्र मध्यमस्तान्पृच्छति ।
> कत्यग्नयः । अग्नयः कति कतिसंख्याकाः । सूर्यासः सूर्याश्च कतिसंख्याकाः ।
> उषास उषसत्व कतिसंख्याकाः । आपश्च कति । उ इति पूरणः । स्विच्छब्दोऽत्र
> विचारणार्थः । हे पितरः वो युष्माकमुपस्पिजं । उपस्पिजमिति स्पर्धायुक्तं
> वचनमुच्यते । पूर्वोक्तं प्रश्नवचनमेतन्न वदामि किंतर्ह्यहमजानन् हे
> कवयो मेधाविनः युष्मान्विद्मने विज्ञानाय कं सुखं स्वरूपपर्यालोचनक्लेशमंतरेण पृच्छामि । अत्रोत्रराणि वालखिल्वसंहितायां दर्शितानि । एक
> एवाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूर्यो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः । एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं
> वि भात्येकं वा इदं वि बभूव सर्वं । ऋ. ८-५८.२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The fires Agni and Vāyu, disputing thus, ask the Pitṛs a question **NOTE**. Of these, the one in the middle region asks them: how many are the fires, how many are the suns, how many the dawns, and how many the waters? The word उ (*u*) is a filler, and the word स्वित् (*svit*) here has the sense of inquiry. "O fathers, I do not speak to you what is spoken in rivalry", for उपस्पिजं (*upaspijaṃ*) is said of speech joined with rivalry; I do not speak the question stated before in that way. Rather, O wise ones, being ignorant, I ask you for knowledge, for ease, without the trouble of reflecting on the nature of the matter. The answers here are shown in the Vālakhilya-saṃhitā: Agni is one, kindled in many ways; the sun is one, spread out over the whole world; Uṣas is one, shining over all this; that which is one has become all this (Ṛ. 8-58.2).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- कति अग्नयः (*kati agnayaḥ*)—how many are the fires
- कति सूर्यासः (*kati sūryāsaḥ*)—how many are the suns
- कति उषसः (*kati uṣasaḥ*)—how many are the dawns
- कति स्विदाहः (*kati svidāhaḥ*)—how many are the deities of the waters **NOTE**
- पितरः (*pitaraḥ*)—O fathers
- वः (*vaḥ*)—with you
- उपस्पिजं (*upaspijaṃ*)—with the intention of rivalry
- न वदामि (*na vadāmi*)—I do not

### Printed p. 572

  speak
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—O wise ones
- विद्मने (*vidmane*)—only for the gaining of knowledge
- कं पृच्छामि (*kaṃ pṛcchāmi*)—I put an easy question

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O fathers, how many are the fires? How many are the suns? How many are the dawns? How many are the deities of the waters? I do not speak with you with the intention of rivalry. O wise ones, I ask this question easily, only for the gaining of knowledge.

##### English translation
How many fires are there, how many suns, how many dawns, how many waters? I address you, O Pitris, not in rivalry, I ask you, sages, in order to know (the truth).
