Vṛtrāsura is of a wicked nature. His nature is known to no one. He has no good understanding. It is his nature always to lie obstructing the waters. It is described that Indra slew such a base-natured Vṛtra with his thunderbolt on the day of the full moon. In this matter the commentator cites a passage of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā and states that it says Indra slew Vṛtra on the full-moon day. Since all the seers have praised Indra's slaying of Vṛtra, it is necessary to give here a detailed account of that slaying. Therefore we set out here the mantra portion of the Yajurveda that gives those details, together with its meaning:

त्वष्टा हतपुत्रो वींद्रग्ं सोममाहरत्तस्मिन्निंद्र उपहवमैच्छत तं नोपाह्वयत पुत्रं मेवधीरिति स यज्ञवेशसं कृत्वा प्रासहा सोममपिबत्तस्य यदत्यशिष्यश तत्त्वष्टाहवनीयमुप प्रावर्तयत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति यदवर्तयत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं यदब्रवीत्स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्वेति तस्मादस्येंद्रः शत्रुरभवत्स संभवन्नग्नीषोमावभि समभवत्स इषुमात्रमिसुमात्रं विष्णज्जवर्धत स इमान् लोकानवृणोद्यदिमान् लोकानवृणोत्तद्वृत्रस्य वृत्रत्वं तस्मादिंद्रोऽभिभेत् ॥ (*tvaṣṭā hataputro vīṃdragṃ somamāharattasminniṃdra upahavamaicchata taṃ nopāhvayata putraṃ mevadhīriti sa yajñaveśasaṃ kṛtvā prāsahā somamapibattasya yadatyaśiṣyaśa tattvaṣṭāhavanīyamupa prāvartayatsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti yadavartayattadvṛtrasya vṛtratvaṃ yadabravītsvāheṃdraśatrurvardhasveti tasmādasyeṃdraḥ śatrurabhavatsa saṃbhavannagnīṣomāvabhi samabhavatsa iṣumātramisumātraṃ viṣṇajjavardhata sa imān lokānavṛṇodyadimān lokānavṛṇottadvṛtrasya vṛtratvaṃ tasmādiṃdro 'bhibhet ‖*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 2 5.2-1)

In this anuvāka the details of Indra's slaying of Vṛtra are told. As the background to this story there is another episode. Although we explained it earlier, it is necessary to relate it here briefly as a preface to the following account. Formerly Tvaṣṭā Prajāpati had a son named Viśvarūpa. He was priest to the gods. Yet, since he was born of an Asura woman, he had a special partiality toward the Asuras. That being so, Indra feared that this Viśvarūpa, though he was our priest, being partial to the Asuras, might wait for his opportunity, help the Asuras, and plot so that the gods would have no kingdom at all. Therefore Indra killed him by a stratagem. This matter is stated here by the sentence त्वष्टा हतपुत्रः (*tvaṣṭā hataputraḥ*). Out of anger that his son had been killed, Tvaṣṭā, when he performed a sacrifice, performed it without inviting Indra to the sacrifice, leaving him out. He did not give him Soma to drink either. Indra, angered by that, came to his sacrifice, and not only obstructed the sacrifice but drank by force the Soma-juice that had been prepared for the sacrifice. Seeing this,

### Printed p. 634

Tvaṣṭā thought that he must take suitable revenge on Indra. He poured the Soma-juice left over after Indra's drinking into the āhavanīya fire and, praying to Agni with स्वाहेंद्रशत्रुर्वर्धस्व (*svāheṃdraśatrurvardhasva*), that is, "May a son be born who will conquer Indra and be an enemy to Indra," offered the remainder of the Soma as a homa in the fire. As he made the homa in this way, because of a change of accent in the mantra, instead of a son who would conquer Indra there came a son who would be conquered by Indra. This son was Vṛtra. This is the order of his origin. That when a change of accent occurs in reciting mantras in sacrifices and the like, harm comes to the sacrificer, is said:

दुष्टः शब्दः स्वरतो वर्णतो ना मिथ्याप्रयुक्तो न तमर्थमाह । स वाग्वज्रो यजमानं हिनस्ति यथेंद्रशत्रुः स्वरतोऽपराधात् ॥ (*duṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ svarato varṇato nā mithyāprayukto na tamarthamāha | sa vāgvajro yajamānaṃ hinasti yatheṃdraśatruḥ svarato 'parādhāt ‖*)

(Pāṇisīyatikṣya) **NOTE**

The great seer Pāṇini took this very mantra as his example and said this. Thus, through the change of accent in the mantra, there was born to Tvaṣṭā, instead of the son who would subdue Indra, as he wished, a son who would be overcome by Indra. **NOTE**

Even so, that Vṛtra kept growing by the oblation offered in the fire to the deities Agni and Soma. He grew every day by the measure of an arrow, **NOTE** and, becoming of huge form, pervaded all these worlds everywhere. Because he was of the nature of pervading all regions, Vṛtra received the name Vṛtra. The word vṛtra, formed from the root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*) that means "cover, close, pervade," indicates the meaningful name "one who pervades everything." Seeing this growth of Vṛtra, Indra feared.

स प्रजापतिमुपाधावङ्चतुर्मेऽजनीति तस्यॆ वज्रग्ं सिक्ता प्रायच्छदेतेन जहीति तेनाभ्यायत ॥ (*sa prajāpatimupādhāvaṅcaturme 'janīti tasyè vajragṃ siktā prāyacchadetena jahīti tenābhyāyata ‖*)

Then Indra went near Prajāpati and prayed: "O Brahmā, an enemy has been born to me. How is he to be slain?" Prajāpati comforted Indra, telling him not to fear, made his thunderbolt sharp and gave it to him, saying "Slay your enemy with this weapon." Indra took it and came to Vṛtra.

तावब्रूतामग्नीषोमौ मा प्रहारावमंतः स्व इति मम वै युवग् स्थ इत्यब्रवीन्मामभ्येतमिति तौ भागधेयमैच्छेतां ताभ्यामेतमग्नीषोमायमेकादशकपालं पूर्णमासे प्रायचत्तावब्रूतामभि संदष्टौ वै स्वो न शक्नुव ऐतुमिति स इंद्रआत्मनः शीतरूरावजनयत्तच्छीतरूरयोर्जन्मय एवग्ं शीतरूरयोर्जन्म वेद नैनग्ं शीतरूरा हतस्ताभ्यामेनमभ्यनयत्तस्माज्जंजभ्यमानादग्नीषोमौ निरक्रामतां ॥ (*tāvabrūtāmagnīṣomau mā prahārāvamaṃtaḥ sva iti mama vai yuvag stha ityabravīnmāmabhyetamiti tau bhāgadheyamaicchetāṃ tābhyāmetamagnīṣomāyamekādaśakapālaṃ pūrṇamāse prāyacattāvabrūtāmabhi saṃdaṣṭau vai svo na śaknuva aitumiti sa iṃdraātmanaḥ śītarūrāvajanayattacchītarūrayorjanmaya evagṃ śītarūrayorjanma veda nainagṃ śītarūrā hatastābhyāmenamabhyanayattasmājjaṃjabhyamānādagnīṣomau nirakrāmatāṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 635

Thereafter, when Indra was ready to strike Vṛtra with his weapon, Agni and Soma stopped Indra, saying "Do not strike." "O Indra, do not strike Vṛtra now. We, the deities Agni and Soma, are dwelling in this Vṛtra's mouth," they said. Indra said: "O Agni and Soma, you are our own people. So leave Vṛtra's body and come to me. After that I shall slay Vṛtra." Hearing that, the deities Agni and Soma said: "O Indra, if we do as you say, what favour will you do us? If you arrange a share in the sacrifice for us also, we shall do as you say." Indra agreed and arranged for them, in the full-moon sacrifice, a share of the oblation of the offering called एकादश कपाल (*ekādaśa kapāla*). **NOTE** Then, although Agni and Soma had thus obtained the boon they wished for, they said to Indra: "O Indra, we cannot come out from Vṛtra's mouth now. We are caught tightly between Vṛtra's teeth. Unless he opens his mouth we cannot come out." Then Indra thought of a means. From his body he created shivering fever and the great heat arising from it. This was the first time that cold-fever afflicted people in the world. The man who knows this order of origin of the cold-fever is not troubled by this cold-fever. Then Indra took the cold and fever that he had created, and made them enter the body of Vṛtrāsura. Then Vṛtrāsura, shivering with cold and exhausted by the heat of the fever, opened his mouth wide to sigh. At once the deities Agni and Soma came out of his mouth.

प्राणापानौ ना एनं तदजहितां प्राणो वै दक्षोपानः क्रतुस्तस्माज्जंजभ्यमानो ब्रूयान्मयि दक्षक्रकू इति प्राणापानावेवात्मन्धत्ते सर्वमायुरेति । (*prāṇāpānau nā enaṃ tadajahitāṃ prāṇo vai dakṣopānaḥ kratustasmājjaṃjabhyamāno brūyānmayi dakṣakrakū iti prāṇāpānāvevātmandhatte sarvamāyureti |*)

Thereafter the airs called prāṇa and apāna left that Vṛtra; that is, they left his body. The word prāṇa has the meaning dakṣa, and the word apāna the meaning kratu. Dakṣa means skill in work and activities, intelligence. Kratu means bodily power for working, capacity. These two left that Vṛtra, who had opened his mouth. Therefore, while performing a sacrificial rite, if one makes a bodily movement or yawns and opens the mouth, the mantra मयि दक्षक्रतू (*mayi dakṣakratū*) must be uttered. **NOTE** If one does so, prāṇa and apāna do not leave the sacrificer but stay firm. Long life results as well.

स देवता वृत्रान्निर्हूय वार्त्र्घ्नग्ं हविः पूर्णमासे निरवपद् घ्नंति वा एनु पूर्णमास अमावास्यायां प्याययंति तस्माद्वार्त्र्घ्नी पूर्णमासेऽनूच्येते वृधन्वती अमावास्यायां ॥ (*sa devatā vṛtrānnirhūya vārtrghnagṃ haviḥ pūrṇamāse niravapad ghnaṃti vā enu pūrṇamāsa amāvāsyāyāṃ pyāyayaṃti tasmādvārtrghnī pūrṇamāse 'nūcyete vṛdhanvatī amāvāsyāyāṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 636

Then Indra called out from Vṛtrāsura's mouth all the deities Agni, Soma and the rest, and on the full-moon day prepared the oblation in the form of the offering of ājya-portions, the means of Vṛtra's slaying. In worldly practice too it is known to all that the enemy called darkness, which covers everything everywhere, is destroyed by the bright moonlight of the full moon. But on the new-moon day, since there is no moonlight, the enemy darkness (Vṛtra) then spreads and grows, covering everything. Therefore, for the slaying of Vṛtra, on the full-moon day, before the oblations called the agniṣomīya ājya-portions,

अग्निर्वृत्राणि जंघनद्दृविणस्युर्विपन्यया । समिद्धः शुक्र आहुतः । (*agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṃghanaddṛviṇasyurvipanyayā | samiddhaḥ śukra āhutaḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-34)

त्वं सोमासि सत्पतिस्त्वं राजोत वृत्रहा । त्वं भद्रो आसि क्रतुः ॥ (*tvaṃ somāsi satpatistvaṃ rājota vṛtrahā | tvaṃ bhadro āsi kratuḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.91-5)

these Ṛks are to be recited as puronuvākyā mantras. Since in both these Ṛks there are words indicating the slaying of Vṛtra, these Ṛks are called वार्त्र्घ्य (*vārtrghya*) Ṛks. For the slaying of Vṛtra took place on the full-moon day. Therefore it is fitting to make the homa on that day, reciting the Ṛks that relate to the slaying of Vṛtra. On the new-moon day darkness has grown. That is, Vṛtra, who pervades everything with darkness, prospers. Therefore on that day, Ṛks containing words formed from the root वृधु-वृद्धौ (*vṛdhu-vṛddhau*) that indicates growth,

अग्निः प्रश्नेन मस्मना शुंभमानस्तस्वं १ स्वां । कविर्विप्रेण वावृधे ॥ (*agniḥ praśnena masmanā śuṃbhamānastasvaṃ 1 svāṃ | kavirvipreṇa vāvṛdhe ‖*) **NOTE**

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-44-12)

सोम गीर्भिष्ट्वा वयं वर्धयामो वटोविदः । सुमृळीको न आ विश ॥ (*soma gīrbhiṣṭvā vayaṃ vardhayāmo vaṭovidaḥ | sumṛḷīko na ā viśa ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-91-1)

are to be recited. These Ṛks, which contain words indicating growth, are called वृधन्वती (*vṛdhanvatī*) Ṛks. They are to be recited on the new-moon day, which has grown with darkness.

तत्सग्गस्थाप्य वार्त्रघ्नग्ं हनिर्वज्रमादाय पुनरभ्यायत ते अब्रूतां द्यावापृथिवी मा प्रहारावयोर्वै श्रित इति ते अब्रूतं वरं वृणावहै नक्षत्रविहिताहमसानीत्यसावब्रवीच्चित्रविहिताहमितीयं शस्त्रान्नक्षत्रविहितासौ चित्रविहितेयं य एवं द्यावापृथिव्योर्वरं वेदैनं वरो गच्छति स आभ्यामेव प्रसूत इंद्रो वृत्रमहन् ॥ (*tatsaggasthāpya vārtraghnagṃ hanirvajramādāya punarabhyāyata te abrūtāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī mā prahārāvayorvai śrita iti te abrūtaṃ varaṃ vṛṇāvahai nakṣatravihitāhamasānītyasāvabravīccitravihitāhamitīyaṃ śastrānnakṣatravihitāsau citravihiteyaṃ ya evaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyorvaraṃ vedainaṃ varo gacchati sa ābhyāmeva prasūta iṃdro vṛtramahan ‖*)

### Printed p. 637

Then Indra, having fully performed the ājya-portion and the oblations that are the means of the slaying of Vṛtra, took the earlier thunderbolt in his hand and rushed toward Vṛtra with the aim of slaying him. Then Heaven and Earth (the earth and the atmosphere) stopped Indra: "O Indra, do not kill this Vṛtra. He abides pervading the whole region from earth to heaven. We cannot give up him who dwells depending on us." When Indra did not agree, Heaven and Earth again said to Indra: "O Indra, if we are to give room for the slaying of Vṛtra, you must grant the boon that we ask." Indra said: "So be it." Then the atmosphere (Dyau) asked as its boon that it should be adorned with stars. The earth asked that it should be furnished with manifold wonderful things such as men, animals, trees, mountains, rivers and seas. Indra gave the boons accordingly. The man who knows this order in which Heaven and Earth obtained their boons obtains the desired objects that he wishes for and is happy. Then Indra, having obtained the consent of Heaven and Earth, struck Vṛtra with the thunderbolt and slew him.

ते देवा वृत्रग्ं हत्वाग्नीषोमावब्रुवन् हव्यं नो वहतमिति तावब्रूतामपतेजसौ वै त्र्यौ वृत्रे वै त्वयोस्तेज इति तेऽब्रुवन् क इदमच्छैतीति गौरित्यब्रुवन्गौर्नाव सर्वस्य मित्रमिति साब्रवीद्वरं वृणै मय्येव सतोभयेन भुनजाध्वा इति तद्गौराहरत्तस्माद्गवि सतोभयेन भुंजत एतद्वा अग्नेस्तेजो यद्धृतमेतत्सोमस्य यत्पयोय एवमग्नीषोमयो स्तेजो वेद तेजस्वीव भवति ॥ (*te devā vṛtragṃ hatvāgnīṣomāvabruvan havyaṃ no vahatamiti tāvabrūtāmapatejasau vai tryau vṛtre vai tvayosteja iti te 'bruvan ka idamacchaitīti gaurityabruvangaurnāva sarvasya mitramiti sābravīdvaraṃ vṛṇai mayyeva satobhayena bhunajādhvā iti tadgaurāharattasmādgavi satobhayena bhuṃjata etadvā agnestejo yaddhṛtametatsomasya yatpayoya evamagnīṣomayo stejo veda tejasvīva bhavati ‖*)

After the slaying of Vṛtra, all the gods who were near Indra said to Agni and Soma: "O deities Agni and Soma, you have now returned from Vṛtra's mouth. From now on carry and offer to us the oblations that are offered in homa for us in sacrifices and the like." To this, Agni and Soma said to the gods: "O gods, we have been in Vṛtra's body for a long time and have been deprived of splendour by his teeth and jaws and the like; that is, our power has shrunk. Our power, or splendour, has all remained standing in Vṛtra." **NOTE** Then the gods deliberated among themselves how to bring back the splendour of Agni and Soma that was in Vṛtra's body, **NOTE** and decided that, since the cow harms no one and behaves with friendliness toward all, they would send her and have the splendour that was in Vṛtra brought. Then they called the cow and told her to bring the splendour that was in Vṛtra. She said: "So be it. But the splendour that I bring must always stay in me, in the form of milk and ghee. People must obtain them from me and perform meals and the like. In this way the boon

### Printed p. 638

is given to me, I shall bring it," said the cow. The gods said "So be it" and gave her the boon accordingly. Having obtained the boon, the cow brought that splendour. As the result of this granting of a boon, even now the people of the world get nourishing food such as milk and ghee from cows from time to time and eat it. Here ghee, or ghṛta, is said to be the splendour of Agni. For that very reason, in sacrifices and the like, people make homa and other offerings in the fire with ghṛta, or ghee, and make the fire blaze. Milk is said to be the splendour of Soma. For Soma is in liquid form like milk, and to increase the taste of the Soma-juice they mix milk with it. This is called gavāśira. By mixing milk in this way the splendour, or essence (taste), of Soma increases. The man who knows the greatness of these splendours of Agni and Soma becomes splendid.

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति किंदेवत्यं पौर्णमासमिति प्राजापत्यमिति ब्रूयात्तेनेंद्रं ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं निरवासाययदिति तस्माज्जेष्ठं पुत्रं धनेन निरवासयंति ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti kiṃdevatyaṃ paurṇamāsamiti prājāpatyamiti brūyātteneṃdraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ niravāsāyayaditi tasmājjeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ dhanena niravāsayaṃti ‖*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-5-20 to 7) **NOTE**

The Brahmavādins ask who is the chief deity of this sacrifice called Paurṇamāsya (the full-moon sacrifice). The answer to be given is that Prajāpati is the deity presiding over the sacrifice. But in this sacrifice Prajāpati has no share of the oblation, has he? Then how is Prajāpati the deity of this sacrifice? The answer: formerly Prajāpati created all the sacrifices. This is stated in the Vedic sentence

प्रजापतिर्यज्ञानसृजताग्निहोत्रं चाग्निष्टोमं च पौर्णमासीं चोक्त्यं चामावास्यां चातिरात्रं च (*prajāpatiryajñānasṛjatāgnihotraṃ cāgniṣṭomaṃ ca paurṇamāsīṃ coktyaṃ cāmāvāsyāṃ cātirātraṃ ca*)

(Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-5-9-) **NOTE**

That is, it is said here that Prajāpati created all sacrifices such as agnihotra, agniṣṭoma, paurṇamāsī (the sacrifice performed on the day of the full moon), ukthya, amāvāsyā (the sacrifice performed on the day of the new moon) and atirātra. All the sacrifices created by Prajāpati became his own property. Therefore, as is the custom in worldly practice, that is, as one gives his property to his eldest son, Prajāpati entrusted the chief deityship of these sacrifices to his eldest son Indra. This is stated in the very passage of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā तेनेंद्रं निरवासाययत्तेनेंद्रः परमां काष्ठामगच्छत् (*teneṃdraṃ niravāsāyayatteneṃdraḥ paramāṃ kāṣṭhāmagacchat*). Therefore all the oblations offered to Indra, the son, in the full-moon sacrifice must be regarded as offered to the father Prajāpati. It is for this very reason that

### Printed p. 639

this sacrifice called Paurṇamāsya is customarily said to be prājāpatya, that is, related to Prajāpati. Following this order, even now in worldly practice it is the custom for a father to give all his property, wealth and the rest, to his eldest son.

**The reason why Prajāpati received this name** **NOTE**

In this account there is an episode:

इंद्रो वैवृत्रं हत्वा सर्वा विजितीर्विजित्याब्रवीत्सजापतिमहमेतवसानि यत्त्वमहं महानसानीति स प्रजासतिरब्रवीदथ कोऽहमिति यदैवैतदवोच इत्यब्रवीत्ततो वै को नाम प्रचापतिरभवत्को वै नाम प्रजापतिर्यन्महानिंद्रोऽभवत्तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं ॥ (*iṃdro vaivṛtraṃ hatvā sarvā vijitīrvijityābravītsajāpatimahametavasāni yattvamahaṃ mahānasānīti sa prajāsatirabravīdatha ko 'hamiti yadaivaitadavoca ityabravīttato vai ko nāma pracāpatirabhavatko vai nāma prajāpatiryanmahāniṃdro 'bhavattanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ ‖*)

(I. Patra - 12-30.) **NOTE**

Formerly, after Indra had slain Vṛtra, having conquered all the regions of the earth, he said to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, you have now gained a great position and are worshipful. From now on I want your high rank." Prajāpati said: "If you take my rank, then who am I (कः (*kaḥ*))? What will my position be?" Indra replied: "O Prajāpati, as you yourself have just said, from now on your name will be कः (*kaḥ*) (Who); that is, you will be denoted by the word क (*ka*)." Therefore from that time Prajāpati became denoted by the word क (*ka*). This is well known. It is for this very reason that this matter is stated in the pratigraha mantras that are to be recited when accepting any gift, namely

क इदं कस्मा अदादित्याह प्रजापतिर्वै कः । प्रजापतॆय एव तद्ददाति (*ka idaṃ kasmā adādityāha prajāpatirvai kaḥ | prajāpatèya eva taddadāti*)

This is a Brāhmaṇa sentence of the other Vedas. Since the word क (*ka*) has the meaning "happiness", in matters and subjects related to Prajāpati, Prajāpati is said to be of the nature of happiness. Since Indra thus took on the greatness of Prajāpati, the appellation Mahān came to Indra; that is, Indra became Mahān Indra. This matter is stated in other Vedas also:

इंद्रो वृत्रमहन्तं देवा अब्रुवन्महान्वा अयमभूद्यो वृत्रमवधीदिति तन्महेंद्रस्य महेंद्रत्वं । (*iṃdro vṛtramahantaṃ devā abruvanmahānvā ayamabhūdyo vṛtramavadhīditi tanmaheṃdrasya maheṃdratvaṃ |*)

The gods, praising Indra's slaying of Vṛtra, said: Because this Indra slew Vṛtra he became Mahendra (gained a high position); that is, he became greater than all the gods. This is the reason for Indra's getting the name Mahendra, it is said.

स महान्भूत्वा देवता अब्रवीदुद्धारं म उद्धरतेति यथाष्टेतिर्हि सृष्टि (*sa mahānbhūtvā devatā abravīduddhāraṃ ma uddharateti yathāṣṭetirhi sṛṣṭi*)

### Printed p. 640

यो वै भवति यः श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते स महान्भवति तं देवा अब्रुवन् स्वयमेव ब्रूष्ट यत्ते भविष्यतीति स एतं माहेंद्रं ग्रहमब्रूत माध्यंदिनं सवनानां निष्केवल्यमुक्थानां तिष्टुभं छंदसां पृष्ठं साम्यां तमस्मा उद्धारमुदहरन् उदस्मा उद्धारं हरंति य एवं वेद। (*yo vai bhavati yaḥ śreṣṭhatāmaśnute sa mahānbhavati taṃ devā abruvan svayameva brūṣṭa yatte bhaviṣyatīti sa etaṃ māheṃdraṃ grahamabrūta mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanānāṃ niṣkevalyamukthānāṃ tiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ sāmyāṃ tamasmā uddhāramudaharan udasmā uddhāraṃ haraṃti ya evaṃ veda|*) **NOTE**

Then Indra, having gained a high position as stated above, called the gods and said: "O gods, since I have gained a high position, arrange on this account, that is, to congratulate me, a honorific reception." In worldly practice too, when a man gains exceptional prosperity, or distinction in learning and the like, or royal honour, since such a man becomes known as eminent among people, it is the custom for people to arrange a reception to congratulate him. Accordingly Indra questioned the gods on this matter. The gods also approved Indra's word and said: "O Indra, how is this reception to be given? How will you be pleased if it is done? You must tell us; we shall act accordingly." Indra said: "Among the grahas (a graha is a special vessel for drinking Soma), the Māhendra graha (the vessel of Soma offered to me, Mahendra) must be the best of all the grahas. Likewise you must approve that, among the three savanas, the Prātaḥsavana, the Mādhyandinasavana and the Tṛtīyasavana, the Mādhyandinasavana; among the śastras (mantras) such as the Āśvinaśastra and the Marutvatīya, the Niṣkevalyaśastra; among the metres such as Gāyatrī, the Triṣṭubh metre; and among the sāman chants, the Bṛhad-Rathantara sāman, which accomplishes the Pṛṣṭha stotra, are the best. For all of these are dear to me. This is the reception that you will give me." The gods agreed, saying "So be it," and approved the pre-eminence of the Māhendra graha and the others in sacrifices and the like. This matter is also stated in other Vedas:

स एतं माहेंद्रमुदहरत वृत्रं हत्वान्यासु देवतास्वधीति यन्माहेंद्रो गृकृत उद्धारमेव तं यजमान उद्धरते व प्रजास्वधि (*sa etaṃ māheṃdramudaharata vṛtraṃ hatvānyāsu devatāsvadhīti yanmāheṃdro gṛkṛta uddhārameva taṃ yajamāna uddharate va prajāsvadhi*)

The yajamāna who performs a sacrifice and knows this obtains pre-eminence and an eminent position among the people.

तं देवा आब्रुवन्सर्वं वा आवोचथा अपि नोऽत्रास्त्विति स नेत्यब्रवीत्कथं वोऽपि स्यादिति तमब्रुवन्नस्येव नोऽस्तु मघवन्निति तानीक्षतैव ॥ (*taṃ devā ābruvansarvaṃ vā āvocathā api no 'trāstviti sa netyabravītkathaṃ vo 'pi syāditi tamabruvannasyeva no 'stu maghavanniti tānīkṣataiva ‖*)

(I. Bṛ- 12-21) **NOTE**

Then the gods said to Indra: "O Indra, we have honoured you and offered you in the sacrifice all the essential things that you wished. You alone have taken all the essential things. Give some of them to us too." Indra said: "That cannot be. I alone desired all these essential things. They all came to me. What reason is there to give them to you?" The gods again said: "O

### Printed p. 641

Indra, do not refuse our prayer in this way. Give us too a little share," they prayed; Indra looked at them with a look of favour. He said nothing more.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्नियं वा इंद्रस्य प्रिया जाया वानवाता प्रासहा नामास्यामेवेच्छामहा इति तथेति तस्यामैच्छंत सैनानब्रवीत्वा तर्वः प्रतिवक्तास्मीति तस्मात्त्रयः पत्याविच्छंते तस्मादु स्स्यनुरात्रं पत्याविच्छते तां प्रातरुपायन्नैतदेव प्रत्यपदृत । (*te devā abruvanniyaṃ vā iṃdrasya priyā jāyā vānavātā prāsahā nāmāsyāmevecchāmahā iti tatheti tasyāmaicchaṃta sainānabravītvā tarvaḥ prativaktāsmīti tasmāttrayaḥ patyāvicchaṃte tasmādu ssyanurātraṃ patyāvicchate tāṃ prātarupāyannaitadeva pratyapadṛta |*) (Ai. Brā. 12-22)

Since Indra said not a word, the gods did not understand Indra's intention. So they spoke among themselves thus: "This woman who is now before us is Indra's beloved wife. She is of the middle class. Her name is Nānātā. **NOTE** Kings have three kinds of wives. Among them it is the custom to call the wife of the best class Mahī, the wife of the middle class Nānātā, and the wife of the lowest class Parivṛtti. For this very reason, among the duties to be performed by women in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the chief queen is designated by the word भूः (*bhūḥ*), the wife called Nānātā by the word भुव (*bhuva*), and the wife called Parivṛtti by the word सुवः (*suvaḥ*). Of these three, the wife of the middle class called Nānātā has the name Prāsahā. For this wife, knowing her husband's wishes, acting accordingly, and being able to do every task by force, is very dear to the king. So, understanding that it was proper to learn the intention of King Indra through her, they put their matter to her. Hearing it, Nānātā said: "O gods, now is not the proper time to tell Indra of your matter and learn his intention. In the world it is the custom for women to tell their husbands any important matter in the night, when they are in privacy. Since in privacy there is no kind of interruption or hindrance, the man listens sympathetically to what the women say and gives a fitting answer. Therefore tonight, when I am in privacy with Indra, I shall bring up your matter and learn Indra's intention. So, if you come tomorrow morning, I shall tell you Indra's reply." The gods said "So be it," and came the next day in the morning and asked; and Nānātā spoke this sentence, in the form of a mantra, as the reply:

यद्वावान पुरुतमं पुराषाळा वृत्रहेंद्रो नामान्यप्राः । अचेति प्रासहस्पतिस्तु विष्मानिति ॥ (*yadvāvāna purutamaṃ purāṣāḷā vṛtraheṃdro nāmānyaprāḥ | aceti prāsahaspatistu viṣmāniti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-74-6)

Among the ancient men, Indra, having slain Vṛtra, in many other battles too became victorious

### Printed p. 642

and has gained fame throughout the world. Therefore Indra has the name Prāsahaspati. Pra means excessive, sahaḥ means strength, patiḥ means lord: one who is lord of excessive strength, very strong; this is a meaningful name. Having gained such a name by the great deed of slaying Vṛtra, he has spread it throughout the world that honorific names such as the Māhendra graha and the Mādhyandinasavana are very dear to him. This Indra also knows what the gods desire. And he is very strong: this is the meaning of the three pādas of this Ṛk. This is what Vāvātā told the gods. **NOTE**

इंद्रो वै प्रासहस्पतिस्तु विष्णान् । यदीमुष्मसि कर्तवे करत्तदिति यदेवैतदवोचामाकरत्तदित्येवैनांस्तदब्रवीत् ॥ (*iṃdro vai prāsahaspatistu viṣṇān | yadīmuṣmasi kartave karattaditi yadevaitadavocāmākarattadityevaināṃstadabravīt ‖*)

Hearing the reply that Vāvātā gave by the three pādas of the mantra as stated above, the gods spoke among themselves by the fourth pāda यदीमुष्मसि कर्तवे करत्तत् (*yadīmuṣmasi kartave karattat*): "If we gods also have a share in the sacrifice, and if Indra arranges that share of the sacrifice for us, our wish will have been fulfilled by Indra." Or, if the sentence of this fourth pāda is regarded as Vāvātā's reply, then the meaning of the fourth pāda is: "O gods, Indra will accomplish, or will do, the matter that you have considered and prayed to Indra for." That is what is stated clearly here.

ते देवा अब्रुवन्यप्यस्या इहास्तु या नोऽस्मिन्न वै कमविददिति तथेति तस्या अप्यत्राकुर्वन् ॥ (*te devā abruvanyapyasyā ihāstu yā no 'sminna vai kamavidaditi tatheti tasyā apyatrākurvan ‖*)

Hearing this reply of Vāvātā, the gods thought: "This Vāvātā has done us gods a great favour. So we must return the favour to her. It is not known whether this Vāvātā has any connection with the niṣkevalya śastra mantra or not. However that may be, let us arrange a fitting connection for this Vāvātā in the niṣkevalya śastra mantra," and they did so.

तस्मादेषात्रापि शस्यते यद्वावान पुरुषमं पुराषाळिति । (*tasmādeṣātrāpi śasyate yadvāvāna puruṣamaṃ purāṣāḷiti |*)

Since the gods thus arranged for Vāvātā, in the niṣkevalya śastra mantra, the connection of this Ṛk (यद्वावान (*yadvāvāna*) Ṛ. Saṃ. 10.74-6), this Ṛk is called the dhāyyā mantra in the niṣkevalya śastra mantra.

सेना वा इंद्रस्य प्रिया जाया वानवा प्रासहा नाम को नाम प्रजापतिः श्वशुरस्तद्यास्य कामे सेना जयेत्तस्या अर्थात्तिष्ठंस्तृणमुभयुतः (*senā vā iṃdrasya priyā jāyā vānavā prāsahā nāma ko nāma prajāpatiḥ śvaśurastadyāsya kāme senā jayettasyā arthāttiṣṭhaṃstṛṇamubhayutaḥ*)

### Printed p. 643

परॆच्छिद्येतरां सेनामभ्यस्येत्प्रासहे कस्त्वा पश्यतीति तद्यथैवादः स्नुषा श्वशुराल्लज्जमाना निलीयमान्यैत्येवमेव सा सेना भज्यमाना निलीयमानैति यत्रैवं विद्वांस्तृणमुभयतः परिच्छिद्येतरां सेनामभ्यस्यति प्रासहे कस्त्वा पश्यतीति । (*parècchidyetarāṃ senāmabhyasyetprāsahe kastvā paśyatīti tadyathaivādaḥ snuṣā śvaśurāllajjamānā nilīyamānyaityevameva sā senā bhajyamānā nilīyamānaiti yatraivaṃ vidvāṃstṛṇamubhayataḥ paricchidyetarāṃ senāmabhyasyati prāsahe kastvā paśyatīti |*)

The praise of Vāvātā, Indra's wife, who spoke this dhāyyā mantra, is given here in some detail. It has been said earlier that Vāvātā is Indra's beloved wife and that her name is Prāsahā. In worldly practice it is said that this Vāvātā, or Prāsahā, exists in the form of an army made ready for battle. For Indra's wife is the deity presiding over the army; in the Veda too it is said इंद्राणी वै सेनाय देवता (*iṃdrāṇī vai senāya devatā*). And since she said को नाम (*ko nāma*), "who am I", it has been explained earlier that Prajāpati is denoted by the word क (*ka*). That Prajāpati is the father-in-law of Indra's wife. That Indra is the son of Prajāpati is said in the Veda itself: प्रजापतिरिंद्रमसृजतानुजावरं देवानां (*prajāpatiriṃdramasṛjatānujāvaraṃ devānāṃ*). This being so, in worldly practice a man who desires battle, if he wishes his army to win victory, must do one thing. At the time of battle, when the two armies stand facing each other to fight, that man must go beyond his army, that is, advance a little from the middle of the army, stand on the ground, take a blade of grass, cut off its root and its tip, and throw the remaining middle part toward the enemy army (in front of him) as one throws an arrow. While throwing it thus, the blade of grass must be thrown with the mantra प्रासहे कस्त्या पश्यति (*prāsahe kastyā paśyati*): "O wife of Indra, named Prāsahā, Prajāpati, who is denoted by कः (*kaḥ*) and is your father-in-law, is looking at you with his eyes." If the blade of grass is thrown in this way with this mantra, the enemy army suffers defeat. This is made clear by an illustration. In worldly practice, in the house of a householder who is a great man and devoted to ancestral custom, when a young daughter-in-law sees her father-in-law, out of shyness she adjusts the end of her sari, draws in her hands and other limbs, and quietly goes off into the inner part of the house. In the same way, by the mantra-accompanied throwing of the blade of grass, the enemy army suffers defeat and, crossing mountains, forests and rivers, retreats and flees to its own country. Leaving this matter here as an aside, they proceed to expand the present context:

तानिंद्र उवाचापि वोऽत्मास्त्विति ते देवा अब्रुवन्निराड्याज्यास्तु निष्केवल्यस्य या त्रयस्त्रिंशदक्षरा त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वै देवा अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वाद. (*tāniṃdra uvācāpi vo 'tmāstviti te devā abruvannirāḍyājyāstu niṣkevalyasya yā trayastriṃśadakṣarā trayastriṃśadvai devā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvāda.*)

### Printed p. 644

शादित्याः प्रजापतिश्च वषट्कारश्च देवता अक्षरभाजः करोत्यक्षरमक्षरमेव तद्देवता अनु प्रपिबंति देवपात्रेणैव तद्देवतास्तृप्यंति । (*śādityāḥ prajāpatiśca vaṣaṭkāraśca devatā akṣarabhājaḥ karotyakṣaramakṣarameva taddevatā anu prapibaṃti devapātreṇaiva taddevatāstṛpyaṃti |*) **NOTE**

Hearing Vāvātā's word (reply), the gods went near Indra, and Indra said to them: "O gods, as you desire, a share of the sacrifice has been given to you in the niṣkevalya śastra of the sacrifice." Hearing that, the gods said: "We (the gods) are thirty-three. Namely, eight Vasus, eleven Rudras and twelve Ādityas; together with these, one Prajāpati and one vaṣaṭkāra; there being thus thirty-three deities in all, by the yājyā mantra of the metre called Virāj, which has thirty-three syllables, that is,

पिबा सोममिंद्र मंदतु त्वा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः । सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा । (*pibā somamiṃdra maṃdatu tvā yaṃ te suṣāva haryaśvādriḥ | soturbāhubhyāṃ suyato nārvā |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-22-1)

by this yājyā mantra, arrange the drinking of Soma." So they prayed to Indra. In this yājyā mantra there should be thirty-three syllables. But instead of that there are only twenty-nine syllables. Even so, by the order of combining the syllables, although the syllables are fewer, it must be regarded that there are thirty-three syllables in all. Thus the thirty-three syllables in the yājyā mantra, each syllable like one deity, satisfy all thirty-three deities. The harm that results if the yājyā oblation is offered with a mantra of another metre, leaving this order, is explained:

यं कामयेतानायतवान् स्यादित्यविराजास्य यजेद्गायत्रा वा त्रिष्टुभा वान्येन वा छंदसा वषट्कुर्यादनायतनवंतमेवैनं तत्करोति यं कामयेतायतनवान् स्यादिति विराजास्य यजेत्पिबा सोममिंद्र मंदतु त्वेत्येतयायतनवंतमेवैनं तत्करोति । (*yaṃ kāmayetānāyatavān syādityavirājāsya yajedgāyatrā vā triṣṭubhā vānyena vā chaṃdasā vaṣaṭkuryādanāyatanavaṃtamevainaṃ tatkaroti yaṃ kāmayetāyatanavān syāditi virājāsya yajetpibā somamiṃdra maṃdatu tvetyetayāyatanavaṃtamevainaṃ tatkaroti |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 12-59) **NOTE**

If the hotṛ wishes that the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice should lose his house and other possessions, then he should not recite the yājyā mantra to be recited in the niṣkevalya śastra with a Ṛk of the Virāj metre, but should make the homa reciting mantras of Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh or another metre. If he does so, the yajamāna's house and other places of residence are destroyed. Therefore, if the yajamāna wishes that the wealth of his house should be lasting, the hotṛ must perform this yājyā homa with the very mantra पिबा सोममिंद्र (*pibā somamiṃdra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-22-1), a Ṛk of the Virāj metre. If he does so, prosperity of houses and other places of residence results for the yajamāna.

### Printed p. 645

**The reason why Indra received the name मरुत्वास् (*marutvās*)**

The eternal companionship of Indra and the Maruts, the relation of king and subjects between them, the offering of oblations in the chief sacrificial acts to Indra together with the Maruts, and the help that the Maruts gave Indra when he waged battle with Vṛtrāsura, are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. An earlier story showing that Indra, joined with the Maruts, stood apart from the other gods is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

आतिथ्येन वै देवा इष्ट्वा । तान्त्समदविंदत्ते चतुर्धाव्यद्रवन्नन्योन्यस्य श्रिया तिष्ठमाना अग्निर्वसुभिः सोमो रुद्रैर्वरुण आदित्यैरिंद्रो मरुद्भिर्भृहस्पतिर्विश्वैर्देवैः ॥ (*ātithyena vai devā iṣṭvā | tāntsamadaviṃdatte caturdhāvyadravannanyonyasya śriyā tiṣṭhamānā agnirvasubhiḥ somo rudrairvaruṇa ādityairiṃdro marudbhirbhṛhaspatirviśvairdevaiḥ ‖*)

(Ca. Brā. 3-4-2-1) **NOTE**

In the past, when the gods performed the ātithya rite, discord arose among them, and, unwilling to join one another, they formed four groups and separated. Agni with the Vasus, Soma with the Rudras, Varuṇa with the Ādityas, Indra with the Maruts, and Bṛhaspati with the Viśvedevas, joining together in this way, made separate groups. **NOTE** In this story the close relation which Indra, having developed companionship with the Maruts, kept with them is told. Moreover, it is said in many places that Indra is the king and the Maruts are the subjects. For example, in the same Rathapatha Brāhmaṇa, **NOTE**

क्षत्रं ना इंद्रो विशो मरुतो विशा वै क्षत्रियो बलवान् भवति । (*kṣatraṃ nā iṃdro viśo maruto viśā vai kṣatriyo balavān bhavati |*)

(Śa. Brā. 4-3-3-6)

Indra is the king, who has the splendour of the warrior. The Maruts are his subjects. It indicates that it is only through the cooperation of his subjects that a king becomes powerful, and that through the help of the Maruts Indra's valour grew. It is because of such a close relation and companionship that the practice of offering oblations addressed to Indra and the Maruts together is seen in the Śrutis. And by Ṛks such as

स नो मरुद्धिर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः । (*sa no maruddhirvṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-171-5)

there is an invocation and an offering of oblation to Indra and the Maruts together. Describing this companionship, in the Bṛhaddevatā

मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat*)

(Bṛ. De. 4-56)

### Printed p. 646

by sentences of this kind the epithet that indicates the relation of these deities is explained. But in one sūkta the mutual hostility between Indra and the Maruts and Indra's anger are indicated as the result of a dispute that took place between them. The dispute between them, which is the root of this anger, is told thus:

क्वंस्यावो मरुतः स्वधासीद्यन्मामेकं समधत्ताहिहेत्ये । अहं ह्युंस्रस्तविषस्तु विष्णान्विश्वस्व शत्रोरनमं वधस्नैः ॥ (*kvaṃsyāvo marutaḥ svadhāsīdyanmāmekaṃ samadhattāhihetye | ahaṃ hyuṃsrastaviṣastu viṣṇānviśvasva śatroranamaṃ vadhasnaiḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-6)

"O Maruts, it is false to say that I slew Ahi (Vṛtra) with your help. Where indeed was that power in you? Since my power is itself extraordinary, without desiring the help of other power, it helped me at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra. I alone am terrible, of marvellous power, and endowed with greatness." Thus Indra, looking at the Maruts with a look of contempt, shows his anger. Here that anger is indicated. It is well known that Indra obtained the help of the Maruts at the time of the slaying of Vṛtrāsura. Even so, when the Maruts mention that matter and ask that, in memory of that help, they too be given a share in the oblation that is due to Indra, Indra says that no help whatever came from the Maruts and that he killed all the enemies by his own power. The authors of the Nirukta, telling this same matter, say thus:

अगस्त्य इंद्राय हविर्निरुप्य मरुद्भः संप्रदित्सांचकार । स इंद्र एत्य परिदेवयांचक्रे । (*agastya iṃdrāya havirnirupya marudbhaḥ saṃpraditsāṃcakāra | sa iṃdra etya paridevayāṃcakre |*)

(Ni. 1.5)

Stating the occasion that when the sage Agastya prepared an oblation for Indra and wished to offer a share in it to the Maruts too, Indra at once objected to it, the authors of the Nirukta quoted, to tell this matter, the Ṛk

न नूनमस्ति नो श्वः कस्तद्वेद यदद्भुतं । अन्यस्य चित्तमभि संचरेण्यमुताधीतं विनश्यति ॥ (*na nūnamasti no śvaḥ kastadveda yadadbhutaṃ | anyasya cittamabhi saṃcareṇyamutādhītaṃ vinaśyati ‖*)

(Ma. Sa. 1-170-1) **NOTE**

In order that the force of that anger might lessen and not harm him, and in order that the share of the oblation rightly due to the Maruts might reach them, the prayer is here addressed to the Maruts. After this conciliatory speech Indra's friendship grew as before and he himself gives a share of his oblation to the Maruts also. The seer in the eighth maṇḍala praises this same matter, saying thus.

### Printed p. 647

वृत्रस्य त्वा श्वसथादीषमाणा विश्वे देवा अजहुर्ये सखायः । मरुद्भरिंद्र सख्यं ते अस्त्वथेमा विश्वाः पृतना जयासि ॥ (*vṛtrasya tvā śvasathādīṣamāṇā viśve devā ajahurye sakhāyaḥ | marudbhariṃdra sakhyaṃ te astvathemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāsi ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-9-6)

O Indra, your friendship with the Maruts is well known. Give them also a share in your oblation, and with their help conquer all your enemies: thus the seer has prayed.

**Indra's slaying of the demon Namuci**

After giving a brief account of this Namuci, we shall then explain how Indra killed him.

The name of Namuci occurs in the Ṛgveda nine times; besides, this name is found also in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 1-7-1-6. 7), the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 12-7-1-10) and other places. In the Ṛgveda he is spoken of as being of demonic nature and as a Dāsa (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-6, 8). In one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-57-7) he is described as a master of magic. The Ṛgveda says that when Indra defeated Namuci, the friendship or support of Namī and Sāytu was with him **NOTE** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-7; 6-20-6). Like the other demons, Namuci too has been slain by Indra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-5; 7-19-5), or struck down and destroyed (1-53-7). Indra slew the demons Vṛtra and Namuci and destroyed a hundred fortresses of the demons (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-5). He does not cut off Namuci's head as he cut off the head of the demon Vṛtra, but kills him by crushing (pounding) him (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5.30-8; 6-20-6), or kills him by twisting his head (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-7), or kills him by twisting (wringing) his head with the foam of water (of the sea) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-14-3 **NOTE**). In some places it is also said that he cut off the head (Tai. Brā. 1-7-1-6, 7). In one place (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-4, 5) Indra sat by the side of Namuci and drank intoxicating liquor; then Sarasvatī, with the help of the Aśvin gods, healed him. These are all the accounts given in the Ṛgveda.

Now I shall explain how the account of Indra's killing of Namuci stands in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa of the Yajurveda. नमुचिः । इंद्रेण सह युद्धं न मुंचतीति नमुचिः (*namuciḥ | iṃdreṇa saha yuddhaṃ na muṃcatīti namuciḥ*). Some commentators have given the derivation of the word Namuci thus: since he does not give up fighting with Indra, he is called Namuci. As this demon was very strong, it was very difficult for Indra to fight with him and conquer him. Therefore Indra had to kill him by a stratagem. In this matter there is a legend in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

### Printed p. 648

इंद्रो वृत्रग्ं हत्वा । असुरान् पराभाव्य । नमुचिमासुरं नालभत । तग्ं शच्यागृह्णात् । तौ समलभेतां । सोऽस्मादभिशुनतरोऽभवत् । सोऽब्रवीत् । संधाग्ं संदधावहै । अथ त्वावस्रक्षामि । न मा शुष्केण नार्देण हनः । न दिवा न नक्तमिति । स एतमसां फेनमसिंचत् । न वा एष शुष्को नार्द्रो व्युष्टासीत् । अनुदितः सूर्यः । न वा एतद्दिवा न नक्तं तस्यैतस्मिन् लोके । अपां फेनेन शिर उदवर्तयत् । तदेनमन्ववर्तत । मित्रद्रुगिति । स एतानपमार्गानजनयत् । तानजुहोत् । तैर्वै स रक्षाग् स्यपाहत । यदपमार्गहोनो भवति । रक्षसामपहत्यै ॥ (*iṃdro vṛtragṃ hatvā | asurān parābhāvya | namucimāsuraṃ nālabhata | tagṃ śacyāgṛhṇāt | tau samalabhetāṃ | so 'smādabhiśunataro 'bhavat | so 'bravīt | saṃdhāgṃ saṃdadhāvahai | atha tvāvasrakṣāmi | na mā śuṣkeṇa nārdeṇa hanaḥ | na divā na naktamiti | sa etamasāṃ phenamasiṃcat | na vā eṣa śuṣko nārdro vyuṣṭāsīt | anuditaḥ sūryaḥ | na vā etaddivā na naktaṃ tasyaitasmin loke | apāṃ phenena śira udavartayat | tadenamanvavartata | mitradrugiti | sa etānapamārgānajanayat | tānajuhot | tairvai sa rakṣāg syapāhata | yadapamārgahono bhavati | rakṣasāmapahatyai ‖*)

(Kṛ. 7-7-1962 **NOTE**)

After Indra had killed the demon Vṛtra, he killed other demons also. But he could not conquer the demon called Namuci. He was very mighty. He did not yield to any kind of weapon. Therefore Indra, wishing to defeat him by his own bodily strength alone, began a wrestling match with him. Yet the more they fought, the more Namuci's strength grew. Indra could not escape from his hold. Then, when Indra asked Namuci to release him, the demon said to Indra: "O Indra, if you are to be released, you must do as I say. Let us now make a pact (an agreement) with each other. You may again wish to fight me by some stratagem and kill me. In such a case the weapon you use to kill me must be neither wet nor dry; you must not kill me by day, and you must not kill me by night either. If you agree to these conditions, I shall release you." Indra agreed, saying "So be it", freed himself from his hold, and began to think how to conquer him. After some time Indra thought of a stratagem. While he was walking on the seashore, the foam of the sea fell within his sight. This foam is neither wet nor dry. "Therefore I shall make this my weapon and kill Namuci. When night has passed and the time of dawn has begun, before the sun rises, it is quite light. That time is not night, because there is no darkness; and it is not day, because the sun has not risen. If at such a time I fight Namuci and kill him with a weapon made of the foam of water, I shall not have broken the word I gave." Having so resolved, he fought Namuci accordingly and cut off his head with that foam. Yet the demon did not die, but pursued Indra to kill him. "O Indra, treacherous to a friend, stand, stand! After promising me earlier that you would not kill me, you have now done such a deed of treachery to a friend.

### Printed p. 649

I shall not leave you without killing you even now," he said. Then Indra, frightened, created the apāmārga, a particular kind of tree, and with its fuel sticks **NOTE** made an offering in the fire for the increase of his vigour. By that Indra's strength grew greater, and he killed that Namuci. Therefore those who wish to be freed from the affliction of the demons should make an offering in the fire with apāmārga fuel sticks for the increase of vigour; by that offering their strength will increase and they will be able to conquer the demons: so the legend runs. This name of Namuci **NOTE** occurs in the Ṛgveda in the Ṛks

नम्मा यदिंद्र सख्या परावति निबर्हयो नमुचिं नाम मायिनं ॥ (*nammā yadiṃdra sakhyā parāvati nibarhayo namuciṃ nāma māyinaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-53-7)

यः पिपुं नमुचिं यो रुधिकां तस्मा इंद्रायांधसो जुहोत । (*yaḥ pipuṃ namuciṃ yo rudhikāṃ tasmā iṃdrāyāṃdhaso juhota |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-14-5)

निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहञ्च वृत्रं नमुचिमुताहन् ॥ (*niveśane śatatamāviveṣīrahañca vṛtraṃ namucimutāhan ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-19-5)

त्वं जघुंथ नमुचिं मुखस्युं दासं कृष्णान ऋषये विमायं ॥ (*tvaṃ jaghuṃtha namuciṃ mukhasyuṃ dāsaṃ kṛṣṇāna ṛṣaye vimāyaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-73-7)

अत्ता दासस्य नमुचेः शिरो यदवर्तयो मनवे गातुमिच्छन् ॥ (*attā dāsasya namuceḥ śiro yadavartayo manave gātumicchan ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-2)

युजं हि मामकृथा आदिदिंद्र शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् ॥ (*yujaṃ hi māmakṛthā ādidiṃdra śiro dāsasya namucermathāyan ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-30-8)

प्र श्येनो न मदिरमंशुमस्मै शिरो दासस्य नमुचेर्मथायन् ॥ (*pra śyeno na madiramaṃśumasmai śiro dāsasya namucermathāyan ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-20-6)

अपां फेनेन नमुचेः शिर इंद्रोदवर्तयः ॥ (*apāṃ phenena namuceḥ śira iṃdrodavartayaḥ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-14-13)

युवं सुराममश्विना नमुचावासुरे सचा ॥ (*yuvaṃ surāmamaśvinā namucāvāsure sacā ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10 131 4)

These are the Ṛks that there are; it occurs nowhere else.

**The reason why Indra got the name Ṛjīṣī** **NOTE**

Ṛjīṣī: Yāska has given the following explanation of this word:

य जिषी सोमो यत्सोमस्य पूयमानस्यातिरिच्यते तदृजेषमपार्जितः भवति तेनर्जिषी सोमः । अथाप्यैंद्रो निगमो भवति ऋजिषी वज्री इति ॥ (*ya jiṣī somo yatsomasya pūyamānasyātiricyate tadṛjeṣamapārjitaḥ bhavati tenarjiṣī somaḥ | athāpyaiṃdro nigamo bhavati ṛjiṣī vajrī iti ‖*)

(Ni. 5-12)

### Printed p. 650

The lifeless, husk-like matter that remains after the Soma plant has been crushed with stones and the juice taken out is called ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*). This ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) is thrown away as useless. On some occasions such ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) is soaked in water and a little more juice is pressed and drawn from it. Such Soma juice is called ऋजीषः सोमः (*ṛjīṣaḥ somaḥ*). At the time of the third pressing, this Ṛjīṣa Soma is mixed with admixtures such as flour and offered to Indra. Because Indra drinks this Ṛjīṣa Soma, it has become customary to call Indra by the word Ṛjīṣī. Moreover, it is well known that Indra's horses, called Hari, eat the husks of the Soma plants called Ṛjīṣa. In this matter Yāska has cited as an example the Vedic sentence बद्धां ते हरीधाना उप ऋजीषं जिघ्रतां (*baddhāṃ te harīdhānā upa ṛjīṣaṃ jighratāṃ*). The meaning of the above sentence is: O Indra, may your horses eat the grain and smell this Ṛjīṣa.

What is Ṛjīṣa? What is the reason for its getting this name? What is its use in the sacrifice? These and similar matters, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, we shall examine here in detail:

सोमो वै राजमुष्मिंल्लोक आसीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन् कथमयमस्मात्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति तेऽब्रुवंश्चंदांसि यूयं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरतेति कथेति ते सुपर्णा भूत्वो दपतन् । (*somo vai rājamuṣmiṃlloka āsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyan kathamayamasmātsomo rājāgacchediti te 'bruvaṃścaṃdāṃsi yūyaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāharateti katheti te suparṇā bhūtvo dapatan |*)

(5. Ṭi. - 13-25 **NOTE**)

In former times King Soma (the Soma plant; it is the custom to call the Soma plant out of respect King Soma), that is, the Soma plant, was in the heavenly world; it was not in this world. Knowing this, the gods and the seers considered how this Soma might be brought here. Then, after deliberating on the matter, they understood that the metres had the power to bring Soma from heaven to earth, and they prayed to the metres: "O metres, for our sake, that is, to be used in our sacrifice, bring the Soma that is in heaven to the earth." Accepting their prayer, the metres took the forms of certain birds well known in the world and flew to the heavenly world. First the Jagatī metre took the form of a bird and flew towards the heavenly world. But before it had gone far it became tired, could not go as far as heaven, and returned. Then the Triṣṭubh metre said that it would bring the Soma and leaped into the sky. But before it had gone a little beyond the middle of the way it became exhausted from fatigue and returned. When the gods saw that the Jagatī and Triṣṭubh metres had thus come back, unable to bring the Soma, they went to the Gāyatrī metre and prayed: "O Gāyatrī, you must bring the Soma for us from heaven."

### Printed p. 651

Gāyatrī agreed, took the form of a falcon and flew to heaven, frightened the guardians of the Soma there, Sthāna **NOTE** Bhrāja and others, carried off the Soma and brought it to the earth. Because she brought the Soma plant, Gāyatrī obtained the most excellent place among the metres.

सा यद्धक्षिणेन पदा समगृभ्यात्तत्प्रातःसवनमभवत्तद्गायत्री स्वमायतनमकुरुत तस्मात्तत्समृद्धतमं मन्यंते सर्वॆषां सवनानामग्रियो मुख्यो भवति श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते य एवं वेदाथ (*sā yaddhakṣiṇena padā samagṛbhyāttatprātaḥsavanamabhavattadgāyatrī svamāyatanamakuruta tasmāttatsamṛddhatamaṃ manyaṃte sarvèṣāṃ savanānāmagriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatāmaśnute ya evaṃ vedātha*) यत्सव्येन पदा समगृभ्यात्तन्माध्यंदिनं सवनमभवत्तद्विस्रंसत तद्विप्रस्तं नान्वाप्पोत्तूर्वं सवनं ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तस्मिंस्किष्टुभं छंदसामदधुरिंद्रं देवतानां तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वेण सवनेनोभाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां समावद्वीर्याभ्यां समावज्जामीभ्यां राध्योति य एवं वेदाथ यन्मुखेन समगृभ्यात्तृतीयसवनमभवत् । (*yatsavyena padā samagṛbhyāttanmādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamabhavattadvisraṃsata tadviprastaṃ nānvāppottūrvaṃ savanaṃ te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tasmiṃskiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāmadadhuriṃdraṃ devatānāṃ tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrveṇa savanenobhābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ samāvadvīryābhyāṃ samāvajjāmībhyāṃ rādhyoti ya evaṃ vedātha yanmukhena samagṛbhyāttṛtīyasavanamabhavat |*)

(I. Cā. 13-26 **NOTE**)

While bringing the Soma plants, the falcon carried them gripping with both her feet and with her beak. The Soma (or Soma plant) that the bird brought holding it with her right foot became the morning pressing. Gāyatrī made it, that is, the morning pressing, her own place. Therefore among all the pressings the morning pressing is held by the sacrificers to be the best of all. In the rite of the morning pressing the application of the mantras and the rest is also special. Therefore the man who knows this matter well is regarded as becoming the best and the chief among his equals. When Gāyatrī brought the Soma plant holding it with the left foot, since the left foot had not so much strength as the right foot, those plants and the like slipped a little from the foot from time to time. For this reason this midday pressing was not equal to the morning pressing in strength and capacity. Seeing this, the gods deliberated and established the Triṣṭubh metre for the metres to be used in the rite of the midday pressing, and Indra, the best among the gods. Through the company of Indra, the best among the gods, and of the Triṣṭubh metre dear to him, the midday pressing obtained a place equal to the morning pressing in strength, capacity and excellence. The man who knows this equality of the morning and midday pressings, their strength and capacity, and their excellence, obtains prosperity and well-being in wealth and the like and lives happily. Then the portion of Soma that Gāyatrī, in the form of the falcon, brought by biting with her beak became known as the third pressing.

### Printed p. 652

तस्य पतंती रसमधयत्तद्वीतरसं नान्वाप्नोत्पूर्वे सवने ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तत्सशुष्पपश्यंस्तद्यदाशिरमवनयंत्याज्येन पशुना चरंति तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्पूर्वाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां सर्वैः सवनैः समावद्वी. र्यैः समावज्जामिभी राध्योति य एवं वेद ॥ (*tasya pataṃtī rasamadhayattadvītarasaṃ nānvāpnotpūrve savane te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tatsaśuṣpapaśyaṃstadyadāśiramavanayaṃtyājyena paśunā caraṃti tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavatpūrvābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ sarvaiḥ savanaiḥ samāvadvī. ryaiḥ samāvajjāmibhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*)

(I. Cā. 13-27)

While Gāyatrī (the falcon) was coming holding the Soma plant in her beak, she kept sipping the juice in the plant little by little. Therefore, that is, because the juice in the Soma plants brought in the beak was not abundant but scanty, this third pressing did not become equal to the morning and midday pressings in strength, capacity and the rest. Therefore the gods, seeing this matter, deliberated and found that the means suited to it lay in the animals. From animals one obtains milk, curds, and the oblation materials such as ghee (clarified butter) obtained from them. If milk is mixed with the Soma juice that is scanty in the plants, that juice becomes strong. If the offerings and the like are made with ghee and with the limbs of the animals, the pressing rite **NOTE** will be complete. Therefore those who know the sacrificial rite, by adding admixtures such as milk to the juice of the Ṛjīṣa used at the third pressing (the husks of the Soma plant that remain after the juice has been taken out at the morning and midday pressings are called ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) **NOTE**), and by making offerings with the ghee obtainable from the animals and with the animals' parts from the heart onward **NOTE**, understand that the third pressing rite becomes equal to the morning and midday pressings in strength, capacity and the rest, and act accordingly. This matter is stated in another recension thus:

ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति कस्मात्सत्याद्यायत्रि कनिष्ठा छंदसाग्ं सती यज्ञमुखं षरियायेति यदेवादः सोममाहरत्तस्माद्यज्ञमुखं पर्यॆत्तस्मात्तेजस्वीनीतमा पद्भां द्वे सवने समगृह्णान्मुखेन्ैकं यन्मुखेन नमगृह्णात्तदधयत्तस्माद्वे सवने शुक्रवती प्रातःसवनं च माध्यंदिनं च तस्मात्तृतियसवन ऋजीषमभिषुण्वंति धीतनिव हि मन्यंते आशिरमवनयति सशुक्रत्वाय ॥ (*brahmavādino vadaṃti kasmātsatyādyāyatri kaniṣṭhā chaṃdasāgṃ satī yajñamukhaṃ ṣariyāyeti yadevādaḥ somamāharattasmādyajñamukhaṃ paryèttasmāttejasvīnītamā padbhāṃ dve savane samagṛhṇānmukhenaikaṃ yanmukhena namagṛhṇāttadadhayattasmādve savane śukravatī prātaḥsavanaṃ ca mādhyaṃdinaṃ ca tasmāttṛtiyasavana ṛjīṣamabhiṣuṇvaṃti dhītaniva hi manyaṃte āśiramavanayati saśukratvāya ‖*)

(Trai. Saṃ. 6.1.6-4 **NOTE**)

Thus the same meaning is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. The man who knows this matter, that is, that the three pressings, the morning, midday and third, have obtained an equal place in strength, capacity and the like and in excellence, will be possessed of all prosperity and will live happily.

### Printed p. 653

**How Indra and Vāyu obtained the first drinking of Soma**

In the Ṛk अग्रं पिब मधूनां (*agraṃ piba madhūnāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-46-1) it is said that Vāyu, before Indra and the other gods, is entitled to drink Soma first. In support of this

आ वायो भूष शुचिपा उप नः सहस्रं ते नियुतो विश्ववार । उपो ते अंधो मद्यमयामि यस्य देव दधिषे पूर्वपेयं ॥ (*ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā upa naḥ sahasraṃ te niyuto viśvavāra | upo te aṃdho madyamayāmi yasya deva dadhiṣe pūrvapeyaṃ ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-92-1)

this Ṛk is cited, and it is pointed out that there the seer prays that Vāyu should drink Soma first. How Vāyu obtained the foremost place among the gods in the drinking of Soma is told in an ancient story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. We explain it here:

देवा वै सोमस्य राज्योऽग्रपेये न समसादयन्नहं प्रथमः पिबीयमहं प्रथमः पिबीयमित्येवाकामयंत ते संपादयंतोऽब्रुवन् हंताजिमयाम स यो न उज्वेष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पास्कृतीति तथेति त अजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिस्पृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेंद्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विनौ (*devā vai somasya rājyo 'grapeye na samasādayannahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamahaṃ prathamaḥ pibīyamityevākāmayaṃta te saṃpādayaṃto 'bruvan haṃtājimayāma sa yo na ujveṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāskṛtīti tatheti ta ajimayusteṣāmājiṃ yatāmabhispṛṣṭānāṃ vāyurmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātheṃdro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāvathāśvinau*)

(Ai. Brā. 9-25)

In former times all the gods, wishing to drink Soma together, fell into a dispute as to which of them should drink Soma first, and a debate began among them, each saying "I first, I first shall drink." As this matter could not be settled in any way, they all assembled, took counsel and came to an agreement, namely: "Let us all together arrange a contest. Whoever wins in it shall be entitled to drink Soma first." When all consented to that, the terms of the contest were fixed thus: they were to run from one place to another place far away, and whoever first reached a rock or a tree standing there was to be reckoned the winner. When all agreed to the compact that the one who thus won, being victorious among them, should drink Soma first, all the gods began to run at the same moment. Among all the gods who ran, Vāyu reached the appointed place ahead of everyone. Indra, coming close behind Vāyu, became second. After Indra, Mitra and Varuṇa, and after them the Aśvin gods, came running and reached the appointed place. Thus among these gods Vāyu ran ahead of all and became the winner.

सोऽवेदिंद्रो वायुमुद्वै जयतीति तमनु परापतत्सह नावथोज्ययावेति स नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोऽजेष्यामीति तृतीयं मेऽथोज्ययावेति (*so 'vediṃdro vāyumudvai jayatīti tamanu parāpatatsaha nāvathojyayāveti sa netyabravīdahamevo 'jeṣyāmīti tṛtīyaṃ me 'thojyayāveti*)

### Printed p. 654

नेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामीति तुरीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति तथेशि तं तुरीयेऽत्यार्जत तत्तु रीयभागिंद्रोऽभवत्रिभाग्वायुः ॥ (*neti haivābravīdahamevojjèṣyāmīti turīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti tatheśi taṃ turīye 'tyārjata tattu rīyabhāgiṃdro 'bhavatribhāgvāyuḥ ‖*)

While Vāyu was running, and Indra behind him, a conversation took place between them in this manner. Indra, seeing Vāyu running swiftly ahead of him, thought: "This Vāyu will run ahead of all and become the winner. Somehow I too must run along with him and win." So resolving, he used all his strength and ran close to Vāyu. Yet no sign appeared that he would leave Vāyu behind and go ahead, and then Indra said to Vāyu: "O Vāyu, we two are ahead of everyone. Therefore let us regard ourselves as having won together and let us both share the first drinking of Soma. Half for me, half for you. Let us thus co-operate and gain the victory." Hearing those words Vāyu said: "O Indra, I am ahead of you, even if only a little. Therefore I alone shall be the winner. In the first drinking of Soma everything must come to me. I cannot give you half." Then Indra said: "Very well, then I do not want half. Of three parts take two yourself, and give me one part only." Vāyu did not agree even to that, saying: "Whatever happens, I shall win. The whole share will come to me, and I do not wish to give you even one part in three." Then Indra again entreated Vāyu: "I do not want even one part in three. Still less: if you give me one part in four, that is enough. Agree at least to that." Being so asked, Vāyu agreed, saying "So be it." Therefore it was arranged that in the Indra-Vāyu cup (that is, when Indra and Vāyu drink Soma together) Indra should have one part and Vāyu three parts.

तौ सहैवेंद्रवायू उदजयतां सह मित्रावरुण् सहाश्विन् त एषामेते यथोज्जि तं भक्षा इंद्रवाय्योः प्रथमोऽत मित्रामरुणयोरथाश्विनोt स एष इंद्रतुरियो ग्रहो गृह्यते यद्यैंद्रवायवः ॥ (*tau sahaiveṃdravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇ sahāśvin ta eṣāmete yathojji taṃ bhakṣā iṃdravāyyoḥ prathamo 'ta mitrāmaruṇayorathāśvinot sa eṣa iṃdraturiyo graho gṛhyate yadyaiṃdravāyavaḥ ‖*)

Thus Indra and Vāyu, co-operating, won the contest and reached the appointed place first. After them Mitra and Varuṇa came and arrived. After them the Aśvin gods came. Therefore, in the order of the places which these gods obtained in the contest, they became entitled to drink Soma; that is, it was arranged that first Indra and Vāyu, then Mitra and Varuṇa, and after them the Aśvin gods should drink Soma. Thus the custom of two gods drinking Soma together came into use. Therefore in the Indra-Vāyu cup only one part in four is arranged for Indra in the drinking of Soma.

### Printed p. 655

तदेतदृषि: पश्यन्नभ्यनूनाच नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिरिति । (*tadetadṛṣi: paśyannabhyanūnāca niyutvā iṃdrasārathiriti |*)

The seer, knowing by divine vision that in the Indra-Vāyu cup Indra has one part in four, expressed this matter in the next Ṛk, namely शतेना नो अभिष्टिभिर्नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*śatenā no abhiṣṭibhirniyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-46-2), by the phrase नियुत्वा इंद्रसारथिः (*niyutvā iṃdrasārathiḥ*). Here, as in the Nirukta statement नियुतो वायोः (*niyuto vāyoḥ*) (Ni. 2-28), the horses called नियुत (*niyuta*) are well known as the vehicle of the god Vāyu. Therefore the word meaning "possessed of niyuts" points to a connection with Vāyu. In the above Ṛk the word नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*) indicates Indra together with Vāyu. Mantras such as अधा व युं नियुतः सश्च तस्माः (*adhā va yuṃ niyutaḥ saśca tasmāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 2-8.1-1) support this matter. The word इंद्रसारथिः (*iṃdrasārathiḥ*) means: Indra who is the charioteer of Vāyu. Since Indra stands in the place of charioteer to Vāyu, this indicates that in the first drinking of Soma Indra has only a fourth part.

तस्माद्दाप्येतर्हि भरताः सत्वनां वित्तिं प्रयंति तुरिये हैव संग्रहीतारो पदंतेऽमुन्वॆनानूकाशेन यदद इंद्रः सारथिरिव भूत्वोऽजयत् ॥ (*tasmāddāpyetarhi bharatāḥ satvanāṃ vittiṃ prayaṃti turiye haiva saṃgrahītāro padaṃte 'munvènānūkāśena yadada iṃdraḥ sārathiriva bhūtvo 'jayat ‖*)

(Ai. Brā. 9-25)

The above matter is explained by an example from worldly practice. Warriors in battle sit in chariots, win the battle with the help of their charioteers, and seize the wealth and other possessions of their enemies. When they have seized them, they give one part of that wealth, that is, one part in four, to the charioteers who helped them. This practice is current in the world. In the same way, in this contest arranged by the gods, Indra acted as charioteer to Vāyu, and since Vāyu was the winner, a fourth part of the first drinking of Soma obtained in the contest became Indra's share. The chief meaning is that Indra gained his fourth part by being the charioteer of Vāyu.

**How Indra slew the demon Varāha**

There is a legend that there was a demon named Varāha and that Indra slew him. Viṣṇu also has a part in it. The account given in the Caraka Brāhmaṇa on this matter is explained here.

विस्गुणयज्ञः । स देवेभ्य आत्मानमंतरधात् । तमन्यदेवता नाविंदन्निंद स्ववेत् । स इंद्रमब्रवीत्को भवानिति । तमिंद्रः प्रत्यब्रवीदहु (*visguṇayajñaḥ | sa devebhya ātmānamaṃtaradhāt | tamanyadevatā nāviṃdanniṃda svavet | sa iṃdramabravītko bhavāniti | tamiṃdraḥ pratyabravīdahu*)

### Printed p. 656

दुर्गाणामसुराणां च हंता भवांस्तु क इति । सोऽब्रवीदहं दुर्गादाहर्ता त्वं तु यदि दुर्गाणामसुराणां हंता ततोऽयं वराहोनाममुष एकविंश्याः पुरां पारेऽश्ममयियानां वसति ततस्मिन्नसुराणां वसु वाममस्ति तमिमं जहीति ॥ तस्येंद्रस्ताः पुरो भित्वा हृदयमनिध्यत् अधि तत्र यदासीत्तद्विष्णुराहरदिति । सोऽयमितिहासः ॥ (*durgāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca haṃtā bhavāṃstu ka iti | so 'bravīdahaṃ durgādāhartā tvaṃ tu yadi durgāṇāmasurāṇāṃ haṃtā tato 'yaṃ varāhonāmamuṣa ekaviṃśyāḥ purāṃ pāre 'śmamayiyānāṃ vasati tatasminnasurāṇāṃ vasu vāmamasti tamimaṃ jahīti ‖ tasyeṃdrastāḥ puro bhitvā hṛdayamanidhyat adhi tatra yadāsīttadviṣṇurāharaditi | so 'yamitihāsaḥ ‖*)

The chief meaning of this is: Viṣṇu is the sacrifice. That Viṣṇu, in the form of the sacrifice, at one time left the gods and went away and stayed in a secret place. The other gods did not know this; only Indra knew. Then, when Indra went to the place where Viṣṇu was, Viṣṇu asked Indra who he was. In reply Indra said: "I am the one who destroys fortresses and demons. But who are you?" Viṣṇu again asked: "I am the one who seizes and brings away from the fortresses the wealth and other possessions belonging to the demons. Who are you? What is the work you do?" Then Viṣṇu said: "If you are, as you say, the destroyer of fortresses and of the wealth of the demons, then the demon named Varāha, who has seized wealth and hidden it with himself, dwells from here at the end of twenty-one forts, in a fort firmly built of stones. He has a great deal of the demons' wealth. Therefore slay that demon." Hearing this, Indra destroyed those cities of the demons and pierced the heart of the demon Varāha. Then Viṣṇu brought all the wealth that was with the demon from there. This is the chief meaning of this legend. The commentator says that this matter is stated also in the Ṛk

अस्येदु मातुः सवनेषु सद्यो महः पितुं पपिवाञ्चार्वन्ना । मुषायद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान्विध्यद्वराहं तिरो अद्रिमस्ता (*asyedu mātuḥ savaneṣu sadyo mahaḥ pituṃ papivāñcārvannā | muṣāyadviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyānvidhyadvarāhaṃ tiro adrimastā*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1.61-6)

and he explains the meaning by relating the words of the present Ṛk and of the quoted example to the legend above.

अस्येदु मातुः इत्यत्र विष्णुना हे इंद्र त्वं दुर्गाणां हंतेत्यात्मानं. कथॆयसि तर्हि वाममुषं वराहमसुरं जहीत्युक्तार्थो विध्यद्वराहुं इति पादेन प्रतिपादितः ॥ (*asyedu mātuḥ ityatra viṣṇunā he iṃdra tvaṃ durgāṇāṃ haṃtetyātmānaṃ. kathèyasi tarhi vāmamuṣaṃ varāhamasuraṃ jahītyuktārtho vidhyadvarāhuṃ iti pādena pratipāditaḥ ‖*)

The statement in the above legend: "O Indra, you only claim to be the destroyer of fortresses and demons. If so, slay the demon named Varāha, who has seized wealth and hidden it with himself", namely the meaning of Viṣṇu's words, is stated in the last quarter of the quoted Ṛk अष्टेदु मातुः (*aṣṭedu mātuḥ*) **NOTE** namely in विद्यद्वराहं शिरो अद्रिमस्ता (*vidyadvarāhaṃ śiro adrimastā*), the demon

### Printed p. 657

Varāha was slain. The Sanskrit passage says:

इंद्रेण च विष्णो त्वं दुर्गादाहर्तेति ब्रूषे मया पुराणि जितान्यसुरश्च घातितस्तस्य वामं वस्वानयेत्युक्तो विष्णुमूर्तिस्तस्य वराहासुरस्य धनं मुमोष । सोऽर्थं मुषायुद्विस्ष्णुः पचतं सहीयान् इति पादेन सूचितः ॥ (*iṃdreṇa ca viṣṇo tvaṃ durgādāharteti brūṣe mayā purāṇi jitānyasuraśca ghātitastasya vāmaṃ vasvānayetyukto viṣṇumūrtistasya varāhāsurasya dhanaṃ mumoṣa | so 'rthaṃ muṣāyudvisṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyān iti pādena sūcitaḥ ‖*)

And Indra said to Viṣṇu: "O Viṣṇu, you only claim to be the one who brings away the wealth from the fortresses. Now I have conquered many enemy cities and killed the demon. Go and bring the wealth that is with that demon." Viṣṇu agreed to this and seized and brought the wealth that was with the demon Varāha. This account is made clear by the quarter of the quoted Ṛk मुषायद्विष्णुः पचतं सहीयान् (*muṣāyadviṣṇuḥ pacataṃ sahīyān*).

स किं पुनर्मुषितवानिति तदत्रोच्यते । विश्वेत्ता इति । हे इंद्र ष्टेषितस्त्वया प्रेरितो विष्णुर्यज्ञरूपी ष्टेषितस्त्वं दुर्गादाहार्ता किल तर्हि त्वं तस्य धनान्याहरेति त्वया प्रेरितः सन्नुरुक्रमो भूत्वा विश्वेत्ता यानि च तत्र स्थितानि तानि सर्वाण्याभरत् । अभरत् । (*sa kiṃ punarmuṣitavāniti tadatrocyate | viśvettā iti | he iṃdra ṣṭeṣitastvayā prerito viṣṇuryajñarūpī ṣṭeṣitastvaṃ durgādāhārtā kila tarhi tvaṃ tasya dhanānyāhareti tvayā preritaḥ sannurukramo bhūtvā viśvettā yāni ca tatra sthitāni tāni sarvāṇyābharat | abharat |*) कानि तानीति । शतं महिषानपरिमितान् प्रशस्तान् पदार्थान् तेषां वाहनरूपान् महिषान्वा क्षीरपाक मोदनं च पक्वमात्रमेवौदनं चाभरत् । (*kāni tānīti | śataṃ mahiṣānaparimitān praśastān padārthān teṣāṃ vāhanarūpān mahiṣānvā kṣīrapāka modanaṃ ca pakvamātramevaudanaṃ cābharat |*)

Moreover, it is said that that Viṣṇu again seized and brought many other things. The details of this are stated clearly in the present Ṛk beginning with विश्वेत्ता (*viśvettā*). O Indra, you said to Viṣṇu, the sacrifice in person: "O Viṣṇu, you claim to be the one who seizes and brings the wealth and other possessions from the fortresses of the demons. If so, take and bring the wealth and other possessions of this demon Varāha." As soon as he was urged by you (by Indra) in this way, Viṣṇu agreed, saying "So be it", went quickly to the city of the demon, and seized and brought all the wealth that was with the demon, that is, whatever things he had been told to bring. What those things were that Viṣṇu brought: the most excellent and countless best objects such as wealth, the buffaloes and other animals that carry them, and food cooked with milk and so on; he seized and brought all, as Indra had said. These details are clearly indicated in the present Ṛk.

विथ्यद्वराहं इत्यत्रोक्तोऽर्थश्च चरमपादेनोच्यते । इंद्रस्तु वराहारं स्वीकृतासुरसर्वस्वं वराहरूपिणं वैमुषमेमुषनामानमथवैमुषं धनानामामोषकं वराहमसुरं हृदयेऽविध्यदिति शेषः ॥ (*vithyadvarāhaṃ ityatrokto 'rthaśca caramapādenocyate | iṃdrastu varāhāraṃ svīkṛtāsurasarvasvaṃ varāharūpiṇaṃ vaimuṣamemuṣanāmānamathavaimuṣaṃ dhanānāmāmoṣakaṃ varāhamasuraṃ hṛdaye 'vidhyaditi śeṣaḥ ‖*)

### Printed p. 658

Now they explain the meaning of the last quarter of the present Ṛk, विद्यद्वराहमिंद्र एमुषं (*vidyadvarāhamiṃdra emuṣaṃ*). This demon named Varāha, being in the form of a boar (varāha), had seized much wealth from many and kept it. Therefore it is customary to call him एमुषं (*emuṣaṃ*), that is, धनानामामोषकं (*dhanānāmāmoṣakaṃ*), one who steals wealth. The meaning that Indra, with his own strength and power, pierced the breast of the demon Eṃuṣa in the form of a boar and killed him is set out in the last quarter of the present Ṛk.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda too the account of this matter is given in the same way.

यज्ञो देवेभ्यो निलायुत विष्णू रूपं कृत्वा स पृथिवीं प्राविशत्तं देवा हस्तान्त्सग्ं रभ्यैच्छन्तमिंद्र उपर्युपर्यत्यक्रामत्सोऽब्रवीत्नोमायमुपर्युपर्यत्यक्रमादित्यहं दुर्गे हंतेत्यथ कस्यमित्यकं दुर्गादाहर्तेति सोऽब्रवीद्दुर्गे वै हंतावोचथावराहोऽयं वाममोषः सप्तानां गिरीणां परस्ताद्वित्तं वेद्यमसुराणां बिभर्ति तं जहि (*yajño devebhyo nilāyuta viṣṇū rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa pṛthivīṃ prāviśattaṃ devā hastāntsagṃ rabhyaicchantamiṃdra uparyuparyatyakrāmatso 'bravītnomāyamuparyuparyatyakramādityahaṃ durge haṃtetyatha kasyamityakaṃ durgādāharteti so 'bravīddurge vai haṃtāvocathāvarāho 'yaṃ vāmamoṣaḥ saptānāṃ girīṇāṃ parastādvittaṃ vedyamasurāṇāṃ bibharti taṃ jahi*) यदि दुर्गॆ हंतासीति सदर्भपुंजीलमुदृह्य सप्तगिरीन् भित्वा तमहन्सोऽब्रविद्दुर्गाद्वा आहर्ता वोचथा एतमाहरेति तमेभ्यो यज्ञ एव यज्ञ माहरद्यत्तद्वित्तं वेध्यमसुराणामविंदंत तदेकं वेद्यै वेदित्वं ॥ (*yadi durgè haṃtāsīti sadarbhapuṃjīlamudṛhya saptagirīn bhitvā tamahanso 'braviddurgādvā āhartā vocathā etamāhareti tamebhyo yajña eva yajña māharadyattadvittaṃ vedhyamasurāṇāmaviṃdaṃta tadekaṃ vedyai veditvaṃ ‖*)

(Tri. Saṃ. 6-2-4, 3 **NOTE**)

To explain how the sacrificial altar came to be called vedi, a legend is told in the Yajurveda:

In former times, for some reason, the sacrifice took the form of Viṣṇu, left the gods and went away. Then that Viṣṇu, in the form of the sacrifice, entered the earth and hid himself so that no one knew. The gods, not seeing him, searched everywhere, holding one another by the hand. Yet they did not find the place where Viṣṇu was. But when Indra was passing over the region where Viṣṇu had hidden himself, Viṣṇu below said: "Who is it? Who is passing over this place where I am?" Hearing that, Indra said: "I am the hero who strikes and destroys the fortresses of the demons. But who are you?" he asked. To that Viṣṇu replied: "I am the one who brings the wealth and other things found there after the fortresses of the demons have been destroyed." And addressing Indra he said: "O man, if you are indeed the one who destroys enemy cities as you claim,

### Printed p. 659

then beyond seven mountains from here there is a demon named Varāha. He has seized the wealth and other possessions of the demons and keeps them inside his strong fort. If you have the power to destroy the forts of the demons as you claim, strike and destroy that demon Varāha. Only then will your power be known." Hearing this, Indra took a bunch of darbha grass that was near, made it his weapon, split the seven impregnable mountains, and struck and killed that demon Varāha. Then he said to Viṣṇu: "O man, as you said, I have split the seven mountains and killed the demon who was there. By this my strength and power have become clear. You said that you are the one who brings the wealth and other things from the fortresses of the demons once they are destroyed. Now, as you claimed, go and bring the wealth and other things that are there. Then your power will become manifest." Viṣṇu said "So be it" and, in the very form of the sacrifice, seized the wealth and other things that were with that demon and brought them to the gods. The chief meaning of this legend is that because the gods obtained the demons' wealth through the sacrifice in this way, the place where the sacrifice is performed came to be called vedi.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रं स्तवेत्यष्टादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रस्य रेणोरार्षं
> त्रैष्टुभमैंद्रं । अनुक्रांतं च । इंद्रं स्तव द्व्यूना रेणुरिति ॥ सूर्यस्तुन्नाम्येकाह इदं सूक्तं निष्केवल्यनिविद्धानं । सूत्रितं च । सूर्यस्तुता यशस्वामः
> पिबा सोममभींद्रं स्तवेति मध्यंदिनः । अ. ९.८ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning इंद्रं स्तव (*iṃdraṃ stava*) is the fifth sūkta, of eighteen Ṛks; its seer is Reṇu of the Viśvāmitra line, its metre Triṣṭubh and its deity Indra. The Anukramaṇī says: इंद्रं स्तव द्व्यूना रेणुरिति (*iṃdraṃ stava dvyūnā reṇuriti*). In the one-day rite named Sūryastut this sūkta is the nividdhāna of the niṣkevalya. A Sūtra is cited for this: in the Sūryastut for one who desires fame, the midday pressing has the sūkta पिबा सोममभींद्रं स्तव (*pibā somamabhīṃdraṃ stava*) (Sāyaṇa gives the reference as A. 9.8 **NOTE**).

The Kannada Anuvāda: This sūkta Indraṃ stava is the fifth sūkta in the seventh anuvāka. In it there are eighteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Reṇu of the Viśvāmitra family; the deity is Indra; the metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इंद्रं स्तव द्व्यूना रेणुः (*iṃdraṃ stava dvyūnā reṇuḥ*). That this sūkta is to be recited as the nividdhāna sūkta among the niṣkevalya-śastra mantras in the one-day iṣṭi called Sūryastut is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: "Sūryastut for one desiring fame; in the midday: Pibā somam abhīndraṃ stava" (Ā. 9.8).

- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 89.
- Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 14, 15, 16.
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 18.
- Seer: Reṇu.
- Deity: Ṛks 1-4 and 6-18, Indra; Ṛk 5, Indra and Soma.
- Metre: Triṣṭubh.
