##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, you must praise Indra, the best of leaders. Sāyaṇa takes the word of praise as an imperative (the verse has a change of case-ending, the vibhakti-vyatyaya). Of this Indra the greatness overcomes the lustres of others; he overcomes as well the ends of the earth up to the ends **NOTE**. And that Indra, the sustainer of men, even exceeding the seas by his greatness and increasing, fills heaven and earth with radiances that keep off darkness.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser) यस्य (*yasya*)—of which Indra
- मह्ना (*mahnā*)—greatness
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—all orbs of light
- वि बबाधे (*vi babādhe*)—which, disregarding them, surpasses them all
- वि जृः अंतान् (*vi jṛḥ aṃtān*)—surpasses even the ends of the earth
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Indra
- चर्षणीधैत् (*carṣaṇīdhait*)—as the sustainer of men
- सिंधुभ्यः (*siṃdhubhyaḥ*)—than all the seas
- महित्वा (*mahitvā*)—by his greatness
- प्र रिरिचानः (*pra riricānaḥ*)—surpassing
- वरोभिः (*varobhiḥ*)—by the radiances that keep off darkness
- आ पप्रौ (*ā paprau*)—has pervaded all heaven and earth, such
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the excellent guide
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- स्तव (*stava*)—praise.

### Printed p. 661

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, praise that Indra, the excellent guide, whose greatness disregards and surpasses all orbs of light, who as the sustainer of men surpasses all the seas by his greatness, and who has pervaded heaven and earth all over with radiances that keep off darkness.

##### English translation
Praise Indra, the chief leader (of rites), whose glory surpass the lustre (of others), and the ends of the earth; the sustainer of man, who exceeding the ocean in magnitude, fills (heaven and earth) with radiance.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स सूर्यः॒ पर्यु॒रू नरां॒स्येंद्रो॑ वनृत्या॒द्रथ्ये॑व च॒क्रा ।  
> अति॑ष्ठंतमप॒स्यं१॒॑१ न सर्ग०॑ कृ॒ष्णा तमां॑सि॒ त्रिष्या॑ जघान ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । सूर्यः । परि । उरु । वरांसि । आ । इंद्रः । ववृत्यात् । रथ्या इव । चक्रा ।  
> अतिष्ठंतं । अपस्यं । न । सर्गं । कृष्णा । तमांसि ! त्वष्या । जघान ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सूर्यः सुवीर्यः स प्रसिद्ध इंद्र उरु बहूनि वरांसि तेजांसि पर्या
> ववृत्यात् । पर्यावर्तयति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्येव यथा सारथी रथसंबंधीनि
> चक्रा चक्राण्यावर्तयति तद्वदित्यर्थः । किंच सोऽयमतिष्ठंतं शीघ्रं गच्छंतमपस्यं
> न कर्मण्यमिव सर्ग० । सृज्यत इति सर्गोऽश्वः । कृष्णानि तमांसि त्रिष्या दीप्ता
> जघान । हंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known Indra of excellent valour makes many lustres revolve all around. An example: as a charioteer makes the wheels of the chariot turn, so he does. Moreover, he, like a swift-going horse that is active in work (the horse is so called as one that is sent forth), destroys the black darkness with his shining radiance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रथ्या (*rathyā*)—the charioteer who drives the chariot
- चक्रा इव (*cakrā iva*)—as he makes the wheels turn
- सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)—of excellent valour
- सः (*saḥ*)—the well-known Indra
- उरु (*uru*)—very great
- वरांसि (*varāṃsi*)—lustres
- परि आ ववृत्यात् (*pari ā vavṛtyāt*)—makes them revolve everywhere

### Printed p. 662

- ष्ठंतं (*ṣṭhaṃtaṃ*)—swift-going **NOTE**
- अपस्यं (*apasyaṃ*)—and active in work
- सर्गं न (*sargaṃ na*)—like a horse
- त्विष्या (*tviṣyā*)—with his own radiance
- कृष्णा तमांसि (*kṛṣṇā tamāṃsi*)—the black darkness
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—destroys.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a charioteer who drives a chariot praises **NOTE** the wheels of the chariot, Indra, of excellent valour and well known, makes the very great lustres revolve everywhere. Like a swift-going horse that is active in work, he destroys the black darkness with his radiance.

##### English translation
The heroic Indra causes numerous rays of light to revolve as a charioteer (effects the rotation of) the wheels of the chariot ; he destroys by his radiance the black darkness like a restless active horse.

#### Ṛk 3 **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स॒मा॒नम॑स्मा॒ अन॑पावृदर्च क्ष्म॒या दि॒वो अस॑मं॒ ब्रह्म॒ नव्यं॑।  
> वि यः पृ॒ष्टेव॒ जनि॑मान्य॒र्य इंद्र॑श्चि॒काय॒ न सखा॑यमी॒षे॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समानं । अस्मै । अनपवृत् । अर्च । क्ष्मया । दिवः । असमं । ब्रह्म । नव्यं ।  
> वि । यः । पृष्ठा इव । जनिमानि । अर्यः । इंद्रः । चिकाय न । सखायं ईषे॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे स्तोतः त्वं समानं मया सहानपावृदपगतिरहितं क्षमया दिवो दिवः
> पृथिव्याश्चासममत्यंतमतिरिक्तं । महदित्यर्थः । नव्यं नवतरमन्यैरकृतपूर्वं
> ब्रह्म स्तोत्रमस्मा इंद्रायार्च । उच्चारय । य इंद्रो जनिमानि यज्ञे यज्ञे
> जातानि पृष्ठेव पृष्ठसंज्ञकानि स्तोत्राणीवार्योऽरीञ्चितून्वि चिकाय विजिनोति
> सखायं च नेषे नेच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O praiser, together with me recite to this Indra a new hymn (brahma, a stotra) never made before by others, that is without interruption, and that exceeds heaven and earth, that is, is very great. That Indra, as the stotras named Pṛṣṭha that are born at every sacrifice, overcomes the foes, and desires no friend.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O praiser) यः इंद्रः (*yaḥ iṃdraḥ*)—which Indra
- जनिमानि (*janimāni*)—produced in the sacrifice

### Printed p. 663

- पृष्ठेव (*pṛṣṭheva*)—like the stotras named Pṛṣṭha
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—the enemies
- वि चिकाय (*vi cikāya*)—seeks out and destroys (and)
- सखायं (*sakhāyaṃ*)—no friend
- न ईषे (*na īṣe*)—does he desire for help
- अस्मै (*asmai*)—to such an Indra
- समानं (*samānaṃ*)—with me
- अनपावृत् (*anapāvṛt*)—that which is without interruption
- क्षया (*kṣayā*)—than the earth
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—than the heavenly world
- असमं (*asamaṃ*)—that which exceeds
- नव्यं (*navyaṃ*)—new
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—stotra
- अर्च (*arca*)—recite.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, to that Indra who, like the stotras named Pṛṣṭha produced at the sacrifice, seeks out and destroys his enemies, and who desires no friend for help, recite a praise that is without interruption, that exceeds the earth and the heavenly world, and that is new.

##### English translation
Sing along with me a new song, unceasing, surpassing heaven and earth, to him who like the prishtha (praises), born at sacrifices, overcomes his enemies, Indra who desires no friend.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑य॒ गिरो॒ अनि॑शितसर्गा अ॒पः प्रेर॑यं॒ सग॑रस्य बु॒ध्नात् ।  
> यो अक्षे॑णेव च॒क्रिया॒ शची॑भि॒र्विष्ट॑क्त॒स्तंभ॑ पृथ॒ीमु॒त द्यां ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राय । गिरः । अनिशितसर्गाः । अपः । प्र । ईरयं । सगरस्य ! बुध्नात् ।  
> यः । अक्षेण इव । चक्रिया । शचीभिः । विश्वक् । तस्तंभ । पृथिवीं । उत । द्यां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रायेंद्रार्थमनिशितसर्गा आतनूकृतविसर्गा उपर्युपरि वर्तमाना
> या गिरः स्तुतयस्ताभिर्गीर्भिः सगरस्यांतरिक्षस्य । सगरं समुद्र इत्यंतरिक्षनामसु
> पाठात् । बुध्नात्पदेशादप उदकानि प्रेरयं । प्रेरयानि । य इंद्रः शचीभिः
> कर्मभिः पृथिवीमुतापि च द्यां दिवं चक्रिया रथचक्राण्यक्षेणेव यथा रथाक्षेण
> तद्वद्विष्टक् सर्वशस्त्रस्तंभ अस्तभ्नात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For Indra, with those hymns that are uninterrupted, their emission not blunted, going on one above another, I send forth waters from the base of the firmament (the firmament is meant, since this word stands in the list of names of the firmament). That Indra holds firmly on every side, by his deeds, the earth and also heaven, as the axle holds the wheels of a chariot.

### Printed p. 664

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चक्रिया (*cakriyā*)—the wheels of the chariot
- आक्षेणेव (*ākṣeṇeva*)—as the wheels are held fast and made to stand firm by the axle-pin
- यः इंद्रः (*yaḥ iṃdraḥ*)—which Indra
- शचीभिः (*śacībhiḥ*)—by his deeds
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heavenly world
- तस्तंभ (*tastaṃbha*)—holds and makes to stand, such
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—to Indra
- अनिशितसर्गाः (*aniśitasargāḥ*)—which are recited continuously without interruption
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—with praises
- सगरस्य बुध्नात् (*sagarasya budhnāt*)—from the base regions of the firmament
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—waters
- प्रेरयं (*prerayaṃ*)—I offer and send forth.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As an axle-pin holds the wheels of a chariot fast and makes them stand firm, that Indra by his deeds holds and makes to stand the earth and the heavenly world; to such an Indra, with praises recited continuously, without interruption (without hindrance), I offer and send forth waters from the base regions of the firmament.

##### English translation
I will utter praises to Indra in unceasing flow, (I will send) waters from the depth of the firmament (to him) who has fixed heaven and earth on both sides by his acts as the wheels of a chariot (are fixed) by the axle,

#### Ṛk 5 **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आपां॑तमन्युस्तृ॒पल॑प्रभर्मा॒ धुनिः॒ शिमी॑वा॒ञ्चरु॑मा ऋजी॒षी ।  
> सोमो॒ विश्वा॑न्यत॒सा वना॑नि॒ नार्वागिंद्रं॑ प्रति॒माना॑नि देभुः ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आपांतमन्युः । त्वपलप्रभर्मा । धुनिः । शिमीवान् । शरुमान् । ऋजीषी ।  
> सोमः । विश्वानि । अतसा । वनानि । न । अर्वाक् । इंद्रं । प्रतिमानानि । देभुः ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आपांतमन्युरापातितमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा ग्रावादिभिः क्षिप्रप्रहारी धुन्नि
> शत्रुणां कंपयिता शिमीवान् कर्मवाइरुमानायुधवानृजीष्यजीषवान्

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Āpātamanyu: one whose wrath has been aroused; tṛpalaprabharmā: one who strikes swiftly with grinding stones and the like; dhuni: one who makes enemies tremble; śimīvān: one possessed of action **NOTE**; śarumān: one possessed of weapons; ṛjīṣī: one possessed of the residue (ṛjīṣa).

### Printed p. 665

> सोमो विश्वानि सर्वाण्यतसातसमयानि वनान्यरण्यानि वर्धयतीति शेषः । प्रतिमानानि प्रतिमानभूतानि । समानानि द्रव्याणेत्यर्थः । इंद्रमर्वाग्न देभुः । दभ्योतिरत्राकर्षणकर्मा । तुलया मीयमानान्यात्माभिमुखतया नाकर्षयंति । लघूनि
> बवंतीत्यर्थः । अन्यत्र प्रतिनिधीयमानानि पुरूणि तान्यात्माभिमुखमाकर्षंति नैवमिंद्रं कुर्वंतीति । सर्वेभ्यो महानिंद्र इत्यर्थः । त्रयः पादाः सौम्यास्तुरीयस्त्वैंद्रः । तथा च यास्क ! आपातितमनुस्त्रप्रप्रहारी क्षिप्रप्रहारी सोमो
> वॆंद्रो वा धुनिर्धूनोतेः शिमीति कर्मनाम शमयतीर्वा शक्नोतेर्वर्जिषी
> सोमो यत्सोमस्य पूयमानस्यातिरिच्यते तदृजीषमपार्जितं भवति तेनर्जिषी
> सोमोऽथाप्यैंद्रो निगमो भवत्यजीषी वज्रीति । सोमः सर्वाण्यतसानि वनानि
> नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि दभ्नुवंति यैरेनं प्रतिमिमते नैनं तानि दभ्नुवंति ।
> नि. ५-१२ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma makes all the woods of atasa grow (this is the word to be supplied). Pratimānāni means things that serve as a counterpart, that is, equal objects. They do not draw Indra: the root meaning here is drawing; things weighed on a balance against him do not draw him towards themselves; they become light. Elsewhere, things set against others draw those towards themselves in many ways; they do not do so with Indra: Indra is greater than all. Three quarters of the verse are addressed to Soma, the fourth to Indra. Accordingly Yāska (Ni. 5-12) explains: āpātamanyu, striking quickly, is Soma or Indra; dhuni is from the root of shaking; śimi is a word for action, or from the roots of calming or of being able; ṛjīṣī is Soma, because what remains over of Soma as it is pressed and is thrown away is the ṛjīṣa, and by it Soma is ṛjīṣī; and there is also an Indra passage, ṛjīṣī, bearer of the thunderbolt; and Soma, all the atasa woods, the objects that measure themselves against Indra do not draw him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आपांतमन्युः (*āpāṃtamanyuḥ*)—he who causes wrath to be shown
- तृपलप्रभर्मा (*tṛpalaprabharmā*)—he who is crushed by the stones
- धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*)—he who makes enemies tremble
- शिमीवान् (*śimīvān*)—the man of action
- शरुमान् (*śarumān*)—he who has weapons
- ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—and he who is called Ṛjīṣa
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—the god Soma
- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- अतसा वनानि (*atasā vanāni*)—the woods filled with atasa trees, he makes to grow
- प्रतिमानानि (*pratimānāni*)—those that reflect Indra
- इंद्रमर्वाक् (*iṃdramarvāk*)—facing Indra
- न देभुः (*na debhuḥ*)—do not show pride.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The god Soma, who causes wrath to be shown, who is crushed by stones, who makes enemies tremble, the man of action, who has weapons, and who is called Ṛjīṣa, makes all the woods filled with atasa trees flourish. Those that reflect Indra do not display pride in front of him.

##### English translation
Appeasing wrath, striking quickly, intimidating foes, doer of great deeds, armed with weapons, possessing the stale residue, Soma nourishes all the Atasa woods, they oppose no impediments against Indra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

To explain the meaning of the word आपांतमन्युः (*āpāṃtamanyuḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:

### Printed p. 666

आपातमन्युः । आपातमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवाञ्चरुमा ऋजीषी । सोमो विशान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥ (*āpātamanyuḥ | āpātamanyustṛpalaprabharmā dhuniḥ śimīvāñcarumā ṛjīṣī | somo viśānyatasā vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ ‖*) **NOTE**

आपातितमन्युस्तृप्रप्रहारी क्षिप्रप्रहारी (सृप्रप्रहारी) सोमो वेंद्रो ना ॥ धुनिर्धुनोतेः । शिमीति कर्मनाम । शमयतीर्वा शक्नोतीर्वा । (*āpātitamanyustṛpraprahārī kṣipraprahārī (sṛpraprahārī) somo veṃdro nā ‖ dhunirdhunoteḥ | śimīti karmanāma | śamayatīrvā śaknotīrvā |*)

ऋजीषी सोमो यत्सोमस्य पूयमानस्यातिरिच्यशे तदृजीषमपार्जितं भवति तेनर्जिषी सोमः । अथाप्यॆंद्रो निगमो भवति । ऋजीषी वज्री इति । (*ṛjīṣī somo yatsomasya pūyamānasyātiricyaśe tadṛjīṣamapārjitaṃ bhavati tenarjiṣī somaḥ | athāpyèṃdro nigamo bhavati | ṛjīṣī vajrī iti |*)

हर्योरस्य स भागो धानाश्चति । धाना भ्राष्टे हिता भवंति फले हिता भवंतीति ना । बद्धां ते हरीधाना उप ऋजीषं जिघ्रतां । इत्यपि निगमो भवति । आदिनाभ्यासेनोपहितेनोपधामादत्ते । बभस्तियर्तिकर्मा ! सोमः सर्वाण्यतसानि वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि दभ्नुवंति यैरेनं प्रतिमिमते नैनं तानि दभ्नुवंत्यर्वागेवैनमप्राप्य विनश्यंतीति । (*haryorasya sa bhāgo dhānāścati | dhānā bhrāṣṭe hitā bhavaṃti phale hitā bhavaṃtīti nā | baddhāṃ te harīdhānā upa ṛjīṣaṃ jighratāṃ | ityapi nigamo bhavati | ādinābhyāsenopahitenopadhāmādatte | babhastiyartikarmā ! somaḥ sarvāṇyatasāni vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni dabhnuvaṃti yairenaṃ pratimimate nainaṃ tāni dabhnuvaṃtyarvāgevainamaprāpya vinaśyaṃtīti |*)

इंद्रप्रधानेत्येके नैघुंटुकं सोमकर्मोभयप्रधानेत्यपरं ॥ (*iṃdrapradhānetyeke naighuṃṭukaṃ somakarmobhayapradhānetyaparaṃ ‖*)

(Ni. 5-12)

Here अपातितमन्युः आपादितदीप्तिः उत्पादितमन्युर्वा शत्रुभिः संग्रामे । (*apātitamanyuḥ āpāditadīptiḥ utpāditamanyurvā śatrubhiḥ saṃgrāme |*): the meaning is a man heated with anger, a man in whom wrath is welling up, one who in fighting with enemies, seized by anger, rushes forward against the enemies, or one who strikes the enemies even while rushing forward in anger. तृप्रप्रहारी क्षिप्रप्रहारी सोमो वेंद्रो वा (*tṛpraprahārī kṣipraprahārī somo veṃdro vā*): Tṛpalaprabharmā means one who strikes enemies swiftly or quickly. These words apply either to the deity Soma or to Indra; both have this kind of strength and capacity. The word धुनिः (*dhuniḥ*) is formed from the root धुनोति (*dhunoti*), which means to shake, to make tremble; the meaning is one who makes the enemies tremble with fear. शिमि (*śimi*) means action, work. शिमीवान् (*śimīvān*) means one who does deeds of daring or work full of valour. Or the word शिमि (*śimi*) may be formed from the root शक्कोति (*śakkoti*); in that case शिमीवान् (*śimīvān*) means one who has strength and capacity. शरुमान् (*śarumān*) means हिंसावान् (*hiṃsāvān*), one who does violence to enemies. Two meanings can be given for the word ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*). The husk that remains after the Soma plants have been crushed and the juice taken out is called ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*); ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) means a substance thrown away because it is useless. From that husk, at the time of the third pressing, a little juice is pressed out once more, and they add to it milk, curds or flour, any one of these, so as to make it fit for drinking (palatable). This kind of Soma juice is called ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*), or Indra, who drinks this kind of Soma juice, is also called ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*).

### Printed p. 667

In this matter the scriptural sentence ऋजीषी वज्री (*ṛjīṣī vajrī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-40-4) supports this meaning. This ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) also, mixed with grain and the like, is used as food for Indra's horse. The word धानाः (*dhānāḥ*) (grains) means what has been pounded in a mortar or what has been placed on boards. This grain and the ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) together become the food of Indra's horses. In this matter there is the scriptural authority: बब्बां ते हरीधाना उप ऋजीषं जिघ्रतां (*babbāṃ te harīdhānā upa ṛjīṣaṃ jighratāṃ*). Here the word बब्बां (*babbāṃ*) is formed from the root बभस्ति (*babhasti*), which means "eat, devour". The word बब्बा (*babbā*): in the root भस् (*bhas*), "to devour", the letter bha is read with abhyāsa, that is, with reduplication, and the final letter sa is dropped; thus it becomes बब् (*bab*), and since the prefix धा (*dhā*) is joined to it, it has become बब्बां (*babbāṃ*).

Next, for the sentence सोमः सर्वाण्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः (*somaḥ sarvāṇyatasā vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ*) the meaning is this: Soma, surpassing all creepers and trees by his greatness, pervades everything. **NOTE** But all such greatness, or strength and capacity, is of no use before Indra. None of them can even come near Indra, or they perish before they approach.

Some say that in this Ṛk Indra is the principal one praised, and that the mention of the god Soma is not so important. Others again say that in this Ṛk two deities, Indra and Soma, are praised.

According to some, the first three pādas of this Ṛk are addressed to the deity Soma, and only the last pāda is on behalf of Indra. However great the glory and the daring deeds of other deities may be, they cannot equal the daring deeds and valour of Indra. According to some, the description of the strength and capacity of the deity Soma is here in order to describe Indra as the most glorious of all.

> न यस्य॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी न धन्व॒ नांतरि॑क्षं॒ नाद्र॑यः॒ सोमो॑

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ यस्येंद्रस्य प्रतिमानभूते न भवतः । न धन्व ।
> उदकमपि प्रतिमानभूतं न भवति । नांतरिक्षं । अंतरिक्षमपि प्रतिमानभूतं न भवति ।
> नाद्रयः । पर्वताश्च प्रतिमानभूता न भवंति । तस्येंद्रस्य सोमोऽक्षाः । क्षरति ।
> किंच यद्यदास्येंद्रस्य मन्युः क्रोधोऽधिनीयमानः शत्रूणामुपरि प्राप्यमाणो भवति तदानीमयमिंद्रो वीळु दृढं शृणाति । हिनस्ति । स्थिराणि रुजति ।
> भिनत्ति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains that heaven and earth are not a match for Indra, and neither is the water, neither the atmosphere, nor the mountains; none of them is a counterpart to him. For such an Indra the Soma flows. Further, when Indra's wrath is directed against the enemies, then this Indra firmly shatters them, and breaks what is strong.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य (*yasya*)—for which Indra
- द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)—heaven and earth
- न (*na*)—cannot be equal
- धन्व (*dhanva*)—the waters
- न (*na*)—cannot be equal
- अंतरिक्षं (*aṃtarikṣaṃ*)—the atmosphere also
- न (*na*)—cannot stand against him
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the mountains
- न (*na*)—cannot be equal; for such an Indra
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*)—flows
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अस्य (*asya*)—Indra's
- मन्युः (*manyuḥ*)—wrath
- अधिनीयमानः (*adhinīyamānaḥ*)—is directed upon the enemies, then Indra
- वीळु (*vīḷu*)—the firm enemies
- शृणाति (*śṛṇāti*)—destroys
- स्थिराणि (*sthirāṇi*)—the secure strongholds of the enemies
- रुजति (*rujati*)—splits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For that Indra to whom heaven and earth cannot be equal, nor the waters, nor the atmosphere, nor the mountains, for that Indra the Soma flows. When Indra's wrath is directed upon the enemies, then Indra destroys even the firm enemies and splits their secure strongholds.

##### English translation
Of whom neither heaven and earth, nor the water, nor the firmament, nor the mountains (are the obstructions) for him both the Soma exude, when his wrath reaching his enemies destroys the strong and breaks the firm.

> पुरः शत्रुनगरी रुरोज । रुजति । भिनत्ति ! शत्रुनगरीर्भित्वा च सिंधून्नदीररदत् ।

> उदकान्याकृणुत । अस्मदभिमुखं करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra slew the asura Vṛtra. Like an axe cutting down forests, he breaks the enemy cities; having broken the enemy cities, he scored the rivers, having rained with water. **NOTE** The word for "like" is used here in the sense of "now". Further, he shatters the cloud as one shatters a new pitcher; he does indeed break it. And Indra, with the Maruts who yoke themselves of their own accord, has turned the waters toward us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—the enemy
- जघान (*jaghāna*)—has destroyed
- स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*)—an axe
- वनेव (*vaneva*)—as it splits the forest trees
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—the enemy cities
- रुरोज (*ruroja*)—he splits
- सिंथून् (*siṃthūn*)—the rivers
- अरदत् (*aradat*)—he made channels so that they might flow
- नवं सुंभः न (*navaṃ suṃbhaḥ na*)—as one breaks a new earthen vessel filled with water **NOTE**
- गिरिं (*giriṃ*)—the cloud
- बिभेद इत् (*bibheda it*)—he split
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- स्वयग्भिः (*svayagbhiḥ*)—together with the Maruts who are united with him
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the waters
- अकृणुत (*akṛṇuta*)—made to flow toward us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra has destroyed the asura Vṛtra. As an axe cuts down forest trees, he splits the enemy cities. To make the rivers flow he has split open and set right their courses. As one breaks a new earthen vessel filled with water, he has split the cloud. Together with the Maruts who are united with him, he has made the waters flow toward us.

##### English translation
(Indra) slew Vritra as an axe (cuts down) a tree ; he demolished the cities (of the foes), he dug out the rivers ; he shattered the cloud like a new pitcher ; with his allies (the Maruts) he recovered the cattle.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, you who are wise, are the one who brings about the debts that concern the worshippers. **NOTE** Further, like a sword cutting the joints of animals, you break the troubles of the worshippers, that is, their afflictions. **NOTE** And as for the supporting rite of Mitra and Varuṇa, which is as it were a yoked friend, the unknowing, cruel people who injure it, severely harm it: you break even them. This is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—wise one
- त्वं ह (*tvaṃ ha*)—you
- त्यत् (*tyat*)—as is known to all
- ऋणयाः (*ṛṇayāḥ*)—you are one who expects from the sacrificers the oblations that should be offered to you
- असिः (*asiḥ*)—a sword
- पर्व न (*parva na*)—as it cuts the joints of animals
- वृजिना (*vṛjinā*)—the sins of the worshippers
- शृणासि (*śṛṇāsi*)—you destroy
- मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*)—like a friend
- युजं (*yujaṃ*)—closely united
- मित्रस्य वरुणस्य (*mitrasya varuṇasya*)—of Mitra and Varuṇa
- धाम (*dhāma*)—the rite that sustains the world
- ये जनाः (*ye janāḥ*)—those unwise people who
- प्र मिनंति (*pra minaṃti*)—injure it, even them you destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who are wise, as is known to all, expect from the sacrificers the oblations that should be offered to you. As a sword cuts the joints of dead animals, you also destroy the sins of the worshippers. You destroy even the unwise who injure the world-sustaining rite of Mitra and Varuṇa, who are united like friends.

##### English translation

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The evil-going people who injure the god Mitra, and the god Aryaman, and the Maruts who are well praised, and the god Varuṇa: against those enemies, that is, aiming at them, O Indra, showerer of desires, sharpen your swift, showering, radiant bolt. O Indra, showerer of desires, against those wicked people who injure the god Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa and the Maruts who are possessed of excellent praise, against such enemies sharpen your swift, golden-hued thunderbolt that destroys enemies.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो द्युलोकस्येंद्र ईशे । ईष्टे। पृथिवा भूमेरपींद्र ईशे। ईश्वरो
> भवति । अपामुदकानामपींद्र ईश्वरो भवति । पर्वतानां मेघानामपींद्र
> ईश्वरो भवति । वृधां वृद्धानामपींद्र एवेश्वरः । मेधिराणां प्राज्ञानमपींद्र
> एवेश्वरो भवति । किंचेंद्रः क्षेमे लब्धस्य धनस्य परिपालने हव्यो ह्वातव्यो
> योगेऽलब्धस्य धनस्य लाभेऽपींद्र एव ह्वातव्यो भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is lord of the heavenly world; of the earth also Indra is lord; of the waters also Indra is lord; of the mountains, that is, the clouds, Indra is lord; of the grown, that is, the aged, Indra alone is lord; of the wise also Indra alone is lord. Further, Indra is to be invoked in kṣema, the protection of wealth already obtained, and also in yoga, the gaining of wealth not yet obtained; Indra alone is to be invoked.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the heavenly world
- ईशे (*īśe*)—is lord
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth also
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra is lord
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अपां (*apāṃ*)—of the waters also is lord

### Printed p. 673

- पर्वतानां इत् (*parvatānāṃ it*)—of the clouds also
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra is lord
- वृधां (*vṛdhāṃ*)—of the aged also
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra is lord
- मेधिराणां (*medhirāṇāṃ*)—of the wise also
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra is lord
- क्षेमे (*kṣeme*)—for protecting wealth that has been gained
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—is prayed to
- योगे (*yoge*)—also for gaining wealth that one does not have
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra is prayed to

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra is lord of heaven and earth altogether. Indra is lord of the waters and of the clouds. Indra is lord of the aged and also of the wise. Indra alone should be praised and prayed to, both for protecting the wealth gained and for obtaining the wealth that has to be gained.

##### English translation
Indra rules over heaven, Indra rules over earth, over the waters, and over the clouds ; Indra rules over the great and over the wise ; Indra, is to be invoked for the acquirement and preservation (of wealth).

> इंद्रोऽकुभ्यो रात्रिभ्यः प्र वृधः । प्रवृद्धः । अहभ्यो दिवसेभ्योऽपि प्र

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra has grown beyond the nights; he has grown beyond the days also, and beyond the atmosphere. He has grown beyond the ocean, the sustainer. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 674

> प्रवृद्धः' वातस्य वायोः प्रथसः प्रथिन्नोऽपि प्रवृद्धः । ज्ञः पृथिव्या अंतात्पर्यंतादपि प्रवृद्धः । सिंधुभ्यो नदीभ्यश्च प्र रिरिचे । अतिरिच्यते । महान्भवतीत्यर्थः
> क्षितिभ्यो मनुष्येभ्योऽपि प्र रिरिचे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He has grown beyond the wind, beyond what is wide and extensive; beyond the earth, up to its limit; and he exceeds the rivers; that is, he is great. He exceeds human beings also.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- अक्तुभ्यः (*aktubhyaḥ*)—more than the nights
- प्र वृधः (*pra vṛdhaḥ*)—has grown, surpassing them in excess
- अहभ्यः (*ahabhyaḥ*)—more than the days
- प्र (*pra*)—has grown, surpassing them
- अंतरिक्षात् (*aṃtarikṣāt*)—more than the atmosphere
- प्र (*pra*)—has surpassed it
- समुद्रस्य (*samudrasya*)—than the oceans
- धासेः (*dhāseḥ*)—than the places that sustain them
- प्र (*pra*)—has grown, surpassing them
- वातस्य (*vātasya*)—than the wind
- प्रथसः (*prathasaḥ*)—than the extensive horizons
- प्र (*pra*)—has surpassed them
- ज्मः (*jmaḥ*)—of the earth
- अंतात् (*aṃtāt*)—he is greater than its end
- सिंधुभ्यः (*siṃdhubhyaḥ*)—than the rivers
- प्र रिरिचे (*pra ririce*)—has grown in excess
- क्षितिभ्यः (*kṣitibhyaḥ*)—than human beings
- प्र (*pra*)—has grown, becoming greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra has grown beyond day and night. He has surpassed the atmosphere and the oceans, the waters' seas. He is greater than the winds, greater than the earth, and he has surpassed the horizons. He is greater than the rivers, and he has surpassed human beings.

##### English translation
Indra is vaster than the nights, vaster than the days, vaster than the firmament or the receptacle of the ocean, vaster than the wind, or space or the ends of the earth; Indra exceeds the rivers and mankind.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र शोशु॑चत्या उ॒षसो॒ न के॒तुर॑सि॒न्वा ते॑ वर्ततामिंद्र  ॒

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तवासिन्वा भेदनरहितं हेतिर्वज्राख्यमायुधं शोशुचत्या
> ज्वलंत्या उषसो न यथोषसः केतुः पताकस्थानीयो रश्मिस्तद्वच्छत्रुषु प्र
> वर्ततां । किंच तपिष्ठेनातिशयेन शत्रूणां तापयित्र्या हेषसा शब्दकारिण्या हेत्या
> द्रोघमित्रान् द्रुग्धानि मित्राणि येषां ते द्रोघमित्राः । ताञ्यत्रून्विध्य ।
> ताडय तत्र । दृष्टांतः । दिव आ सृजानः सृज्यमानोऽश्मेव । यथाशनिर्वृक्षान्विध्यति
> तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, let your unbroken weapon, the one called the thunderbolt, go forth against the enemies, like the banner-like ray of the blazing dawn. Further, with your most burning, roaring weapon, strike the enemies, those who have wronged their friends; smite them there. The illustration: like a stone hurled from heaven, as the thunderbolt strikes trees; this is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शोशुचत्याः (*śośucatyāḥ*)—of the shining
- उषसः (*uṣasaḥ*)—dawn
- केतुःन (*ketuḥna*)—like the ray that is like a banner
- असिन्वा (*asinvā*)—unbroken
- ते हेतिः (*te hetiḥ*)—your thunderbolt
- प्र वर्ततां (*pra vartatāṃ*)—let it be hurled upon the enemies
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the atmosphere
- आ सृजानः (*ā sṛjānaḥ*)—swiftly hurled
- आश्मेव (*āśmeva*)—like a thunderbolt
- तपिष्ठेन (*tapiṣṭhena*)—burning
- हेषसा (*heṣasā*)—and roaring, with your weapon
- द्रोघमित्रान् (*droghamitrān*)—the enemies who wish harm
- विध्य (*vidhya*)—strike

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let your unbroken thunderbolt, like the banner-like ray of the shining dawn, be hurled upon the enemies. Swiftly hurled from the atmosphere, strike the enemies who wish harm with your weapon that burns and roars like the thunderbolt.

##### English translation
May your unbroken weapon, Indra, proceed (against your foes) like the banner of the shining dawn, like a stone cast down from heaven pierce those whose friendship is deceitful with your consuming loud-sounding (weapon).

> अनु । इंद्रं । रोदसी इति । वावशाने इति । अनु । आपः । अजिहत । जायमानं ।

### Printed p. 676

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जायमानं प्रादुर्भवंतमिंद्रं मासाश्चैत्रादयोऽन्वजिहत । अनुगच्छंति ।
> अहेति पूरणः । वनान्यरण्यान्यपींद्रमन्वजिहत । इदिति पूरणः । ओषधीरोषध्योऽपींद्रमनुगच्छंति । पर्वतासः पर्वता अपींद्रमनुगच्छंति । वावशाने
> कामयमाने रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यावपींद्रमनुगच्छतः । आप उदकान्यपींद्रमनुगच्छंति । मासाद्यधिष्ठातृदेवताः प्रादुर्भवंतमिंद्रमनुगच्छंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As Indra is born, that is, manifests himself, the months beginning with Caitra follow him; the particle "aha" is only a filler. The forests also follow Indra; the particle "it" is only a filler. The plants follow Indra, and the mountains follow him. Heaven and earth, which are desirous, follow Indra, and the waters follow Indra. The meaning is that the presiding deities of the months and the rest follow Indra as he manifests himself.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जायमानं इंद्रं (*jāyamānaṃ iṃdraṃ*)—as soon as Indra is born
- मासाः (*māsāḥ*)—the months beginning with Caitra
- अन्वजिहत (*anvajihata*)—follow him
- वनानि (*vanāni*)—the forest trees
- अनु (*anu*)—obey his command
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the herbs
- अनु (*anu*)—are obedient to Indra's command
- पर्वतासे (*parvatāse*)—the mountains
- अनु (*anu*)—bow their heads to Indra
- नावशाने (*nāvaśāne*)—loving each other
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—follow Indra
- आर्प (*ārpa*)—the waters
- अनु (*anu*)—obey Indra's command

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As soon as Indra is born, the months beginning with Caitra follow him. The forest trees obey his command. The herbs are obedient to Indra's command. The mountains bow their heads to Indra. Heaven and earth, which love each other, and the waters obey Indra's command.

##### English translation
The months attend upon Indra as soon as born, the forests attend upon him, the plants, the mountains, the affectionate heaven and earth and the waters (attend upon) him.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ते तव सा हेतिरिषुर्वा चेत्या चेतयितव्या शत्रुषु क्षेप्तव्या कर्हि
> स्वित् कदा वासत् । भविष्यति । यद्यदा हेत्या त्वमघस्य । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी ।
> अहतमेषद्युद्धार्थनागच्छद्रक्षो भिनदः अभिनत् । यद्यदा च शक्त्या मित्रक्रुवो
> मित्राणां क्रूरस्य कर्मणः कर्तारो जनाः पृथिव्याः संबंधिनि शसने विशसनस्थाने
> गावो न पशव इवापृगापर्चनाहताः संतोऽमुयानया पृथिव्या संगता युद्धे
> शयंते शेरते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when, or where, will that weapon or arrow of yours be, which is to be directed and hurled against the enemies, when with your weapon you split the demon who comes eager for battle, **NOTE** and when those who betray their friends and do cruel deeds, belonging to the earth, struck down, like cattle at the place of slaughter, lie united with this earth in battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अघस्य (*aghasya*)—sinful in deed
- एषत् (*eṣat*)—and eager for battle
- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the demon
- भिनदः (*bhinadaḥ*)—you split
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—belonging to the earth
- मित्रक्रुवः (*mitrakruvaḥ*)—the wicked who betray their friends
- शसने (*śasane*)—at the time of cutting
- गावो न (*gāvo na*)—as cattle fall and writhe on the ground
- आपृक् (*āpṛk*)—when struck with the thunderbolt
- आमुया (*āmuyā*)—joined with the earth
- शयंते (*śayaṃte*)—they roll about, then
- ते (*te*)—your
- साचेत्या (*sācetyā*)—the weapon that is to be hurled against the enemies
- कर्हि स्वित् (*karhi svit*)—in what place
- आसत् (*āsat*)—will it be?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when you split the demon who is sinful in deed and eager for battle, and when the wicked who belong to the earth and betray their friends are struck down by your thunderbolt and roll about on the ground as cattle roll about at the time of their cutting, then where will your weapon be, which is to be hurled against those enemies?

##### English translation
Where was your (shaft), Indra, (which ought) to be hurled (against your enemies) when you clove the Rakshasas hastening to war, and when the Mitrakrus lay on the ground there in confusion like cattle at the place of immolation ?

> अंधेन । अमित्राः । तमसा । सचंतां । सुज्योतिषः । अक्तवः । तान् । अभि ।  
> स्युरितिस्सुः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शत्रूयंतो मह्यत्यंतं व्राधंतोऽस्मान्बाधमानाः ओगणासः
> संघीभूता ये शत्रवो नोऽस्मानभि ततस्रे निक्षिपंति तेऽमित्राः शत्रवोऽंधेन
> तमसा महतांधकारेण सचंतां । संगच्छंतां । किंच तानमित्रान् सुज्योतिषो
> दिवसा अक्तवो रात्रयश्चाभि ष्युः । अभिभवंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, those enemies who desire to be our foes, who exceedingly oppress us, and who, assembled in a mass, cast themselves upon us: let those enemies be joined with blind, that is, great darkness. Further, may the bright days and the nights overpower those enemies.

## Sūkta 90 (Maṇḍala 10)

**Introduction**

Apart from the गायत्रीमंत्र (*gāyatrīmaṃtra*), it is the पुरुषसूक्त (*puruṣasūkta*) that is most used in the ऋग्वेद (*ṛgveda*). In its excellence and in its treatment of its subject, since the doctrines set out in it are very profound, and since weighty matters are contained in it, such as the nature of the Supreme Person (the Supreme Brahman), his power and capacity, the account of creation, the origin of the Vedas and the rest, and the nature of sacrifice, this पुरुषसूक्त (*puruṣasūkta*) has exceptional importance. With slight differences this पुरुषसूक्त (*puruṣasūkta*) is recited also in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the कृष्णयजुर्वेद (*kṛṣṇayajurveda*) (Tai. Ā. 3-12, 13), in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā of the शुक्लयजुर्वेद (*śuklayajurveda*) (Vā. Saṃ. 31-1 to 16), and in the अथर्ववेद (*atharvaveda*) (अथर्ववेद (*atharvaveda*) 19-6). Besides this, an explanation of some parts of this sūkta is found in works such as the शतपथब्राह्मण (*śatapathabrāhmaṇa*), the तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मण (*taittirīyabrāhmaṇa*), the तैत्तिरीय आरण्यक (*taittirīya āraṇyaka*), the निरुक्त (*nirukta*), the श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषत्तु (*śvetāśvataropaniṣattu*) and the बृहदारण्यकोपनिषत्तु (*bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣattu*).

Even among English scholars there are various differences of opinion about the antiquity of this sūkta. Because this sūkta describes the order of origin of the four castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇa, it is the opinion of scholars such as Max Muller that this kind of division of castes did not exist in very ancient times, and that therefore this sūkta cannot be regarded as very ancient. Scholars such as Dr. Haug hold that, since words such as ब्राह्मण (*brāhmaṇa*) are found in other mantras of the ऋग्वेद (*ṛgveda*), since its language is not modern, and since the question of the human sacrifice is stated in it, it is proper that this sūkta should belong to the group of ancient sūktas. We shall examine this matter on another occasion.

### Printed p. 683

The reason why this sūkta is called the पुरुषसूक्त (*puruṣasūkta*) is that the greatness of the Puruṣa is set forth in it. Puruṣa here does not mean "a man", the sense of the word पुरुष (*puruṣa*) used in worldly usage to indicate the difference of sex between woman and man. The meaning is the Supreme Person, the Lord of all. That Supreme Person, or Parabrahman, has neither difference of sex nor form. There are many Śrutis that set forth that Puruṣa means Parabrahman. Among them the chief works are the त्रित्तिरीयारण्यक (*trittirīyāraṇyaka*), the तैत्तिरीयोपनिषत् (*taittirīyopaniṣat*), the बृहदारण्यकोपनिषत् (*bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣat*), the श्वेताश्वतरोपनिषत् (*śvetāśvataropaniṣat*), the वाजसनेय संहिता (*vājasaneya saṃhitā*), the अथर्ववेद (*atharvaveda*) and the निरुक्त (*nirukta*). Besides these, there is a detailed explanation of it also in the Purāṇas such as the भागवत (*bhāgavata*) and the विष्णु पुराण (*viṣṇu purāṇa*).

In the तैत्तिरीयारण्यक (*taittirīyāraṇyaka*) there is a tale about how the name Puruṣa came to the Parabrahman, who is denoted by words such as Parameśvara and Prajāpati. It is described here. That before creation everything consisted of water, and how Prajāpati then made creation, is told in the शैत्तिरीयारण्यक (*śaittirīyāraṇyaka*) (Tai. A. 1.23) thus— **NOTE**

आपो वा इदमासन्स्तिलमेव ! स प्रजापतिरेकः पुष्करपर्णॆ समभवत् । तस्यांतर्मनसि कामः समवर्तत । इदग्ं सृजेयमिति । तस्माद्यत्पुरुषो मनसाभिगच्छति । तद्वाचा वदति । तक्कर्मणा करोति । तदेषाभ्यनूक्ता । कामस्तदग्रे समवर्तताधि । मनसो रेतः प्रथमं यदासीत् । सतो बंधुमसति निरविंदन् । कृदि प्रतीष्या कवयो मनीषेति । उप्पैनं तदुप नमति । यत्कामो भवति । य एवं वेद । स तपोऽतप्यत । स तपस्तप्ता । शरीरमधूनुत ॥ (*āpo vā idamāsanstilameva ! sa prajāpatirekaḥ puṣkaraparṇè samabhavat | tasyāṃtarmanasi kāmaḥ samavartata | idagṃ sṛjeyamiti | tasmādyatpuruṣo manasābhigacchati | tadvācā vadati | takkarmaṇā karoti | tadeṣābhyanūktā | kāmastadagre samavartatādhi | manaso retaḥ prathamaṃ yadāsīt | sato baṃdhumasati niraviṃdan | kṛdi pratīṣyā kavayo manīṣeti | uppainaṃ tadupa namati | yatkāmo bhavati | ya evaṃ veda | sa tapo 'tapyata | sa tapastaptā | śarīramadhūnuta ‖*)

(Trai. Ā. 1-23-19) **NOTE**

Before the creation of this world that is seen by our eyes, water alone filled everywhere. There was nothing else. There were no gods, no men, no other material things at all. In the middle of that water that covered everywhere, on a lotus leaf (पुष्करपर्ण (*puṣkaraparṇa*)) Prajāpati alone was present. Then in the mind of that Prajāpati the wish arose to create this world. In the world, among men and the others created by Prajāpati, before doing any act, when the desire or wish to do that act arises, that person speaks that wish in words. After that he sets about doing the act. Just as in this worldly practice, to Prajāpati also, when the wish to create the world arose, he uttered it in a sentence and set about the work. This matter—

### Printed p. 684

is stated in the Ṛk that reads कामस्तदग्रे समवर्तताधि मनसो रेतः प्रथमं यदासीत् । सतो बंधुमसति निरविंदन् हृदि प्रतीष्या कवयो मनीषा ॥ (*kāmastadagre samavartatādhi manaso retaḥ prathamaṃ yadāsīt | sato baṃdhumasati niraviṃdan hṛdi pratīṣyā kavayo manīṣā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-129-4). The wish to create the world arose first in the mind of Parameśvara (Prajāpati). Just as the semen or seed of the male is the first cause of the generation of offspring, so for Parameśvara's creation of the world his wish to create becomes the seed, that is, the cause. This wish arose first in Prajāpati. That wish itself, turned into action, became the creation of the world. The chief purport of this Ṛk is that the wise, who are of surpassing understanding and intelligence, can by deliberating well in their minds know the secret of such matters as the attainment of another birth, which binds beings through the deeds and the like done by creatures in the former kalpa. Therefore the man who knows the greatness of desire obtains it. In this way Prajāpati performed austerity (तपस्सु (*tapassu*)) with the wish to create. When ṛṣis, men and others perform austerity, they wear out the body with toil through hard practices such as drying up the body and keeping vows. But in the matter of Prajāpati's austerity there is no such drying up of the body. There is only reflection or meditation. For he is true in his resolve; it is enough if he meditates that something should be so, and so it comes to be. He need not, like others, set about works with the body or with limbs such as the hands. Prajāpati, having performed such austerity in the form of meditation, once shook (set trembling) his body.

तस्य यन्माग्ंसमासीत् । ततोऽरुणाः केतवो वातरशना ऋषय उदतिष्ठन् । ये नखाः । ते वैखानसाः । ये वालाः । ते वालखिल्याः । यो रसः । सोऽपां । अंतरतः कूर्मं भूतग्ं सर्पंतं । तमब्रवीत् । नुम वै त्वङ्म्याग्ंसा । समभूत् । नेत्यब्रवीत् । पूर्वमेवाहमिहासमिति । (*tasya yanmāgṃsamāsīt | tato 'ruṇāḥ ketavo vātaraśanā ṛṣaya udatiṣṭhan | ye nakhāḥ | te vaikhānasāḥ | ye vālāḥ | te vālakhilyāḥ | yo rasaḥ | so 'pāṃ | aṃtarataḥ kūrmaṃ bhūtagṃ sarpaṃtaṃ | tamabravīt | numa vai tvaṅmyāgṃsā | samabhūt | netyabravīt | pūrvamevāhamihāsamiti |*) तत्पुरुषस्य पुरुषत्वं । स सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः । सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् । भूत्योदतिष्ठत् । तमब्रवीत् । त्वं वै पूर्वग्ं समभूः । त्वमिदं पूर्वः कुरुष्टेति । (*tatpuruṣasya puruṣatvaṃ | sa sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ | sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt | bhūtyodatiṣṭhat | tamabravīt | tvaṃ vai pūrvagṃ samabhūḥ | tvamidaṃ pūrvaḥ kuruṣṭeti |*) स इत आदायापः । अंजलिना पुरस्तादुपादधात् । एवा ह्येवेति । तत आदित्य उदतिष्ठत् । सा प्राचीदिक् । (*sa ita ādāyāpaḥ | aṃjalinā purastādupādadhāt | evā hyeveti | tata āditya udatiṣṭhat | sā prācīdik |*) अथारुणः केतुर्दक्षिणत उपादधात् । एवाह्यग्न इति । ततो ना अग्निरुदतिष्ठत् । सा दक्षिणादिक् । (*athāruṇaḥ keturdakṣiṇata upādadhāt | evāhyagna iti | tato nā agnirudatiṣṭhat | sā dakṣiṇādik |*) अथारुणः केतुः पश्चादुपावधात् । एवा हि वायो इति ! ततो वायुरुदतिष्ठत् ; सा प्रतीचीदिक् । (*athāruṇaḥ ketuḥ paścādupāvadhāt | evā hi vāyo iti ! tato vāyurudatiṣṭhat ; sā pratīcīdik |*) अथारुणः केतुरुत्तरत उपादधात् । एवाहींद्रेति । ततो ना इंद्र उदतिष्ठत् । (*athāruṇaḥ keturuttarata upādadhāt | evāhīṃdreti | tato nā iṃdra udatiṣṭhat |*)

### Printed p. 685

सोदीची दिक् । अथारुणः केतुर्मध्य उपादधात् । एवा हि पूषन्निति । ततो वै पूषोदतिष्ठत् । सेयं दिक् । अथारुणः केतुरुपरिष्टादुपादधात् । एवा हि देवा इति । ततो देवमनुष्याः पितरः ! गंधर्वाप्स. रसश्चोधतिष्ठन् । सोर्ध्वा दिक् । या विप्रुषो वि परापतन् । ताभ्योS. सुरा रक्षागंसि पिशाचाश्चोदतिष्ठन् । तस्मात्ते पराभवन् । विपुड्भो हि ते समभवन् ॥ (*sodīcī dik | athāruṇaḥ keturmadhya upādadhāt | evā hi pūṣanniti | tato vai pūṣodatiṣṭhat | seyaṃ dik | athāruṇaḥ keturupariṣṭādupādadhāt | evā hi devā iti | tato devamanuṣyāḥ pitaraḥ ! gaṃdharvāpsa. rasaścodhatiṣṭhan | sordhvā dik | yā vipruṣo vi parāpatan | tābhyoS. surā rakṣāgaṃsi piśācāścodatiṣṭhan | tasmātte parābhavan | vipuḍbho hi te samabhavan ‖*)

(Trai. 3, 1-23-2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7) **NOTE**

When he shook thus, from his flesh arose three kinds of ṛṣis called Aruṇas, Ketus and Vātaraśanas. From the nail (nakha) arose the sages called Vaikhānasas, and from the hair (keśa) the ṛṣis named Vālakhilyas. From the rasa (blood), the essence of the body, a tortoise (kūrma) was born. Prajāpati saw that tortoise moving about in the middle of the water and said thus: "O tortoise, you have arisen from my flesh and skin." The tortoise said: "Not so; I have not arisen from your flesh. Only this tortoise form, which is my body, has arisen. I, who exist in the form of consciousness in all things, **NOTE** was in the water even before the arising of the tortoise. Because I have existed from before, the name Puruṣa has come to me." Having said so, in order to manifest his own power he took the Virāṭ form (the great form) and appeared there with thousands of heads, thousands of eyes, thousands of feet and other innumerable limbs. Then Prajāpati, seeing the Supreme Self in the Virāṭ form, said: "You yourself make the world." Accordingly that Supreme Self, filling his hand (cupped palm) with water and facing east, uttered the words एवाह्येव (*evāhyeva*) and scattered that water upward. From it Āditya arose, and that direction came to be called the east. In the same way, when he scattered water toward another direction with एवाह्यग्ने (*evāhyagne*), Agni arose there, and that became the south. Another time, when he scattered water with एवा हि वायो (*evā hi vāyo*), Vāyu arose, and that became the west. Then, when he scattered it with एवाहींद्र (*evāhīṃdra*), Indra arose, and that became the north. In the middle, when he scattered water with एवाहि पूषन् (*evāhi pūṣan*), the god Pūṣan arose; that is the lower part. In the upper part, when he scattered water with एवा हि देवाः (*evā hi devāḥ*), there arose the other gods, men, fathers, gandharvas and apsarases. That became known as the upward direction. Thus, while the Supreme Self was scattering water all around, from some drops of that water that were flung far and fell, the asuras, the hosts of rākṣasas and the piśācas arose. Because they arose from drops flung far away, these asuras and the others were defeated by the gods.

तदेषाभ्य नूक्ता । आप्रो ह यद्भृहतीर्गर्भमायन् । दक्षं दधाना (*tadeṣābhya nūktā | āpro ha yadbhṛhatīrgarbhamāyan | dakṣaṃ dadhānā*)

### Printed p. 686

जनयंतीः स्वयंभुं । तत इमेऽध्यसृज्यंत सर्गाः । अद्भो वा इदग्ं समभूत् । तस्मादिदग्ं सर्वं ब्रह्म स्वयंभ्विति । तस्मादिदग्ं सर्वग्ं शिथिलमिवाध्रुवमिवाभवत् । प्रजापतिर्नाव तत् । आत्मनात्मानं विधाय । तदेवानु प्रानिशत् ॥ (*janayaṃtīḥ svayaṃbhuṃ | tata ime 'dhyasṛjyaṃta sargāḥ | adbho vā idagṃ samabhūt | tasmādidagṃ sarvaṃ brahma svayaṃbhviti | tasmādidagṃ sarvagṃ śithilamivādhruvamivābhavat | prajāpatirnāva tat | ātmanātmānaṃ vidhāya | tadevānu prāniśat ‖*)

(Śrī. Ā. 1-23-8) **NOTE**

The account of how gods, men and the others were created from water in this way is stated clearly in the Ṛk of the Ṛgveda—

आपो ह यद्बृहतीर्विश्वमायन्गर्भं दधाना जनयंतीरग्निं । ततो देवानां समवर्ततासुरेकः कस्मै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ (*āpo ha yadbṛhatīrviśvamāyangarbhaṃ dadhānā janayaṃtīragniṃ | tato devānāṃ samavartatāsurekaḥ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-7; अथर्व (*atharva*) 4-2-6; वाजसनेय (*vājasaneya*) Saṃ 27,-25; 32.7; Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-1; 4.1-8.5; Tai. Ā. 1.23-8)

Before creation the water that covered everywhere bore a germ. That germ grew and produced the Supreme Self (Prajāpati) in the form of a tortoise, whose name is Svāyuṃbhuva. That is, the Supreme Self himself appeared from the water in the form of a tortoise. After that, all the other creations proceeded from that tortoise-formed Prajāpati. Therefore everything arose from these waters. Therefore the whole created world is also of the nature of Brahman called Svayambhū. Because it arose from water, the whole world, without a firm foundation, was shaking in the middle of the water like waves. Therefore Prajāpati, whose nature is being, consciousness and bliss, by his power fitted a part of himself into things according to the form of each thing, that is, he himself entered into them by his consciousness (चिद्रूप (*cidrūpa*)) and established them firmly so that they would not shake.

तदेषाभ्यनूक्ता । विधाय लोकान्विधाय भूतानि । विधाय सर्वाः प्रदिशो दिशश्च । प्रजापतिः प्रथमजा ऋतस्य । आत्मानात्मानमभिसंविवेशेति । सर्वमेवेद (*tadeṣābhyanūktā | vidhāya lokānvidhāya bhūtāni | vidhāya sarvāḥ pradiśo diśaśca | prajāpatiḥ prathamajā ṛtasya | ātmānātmānamabhisaṃviveśeti | sarvameveda*)

(Trai. Ā. 1.23.9) **NOTE**

This account is told thus in the **NOTE**

विधाय लोकान्विधाय भूतानि विधाय सर्वाः प्रदिशो दिशश्च । प्रजापतिः प्रथमजा ऋतस्य आत्मनात्मानमभिसंविवेश ॥ (*vidhāya lokānvidhāya bhūtāni vidhāya sarvāḥ pradiśo diśaśca | prajāpatiḥ prathamajā ṛtasya ātmanātmānamabhisaṃviveśa ‖*)

Prajāpati carried on the work of creation from the water that existed before everything. He made this world that is seen by our eyes, and all the beings that dwell in them, that is, the creatures, and the quarters and the intermediate quarters, and entered into them in the form of consciousness: this is

### Printed p. 687

the chief purport of this mantra. (This mantra is not in the Ṛgveda. The commentators have said that it is in another śākhā. Which śākhā it is cannot be known.) Prajāpati, having thus finished the whole work of creation and entered by his form of consciousness into the things created, stands within them and carries on the affairs of the world. The man who knows this order of creation of the Supreme Self obtains the fruits that a man should obtain in this world, enjoys them and is happy. Since many profound Vedāntic principles are contained in every Ṛk of this sūkta, those matters will be explained at the proper places.

The sūkta that is addressed to the Supreme Person and praises the greatness of the Supreme Person is called the पुरुषसूक्त (*puruṣasūkta*).

द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च । क्षरस्सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते । उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः । यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः ॥ (*dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca | kṣarassarvāṇi bhūtāni kūṭastho 'kṣara ucyate | uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ | yo lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ ‖*)

The two principles called क्षर (*kṣara*) and अक्षर (*akṣara*) are particular manifestations of Īśvara. The mass of the world that, having arisen, then perishes, has the form of the Puruṣa called क्षर (*kṣara*). In contrast to this, the Self that has attained eternal existence, and that stands in its pure own nature, without relation to the world, which is of non-conscious nature, is called the Puruṣa named अक्षर (*akṣara*). Īśvara is beyond these two groups of things, क्षर (*kṣara*) and अक्षर (*akṣara*). The Śrutis praise him as the highest Person. He is the Supreme Self. This Supreme Person pervades the three worlds and holds all of them in himself. The aim of the Puruṣasūkta is to praise the greatness of such a Supreme Person, who pervades the world and is also beyond the world.

अव्ययः कः ? ईश्वरः सर्वज्ञः नारायणाख्यः ईशनशीलः । (*avyayaḥ kaḥ ? īśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ nārāyaṇākhyaḥ īśanaśīlaḥ |*)

(Bha. Gī. Paṃ. Bhā. 15-17) **NOTE**

Śaṅkarācārya has made clear in his commentary on the Bhagavadgītā who the Īśvara free from decay is: he is the Supreme Self in the form of Nārāyaṇa, the lord of the whole world. Since the mantras of the Puruṣasūkta are addressed to Nārāyaṇa, the highest Person, it has the name Nārāyaṇa or Nārāyaṇīya.

Moreover, since this sūkta was seen and recited by a great ṛṣi named Nārāyaṇa, it can also be said that the derivation of the name of this sūkta is that it has the name Nārāyaṇa or Nārāyaṇīya. This section is, as पूर्वनारायण (*pūrvanārāyaṇa*) and उत्तरनारायण (*uttaranārāyaṇa*),

### Printed p. 688

in two parts in the तैत्तिरीयारण्यक (*taittirīyāraṇyaka*). Of them, the पूर्वनारायण (*pūrvanārāyaṇa*) is the one that is famous as the Puruṣasūkta.

Who is the great ṛṣi named Nārāyaṇa, the seer of the Puruṣasūkta? Whether this ṛṣi is a historical person like Gotama and Viśvāmitra, it is not easy to state an exact opinion. The name Nārāyaṇa is not specified anywhere in the Ṛk-saṃhitā. In the Brāhmaṇas and the rest, or in the Upaniṣads, no seer of the sūkta named Nārāyaṇa is indicated. Neither the authors of the Nirukta nor the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have told this. Therefore, just as in some other places the name of the seer of sūktas is told according to the subject of the sūktas, so for this sūkta too the naming of the seer is according to the subject of the sūkta. In the same way some other illustrations can be shown. For example, for the sūkta addressed to Hiraṇyagarbha, हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre*) (10-121), it is stated that Hiraṇyagarbha Prājāpatya, the son of Prajāpati, is the seer. The sūktas 10-81 and 82 praise the greatness of Viśvakarman. It is stated that Viśvakarman Bhauvana, that is, Viśvakarman the son of Bhuvana, is the seer of these sūktas. Likewise, the sūktas 10-83 and 84, यस्ते मन्योऽविधद्वज्र सायक (*yaste manyo 'vidhadvajra sāyaka*) and त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुजंतः (*tvayā manyo sarathamārujaṃtaḥ*), are also known as composed by the great ṛṣi Manyu, the son of Tapas. The sūkta नासदासीन्नो सदासीत् (*nāsadāsīnno sadāsīt*) (10-129) is a sūkta that praises Prajāpati. The saying that this sūkta was seen by Prajāpati Pārameṣṭhya also follows the same tradition. In the same way the view that the laudatory sūkta यो यज्ञो विश्वतस्तंतुभिः (*yo yajño viśvatastaṃtubhiḥ*) (10-120) was seen by Yajña Prājāpatya is likewise stated with reference to the main subject of the sūkta.

If these many examples are examined, it can be said that for the present Puruṣasūkta also, according to the subject of this sūkta, the same name is applied to the seer of the sūkta. But here there is room for another question. It is this: the main subject of the Puruṣasūkta is Īśvara, who is famous by names such as Puruṣa, Parama-puruṣa and Paramātman. The word Nārāyaṇa is not found here at all. How, then, is the name of the seer of the sūkta famous as Nārāyaṇa? If one objects thus, the answer, on the basis of Śruti passages, can be that the two names Puruṣa and Nārāyaṇa are particular manifestations of the one non-dual Īśvara and are not different.

Just as that which is related to Rāma is called the Rāmāyaṇa, one who is related to Nara can be called Nārāyaṇa. Here it can also be understood as the son of Nara. The word नर (*nara*) is also used in the very sense of Puruṣa. The origin of Puruṣa from the Īśvara called Virāṭ, and the origin of Virāṭ from the Supreme Person

### Printed p. 689

as has been stated in the Puruṣasūkta itself, Nārāyaṇa is the son of Puruṣa. Nārāyaṇa himself is Puruṣa; father and son are one and the same. This is not said in the worldly sense but in the spiritual sense. Or else, the words Prajāpati, Viśvakarman, Hiraṇyagarbha and so on are all synonymous names of the Supreme Self (Paramātman) who is called Puruṣa. Whenever the fundamental principle of the Supreme Self is described by these synonymous names, there is a description that the Supreme Self moved about, before creation, upon the support of the waters (udaka).

तमिद्दर्भं प्रथमं दध्र आपो यत्र देवाः समगच्छंत विश्वे । अजस्य नाभावध्येकमर्पितं यस्मिन्विश्वानि भुवनानि तस्थुः ॥ (*tamiddarbhaṃ prathamaṃ dadhra āpo yatra devāḥ samagacchaṃta viśve | ajasya nābhāvadhyekamarpitaṃ yasminviśvāni bhuvanāni tasthuḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-6)

The waters first bore that Supreme Self, in the form of Viśvakarman, in whom all the gods have assembled together. The sūkta that praises Viśvakarman and expounds the spiritual principle states that this non-dual Supreme Principle contains all the worlds; it is just like this.

आपो ह यद्बृहतीर्गर्भमायन् गर्भं दधाना जनयंतीरग्निं । ततो देवानां समवर्ततासुरेकः कस्यै देवाय हविषा विधेम ॥ (*āpo ha yadbṛhatīrgarbhamāyan garbhaṃ dadhānā janayaṃtīragniṃ | tato devānāṃ samavartatāsurekaḥ kasyai devāya haviṣā vidhema ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-121-7)

The sūkta that praises Hiraṇyagarbha says that the waters, which have the natural capacity to bring forth all created beings, bore in their womb Prajāpati, who is of the form of Hiraṇyagarbha; and likewise passages such as सलिलं सर्वमा इदं (*salilaṃ sarvamā idaṃ*) (10.29-3) praise the Supreme Self who moved upon the water before creation. In the same way, in the present context too, it can be said that the word Nārāyaṇa shows the direct relation of the Supreme Self with the water. The authors of the Smṛtis and the Paurāṇikas make this very meaning clear. How? Thus:

आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः । ता यदस्यायनं पूर्व० तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ (*āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ | tā yadasyāyanaṃ pūrva0 tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ‖*)
(Manu 1-10)

The name nārā is well known for the āpas (waters). These very waters have arisen from the Supreme Self, who is called Nara. When he was in the form of Brahman, these were his support. For that reason the Supreme Self has the name Nārāyaṇa. That is, he who has the nāras (waters) as his ayana (support) is Nārāyaṇa. The very waters that bore the Supreme Self called Viśvakarman, Hiraṇyagarbha and Prajāpati are the waters that bore the Supreme Self called Nārāyaṇa.

### Printed p. 690

Thus it can only be said that different sūkta-s have recited one and the same description in different ways; it cannot be said that the elements of this description are different. Therefore Parama-puruṣa and Nārāyaṇa are synonymous names. Since the subject of the sūkta that describes the greatness of Puruṣa is the Puruṣa called Nārāyaṇa, it would not be wrong to say that, in accordance with the subject of the sūkta, the name of the seer too is Nārāyaṇa. Śruti passages also are the authority for this. For example, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa describes in the following way the occasion that points to the identity of Puruṣa and Nārāyaṇa.

पुरुषो ह नारायणोऽकामयत। अतितिष्ठेयग्ं सर्वाणि भूतान्यहमेवेदग्ं सर्वग्ं स्यामिति स एतं पुरुषमॆधं पंचरात्रं यज्ञक्रतुमपश्यत्तमाहरत्तेनायजत तेनेष्टात्यतिष्ठत्सर्वाणि भूतानीदग्ं सर्वमभवदतितिष्ठति सर्वाणि भूतानीदग्ं सर्वं भवति य एवं विद्वान् पुरुषमेधेन यजते यो वै तदेवं वेद ॥ (*puruṣo ha nārāyaṇo 'kāmayata| atitiṣṭheyagṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyahamevedagṃ sarvagṃ syāmiti sa etaṃ puruṣamèdhaṃ paṃcarātraṃ yajñakratumapaśyattamāharattenāyajata teneṣṭātyatiṣṭhatsarvāṇi bhūtānīdagṃ sarvamabhavadatitiṣṭhati sarvāṇi bhūtānīdagṃ sarvaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān puruṣamedhena yajate yo vai tadevaṃ veda ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-6-1-1)

Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa wished: "May I surpass all beings; may I alone, pervading all this, be the non-dual one." Then, by meditation, he came to know the greatness of the rite called Pañcarātra, which is of the form of the Puruṣamedha. Afterwards he also performed that sacrifice. As its result he pervaded the entire world and also extended beyond it. Thus there is praise of Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa: one who knows this principle and performs the Puruṣamedha in the same way grows, pervading all and surpassing all. Moreover, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also has the description that, by the performance of this sacrifice of five nights, a greatness arises for the very sūkta that is addressed to Puruṣa and praises him, and that it becomes famous throughout the world.

पुरुषग्ं ह नारायणं प्रजापतिरुवाच । यजस्व यजस्वेति स होवाच यजस्व यजस्वेति वाव त्वं मामात्थ त्रिरयक्षि वसवः प्रातःसवनेन रुद्रा माध्यंदिनेन सवनेनादित्यास्तृतीयसवनेनाथ मम यज्ञवास्त्वेवाहमास इति ॥ (*puruṣagṃ ha nārāyaṇaṃ prajāpatiruvāca | yajasva yajasveti sa hovāca yajasva yajasveti vāva tvaṃ māmāttha trirayakṣi vasavaḥ prātaḥsavanena rudrā mādhyaṃdinena savanenādityāstṛtīyasavanenātha mama yajñavāstvevāhamāsa iti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 12-3-4-1)

Prajāpati instructed Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa: "Perform the sacrifice and offer the oblation." Then Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa answered: "Your instruction is well and good; I too have performed the sacrifice three times and offered the oblation. When I offered the morning libation, the Vasus grew strong; at the midday libation the Rudras; and at the third libation the Ādityas. All of them occupied all the regions. For me only the place of the sacrificial offering has remained; I sit upon that alone." Then Prajāpati again said:

### Printed p. 691

यज्ञस्यैवाहं वै ते तद्वक्ष्यामि यथा त उक्कानि मणिरिव सूत्र ओतानि भविष्यंति सूत्रमिव वा मणाविति । (*yajñasyaivāhaṃ vai te tadvakṣyāmi yathā ta ukkāni maṇiriva sūtra otāni bhaviṣyaṃti sūtramiva vā maṇāviti |*)
(Śa. Brā. 12-3-4-2)

"Perform the sacrifice again and offer the oblation. As a result, the mantras that praise you, Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa, will become famous in the world. In the way that beads are strung on a thread, or in the way that the thread that joins the beads, united with the beads, becomes the maker of beauty, in that way the mantras that praise you will become a source of delight." So he said.

But what is this sacrifice? What is its nature? What is the satra of the form of five nights? This will be examined in the present context, and afterwards it will be explained how the Śruti passages have described the nature of the Supreme Person who carries out this sacrifice. The above explanations show that Nārāyaṇa in the form of Puruṣa is the seer named Nārāyaṇa, the maker of the sūkta, and that Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Self, is the performer of the sacrifice of the Pāñcarātra form. The very sacrifice by which, when performed with the Puruṣamedha as a five-night rite, the business of the world was brought about, is also laid down in the Puruṣasūkta. Here the explanation is that the gods performed the sacrifice by offering as oblation the Puruṣa himself. As the result of this sacrifice, a fivefold creation comes about. They are as follows:

1) पशून् ताश्चक्रे वायव्यानारण्यान् ग्राम्याश्च ये (*paśūn tāścakre vāyavyānāraṇyān grāmyāśca ye*)

As the result of this sacrifice, the birds that move in the atmosphere, the wild beasts of the forest, and the cattle, horses and others that dwell in villages came into being.

2) ऋचः सामानि जज्जिरे । छंदांसि जज्जिरे तस्मादजुस्तस्मादजायत ॥ (*ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajjire | chaṃdāṃsi jajjire tasmādajustasmādajāyata ‖*)

From that same Virāṭ-puruṣa, as the result of the sacrifice, the Ṛk mantras and the Sāmans came into being. From him also the metres such as the Gāyatrī, and the Yajus formulas, came into being.

3) ब्राह्मणोऽस्य मुखमासीद्वाहू राजन्यः कृतः (*brāhmaṇo 'sya mukhamāsīdvāhū rājanyaḥ kṛtaḥ*)

As the result of this sacrifice, from the mouth of Puruṣa the Brāhmaṇa, from the arms the Kṣatriyas, from the thighs the Vaiśyas, and from the feet the Śūdras, all mankind, came into being.

4) चंद्रमा मनसो जातश्चक्षोः सूरो अजायत । मुखादिंद्रश्चाग्निश्च प्राणाद्वायुरजायत ॥ (*caṃdramā manaso jātaścakṣoḥ sūro ajāyata | mukhādiṃdraścāgniśca prāṇādvāyurajāyata ‖*)

From the mind of this Virāṭ-puruṣa the moon, from the eye the sun, from the mouth Indra and Agni, and likewise all the gods, came into being.

### Printed p. 692

5) नाभ्या आसीदंतरिक्षं शीर्षोण द्यौः समवर्तत । पद्भां भूमिर्दिशः शोत्रात्तथा लोका अकल्पयन् ॥ (*nābhyā āsīdaṃtarikṣaṃ śīrṣoṇa dyauḥ samavartata | padbhāṃ bhūmirdiśaḥ śotrāttathā lokā akalpayan ‖*)

As the result of the Virāṭ sacrifice, from the navel of Virāṭ-puruṣa the atmosphere, from the head the heavenly world, from the feet the earth, from the ear the directions, and thus all the worlds came into being. In some places the relation of cause and effect is shown, namely that the creation of the world, which consists of these five divisions, came about as the result of the sacrifice of five nights. These five parts are described in one way in one place and in another way in another. Explaining these same five elements in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, it says thus:

स एष पांक्तो यज्ञः पांक्तः पशुः पांक्तः पुरुषः पांक्तमिदं सर्वं यदिदं किं च तदिदं सर्वमाप्नोति ॥ (*sa eṣa pāṃkto yajñaḥ pāṃktaḥ paśuḥ pāṃktaḥ puruṣaḥ pāṃktamidaṃ sarvaṃ yadidaṃ kiṃ ca tadidaṃ sarvamāpnoti ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 1-4-13)

The sacrifice is fivefold; the sacrificial animal is fivefold; Puruṣa too is of five kinds. This universe, and everything contained in the universe, exists only in five kinds. One who knows this principle obtains all good. So it is said. In the same way, stating this very matter in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad:

साङ्कं ना इदग्ं सर्वं । साङ्कीनैव साङ्कग् स्पृणोतिति । (*sāṅkaṃ nā idagṃ sarvaṃ | sāṅkīnaiva sāṅkag spṛṇotiti |*)
(Tai. U. 1.-7) **NOTE**

All this universe consists of five kinds. The scholar who knows the universe that comprises these five kinds of principles also obtains good of five kinds. So it praises.

Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa performed the universal sacrifice of the form of five nights. As its result he became all-pervading and surpassed everything. Just as it has been praised, in passages beginning विश्वकर्मन् हविषा वावृधानः (*viśvakarman haviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ*) (10-81-6), that Viśvakarman, having praised Viśvakarman and offered himself as the oblation, became pervader of the world, in the same way here the sacrifice performed by the Supreme Person and its fruits are praised.

If the controller of the world and the lord of the world is denoted here by the word Puruṣa, then the derivation of the word Puruṣa here, and the way in which this word Puruṣa shows lordship of the world and control of the world, are matters to be examined in the present context.

There are two kinds of derivation of the word Puruṣa. Both kinds of derivation explain the nature of Puruṣa as the Supreme Self. First:

आत्मेवैदमग्र आसीत्पुरुषविधः सोऽनुवीक्ष्य नान्यदात्मनोऽपश्यत्सोऽहमस्मीत्यग्रे व्याहरत्ततोऽहं नामाभवत्तस्मादस्येतर्ह्यामंत्रितोऽहमयमित्येवाग्र उक्ताथान्यन्नाम प्रब्रूते यदस्य भवति स यत्पू- र्वोऽस्मात्सर्वस्मात्सर्वान्साप्मन औषत्तस्मात्पुरुष ओषति ह वै स तं योऽस्मात्सूर्वो बुभूषति य एवं वेद । (*ātmevaidamagra āsītpuruṣavidhaḥ so 'nuvīkṣya nānyadātmano 'paśyatso 'hamasmītyagre vyāharattato 'haṃ nāmābhavattasmādasyetarhyāmaṃtrito 'hamayamityevāgra uktāthānyannāma prabrūte yadasya bhavati sa yatpū- rvo 'smātsarvasmātsarvānsāpmana auṣattasmātpuruṣa oṣati ha vai sa taṃ yo 'smātsūrvo bubhūṣati ya evaṃ veda |*)

### Printed p. 693

(Bṛ. U. 1-4-1)

Before the creation of the world the Self, in the form of Puruṣa, was non-dual. Seeing that there was no one other than himself, he understood: "I am here." This notion of "I" is the root of all the personal dealings of all persons in the world. How this Self has the usage Puruṣa is as follows: before the creation of the world he burned (उष् (*uṣ*)-औषत् (*auṣat*)) all the sins, in advance (पूर्व (*pūrva*)). Therefore (पूर्व (*pūrva*)+उष् (*uṣ*)) the name पूरुषः (*pūruṣaḥ*) (पुरुषः (*puruṣaḥ*)) became famous. Such is the one kind of derivation. **NOTE**

Second:

पुरश्चक्रे द्विपदः पुरश्चक्रे चतुष्पदः । पुरः स पक्षी भूत्वा पुरः पुरुष आविशदिति ॥ स वा अयं पुरुषः सर्वासु पूर्षु पुरिशयोs नैनेव किंचनानावृतं नैनेन किंचनासंवृतं ॥ (*puraścakre dvipadaḥ puraścakre catuṣpadaḥ | puraḥ sa pakṣī bhūtvā puraḥ puruṣa āviśaditi ‖ sa vā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvāsu pūrṣu puriśayos naineva kiṃcanānāvṛtaṃ nainena kiṃcanāsaṃvṛtaṃ ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 2-5-18)

The Lord made cities in the form of human beings, with two feet. He also made cities in the form of animals and the like, with four feet; and, taking the form of a bird, he entered the cities of that form. Thus the name Puruṣa arises because he entered all the cities (bodies) produced from himself, and because he lies in these cities. There is nothing that is not covered by this Puruṣa, nor anything that is not enveloped by him. That is, he is all-pervading and the inner controller of all. Explaining this very matter, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa says:

इमे वै लोकाः पूरयमेव पुरुषो योऽयं पवते सोऽस्यां पुरि शेते तस्मात्पुरुषः ॥ (*ime vai lokāḥ pūrayameva puruṣo yo 'yaṃ pavate so 'syāṃ puri śete tasmātpuruṣaḥ ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 13-6.2-1)

All the worlds are like a fortress. Puruṣa fills them with air (vitality), and because he lies pervading all these worlds that are like a fortress (पुरि शेते (*puri śete*)), he has the name Puruṣa. So it is stated.

By the analogy of the human puruṣa who dwells in a body, the meaning is not that the nature of the Supreme Puruṣa, the Self of the universe, is likewise limited by distance and attended by limiting adjuncts like a human being. The entire universe is the body of this Supreme Puruṣa, and his nature transcends the universe. But the description is just like the description of a human body. How?

### Printed p. 694

पंच संपद्यंते पांक्तोऽयं पुरुषः पंचधा विहितो लोमानि त्वज्ञांसमस्थिमज्जा स यावानेव पुरुषस्तावंतं यजमानं संस्कृत्याग्नौ देवयोन्यां जुहोत्यग्निर्वॆ देवयोनिः सोग्नेर्देवयोन्या आहुतिभ्यः संभूय हिरण्यशरीर ऊर्ध्वः स्वर्गं लोकमेति । (*paṃca saṃpadyaṃte pāṃkto 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ paṃcadhā vihito lomāni tvajñāṃsamasthimajjā sa yāvāneva puruṣastāvaṃtaṃ yajamānaṃ saṃskṛtyāgnau devayonyāṃ juhotyagnirvè devayoniḥ sognerdevayonyā āhutibhyaḥ saṃbhūya hiraṇyaśarīra ūrdhvaḥ svargaṃ lokameti |*)
(Ai. Brā. 2-14)

(By the offering of the immortal oblation all wealth is obtained.) This is fivefold. Puruṣa too consists of five kinds of principles. By offering the oblation corresponding to these five principles, namely hair, skin, flesh, bone and fat, it is as if it were offered into Agni, the birthplace of all the gods. Since the nature of Agni too is fivefold in this way, Agni is satisfied by this offering of divided kind (this Agni is the reflection, of the form of radiance, of the Supreme Puruṣa). **NOTE**

Prajāpati is the Supreme Puruṣa; the Puruṣa who has a body composed of seventeen parts is Prajāpati. Prajāpati and Puruṣa are of the nature of Agni. How is that? Thus:

यद्वेव सप्तदश । सप्तदशो वै पुरुषो दश प्राणाश्चत्वार्यंगानि आत्मा पंचदशो ग्रीवाः षोडश्यः शिरः सप्तदशं पुरुषः प्रजापतिः प्रजापतिरग्निर्यावानग्निर्यावत्यस्य मात्रा तावतैवैनमेतत्समिंधे ॥ (*yadveva saptadaśa | saptadaśo vai puruṣo daśa prāṇāścatvāryaṃgāni ātmā paṃcadaśo grīvāḥ ṣoḍaśyaḥ śiraḥ saptadaśaṃ puruṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatiragniryāvānagniryāvatyasya mātrā tāvataivainametatsamiṃdhe ‖*)
(Śa. Brā. 6-2-2-9)

Puruṣa consists of seventeen principles. They are: ten vital breaths, four limbs; the self (body?) is the fifteenth; the throat is the sixteenth; the head is the seventeenth. The Puruṣa who consists of these seventeen principles is Prajāpati. Prajāpati is Agni. As the measure of Agni is, so is the measure of Prajāpati. Then what is the nature of the body of this Supreme Puruṣa, the Self of the universe? Which is his head? Which is his eye? Which is his breath? The answers to such questions are as follows:

तान्होवाचैते वै खलु यूयं पृथगिवेममात्मानं वैश्वानरं विद्वांसोऽन्नमत्थ यस्त्वेतमेवं प्रादेशमात्रमभिविमानमात्मानं वैश्वानरमुपास्ते स सर्वेषु लोकेषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु सर्वेष्वात्मस्वन्नमत्ति ॥ (*tānhovācaite vai khalu yūyaṃ pṛthagivemamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vidvāṃso 'nnamattha yastvetamevaṃ prādeśamātramabhivimānamātmānaṃ vaiśvānaramupāste sa sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣvātmasvannamatti ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 5-18-1) **NOTE**

Knowing this Self of the universe as different from you, you eat food. But he who worships the Self called Vaiśvānara, who is of the measure of a span (the detail of the description "span-measure" is given in the first of the words अत्यतिष्ठद्व शांगुलं (*atyatiṣṭhadva śāṃgulaṃ*)

### Printed p. 695

foot of the Ṛk is explained) **NOTE**. Those who worship this Self of the universe eat the food belonging to all the worlds, by the pervading power of the Self of the universe that lies hidden in all beings and in all selves.

तस्य ह ना एतस्यात्मनो वैश्वानरस्य मूर्धैव सतेजा चक्षुर्विश्वरूपः प्राणः पृथग्वर्तात्मा संदेहो बहुलो बस्ति रेव रयिः पृथिव्येव पादावुर एव वेदिर्लोमानि बर्हिर्हृदयं गार्हपत्यो मनोऽन्वाहार्यपचनआस्यमाहवनीयः ॥ (*tasya ha nā etasyātmano vaiśvānarasya mūrdhaiva satejā cakṣurviśvarūpaḥ prāṇaḥ pṛthagvartātmā saṃdeho bahulo basti reva rayiḥ pṛthivyeva pādāvura eva vedirlomāni barhirhṛdayaṃ gārhapatyo mano 'nvāhāryapacanaāsyamāhavanīyaḥ ‖*)
(Bhā. U. 5-18-2) **NOTE**

The radiant heaven is the head of the Self of the universe. Ādityā, of all forms, is the eye. The air, with its many courses, is the breath. The expansive sky is the body. The belly is the mine of wealth. The earth, the support of all, is the foot. The sacrificial ground is the heart. The darbha grass is the hair. The Gārhapatya fire is the heart. The Anvāhāryapacana is the mind. The Āhavanīya is the mouth.

अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयान् (*aṇoraṇīyān mahato mahīyān*). There is the description that this Supreme Puruṣa is smaller than the most minute thing and greater than the greatest thing. The description महतो महीयान् (*mahato mahīyān*) has been made clear by examples showing how this Supreme Self pervades the whole universe. In the same way the description अणोरणीयान् (*aṇoraṇīyān*) is made clear by some of the following Upaniṣad passages. And it is also described that this greatness, which is beyond the reach of sense perception, shines with exceedingly great light.

अंगुष्ठ मात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति । ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते ॥ (*aṃguṣṭha mātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati | īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate ‖*)

This Supreme Puruṣa, who is only of the measure of a thumb, is the inner controller in the self of every individual. He is the lord of all beings that existed before and of all things that will come into being hereafter. No one shrinks from him.

अंगुष्ठ मात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिवाधूमकः । ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः ॥ (*aṃguṣṭha mātraḥ puruṣo jyotirivādhūmakaḥ | īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ ‖*)
(Kaṭha. 4-13) **NOTE**

This Supreme Puruṣa, of the measure of a thumb, is like an exceedingly bright flame without smoke. He alone is the lord of the entire world. He alone is the non-dual lord today and for the ages that are to come.

### Printed p. 696

अंगुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषोंतरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये सन्नि विष्टः । तं स्वाच्छरीरात्पृवृहेन्मुंचादिवेषीकां धैर्य्येण । तं विद्याच्चुक्रममृतं तं विद्याच्चुक्रममृतमिति ॥ (*aṃguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣoṃtarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye sanni viṣṭaḥ | taṃ svāccharīrātpṛvṛhenmuṃcādiveṣīkāṃ dhairyyeṇa | taṃ vidyāccukramamṛtaṃ taṃ vidyāccukramamṛtamiti ‖*)
(Kaṭha. 6-17)

This Puruṣa, of the measure of a thumb, is always established in the heart of people. As one draws an arrow out of a reed, so one should make this Self come out of the body; that is, one should take care with courage that the impurity of his body does not cling to him. One should know the nature of this Supreme Self, who is pure and eternal.

This Supreme Self is not only established in the heart of individual persons; he himself pervades the entire orb of luminaries and shines with exceeding brightness.

य एषोऽंतरादि ै हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दृश्यते हिरण्मय श्मश्रुर्हिरण्यकेश आप्रणखात्सर्व एव सुवर्णः ॥ (*ya eṣo 'ṃtarādi ai hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇmaya śmaśrurhiraṇyakeśa āpraṇakhātsarva eva suvarṇaḥ ‖*)
(Bhā. Tā. 1-6-6) **NOTE**

For the Supreme Puruṣa who is within Ādityā, the eye of the world, the beard and the hair are golden. From the nails onward all his limbs are of the nature of light. Moreover, that which has the form of Brahman, true and eternal, is called by the name Supreme Puruṣa. The water, because of which Puruṣa is called by the name Nārāyaṇa, since it was the ayana of the Supreme Puruṣa, is the source of the primal principle of the form of truth; and that principle is famous by names such as Supreme Puruṣa, Prajāpati and Nārāyaṇa. How? Thus:

आप एवेदमग्र आसुस्ता आपः सत्यमसृजंत सत्यं ब्रह्म ब्रह्म प्रजापतिं प्रजापतिर्देवांस्ते देवाः सत्यमेवोपासते तदेतत्त्र्यक्षरं सत्यमिति स इत्येकमक्षरं तित्येकमक्षरं यमित्येकमक्षरं प्रथमोत्तमे अक्षरे सत्यं मध्यतोऽनृतं तदेतदनृतमुभयतः सत्येन परिगृहीतं सत्यभूयमेव भवति नैवं विद्वांसमनृतं हिनस्ति ॥ (*āpa evedamagra āsustā āpaḥ satyamasṛjaṃta satyaṃ brahma brahma prajāpatiṃ prajāpatirdevāṃste devāḥ satyamevopāsate tadetattryakṣaraṃ satyamiti sa ityekamakṣaraṃ tityekamakṣaraṃ yamityekamakṣaraṃ prathamottame akṣare satyaṃ madhyato 'nṛtaṃ tadetadanṛtamubhayataḥ satyena parigṛhītaṃ satyabhūyameva bhavati naivaṃ vidvāṃsamanṛtaṃ hinasti ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 5-5-1)

Before creation there was only water. From that water Brahman, of the nature of truth, came forth, and from that Brahman Prajāpati came into being. From Prajāpati the gods came into being. Afterwards the gods worshipped truth, the source of the whole universe. This truth has three syllables: sa, t and ya are those three syllables. Among them, sa and ya reflect the eternal and ultimate principle; t reflects the principle of the world, which is non-eternal and not ultimate. The non-eternal world is enclosed on both sides by the eternal, permanent reality. One who knows this principle is not harmed by what is non-eternal and untrue.

### Printed p. 697

तद्यत्तत्सत्यमसौ स आदित्यो य एष एतस्मिन्मंडले पुरुषो यश्चायं दक्षिणेऽक्षन् पुरुषस्तावेतावन्योस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठितौ रश्मिभिरेषोऽस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितः प्राणैरयममुष्मिन् स यदोत्क्रमिष्यन् भवति शुद्धमेवैतन्मंडलं पश्यति नैनमेते रश्मयः प्रत्यायंति ॥ (*tadyattatsatyamasau sa ādityo ya eṣa etasminmaṃḍale puruṣo yaścāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣastāvetāvanyosminpratiṣṭhitau raśmibhireṣo 'smin pratiṣṭhitaḥ prāṇairayamamuṣmin sa yadotkramiṣyan bhavati śuddhamevaitanmaṃḍalaṃ paśyati nainamete raśmayaḥ pratyāyaṃti ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 5-5-2)

The Ādityā who shines in the heavenly world reflects that truth. The Puruṣa within the orb of Ādityā and the Puruṣa who shines here in the right eye are supported by each other. By the rays of that Puruṣa this Puruṣa is endowed with vitality, and by the breath of this one that Puruṣa. At the time of death there arises the knowledge that these two elements are principles belonging to one and the same Puruṣa.

य एष एतस्मिन्मंडले पुरुषस्तस्य भूरिति शिर एकं शिर एकमेतदक्षरं भुव इति बाहू द्वा बाहू द्वे एते अक्षरे स्वरिति प्रतिष्ठा द्वे प्रतिष्ठे द्वे एते अक्षरे तस्योपनिषदहरिति हंति साप्मानं जहाति च य एवं वेद । (*ya eṣa etasminmaṃḍale puruṣastasya bhūriti śira ekaṃ śira ekametadakṣaraṃ bhuva iti bāhū dvā bāhū dve ete akṣare svariti pratiṣṭhā dve pratiṣṭhe dve ete akṣare tasyopaniṣadahariti haṃti sāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda |*)
(Bṛ. U. 5-3) (Bṛ. Tā. 5-2-3) **NOTE**

The head of the Puruṣa within the orb of Ādityā is the principle indicated by the one syllable bhūḥ. The two syllables of bhuvaḥ are the two arms; svar, consisting of two syllables, reflects the two feet. The Upaniṣad principle reflects ahas. One who knows this principle becomes free from sin. This is the description of the nature of the Puruṣa within the orb of Ādityā. Is it not so?

योऽयं दक्षिणेऽक्षन्नुरुषस्तस्य भूरिति शिर एकं शिर एकमेतदक्षरं भुव इति बाहू द्वा बाहू द्वे एते अक्षरे स्वरिति प्रतिष्ठा द्वे प्रतिष्ठे द्वे एते अक्षरे तस्योपनिषदहमिति हंति पाप्मानं जहाति च य एवं वेद ॥ (*yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣannuruṣastasya bhūriti śira ekaṃ śira ekametadakṣaraṃ bhuva iti bāhū dvā bāhū dve ete akṣare svariti pratiṣṭhā dve pratiṣṭhe dve ete akṣare tasyopaniṣadahamiti haṃti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda ‖*)
(Bṛ. U. 5-5-4) (Bṛ. 5-5-4)

The head of the Puruṣa in the right eye is reflected by the syllable bhūḥ. One syllable stands for one head; the two syllables bhuvaḥ for the two arms; the two syllables svar reflect the two feet. The mysterious principle called Upaniṣad indicates the notion of "I". One who knows this principle becomes free from sin.

मनोमयोऽयं पुरुषो भाः सत्यस्तस्मिन्नंतर्हृदये यथा व्रीहिर्वा यवो ना स एष सर्वस्येशानः सर्वस्याधिपतिः सर्वमिदं प्रशास्ति. यदिदं किंच ॥ (*manomayo 'yaṃ puruṣo bhāḥ satyastasminnaṃtarhṛdaye yathā vrīhirvā yavo nā sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ sarvasyādhipatiḥ sarvamidaṃ praśāsti. yadidaṃ kiṃca ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 5-5-5)

### Printed p. 698

This Puruṣa in the interior of the heart is made of mind and is of the form of light; he exists in the form of a grain of rice and in the form of a grain of barley. He is the lord of all the worlds. He rules this entire universe. Everything is subject to his will. In such terms the divine nature of the Supreme Puruṣa is described.
