In the present context, what the chief elements of the Puruṣa described in this sūkta of the Ṛk Saṃhitā are can be examined in outline. It has been stated before that all the deities described and praised in the Ṛk Saṃhitā are particular manifestations of this Supreme Puruṣa. Even so, if one examines, among the deities such as Agni who reflect the individual aspects of this Puruṣa, the chief natures of which deity are described in the Puruṣa to whom this sūkta is addressed, it can be said that the natures of the three deities Agni, Sūrya and Viṣṇu are all manifested in Puruṣa and show the great glory of Puruṣa.

1. He is the womb of all moving and unmoving things; the lord of the plants and of the waters; the chief representative of the sacrifice; the same special qualities that are seen in Agni are described in Puruṣa.

2. The greatness that is in Sūrya, established by surpassing all the worlds and occupying the upper region, is stated to be in Puruṣa too.

3. The extraordinary quality of Viṣṇu, who pervades all the worlds such as heaven and earth and the atmosphere, is the very special quality of Puruṣa. How? Thus:

The word सहस्र (*sahasra*), expressing a quality, is used with reference to Agni on many occasions. For example:

सहस्राक्षो विचर्षणिरग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति । होता गृणीत उक्त्र्यः ॥ (*sahasrākṣo vicarṣaṇiragnī rakṣāṃsi sedhati | hotā gṛṇīta uktryaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-29-12)

Just as the epithets सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् (*sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt*) describe the countless eyes and the pervading feet of Puruṣa, so in this Ṛk the countless spread of the light of Agni is stated. It can be said that these epithets used of Agni in Ṛk-s such as तस्मै सहस्रमक्षिभिर्वि चक्षे (*tasmai sahasramakṣibhirvi cakṣe*) (10.79-5) are a description of Puruṣa, who is of the form of Agni. Likewise:

उक्षा समुद्रो अरुषः सुपर्णः पूर्वस्य योनिं पितुरा विवेश । मध्ये दिवो निहितः पृश्निरश्मा वि चक्रमे रजसस्पात्यंतौ ॥ (*ukṣā samudro aruṣaḥ suparṇaḥ pūrvasya yoniṃ piturā viveśa | madhye divo nihitaḥ pṛśniraśmā vi cakrame rajasaspātyaṃtau ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-47-3)

### Printed p. 699

Sūrya, the showerer of desires, of attractive form, has entered the atmosphere, the producer of water. Afterwards he has entered the heavenly world and pervades everywhere. When the greatness of Sūrya is stated, that he pervades the heavenly world and the atmosphere and moves everywhere, it is the pervading quality of Puruṣa that is described. Moreover:

विभ्राजङ्ज्यतिषा स्वरंगच्छो रोचनं दिवः । येनेमा विश्वा भुवनान्याभृता विश्वकर्मणा विश्वदेव्यावता ॥ (*vibhrājaṅjyatiṣā svaraṃgaccho rocanaṃ divaḥ | yenemā viśvā bhuvanānyābhṛtā viśvakarmaṇā viśvadevyāvatā ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-4)

O Ādityā, by your divine radiance you illumine the whole world. You have taken refuge in the most excellent divine world. Spreading your divine radiance, which is the cause of all sacrifices and gratifying to all the gods, you nourish all the worlds. Such a description is the very description of the Supreme Lord who is of the form of Ādityā.

This Supreme Puruṣa within Ādityā is the impeller and controller, the nourisher and protector, of all these activities.

पूषन्नेकर्षे यम सूर्य प्राजापत्य व्यूह रश्मिन् समूह । तेजो यत्ते रूपं कल्याणतमं तत्ते पश्यामि योऽसावसौ पुरुषः सोऽहमस्मि ॥ (*pūṣannekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmin samūha | tejo yatte rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tatte paśyāmi yo 'sāvasau puruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi ‖*)
(Ī 6) **NOTE**

O Ādityā, who are of the form of Prajāpati, you are the nourisher of the world. You alone have the power of sight that beholds all the worlds. You alone are the controller of the world. Spread your rays for the illumination of the world. Spread your radiance. Your divine form is visible to me. The Supreme Puruṣa, who dwells in the divine world, is within the interior of my heart as well.

The chief subject of the Puruṣasūkta is to describe and praise the divine glory of the Supreme Puruṣa, who is praised in many ways in such terms. The chief purport of the mantras in this sūkta is explained according to one's understanding. Since the exposition of a spiritual principle is involved, many omissions and faults are natural in this context. Even so, the purport of the mantras is explained taking the Śruti passages themselves as the basis.

On the use (viniyoga), the fruit as stated (phalaśruti), the greatness (māhātmya) and similar matters of this sūkta, the great sage Śaunaka has said as follows in his work called the Ṛgvidhāna:

### Printed p. 700

शुक्लपक्षे शुभे वारे सुनक्षत्रे सुगोचरे । द्वादश्यां पुत्रकामाय चरुं कुर्वीत वैष्णवं ॥ दंपत्योरुपवासः स्यादेकादश्यां सुरालये । ऋग्भिः पोडशभिः सम्यगर्चयित्वा जनार्दनं । चरुं पुरुषसूक्तेन श्रपयेत्पुत्रकाम्याया । प्राप्नुयाद्वैष्णवं पुत्रमचिरात्संततिक्षमं ॥ (*śuklapakṣe śubhe vāre sunakṣatre sugocare | dvādaśyāṃ putrakāmāya caruṃ kurvīta vaiṣṇavaṃ ‖ daṃpatyorupavāsaḥ syādekādaśyāṃ surālaye | ṛgbhiḥ poḍaśabhiḥ samyagarcayitvā janārdanaṃ | caruṃ puruṣasūktena śrapayetputrakāmyāyā | prāpnuyādvaiṣṇavaṃ putramacirātsaṃtatikṣamaṃ ‖*)

A man who desires a good son should, together with his wife, keep a fast with discipline on the Ekādaśī tithi, and in the bright fortnight, on the Dvādaśī tithi with an auspicious day and star, recite the sixteen Ṛk-s of this Puruṣasūkta, worship the deity Viṣṇu by the procedure stated in the Kalpa, and then offer the homa; then he will soon obtain a son who will advance the family and bring offspring.

त्वादश द्वादशीः सम्यक् पयसा निर्वपेच्चरुं । यः करोति सहस्रं स्याद्याति विष्णोः परं पदं ॥ (*tvādaśa dvādaśīḥ samyak payasā nirvapeccaruṃ | yaḥ karoti sahasraṃ syādyāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padaṃ ‖*)

In this way, the man who on twelve Dvādaśī days offers homa a thousand times with parameśanna prepared with milk and with caru (cooked rice) obtains, after death, the excellent state that is called the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

हुत्वाग्निं विधिवत्सम्यगृग्भिः षोडशभिर्द्विजः । कृतांजलिपुटो भूत्वा स्तवं ताभिः प्रयोजयेत् ॥ (*hutvāgniṃ vidhivatsamyagṛgbhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirdvijaḥ | kṛtāṃjalipuṭo bhūtvā stavaṃ tābhiḥ prayojayet ‖*)

The twice-born man, having duly established the fire and offered homa with the sixteen Ṛk-s of this Puruṣasūkta, should then, with folded hands, praise by reciting those same sixteen mantras.

केशवं मार्गशीर्षे तु पौषे नारायणं स्मृतं । माधवं माघमासे तु गोविंदं फाल्गुने तथा ॥ चैत्रे चैव तथा विष्णुं वैशाखे मधुसूदनं । ज्येष्ठे त्रिविक्रमं विद्यादाषाधे वामनं विदुः ॥ श्रावणे श्रीधरं विद्यादृषीकेशं ततः परे । आश्विने पद्मनाभं तु दामोदरं च कार्तिके ॥ द्वादशैतानि नामानि ऋष्यशृंगोऽब्रवीन्मुनिः ! पूजयेन्वासनामभिः सर्वान्नामान्समश्नुते ॥ (*keśavaṃ mārgaśīrṣe tu pauṣe nārāyaṇaṃ smṛtaṃ | mādhavaṃ māghamāse tu goviṃdaṃ phālgune tathā ‖ caitre caiva tathā viṣṇuṃ vaiśākhe madhusūdanaṃ | jyeṣṭhe trivikramaṃ vidyādāṣādhe vāmanaṃ viduḥ ‖ śrāvaṇe śrīdharaṃ vidyādṛṣīkeśaṃ tataḥ pare | āśvine padmanābhaṃ tu dāmodaraṃ ca kārtike ‖ dvādaśaitāni nāmāni ṛṣyaśṛṃgo 'bravīnmuniḥ ! pūjayenvāsanāmabhiḥ sarvānnāmānsamaśnute ‖*)

In the procedure of worship and homa stated above, one should perform the worship and the rest reciting the names of a different form of Viṣṇu in each month. How? In the month Mārgaśīrṣa, Keśava; in the month Puṣya

### Printed p. 701

Nārāyaṇa; in the month Māgha, Mādhava; in the month Phālguṇa, Govinda; in the month Caitra, Viṣṇu; in the month Vaiśākha, Madhusūdana; in the month Jyeṣṭha, Trivikrama; in the month Āṣāḍha, Vāmana; in the month Śrāvaṇa, Śrīdhara; in the month Bhādrapada, Hṛṣīkeśa; in the month Āśvayuja, Padmanābha; in the month Kārtika, Dāmodara. In this way the twelve different forms are to be worshipped in the twelve months. The sage named Ṛṣyaśṛṅga has stated this order. The man who worships in this prescribed order obtains all his desires and is happy.

आयुष्मंतं सुतं सूते यशोमेधासमन्वितं । धनवंतं प्रजावंतं धार्मिकं सात्विकं तथा ॥ (*āyuṣmaṃtaṃ sutaṃ sūte yaśomedhāsamanvitaṃ | dhanavaṃtaṃ prajāvaṃtaṃ dhārmikaṃ sātvikaṃ tathā ‖*)

The man who performs the worship and the rest by the procedures stated above will obtain a good son. That son, endowed with long life, fame, intelligence, wealth, offspring and a bent towards dharma, will be known as a good son.

समिधोऽश्वत्थवृक्षस्य हुत्वाग्निं जुहुयात्पुनः । उपस्थानं हुताशस्य ध्यात्वार्च्य मधुसूदनं ॥ हविर्होमं ततः कुर्यात्प्रत्यृचं वाग्यतः शुचिः । सूक्तेन जुहुयादाज्यमादावंते च पूर्ववत् ॥ हविश्लेषं नमस्कृत्वा नारी नारायणं पतिं । भक्षयित्वा हविश्लेषं लब्धाशीः संविशेत् क्षपां ॥ ततस्तु कर्म कृत्वेदं कर्तव्यं द्विजतर्पणं । द्वितीया स्त्री निवर्तेत यावद्गर्भं न विंदति ॥ अपुत्रा मृतपुत्रा वा या च कन्यां प्रसूयते । क्षिप्रं सा जनयेत्पुत्रमृष्यशृंगो यथाब्रवीत् ॥ (*samidho 'śvatthavṛkṣasya hutvāgniṃ juhuyātpunaḥ | upasthānaṃ hutāśasya dhyātvārcya madhusūdanaṃ ‖ havirhomaṃ tataḥ kuryātpratyṛcaṃ vāgyataḥ śuciḥ | sūktena juhuyādājyamādāvaṃte ca pūrvavat ‖ haviśleṣaṃ namaskṛtvā nārī nārāyaṇaṃ patiṃ | bhakṣayitvā haviśleṣaṃ labdhāśīḥ saṃviśet kṣapāṃ ‖ tatastu karma kṛtvedaṃ kartavyaṃ dvijatarpaṇaṃ | dvitīyā strī nivarteta yāvadgarbhaṃ na viṃdati ‖ aputrā mṛtaputrā vā yā ca kanyāṃ prasūyate | kṣipraṃ sā janayetputramṛṣyaśṛṃgo yathābravīt ‖*)

Now the procedure of the homa will be explained. Having duly established the fire, one should offer homa in it with kindling sticks of the aśvattha tree. After the homa, meditating on the form of Madhusūdana, one should pray to the fire. Then one should again offer the oblation in the fire with each mantra. While offering the homa one should be pure and, without speaking much, recite only the mantras. When offering homa with the mantras of this sūkta, one should offer homa with ājya (ghee) at the beginning and at the end. Afterwards the wife of that man should bow to the remains of the oblation, to Nārāyaṇa and to her husband, eat the remains of the oblation, receive the blessing of the Brāhmaṇas, and join her husband in the night.

### Printed p. 702

Having pleased the Brāhmaṇas with meals and the like, one should bring this rite to its conclusion. If his wife does not conceive on the very first day, then on the second day the man should try for conception. Even if the child born of the first conception dies, or a daughter is born and not a son, in the second conception a son will certainly be obtained. The great sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga himself has said this.

अर्चनं संप्रवक्ष्यामि विष्णोरमिततेजसः । यत्कृक्वा मुनयः सर्वे ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमाप्नुयः ॥ अप्सव्वगौ हृदये सूर्ये स्थंडिले प्रतिमासु च । षट्स्वतेषु हरेः सम्यगर्चनं मुनिभिः स्मृतं ॥ अग्नौ क्रियावतां देवो दिवि देवो मनीषिणां । प्रतिमास्वल्पबुद्धीनां योगिनां हृदये हरिः ॥ आपो ह्यायतनं तस्य तस्मात्तासु सदा हरिः । तस्य सर्वगतत्वाच्च स्थंडिले भावितात्मनां ॥ (*arcanaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ | yatkṛkvā munayaḥ sarve brahmanirvāṇamāpnuyaḥ ‖ apsavvagau hṛdaye sūrye sthaṃḍile pratimāsu ca | ṣaṭsvateṣu hareḥ samyagarcanaṃ munibhiḥ smṛtaṃ ‖ agnau kriyāvatāṃ devo divi devo manīṣiṇāṃ | pratimāsvalpabuddhīnāṃ yogināṃ hṛdaye hariḥ ‖ āpo hyāyatanaṃ tasya tasmāttāsu sadā hariḥ | tasya sarvagatatvācca sthaṃḍile bhāvitātmanāṃ ‖*)

Now I shall state the procedure of worship of the image of Viṣṇu, of great glory and radiance. All the sages too worshipped this Viṣṇu and by that very worship obtained the state of Brahmā. If this Viṣṇu is to be worshipped, one may invoke the deity and worship in six kinds of objects: water, fire, the heart, the sun, the sthaṇḍila (mandala), and images. Sacrificers devoted to ritual action may meditate on the form of Viṣṇu in the fire and worship. Intelligent followers of the Vedānta may meditate on the Lord in the orb of the sun and worship. Ordinary people of small understanding may set up images, invoke the deity in them and worship. Yogis and ascetics may realise directly the Supreme Self in the lotus of their own heart and adore him. Water (the ocean of milk) is always the dwelling-place of Viṣṇu; therefore the presence of the Supreme Self is always in water. The word Nārāyaṇa means one who dwells in water. Therefore one may also meditate on the form of Viṣṇu in water and worship. Those who regard the Supreme Self as pervading all things from within may meditate on Viṣṇu in the sthaṇḍila or mandala, worship and meditate. The wise sages say that Viṣṇu may be worshipped in all these six ways.

दद्यात्पुरुषसूक्तेन यः पुष्पाण्यप विव वा । अर्चितं स्याज्जगदिदं तेन सर्वं चराचरं ॥ (*dadyātpuruṣasūktena yaḥ puṣpāṇyapa viva vā | arcitaṃ syājjagadidaṃ tena sarvaṃ carācaraṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 703

While worshipping with the mantras of this Puruṣasūkta one should offer flowers, water and other articles of worship to the deity. If one does so, it is as though the entire world, moving and unmoving, had been worshipped.

अनुष्टुभस्य सूक्तस्य त्रिष्टबंतस्य देवता । पुरुषो वै जगद्बीजमृषिर्नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ नारायण महाबाहो शृणुष्टैकमनाः प्रभो । वक्ष्ये पुरुषसूक्तस्य विधानं त्वर्चनं प्रति ॥ अग्निकार्यं जपविधिं स्तोत्रं चैव सदात्मकं । (*anuṣṭubhasya sūktasya triṣṭabaṃtasya devatā | puruṣo vai jagadbījamṛṣirnārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ‖ nārāyaṇa mahābāho śṛṇuṣṭaikamanāḥ prabho | vakṣye puruṣasūktasya vidhānaṃ tvarcanaṃ prati ‖ agnikāryaṃ japavidhiṃ stotraṃ caiva sadātmakaṃ |*)

The seer of this Puruṣasūkta is Nārāyaṇa; the deity is the Supreme Puruṣa, the cause of the world; the metre is Anuṣṭup, and only the last Ṛk is in the Triṣṭup metre. O Nārāyaṇa, lord of all and of great prowess, please listen with one mind to what I say. Now I shall state in detail the procedure of worship of this Puruṣasūkta, the order of recitation, the procedure of homa and the order of reciting the hymn of praise.

स्नात्वा यथोक्तविधिना प्राङ्मुखु शुद्धमानसः . प्रथमां विन्यसेद्वामे द्वितीयां दक्षिणे करे । तृतीयां वामपादे तु चतुर्थीं दक्षिणे न्यसेत् ॥ पंचमीं वामजानुनि षष्ठीं वै दक्षिणे न्यसेत् । सप्तमीं वामकट्यां तु अष्टमीं दक्षिणे कटा ॥ नवमीं नाभिमध्ये तु दशमीं हृदये न्यसेत् । एकादशीं कंठदेशे द्वादशीं वामबाहुके ॥ त्रयोदशीं दक्षिणे बाहावास्ये चैव चतुर्दशीं । अक्ष्णोः पंचदशीं चैव षोडशीं मूर्धिन् विन्यसेत् ॥ एवं न्यासविधिं कृत्वा पश्चात्तापजां समारभेत् ॥ (*snātvā yathoktavidhinā prāṅmukhu śuddhamānasaḥ . prathamāṃ vinyasedvāme dvitīyāṃ dakṣiṇe kare | tṛtīyāṃ vāmapāde tu caturthīṃ dakṣiṇe nyaset ‖ paṃcamīṃ vāmajānuni ṣaṣṭhīṃ vai dakṣiṇe nyaset | saptamīṃ vāmakaṭyāṃ tu aṣṭamīṃ dakṣiṇe kaṭā ‖ navamīṃ nābhimadhye tu daśamīṃ hṛdaye nyaset | ekādaśīṃ kaṃṭhadeśe dvādaśīṃ vāmabāhuke ‖ trayodaśīṃ dakṣiṇe bāhāvāsye caiva caturdaśīṃ | akṣṇoḥ paṃcadaśīṃ caiva ṣoḍaśīṃ mūrdhin vinyaset ‖ evaṃ nyāsavidhiṃ kṛtvā paścāttāpajāṃ samārabhet ‖*)

After bathing according to the prescribed procedure, with a pure mind, seated facing east, before beginning the worship one should perform nyāsa on the various limbs with the sixteen Ṛk-s of the Puruṣasūkta as stated below. How? The first Ṛk on the left hand, the second Ṛk on the right hand, the third Ṛk on the left foot, the fourth Ṛk on the right foot, the fifth Ṛk on the left knee, the sixth Ṛk on the right knee, the seventh Ṛk on the left (vāma) hip, the eighth Ṛk on the right hip, the ninth Ṛk on the navel, the tenth

### Printed p. 704

Ṛk in the region of the heart, the eleventh Ṛk in the region of the throat, the twelfth Ṛk on the left arm, the thirteenth Ṛk on the right arm, the fourteenth Ṛk on the face, the fifteenth Ṛk on the eyes, and the sixteenth Ṛk on the head, reciting each, one should perform the nyāsa. Having performed the nyāsa in this way, one should then begin the worship.

यथा देहे तथा देवे न्यासु कृत्वा विधानतः ॥ मंत्रन्यासं पुरा कृत्वा स्वदेहे देवतासु च । गायत्रो ०कारं न्यस्तांग्यः पूजयेद्विष्णुमव्ययं ॥ (*yathā dehe tathā deve nyāsu kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ‖ maṃtranyāsaṃ purā kṛtvā svadehe devatāsu ca | gāyatro 0kāraṃ nyastāṃgyaḥ pūjayedviṣṇumavyayaṃ ‖*)

As stated before, that is, as nyāsa has been performed on the limbs of one's own body, so one should perform nyāsa on the limbs of the deity of the worship, duly and with mantras. Having first performed the mantra-nyāsa, one should then perform nyāsa with the Gāyatrī mantra and with the Oṃkāra, that is the praṇava mantra, and then worship the imperishable Viṣṇu.

उच्छ्वासावाहने नृस्तः स्थिरायामुद्धवार्चने । अस्थिरायां विकल्पति स्यात् स्थंडिले तु भवेद्वयं ॥ उच्छ्वासावाहने न्यस्तः स्थावरे वै यथा तथा । शालिग्रामार्चने नैव ह्यावाहनविसर्जने ॥ शालिग्रामे तु भगवानादिभूतो यथा हरिः । न तथान्यत्र सूर्यादौ वैकुंठे वापि सर्वगः ॥ (*ucchvāsāvāhane nṛstaḥ sthirāyāmuddhavārcane | asthirāyāṃ vikalpati syāt sthaṃḍile tu bhavedvayaṃ ‖ ucchvāsāvāhane nyastaḥ sthāvare vai yathā tathā | śāligrāmārcane naiva hyāvāhanavisarjane ‖ śāligrāme tu bhagavānādibhūto yathā hariḥ | na tathānyatra sūryādau vaikuṃṭhe vāpi sarvagaḥ ‖*)

When invoking the deity one should proceed by the order of inhalation (pūraka); when worshipping, by the order of retention (kumbhaka); when dismissing, by the order of exhalation (recaka) called udvāsana. In an unstable sthaṇḍila (mandala), image and the like, it may be done in both ways. Since the presence of the deity is always in the śāligrāma, there is no need there for invocation and dismissal. But in the sun and the like it cannot be done so. Since the Supreme Puruṣa always pervades Vaikuṇṭha and all other places, one should meditate with the thought that the Supreme Puruṣa is present in the sun and the rest as well.

आद्ययावाहयेद्देवमृचा तु पुरुषोत्तमं । द्वितीययासनं दद्यात्पाद्यं चैव तृतीयया ॥ अर्घ्यं चतुर्थ्या दातव्यं पंचम्याचमनीयकं । षष्ठ्या स्नानं प्रकुर्वीत सप्तम्या वस्त्रमेव च ॥ (*ādyayāvāhayeddevamṛcā tu puruṣottamaṃ | dvitīyayāsanaṃ dadyātpādyaṃ caiva tṛtīyayā ‖ arghyaṃ caturthyā dātavyaṃ paṃcamyācamanīyakaṃ | ṣaṣṭhyā snānaṃ prakurvīta saptamyā vastrameva ca ‖*)

### Printed p. 705

यज्ञोपवीतमष्टम्या नवम्या चानुलेपनं । पुष्पं दशम्या दातव्यमेकादश्या तु धूपकं ॥ द्वादश्या दीपकं दद्यात् त्रयोदश्या निवेदनं । चतुर्दर्श्या नमस्कारं पंचदश्या प्रदक्षिणं ॥ स्नाने वस्त्रे च नैवेद्ये दद्यादाचमनीयकं । दक्षिणां तु यथाशक्ता षोडश्या तु प्रदापयेत् ॥ (*yajñopavītamaṣṭamyā navamyā cānulepanaṃ | puṣpaṃ daśamyā dātavyamekādaśyā tu dhūpakaṃ ‖ dvādaśyā dīpakaṃ dadyāt trayodaśyā nivedanaṃ | caturdarśyā namaskāraṃ paṃcadaśyā pradakṣiṇaṃ ‖ snāne vastre ca naivedye dadyādācamanīyakaṃ | dakṣiṇāṃ tu yathāśaktā ṣoḍaśyā tu pradāpayet ‖*)

The procedure of the worship with sixteen offerings (upacāra) according to the procedure of the Puruṣasūkta is stated. **NOTE** With the first Ṛk (सहस्रशीर्षा (*sahasraśīrṣā*)) one should make the invocation. With the second Ṛk (पुरुष एवेदं (*puruṣa evedaṃ*)) one should offer the seat. With the third Ṛk (एतावानस्य (*etāvānasya*)) the water for the feet, with the fourth Ṛk (त्रिपादूर्ध्व (*tripādūrdhva*)) the arghya, with the fifth Ṛk (तस्माद्विराळजायत (*tasmādvirāḷajāyata*)) the water for sipping. With the sixth Ṛk (यत्पुरुषेण (*yatpuruṣeṇa*)) the bath is to be performed. With the seventh Ṛk (तं यज्ञं बर्हिषि (*taṃ yajñaṃ barhiṣi*)) the garment, and with the eighth Ṛk (तस्माद्यज्ञात्सर्वहुतः संभृतं (*tasmādyajñātsarvahutaḥ saṃbhṛtaṃ*)) one should offer the sacred thread; with the ninth Ṛk (तस्माद्यज्ञात्सर्वहुत ऋचः (*tasmādyajñātsarvahuta ṛcaḥ*)) one should anoint with sandal paste. With the tenth Ṛk (तस्मादश्वा (*tasmādaśvā*)) one should offer a flower and worship. With the eleventh Ṛk (यत्पुरुषं व्यदधुः (*yatpuruṣaṃ vyadadhuḥ*)) one should let the incense be smelt. With the twelfth Ṛk (ब्राह्मणोऽस्य (*brāhmaṇo 'sya*)) one should light the lamp. With the thirteenth Ṛk (चंद्रमा मनसो (*caṃdramā manaso*)) one should offer the food. With the fourteenth Ṛk (नाभ्या आसीत् (*nābhyā āsīt*)) one should circumambulate, and with the fifteenth Ṛk (सप्तास्यासन्परिधयः (*saptāsyāsanparidhayaḥ*)) make the salutation. After the offering of bath, garment, food and water for sipping in this way, with the sixteenth Ṛk (यज्ञेन यज्ञं (*yajñena yajñaṃ*)) one should offer a fee according to one's ability. This is the order of the sixteen offerings.

ततः प्रादक्षिण्यं कृत्वा जपन्कुर्यात्समाहितः । यथाशक्ति जपित्वा तु सूक्तं तस्य निवेदयेत् ॥ (*tataḥ prādakṣiṇyaṃ kṛtvā japankuryātsamāhitaḥ | yathāśakti japitvā tu sūktaṃ tasya nivedayet ‖*)

After the worship, one should circumambulate the deity, and with a collected mind and with faith recite the sūkta as far as one is able, and offer it to the deity. This is the procedure of recitation.

देवस्य दक्षिणे पार्श्वे कुंडं स्थंडिलमेव ना कारयेत्प्रथमेनैव द्वितीयेन तु प्रोक्षणं ॥ तृतीयेनाग्निमादध्याच्चतुर्थेन समिंधनं । पंचमेनाज्यश्रपणं चरोश्च श्रपणं तथा ॥ (*devasya dakṣiṇe pārśve kuṃḍaṃ sthaṃḍilameva nā kārayetprathamenaiva dvitīyena tu prokṣaṇaṃ ‖ tṛtīyenāgnimādadhyāccaturthena samiṃdhanaṃ | paṃcamenājyaśrapaṇaṃ carośca śrapaṇaṃ tathā ‖*)

### Printed p. 706

षष्ठेनैवाग्निमध्यॆ तु कल्पयेत्स्माद्ममासनं । चिंतयेद्देवदेवेशं कालानलसमप्रभं ॥ ततो गंधं च पुष्पं च धूपदीपनिवेदनं । अनुज्ञाप्य ततः कुर्यात्सप्तम्यादि यथाक्रमं ॥ समिधस्तावतीः पूर्वं जुहुयादभिघारिताः । ततो घृतेन जुहुयाच्चरुणा च ततः पुनः ॥ (*ṣaṣṭhenaivāgnimadhyè tu kalpayetsmādmamāsanaṃ | ciṃtayeddevadeveśaṃ kālānalasamaprabhaṃ ‖ tato gaṃdhaṃ ca puṣpaṃ ca dhūpadīpanivedanaṃ | anujñāpya tataḥ kuryātsaptamyādi yathākramaṃ ‖ samidhastāvatīḥ pūrvaṃ juhuyādabhighāritāḥ | tato ghṛtena juhuyāccaruṇā ca tataḥ punaḥ ‖*)

Now the procedure of the homa is stated. On the right side of the deity one should establish the fire, with a sthaṇḍila, or one may establish the fire in a kuṇḍa. In this work of establishing the fire, the fire-pit or the sthaṇḍila is to be constructed with the first Ṛk, that is, by reciting the first Ṛk. With the second Ṛk one should sprinkle it with water. With the third Ṛk one should bring the fire from the house of a Śrotriya. With the fourth Ṛk one should kindle the fire. With the fifth Ṛk one should place the ghee and the caru near the fire and prepare them. With the sixth Ṛk one should sit near the fire, facing east, in the padmāsana posture, and meditate on the Lord of the gods, shining with great brilliance like the sun of the time of dissolution. **NOTE** Then, having offered scent, flowers, lamp, food and the like, and having obtained the permission of the god Agni, with the seventh Ṛk one should smear the kindling sticks with ghee and offer homa in the fire. Afterwards one should offer homa with ājya (ghee) and then with caru (cooked rice).

एवं हुत्वा ततश्चैव अनुज्ञाप्य यथाक्रमं । अग्नेर्भगवतस्तस्य समीपे स्तोत्रमुच्चरेत् ॥ (*evaṃ hutvā tataścaiva anujñāpya yathākramaṃ | agnerbhagavatastasya samīpe stotramuccaret ‖*)

यतं शे पुंडरीकाक्ष नमस्ते विश्वभावन । नमस्तेऽस्तु हृषिकेश महापुरुष पूर्वज ॥ देवानां दानवानां च सामान्यमधिदैवतं । सर्वदा चरणद्वंद्वं व्रजामि शरणं तव ॥ एकस्त्वमसि लोकस्य सृष्टा संहारकस्तथा । अव्यक्तश्चानुमंता च गुणमायासमावृतः ॥ संसारसागरं घोरमनंशं क्लेशभाजनं । त्वमेव शरणं प्राप्य निस्तरंति मनीषिणः ॥ न ते रूपं न चाकारो नायुधानि न चास्पदं । तथापि पुरुषाकारो भक्तानां त्वं प्रकाशसे ॥ (*yataṃ śe puṃḍarīkākṣa namaste viśvabhāvana | namaste 'stu hṛṣikeśa mahāpuruṣa pūrvaja ‖ devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca sāmānyamadhidaivataṃ | sarvadā caraṇadvaṃdvaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ tava ‖ ekastvamasi lokasya sṛṣṭā saṃhārakastathā | avyaktaścānumaṃtā ca guṇamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ ‖ saṃsārasāgaraṃ ghoramanaṃśaṃ kleśabhājanaṃ | tvameva śaraṇaṃ prāpya nistaraṃti manīṣiṇaḥ ‖ na te rūpaṃ na cākāro nāyudhāni na cāspadaṃ | tathāpi puruṣākāro bhaktānāṃ tvaṃ prakāśase ‖*)

### Printed p. 707

नैव किंचित्परोक्षं ते प्रत्यक्षोऽसि न कस्यचित् । नैव किंचिदसाध्यं ते न च साध्योऽसि कस्यचित् ॥ कार्याणां कारणं पूर्वं वचसां वाच्यमुत्तमं । योगिनां परमा सिद्धिः परमं ते पदं विदुः ॥ (*naiva kiṃcitparokṣaṃ te pratyakṣo 'si na kasyacit | naiva kiṃcidasādhyaṃ te na ca sādhyo 'si kasyacit ‖ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ vacasāṃ vācyamuttamaṃ | yogināṃ paramā siddhiḥ paramaṃ te padaṃ viduḥ ‖*)

अहं भीतोऽस्मि देवेश संसारेऽस्मिन्महाभये । त्राहि मां पुंडरीकाक्ष न जाने परमं पदं ॥ कालेष्टपि च सर्वॆषु दिक्षु सर्वासु चाच्युत । शरीरे जगतश्चासि वर्तते मे महद्भयं ॥ (*ahaṃ bhīto 'smi deveśa saṃsāre 'sminmahābhaye | trāhi māṃ puṃḍarīkākṣa na jāne paramaṃ padaṃ ‖ kāleṣṭapi ca sarvèṣu dikṣu sarvāsu cācyuta | śarīre jagataścāsi vartate me mahadbhayaṃ ‖*)

त्वत्पादकमलादन्यन्न मे जन्मांतरेष्टपि । विज्ञानं यदिदं प्राप्य यदिदं स्थानमर्जितं ॥ जन्मांतरेऽपि मे देव मा भूदस्य परिक्षयः दुर्गतावपि ज्ञातस्य त्वद्दतो मे मनोरथः ॥ यदि नाशं न विंदेत तावतास्मि कृती सदा । कामये विष्णुपादौ तु सर्वजन्मसु केवलं ॥ (*tvatpādakamalādanyanna me janmāṃtareṣṭapi | vijñānaṃ yadidaṃ prāpya yadidaṃ sthānamarjitaṃ ‖ janmāṃtare 'pi me deva mā bhūdasya parikṣayaḥ durgatāvapi jñātasya tvaddato me manorathaḥ ‖ yadi nāśaṃ na viṃdeta tāvatāsmi kṛtī sadā | kāmaye viṣṇupādau tu sarvajanmasu kevalaṃ ‖*)

Having offered homa in this way and obtained the permission of the Lord of the gods, one should sit near the fire and praise the Lord as stated below: O lotus-eyed one, O creator of the world, O Hṛṣīkeśa, O one of great glory, you are the god of the gods and of the dānavas, that is, you are their lord. I always take refuge at your two feet. You alone are the creator and the destroyer of this world. You are of unmanifest nature; it is not possible even to meditate on you. You are united with the guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas, and with māyā (prakṛti). The discerning, taking refuge in you alone, become able to cross this terrible and sorrowful ocean of saṃsāra. You have no fixed form or shape. You have no weapon and no abode. Yet, in order to favour your devotees, you take the human form and shine. In the world there is nothing that is unseen or unknown to you, yet you alone are not directly visible to anyone. There is nothing impossible for you. No one can know your nature. You are the cause of all effects. You are praised by words. For yogis you alone are the siddhi, that is, the fixed place; your abode is famed as the supreme highest state. O Lord of the gods, fallen into this terrible ocean of saṃsāra and suffering, I am afraid, not seeing the way to be freed from it. O lotus-eyed one, protect me. Your supreme state

### Printed p. 708

Your supreme state I cannot know. At all times, in all places, in my own body and in this world, great fear comes upon me. Through birth after birth, apart from your lotus feet I have no other refuge. May knowledge of you and devotion to you be mine in the next birth also; may it never be destroyed. Whatever misfortune may befall me, that is, whatever time of hardship may come, may my mind always remain fixed on you; may it not perish. Then I shall count myself blessed. In all births I desire that my mind rest at the feet of Viṣṇu alone.

पुरुषस्य हरेः सूक्तं स्वर्ग्यं धन्यं यशस्करं । आत्मज्ञानमिदं पुण्यं योगध्यानमिदं परं ॥ (*puruṣasya hareḥ sūktaṃ svargyaṃ dhanyaṃ yaśaskaraṃ | ātmajñānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ yogadhyānamidaṃ paraṃ ‖*)

This Puruṣa-sūkta is most excellent. The man who recites it is blessed. It brings fame, the world of heaven, knowledge of the Self and the accomplishment of yoga.

फलाहारो भवेन्मासं पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि । फलानि भुक्तोपवसेन्मासमद्भिश्च वर्तयेत् ॥ अरण्ये निवसेन्नित्यं जपन्नेतमृषिं सदा । त्रिस्त्रिषवणकालेषु स्नायादप्सु समाहितः ॥ आदित्यमुपतिष्ठेत सूक्तेनानेन नित्यशः । अज्याहुतीरनेनैव हुत्वैतं चिंतयेदृषिं ॥ (*phalāhāro bhavenmāsaṃ paśyatyātmānamātmani | phalāni bhuktopavasenmāsamadbhiśca vartayet ‖ araṇye nivasennityaṃ japannetamṛṣiṃ sadā | tristriṣavaṇakāleṣu snāyādapsu samāhitaḥ ‖ ādityamupatiṣṭheta sūktenānena nityaśaḥ | ajyāhutīranenaiva hutvaitaṃ ciṃtayedṛṣiṃ ‖*)

ऊर्ध्वं मासात्फलाहारस्त्रिभिर्वर्षैर्जयेद्दिवं । तद्भक्तस्तन्मनायुक्तो दश वर्षाण्यनन्यभाक् । साक्षात्पश्यति तं देवं नारायणमनामयं । ग्राह्यमत्यंतयत्नेन स्रष्टारं जगतोऽव्ययं ॥ (*ūrdhvaṃ māsātphalāhārastribhirvarṣairjayeddivaṃ | tadbhaktastanmanāyukto daśa varṣāṇyananyabhāk | sākṣātpaśyati taṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayaṃ | grāhyamatyaṃtayatnena sraṣṭāraṃ jagato 'vyayaṃ ‖*)

The manner of worshipping the god of gods by this Puruṣa-sūkta procedure is now told. For one month one must fast, eating only fruits. Water alone may be drunk; nothing else may be taken. If this is done for one month, that man attains realization of the Self. While performing this vow he must dwell always in the forest. He must always meditate on Nārāyaṇa, the seer of this sūkta. At the three times, morning, noon and evening, having bathed in rivers and the like and become pure, he must pray to (worship) Āditya, reciting this Puruṣa-sūkta. In the consecrated fire, reciting the mantras of this sūkta

### Printed p. 709

and meditating on Nārāyaṇa, he must offer oblations of ghee. So he must do daily. **NOTE**. After a month has passed he must eat fruits. If he does this for three years, the world of heaven also comes into that man's hand. In this manner, if for ten years he worships with the mind fixed on the god of gods alone, Nārāyaṇa himself will appear before him. He who is the creator of the world, imperishable, and prayed to by all, Nārāyaṇa, must be worshipped with effort.

गृहस्थधर्मे वर्तेत न्यायक् प्तः शुचिव्रतः । एतं देवं चिंतयेत नारायणमनामयं ॥ अर्धरात्रे त्यक्तनिद्र उत्थाय शुचिर्वाग्यतः ॥ संप्रसुप्तेषु भूतेषु योगं युंजीत योगवित् ! ऋज्वासीनः समे देशे निवाते शब्दवर्जिते । सव्यं पाद्मं दक्षिणस्य जानुनि श्लेषयेत्ततः ॥ संहृत्य दक्षिणं पाद्मं सव्यॆ जानुनि ऋच्छति ॥ ब्रह्मांजलिकृतः स्वस्थो योगसंमीलितेक्षणः ॥ (*gṛhasthadharme varteta nyāyak ptaḥ śucivrataḥ | etaṃ devaṃ ciṃtayeta nārāyaṇamanāmayaṃ ‖ ardharātre tyaktanidra utthāya śucirvāgyataḥ ‖ saṃprasupteṣu bhūteṣu yogaṃ yuṃjīta yogavit ! ṛjvāsīnaḥ same deśe nivāte śabdavarjite | savyaṃ pādmaṃ dakṣiṇasya jānuni śleṣayettataḥ ‖ saṃhṛtya dakṣiṇaṃ pādmaṃ savyè jānuni ṛcchati ‖ brahmāṃjalikṛtaḥ svastho yogasaṃmīlitekṣaṇaḥ ‖*)

ओमित्युक्ता स्वं हृदयं चिंतयेदविशंकितः । तत्रात्मानं समादध्यादिंद्रियाणि मनस्तथा ॥ न चेद्बुध्येत किंचान्यन्न पश्येच्छृणुयान्न च । न मनस्केद्यदा योगं तदा प्राप्तः स उच्यते ॥ हृद्येतमृषिमभ्यसेत्पश्यन्निव यथाश्रुति । (*omityuktā svaṃ hṛdayaṃ ciṃtayedaviśaṃkitaḥ | tatrātmānaṃ samādadhyādiṃdriyāṇi manastathā ‖ na cedbudhyeta kiṃcānyanna paśyecchṛṇuyānna ca | na manaskedyadā yogaṃ tadā prāptaḥ sa ucyate ‖ hṛdyetamṛṣimabhyasetpaśyanniva yathāśruti |*)

The householder, having become pure through bathing and the like, must meditate on Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme. At night, when all are lying asleep, he must give up sleep, rise from his bed, and, pure and restrained in speech, practise yoga. Seated comfortably in a clean, solitary place, level, without pits or mounds, and free from noises such as tumult, he must be intent on yoga. Folding the right leg over the left leg and joining it at the knee-joint, and likewise folding the other leg and joining it at the knee-joint of the left leg, that is, sitting in the lotus posture, with folded hands, with no thought in the mind, fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose or on the middle of the brows, and reciting the praṇava mantra, he must meditate on the Self in the lotus of his heart. He must restrain the senses and the mind, that is, stop their outward activity. **NOTE** He must not set his gaze on other

### Printed p. 710

objects, must hear no sound with the ears, and must not turn his attention in the mind to any subject other than the meditation he is performing. If he does so, yoga will be accomplished. As he has heard and seen, he must think in his heart of Nārāyaṇa, the seer of the sūkta.

प्राणानायम्य चासीनो यावत्तं चिंत्येदृषिं । उच्छ्वसिष्यन्नधो नाभिं गमयित्वा मनस्तथा । उच्छ्वसेदेवमसकृत्तन्मना योगमुन्नयेत् एवं हि युंजन्यामान्यं न पश्येच्छृणु हन्न च । तदा शनैर्नयेच्चेतो हृदयादूर्ध्वमेव तु । (*prāṇānāyamya cāsīno yāvattaṃ ciṃtyedṛṣiṃ | ucchvasiṣyannadho nābhiṃ gamayitvā manastathā | ucchvasedevamasakṛttanmanā yogamunnayet evaṃ hi yuṃjanyāmānyaṃ na paśyecchṛṇu hanna ca | tadā śanairnayecceto hṛdayādūrdhvameva tu |*)

समौ तु जत्रू चास्यं च नासिकानयने भ्रुवौ । भ्रुवोर्मध्यॆ परं स्थानं तत्रैतद्धारयेत्स्थिगं । ललाटदेशे धार्याथ मूर्धानं गमयेत् । उच्छ्वसंश्च यथाकालं नाभिं गत्वोच्चिपेत्पुनः । एतत्परं स्थानमुक्तं ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः । एवं युक्तो महात्मानमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ (*samau tu jatrū cāsyaṃ ca nāsikānayane bhruvau | bhruvormadhyè paraṃ sthānaṃ tatraitaddhārayetsthigaṃ | lalāṭadeśe dhāryātha mūrdhānaṃ gamayet | ucchvasaṃśca yathākālaṃ nābhiṃ gatvoccipetpunaḥ | etatparaṃ sthānamuktaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ | evaṃ yukto mahātmānamātmānaṃ pratipadyate ‖*)

First, seated comfortably on the seat and meditating on Nārāyaṇa, the seer, he must practise prāṇāyāma. Keeping the mind steady, he must control the vital breath by inhalation and exhalation so that it extends from the navel downwards; that is, according to the order of prāṇāyāma, for the prescribed measures of time he must perform inhalation, exhalation and kumbhaka (stopping the breath and holding it in the heart), and so on, as instructed by the guru. At that time he must not fix the mind on other subjects. He must look at nothing and hear nothing. Doing so, he must slowly bring his mind **NOTE** up from the heart and hold the gaze steadily on the tip of the nose or on the middle of the brows (bhrū). After that he must practise dhāraṇā in due order on the forehead and on the head. There must be order in inhalation and exhalation. The mūrdha region, that is, the place on the crown of the head, is called the place of Brahman (brahmarandhra). By the practice of yoga, bringing the mind step by step and fixing it in that place of Brahman, yoga is accomplished and realization of the Self comes.

यदि स्यात्सुकृती शुद्धो यदि वा पापकृत्तमः । उपलभ्य परं ब्रह्म गतिं ज्ञात्वा भवेच्छुचिः ॥ सर्वपापानुबद्धश्चेत् बुद्धैतत्पयतो जपेत् । अभिजिज्ञासनादेव गच्छेत परमां गतिं ॥ (*yadi syātsukṛtī śuddho yadi vā pāpakṛttamaḥ | upalabhya paraṃ brahma gatiṃ jñātvā bhavecchuciḥ ‖ sarvapāpānubaddhaścet buddhaitatpayato japet | abhijijñāsanādeva gaccheta paramāṃ gatiṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 711

A man who thus practises yoga, whether he be a virtuous man doing good deeds or a sinner practising sins, if he has attained realization of Brahman, becomes pure and freed from all sin. Therefore the discerning man, having thus performed the recitation of the mantra and, through yoga and the like, become free of sin, must attain the highest state.

धारणा तु पृथक्कार्या धर्मेणानेन नित्यशः । अदित्वेऽग्ना चंद्रमसि वृक्षाग्रेषु च धारयेत् ॥ पर्वताग्रे समुद्रॆ वा यत्र वापि मनो रमेत् । न त्वेव विषयान्पाप्य धारयीत कदाचन । बह्वत्र दुःखं जानीयात्सध्वंसे धारणाकृते । (*dhāraṇā tu pṛthakkāryā dharmeṇānena nityaśaḥ | aditve 'gnā caṃdramasi vṛkṣāgreṣu ca dhārayet ‖ parvatāgre samudrè vā yatra vāpi mano ramet | na tveva viṣayānpāpya dhārayīta kadācana | bahvatra duḥkhaṃ jānīyātsadhvaṃse dhāraṇākṛte |*)

In the course of the practice of yoga there are eight limbs: yama, niyama, āsana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, dhyāna and samādhi. Of these, the first five are known as the outer limbs and the last three as the inner limbs. To explain here the nature of all these eight limbs is not to the purpose. Since only the subject called dhāraṇā is mentioned here, it is necessary to explain it briefly. When meditating on the subject of an object, thinking of that object itself and making the mind rest in it alone is called dhāraṇā. Dhāraṇā means making the mind rest with one-pointedness only in a definite object, so that it does not move to other subjects. Because the mind is fickle, and because in the waking state the mind is never without work even for a moment, to make the mind stand steadily in one subject is very hard to accomplish. This is achieved only by practice over a long time. When thinking about a subject, that object or subject must have been experienced at least once. That is, when meditating on the sea, one must have seen the sea at least once. If one has not seen it, one cannot meditate on it fully. For this very reason it is not possible, in the beginning, to meditate on deities whom we have never seen. For this very reason, that is, when carrying out the method of meditating on an object, one must choose an object that is seen by our eyes and has been experienced, fix the mind on it and meditate. That has been said here by way of examples. That is, when practising, one must first fix the mind on Āditya (the sun), fire, the moon, a tree, a mountain, the sea, or any object one wishes, and practise the method of meditation. But one must never meditate on the pleasures of sense objects such as desire and women. From that arise great harm and sorrow; from that the accomplishment of yoga does not arise. Having strengthened the practice by meditating on visible objects such as the sun, one must afterwards meditate on deities and the like that are not visible.

### Printed p. 712

धार्मिकाणां कुले शुद्धे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते । मूर्ध्नि ब्रह्म यदा विंदेत् तमेव ऋषिसत्तमं । तदा मूर्ध्नः परं ज्योतिर्नक्षत्रपथमुन्नयेत् ॥ योगी योगेश्वरं प्राप्य निर्द्वंद्वः परमात्मवित् । सर्वत्रैवात्मनात्मानं पश्येदृषिपरायणः ॥ य (*dhārmikāṇāṃ kule śuddhe yogabhraṣṭo 'bhijāyate | mūrdhni brahma yadā viṃdet tameva ṛṣisattamaṃ | tadā mūrdhnaḥ paraṃ jyotirnakṣatrapathamunnayet ‖ yogī yogeśvaraṃ prāpya nirdvaṃdvaḥ paramātmavit | sarvatraivātmanātmānaṃ paśyedṛṣiparāyaṇaḥ ‖ ya*)

If a yogi engaged in the practice of yoga dies before attaining accomplishment, the yoga he has practised up to then is not wasted. As its reward he will be born in the next birth in a pure, good family. One engaged in yoga must bring his mind step by step to the mūrdha, that is, to the brahmarandhra in the head. If he does so, a divine light goes out from that brahmarandhra and reaches the sphere of the stars. That is, the seeker attains realization of the Supreme Self, the Lord of yogis. After realization of the Self, the nature of the Supreme Self becomes well known to the yogi. He becomes nirdvandva, that is, he sees no difference at all between pleasure, pain and the like. For him pleasure is one and pain is one. Without sorrow, with an ever peaceful mind, he experiences supreme bliss alone. Besides this, another meaning can be given for nirdvandva. Nirdvandva means free from duality, without a second thing, that is, one thing only. The whole universe, moving and unmoving, is the form of the Supreme Self. To know from experience that apart from that Supreme Self there is no second thing at all is called the nirdvandva state of mind. The yogi who has attained such a state of mind knows that in all beings and in all moving and unmoving things there is the one Self alone, and that there is in the universe no thing other than the Self; that is, knowing the true nature, he rejoices.

जपेच्चैव सदा स्नातः पवित्रमिदमुत्तमं । अपि पातकसंयुक्तः कालेन सुकृती भवेत् । तपःपरायणो नित्यं सत्यवागनसूयिकः । जपन्नेतमृषिं विप्रः कालेन स वनी भवेत् । येन येन स कामेन जपेदिममृषिं सदा । स स कामः समृद्धः स्याच्छ्रद्धधानस्य कुर्वतः ॥ (*japeccaiva sadā snātaḥ pavitramidamuttamaṃ | api pātakasaṃyuktaḥ kālena sukṛtī bhavet | tapaḥparāyaṇo nityaṃ satyavāganasūyikaḥ | japannetamṛṣiṃ vipraḥ kālena sa vanī bhavet | yena yena sa kāmena japedimamṛṣiṃ sadā | sa sa kāmaḥ samṛddhaḥ syācchraddhadhānasya kurvataḥ ‖*)

To recite these sūkta mantras, one must bathe and become pure, and only then recite this excellent mantra. Even if one has committed many sins and grave offences, the man who recites this mantra will in course of time make atonement for the sins and become virtuous. While reciting this mantra the seeker must be engaged in austerity alone, speak only true words, be without hatred or envy toward anyone, and remain with a peaceful mind. These sūkta mantras must be recited in a solitary, unobstructed, pure

### Printed p. 713

forest region. When one meditates on Nārāyaṇa, the seer of this sūkta, that is, on Parameśvara, whatever desires one wishes in the mind and meditates with faith, those desires will be fulfilled without fail.

होमं नाप्यथवा जाप्यमुपहारमथो चरुं । कुर्वीत येन कामेन तत्सिद्धिमवधारयेत् ॥ (*homaṃ nāpyathavā jāpyamupahāramatho caruṃ | kurvīta yena kāmena tatsiddhimavadhārayet ‖*)

ज्ञातिश्रैष्ठ्यं महद्वित्तं यशो लोके परां गतिं । ज्ञानेन विप्रमोक्षं च तत्सिद्धिमवधारयेत् ॥ ज्ञानगम्यं परं सूक्ष्मं व्याप्य सर्वमवस्थितं । ग्राह्यमत्यंतयत्नेन ब्रह्माभ्येति सनातनं ॥ (*jñātiśraiṣṭhyaṃ mahadvittaṃ yaśo loke parāṃ gatiṃ | jñānena vipramokṣaṃ ca tatsiddhimavadhārayet ‖ jñānagamyaṃ paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ vyāpya sarvamavasthitaṃ | grāhyamatyaṃtayatnena brahmābhyeti sanātanaṃ ‖*)

Having recited these Puruṣa-sūkta mantras, or having offered homa in the fire with the sūkta mantras and partaken of the remainder of the oblation, whatever wish is in the mind, all of it will be accomplished. The man who does so becomes esteemed and honoured among his kinsmen, gains fame and wealth, and lives happily. At the end he also attains an excellent, good state. Besides, through excellent knowledge of Brahman he also obtains liberation. Therefore the discerning man must meditate with the utmost effort on the Supreme Brahman, who is known by pure knowledge alone, who is most subtle, who pervades all things and is eternal, and so attain accomplishment.

सहस्रशीर्षेति सूक्तं सर्वकामफलप्रदं । वेदगर्भशरीरेण स वै नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ (*sahasraśīrṣeti sūktaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradaṃ | vedagarbhaśarīreṇa sa vai nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ‖*)

ब्रह्मेंद्ररुद्रपर्जन्या अत्र सूक्ते व्यवस्थिताः । अत्रस्थमेतद्दृष्टव्यं जगत्स्थावरजंगमं । अनासादयमानोऽपि भक्तिं न परिहापयेत् ! भक्तानुकंपी भगवान् श्रूयते पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ (*brahmeṃdrarudraparjanyā atra sūkte vyavasthitāḥ | atrasthametaddṛṣṭavyaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamaṃ | anāsādayamāno 'pi bhaktiṃ na parihāpayet ! bhaktānukaṃpī bhagavān śrūyate puruṣottamaḥ ‖*)

This sūkta called Sahasraśīrṣā grants all desired objects to those who recite it. In this sūkta Nārāyaṇa, who is the subject taught in the Vedas, is praised. Besides, other deities such as Brahmā, Indra, Rudra and Parjanya, and also the world of moving and unmoving things, are set forth in it. Even if one cannot rightly understand the ultimate meaning set forth in this sūkta, one must not give up devotion to this sūkta and to Nārāyaṇa, the subject of the sūkta. For it is renowned that the Lord, the Supreme Person, looks upon his devotees with a compassionate eye and fulfils their prayers.

### Printed p. 714

पूजार्थं तस्य देवस्य वन्यान्वयमुपार्जितान् । आरण्यकविधानेन निर्वपेत्पत्यहं चरुं ॥ नारायणाय स्वाहेति मंत्रांते जुहुयाद्वविः । आसहस्रात्ततत्चक्षुर्दिव्यं होतुर्ददाति सः ॥ (*pūjārthaṃ tasya devasya vanyānvayamupārjitān | āraṇyakavidhānena nirvapetpatyahaṃ caruṃ ‖ nārāyaṇāya svāheti maṃtrāṃte juhuyādvaviḥ | āsahasrāttatatcakṣurdivyaṃ hoturdadāti saḥ ‖*)

अपि ना चरुसहस्रं तंत्रेणैकेन निर्वपेत् । यावंतो वापि शक्यंते अह्ना सर्वान्समापयेत् ॥ सहस्रस्येप्सितानां च कामानां लभते फलं । पुरुषायुःसमायुक्तः सिद्धो वापि चरेन्महीं ॥ (*api nā carusahasraṃ taṃtreṇaikena nirvapet | yāvaṃto vāpi śakyaṃte ahnā sarvānsamāpayet ‖ sahasrasyepsitānāṃ ca kāmānāṃ labhate phalaṃ | puruṣāyuḥsamāyuktaḥ siddho vāpi carenmahīṃ ‖*)

The deity Nārāyaṇa, the subject of this sūkta, must be worshipped with flowers and the like obtained in the forests and brought by oneself, according to what is said in the Āraṇyaka scripture, and homa with caru must be offered daily. When offering homa, at the end of every mantra the words नारायणाय स्वाहा (*nārāyaṇāya svāhā*) must be added. If homa is offered in this way a thousand times, the Supreme Self grants to the man who has offered it divine sight, that is, the power to see and know all things that are not possible for ordinary people. Or else this caru homa may be performed by the method taught in the Tantra. As far as possible these homa rites must be completed in the daytime. The man who so practises, obtaining thousands of the desires he wishes, will live in this world the span of life of a man, that is, a hundred years, and be happy. Or, having become accomplished, he will be able to travel over this whole earth.

ध्येयः सदा सवितृमंडलमध्यवर्ति नारायणः सरसिजासनसन्निष्टः । केयूरवान् मकरकुंडलवान् किरीटी हारी हिरण्मयवपुर्धृतशंखचक्रः ॥ (*dhyeyaḥ sadā savitṛmaṃḍalamadhyavarti nārāyaṇaḥ sarasijāsanasanniṣṭaḥ | keyūravān makarakuṃḍalavān kirīṭī hārī hiraṇmayavapurdhṛtaśaṃkhacakraḥ ‖*)

Nārāyaṇa, the subject of the sūkta, must be meditated on in this way. This form of Nārāyaṇa always shines, abiding within the orb of Āditya. He is seated on a lotus seat. He wears divine ornaments such as armlets, makara earrings, a crown and a necklace. Holding the conch and the discus in his hands, he shines with the radiance of a golden body.

एतत्तु यः पठति केवलमेव सूक्तं नारायणस्य चरणावभिवंद्य वंद्या । (*etattu yaḥ paṭhati kevalameva sūktaṃ nārāyaṇasya caraṇāvabhivaṃdya vaṃdyā |*)

### Printed p. 715

पाठेन तेन परमेण सनातनस्य, स्थानं जरामरणवर्जितमेति विष्णोः ॥ (*pāṭhena tena parameṇa sanātanasya, sthānaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitameti viṣṇoḥ ‖*)

The man who, bowing with devotion to the supremely venerable lotus feet of this Nārāyaṇa, recites this Puruṣa-sūkta merely (even once only), attains, through the power of reciting that sūkta, the place of liberation called the supreme state of that eternal Viṣṇu, free from old age and death.

हविषाग्नौ जले पुष्पैर्ध्यानेन हृदये हरिं । यजंति सूरयो नित्यं जस्यॆ न रविमंडले ॥ (*haviṣāgnau jale puṣpairdhyānena hṛdaye hariṃ | yajaṃti sūrayo nityaṃ jasyè na ravimaṃḍale ‖*)

The manner of worshipping this god of gods is this: in fire, oblations and the like must be offered as homa. In water, he must be worshipped with flowers. In the heart, he must be worshipped with meditation. In the orb of the sun, one must meditate on the god and recite japa. In these various ways, discerning men worship Nārāyaṇa every day.

बिल्वपत्रं शमीपत्रं पत्रं भृंगारकस्य च । मालतीकुशपद्मं च सद्यस्तुष्टिकरं हरेः ॥ यन्नोपपद्यते किंचित्तं ध्यायेन्मनसैव तु । संपद्यंते प्रसादात्तु देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥ (*bilvapatraṃ śamīpatraṃ patraṃ bhṛṃgārakasya ca | mālatīkuśapadmaṃ ca sadyastuṣṭikaraṃ hareḥ ‖ yannopapadyate kiṃcittaṃ dhyāyenmanasaiva tu | saṃpadyaṃte prasādāttu devadevasya cakriṇaḥ ‖*)

Bilva leaf, śamī leaf, leaf of Śṛṅgāraka **NOTE**, mālatī flower, kuśa (darbha leaf), and padma, or lotus flower: all these are exceedingly dear to Nārāyaṇa. Therefore he must be worshipped with them. If any of these cannot be obtained, one must imagine it in the mind and worship with it. If one does so, by the grace of that god of gods, the discus-bearer, all desired aims will be accomplished.

पत्रैश्च पुष्पैश्च फलैश्च तोयैरक्रीतलब्धैश्च सदैव सत्सु । भक्तैकलभ्ये पुरुषे पुराणे मुक्त्यै किमर्थं क्रियते न यत्नः ॥ (*patraiśca puṣpaiśca phalaiśca toyairakrītalabdhaiśca sadaiva satsu | bhaktaikalabhye puruṣe purāṇe muktyai kimarthaṃ kriyate na yatnaḥ ‖*)

What is the use of not striving for liberation by worshipping that ancient Supreme Person, who is attainable by devotion alone, with leaves, flowers, fruits and water obtained by oneself or earned by one's own labour, without giving money and the like in exchange?

इत्येवमुक्तः पुरुषस्य विष्णोर्चाविधिः विष्णु कुमारनाम्मा । (*ityevamuktaḥ puruṣasya viṣṇorcāvidhiḥ viṣṇu kumāranāmmā |*) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 716

मुक्त्यैकमार्गप्रतिबोधनाय दृष्ट्वा विधानं त्वह नारदोक्तं ॥ (*muktyaikamārgapratibodhanāya dṛṣṭvā vidhānaṃ tvaha nāradoktaṃ ‖*)

Following this procedure of worship, which was spoken by the great seer Nārada, and which is a means to the path of liberation, one named Viṣṇu Kumāra has thus set out the order of worship of the Supreme Person, the venerable Viṣṇu (Nārāyaṇa).

Here ends the introduction relating to the Puruṣa-sūkta in the Ṛgvidhāna spoken by Śaunaka.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सहस्रशीर्षेति षोडशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । नारायणो नामर्षिरंत्या त्रिष्टुप्
> शिष्टा अनुष्टुभः । अव्यक्तमहदादिविलक्षणश्चेतनो यः पुरुषः । वे. सू. १-४-१ ।
> पुरुषान्न परं किंचित् । क. उ. ३-११ । इत्यादिश्रुतिषु प्रसिद्धः स देवता तथा
> चानुक्रांतं । सहस्रशीर्षा षोळश नारायणः पौरुषमानुष्टुभं त्रिष्टुबंतं त्विति ॥
> गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning सहस्रशीर्षा (*sahasraśīrṣā*) is the sixth sūkta and has sixteen Ṛks. Its seer is the seer named Nārāyaṇa. The last Ṛk is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining Ṛks are in Anuṣṭubh. Its deity is the Puruṣa, the conscious being who is distinct from the unmanifest, the Mahat and the rest (Ve. Sū. 1-4-1), and who is known in the śruti texts, for example in "There is nothing beyond the Puruṣa" (Ka. U. 3-11). **NOTE** Sāyaṇa adds that the Anukramaṇī lists it accordingly: the sūkta Sahasraśīrṣā, sixteen Ṛks, seer Nārāyaṇa, the Puruṣa as deity, Anuṣṭubh, with the last in Triṣṭubh. The application in ritual has been stated earlier.

The Kannada Anuvāda: This sūkta called सहस्रशीर्षा (*sahasraśīrṣā*) is the sixth sūkta in the seventh Anuvāka. It has sixteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the seer named Nārāyaṇa. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre and the remaining Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre. The deity of this sūkta is the Supreme Person himself, who is distinguished by qualities such as the unmanifest and the Mahat (Vedāntasūtra 1-4-1), and who is famed in the śruti passages, in the sense that there is no other thing than this Puruṣa (Ka. U. 3-11). In the Anukramaṇī it is said सहस्रशीर्षा षोळश नारायणः पौरुषमानुष्टुभं त्रिष्टुबंतं तु (*sahasraśīrṣā ṣoḷaśa nārāyaṇaḥ pauruṣamānuṣṭubhaṃ triṣṭubaṃtaṃ tu*). The application in ritual has been stated before.

- Maṇḍala 10; Anuvāka 7; Sūkta 90.
- Aṣṭaka 8; Adhyāya 4; Vargas 13, 18, 19.
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 16.
- Seer: Nārāyaṇa.
- Deity: Puruṣa.
- Metre: Ṛks 1-15, Anuṣṭubh; Ṛk 16, Triṣṭubh.
